author: shourjoguha
body:
## Why

Three axes measured the wrong thing. **Strength** was a mean best e1RM — "how heavy can you lift", not "how much work did you do". **Power** was plyometric *minutes*, chosen because minutes were already being aggregated. **Endurance** counted aerobic minutes weighted by average HR, so it couldn't see dense strength work and discarded `hr_max` entirely: an interval session and a steady-state session at the same average HR scored identically.

## Strength & power — scaled training volume

`setVolume` reads the parts of a set the app was throwing away:

| Scalar | Effect | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `/side` | ×2 | Reps are logged per side and **nothing in the codebase doubled them** — half of every unilateral set has always been invisible to every metric |
| `(p)` | ×1.2 | A paused rep is more time under tension |
| RPE | ±5%/point | Near-failure work is a bigger stimulus at equal tonnage |

Absent RPE scores **1.0, never a penalty** — otherwise the metric rewards the habit of logging RPE rather than the training.

Time and distance convert to rep-equivalents through `LOAD.repSeconds` and `LOAD.metersPerMinute` — the same constants `setMinutes` uses — so a plank, a carry and a set of squats stay commensurable the way they already do on the body map.

**Strength** additionally weights each set by load relative to that movement's own best e1RM. The e1RM machinery isn't discarded; it moves from *being* the metric to setting the intensity reference. **Power** biases toward low-rep sets, or 20 tired jumps would outrank 6 sharp ones.

### One correction to the plan

I claimed intensity weighting would put a heavy block "within ~5%" of a light one. That was wrong — I'd estimated it loosely. Volume-based strength inherently favours volume, and no sane weighting makes 5×3 equal 5×10. What the weighting actually does is stop a peaking block reading as a *collapse*, so the test asserts that (the gap narrows vs raw tonnage) rather than a magnitude I guessed at.

## Endurance — three components

```
endurance = HR-weighted aerobic minutes
          + dense strength work
          + (hr_max − hr_avg) × session length × conditioning boost
```

The spread term is the interval signature — the only thing separating a threshold session from steady state at the same average HR — scaled by session length and boosted when a conditioning block was actually logged, per your instruction.

**Actual rest between sets is never recorded anywhere.** `TIMERS.restPresets` is UI config and no rest-timer result is persisted; `LogItem.restSeconds` is user-set *intent* defaulting to 120. So density averages the two reads that do exist: prescribed rest, and working-minutes over wall-clock elapsed (measured, but conflates rest with faffing). Neither is complete alone.

## The trap in this change

Redefining a metric **poisons** the stored baseline rather than resetting it. The radar scores against the median of past values, so a baseline holding both a kilogram e1RM (~110) and a volume figure (~thousands) describes neither — and there's no symptom. The polygon still draws, the vertices still fill, the numbers are just wrong.

So metrics carry `ASPECT_METRICS_VERSION`. Migration `0019` adds the column and clears stale rows; `getAspectSnapshots` filters on it. **The read filter is the guard that matters** — the migration cleans up, but a bare `DELETE` migration would have fixed today and wiped a good baseline the next time it ran.

## Verification

**464 tests** — 36 in `bodyLoad` covering each scalar independently, missing-RPE neutrality, time/distance conversion parity, the heavy-vs-light regression, both density reads, and NaN guards for a set carrying nothing but `completed: true`. `astro check` clean, `audit:docs` / `audit:mobile` / `audit:flicker` green.

**Migration applied to the live project and confirmed**: column present with default 1, 24 stale rows cleared, RLS still enabled with its 5 policies.

**Throwaway probe across five baseline depths** (`audit:mobile` still can't see this surface). The four chart renderings all hold — unscored / thin / mixed / settled — plus a fifth case worth its keep: a full 30-week baseline written under the *old* version renders identically to having no baseline at all, proving the version filter actually bites.

## Note

`total_seconds` is capped at 7200 by migration `0015`, so a genuinely long session under-reports elapsed time and reads as denser than it was. And the constants (`pauseFactor`, `rpePerPoint`, `refIntensity`, `densityWeight`, `conditioningBoost`) are judgement calls — relative scoring means their absolute values matter little, but the **mix** does: a large `densityWeight` would turn endurance into a strength proxy. Worth reviewing against real data once a baseline rebuilds.

author: nickk02
body:
Closes the bug left open last session. **The nav rail was never broken.** PR #20's fix was correct. The hero image drew on top of it.

## One bug, two symptoms

WinUI3 panels do not clip children to their bounds, and there is no `ClipToBounds`. The `TranslateTransform X="-110"` that moved the Lich King left overflowed HomePage's own left edge and drew over MainWindow's nav column.

- "Settings is missing" - the whole rail was covered, not one item.
- "The hero does not fill the launcher" - the same 110px shift left a gap on the right.

## Changes

**A clip on `RootGrid`**, re-cut on `SizeChanged`. This fixes the bug class, whatever overflows next.

**The pan is now a negative left margin, not a `RenderTransform`.** Review this part. A transform moves the image after layout, which is why panning left opened a gap on the right. A negative left margin makes the layout box 110px wider and starts it 110px early, so the art still reaches the right edge and there is real content to show. This replaces both the transform and the explicit-Width step from the plan, with no arithmetic in code-behind.

**Play button contrast.** It used the default style over dark art and was hard to see. It now uses the palette already in the page: `#CBB98A` from the login border and `#F0C860` from the active nav item. The state brushes are set as `Button.Resources`, because the default template replaces `Background` and `Foreground` on hover and press.

## Verification

Builds clean at Release x64 with 0 errors. The two warnings are pre-existing: the duplicate `WindowsAppRuntimeAutoInitializer.cpp` and the `GetCurrentTime` macro warning.

**Not visually confirmed.** The built exe runs and opens a real 900x620 window, but screen capture is unavailable, so I have not seen the result.

author: nkcodec
body:
fix(library): 4 post-#318 audit fixes — parent AQE config, streaming limitation, manifest validation, doc correctness

Post-#318 audit caught 3 HIGH + 2 MED + several LOW. This PR addresses 4
of the actionable findings. One MED (rename `salt` to
`aqeSkewPartitionFactor`) is deferred as a backwards-compat decision.

**Fix #1 — Library now sets the parent `adaptive.enabled` config.**
PR #318 set `spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled = true` but did NOT
set the parent `spark.sql.adaptive.enabled`. Without the parent, the
skew child is a no-op (Spark ignores skew settings when AQE itself is
disabled). The library now sets both, in the correct order. Operator
who explicitly disabled AQE for compliance/audit reasons will see it
re-enabled — this is documented in the salt Scaladoc as an explicit
trade-off of `withSalt`.

**Fix #2 — Streaming path properly threads salt + broadcastJoinThreshold.**
The `batchModel` constructor in `SemanticTableStreaming.scala:237`
previously omitted both `salt = this.salt` and
`broadcastJoinThreshold = this.broadcastJoinThreshold`. A streaming
source with `withSalt(n)` would silently lose skew handling on its
first micro-batch (cold session) and on every batch (race against any
concurrent reader). Both fields are now threaded.

**Fix #3 — Static-stream join plan now gets AQE config too.**
The static-stream path constructs the streaming query plan at
`writeStream.start()` time. Spark planning reads SQLConf at that
moment. PR #318's fix only applied AQE inside `batchModel.toDataFrame`
(foreachBatch path), missing the static-stream path entirely. The
library now extracts the AQE config setup into a helper
`applyAqeSkewConfig(spark)` called from BOTH:
- `toDataFrameInternal` (batch terminal)
- `toStreamingQuery` (streaming terminal — BEFORE writeStream triggers
  Spark planning)

**Fix #3a — Documented Spark's streaming AQE limitation.**
Spark's `ResolveWriteToStream` rule disables AQE for streaming
DataFrames automatically (warning:
`spark.sql.adaptive.enabled is not supported in streaming DataFrames/
Datasets and will be disabled`). So `withSalt` on a streaming model
CANNOT enable skew handling at the streaming query level. The library
now applies the config (the factor is set), but Spark overrides
`adaptive.enabled = false` during streaming plan construction. This
is documented in the salt Scaladoc. The skew-handling hint is
therefore only effective for batch joins (`join_one` / `join_many`).
For streaming queries, the library is a no-op — operators should use
batch-mode joins or accept the Spark AQE limitation.

**Fix #4 — Manifest reader validates `salt >= 1`.**
The setter converts `withSalt(0)` to `None` (the disable sentinel),
so `salt = 0` in a hand-rolled manifest is malformed. The reader now
rejects `salt = 0` and negative values with a clear `IllegalArgumentException`
pointing at the JSON path. The schema's `minimum: 1` covers
library-emitted manifests; the reader closes the hand-rolled gap.

**Fix #5 — Corrected the AQE terminology in Scaladoc.**
PR #318's Scaladoc said "broadcasts them automatically" — wrong.
Spark AQE (per `OptimizeSkewedJoin.scala`) "divides each skewed
shuffle partition into smaller sub-partitions and replicates the
matching partition on the other side of the join." The Scaladoc on
`SemanticTable.salt`, `withSalt`, and the `toDataFrameInternal` comment
are all updated to the corrected wording. Also fixed the stale
`readRuntime` Scaladoc (still claimed a two-element tuple).

Tests: 903 pass on Spark 3.5.8 + 4.1.1 (was 898, +5 = the 5 new
post-audit tests).

Deferred (not blocking):
- Rename `salt` to `aqeSkewPartitionFactor` (Architect's MED) —
  requires API break; current name matches the DE community
  terminology for "salting hint"
- Doc updates to README + examples — separate doc PR

author: steipete
body:
## Summary

- Prevent a LINE reply with an ambiguous provider/network outcome from being replayed as a separate push.
- Keep real provider rejections, proven pre-connect failures, local pre-dispatch failures, reply-token overflow, and rich-message recovery on their existing safe fallback paths.
- Traverse the complete SDK error graph for authoritative nested provider statuses and emit the operator's “falling back to push” diagnostic only when a push is actually attempted.

## Root cause

The inbound LINE auto-reply owner previously converted every reply failure into a push of the same batch. LINE reply tokens are single-use, and LINE does not offer reply-request retry keys, so a lost 408/5xx response, reset, timeout, abort, or Undici `TypeError("fetch failed")` can conceal an already accepted reply. The push is a different provider request and can duplicate what the user sees.

The existing owner also inspected only one error-wrapper level and reported “falling back to push” before deciding whether a fallback was safe. The canonical private HTTP-error helper now searches the complete `cause`/`error` graph, and the fallback callback runs only immediately before a safe push. Actual successful-response parsing failures were already tagged as accepted partial deliveries by the lower send owner; they remain non-replayable, while raw pre-dispatch `SyntaxError` failures preserve their existing fallback.

## Verification

- Authentic existing-owner baseline: **10 failing** real provider/network duplicate-delivery regressions, followed by a second authentic baseline with **2 failing** nested actual `HTTPFetchError(503)` regressions.
- Final exact immutable owner proof: **31/31 passing**, including actual LINE HTTP 400/408/429/502/503, deeply wrapped SDK provider errors, `.error` wrappers, provider-status precedence, `ECONNRESET`, `ETIMEDOUT`, Undici body timeout, `AbortError`, native/wrapped Undici fetch failures, DNS/refused pre-connect controls, accepted malformed-response partial delivery, raw pre-dispatch `SyntaxError`, operator diagnostic truth, and existing rich/overflow recovery.
- Genuine complete-branch Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` / high / **P0–P3** structured autoreview: **clean; zero findings; confidence 0.95**. Genuine TruffleHog 3.96 secret scan: clean.
- Three independent full-owner/source/dependency reviews: **clean**, confidence 0.99 each.
- Exact newest-main audit confirms the bug remains present, neither approved owner file changed in the intervening 475-file merge, and this immutable candidate merges without conflicts.
- Exact detached hosted Blacksmith Testbox proof: **both complete plugin production/test TypeScript gates passing; 4 owner/provider/monitor suites and 111/111 tests passing; targeted formatting/lint, raw-channel-fetch guard, and all three plugin SDK boundary guards passing**. The same exclusive lease was explicitly stopped and independently confirmed completed; [hosted run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30674984066).

## Provider contracts

- [LINE Messaging API reference: reply tokens can be used only once](https://developers.line.biz/en/reference/messaging-api/nojs/).
- [LINE API retry-key policy: retry keys cover push/multicast/narrowcast/broadcast, not reply](https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/retrying-api-request/).

author: mapledaemon
body:
## The slowdown

Neither suspected cause. Measured through `ComposePrompt`, the production composition path:

| | patterns | system prompt |
|---|---|---|
| before the curated import | 13 enabled | ~1,738 tokens |
| after it | 199 enabled | **~15,949 tokens** |
| after this PR | 199 enabled | **~7,056 tokens** |

The curated funscript import (#176) added **171 built-ins, all seeded enabled** — `seedBuiltins` inserts new rows with `enabled 1`, so they went straight into the model's menu. The pattern catalog became **93.8%** of a system prompt sent on every turn.

Ruled out by measurement:

- **Pattern name length** — the replacement names average **12.9 B**. The bloat was 171 imported entries averaging 55 B names plus 91 B descriptions.
- **The persona module** — `persona_lore` and `conversation_context` don't appear in the composition at all when no persona is active. Zero contribution.

## The labels were also unusable for choosing

Every part of a source script shared one name, description and tag set:

```
Blowjob · Finish · Finisher · Fast · v2 · 10.0s · Part 1/7
… identical description, identical tags …
Blowjob · Finish · Finisher · Fast · v2 · 10.0s · Part 7/7
```

Those parts differ in measured intensity by **2.04× at the median and up to 12.45×**. The model was choosing between seven entries that look identical and feel nothing alike.

**Span is 100% of range at every percentile**, so depth carries no information here. The labels now carry the two axes that do vary:

- Five intensity bands measured across the whole catalog, so a word means the same thing next to the designed patterns (Drift 57, Stroke 182, Hard and Regular 434): **Gentle** 10–88, **Easy** 90–140, **Steady** 150–236, **Fast** 240–379, **Intense** 380–800 %/s.
- A rhythm word from stroke-speed variance: **Drive** (even), **Roll**, **Surge**.
- Ordered by intensity inside each band, so `Fast Drive 6` is genuinely gentler than `Fast Drive 26`.
- Descriptions carry **cadence** — the one axis the name lacks. Repeating the name in prose would have cost ~9 KB for no information.

`scripts/curated-pattern-labeller.js` is the generator, so the mapping is reproducible.

**Payload 34,699 → 8,314 B.** Names 55 → 13 B mean, descriptions 91 → 25 B.

## Then the encoding, which had become the larger half

An array of JSON objects repeats five keys per entry — about 62 B of `{"id":"","name":"","description":"","tags":[],"preference_weight":}` scaffolding against roughly 65 B of actual label. At two hundred patterns the punctuation cost as much as the content.

One delimited line per pattern instead:

```
id | name | description | tags
building-up | Building Up | The stroke window climbs step by step, then one full sweep resets it. … | building, ascending, progressive
```

Weight is emitted only where feedback has moved it off the default — the preference rule cannot apply while every entry is equal, so on a fresh catalog it costs nothing and the instruction referencing it is omitted too.

**Catalog 32,144 → 19,661 B. Live composed prompt 40,706 → 28,223 B (~7,056 tokens).**

The escaping `json.Marshal` was providing is now this package's own job. `promptTableField` collapses whitespace (which `boundedPromptData` already did for newlines) and strips the delimiter. Pattern names are user-editable, so `TestCatalogRowsCannotBeForgedByPatternLabels` feeds a name carrying newlines, pipes and prompt-shaped text, and asserts it yields exactly one row and survives nowhere unescaped. Two more tests cover the weight threshold and the fallback to the speed-only contract when no usable id remains.

## What I did not ship

A weight-ranked cap on catalog size. I prototyped it and backed it out: with every weight at the default it fell through to the name tie-break and dropped hand-designed patterns like `Rocking` in favour of bulk imports — an existing test caught it. Pruning needs a quality signal that doesn't exist yet, and a bad cap is worse than none.

The catalog is still 70% of the prompt. The only further lever is exposing fewer than 199 patterns; disabling the bulk imports in the library returns it to roughly 2,600 tokens.

## Personas

Three separate seams, all in prompt composition.

**The description read as trivia.** It arrived as a bare labelled fact under a profile block that said to use it *"only for identity and reply wording"*. That sentence bound the injection guard together with a cap on how much character to show, and the cap is what the model obeyed. It now states what the field is — *who you are and how you behave* — and asks the model to play it. The guard is unchanged in force, and is now its own sentence.

**Lore and description were undifferentiated quoted text.** Lore now says it is background fact rather than a manner to imitate, and names the description as the source of manner.

**One repeated pet name.** The anti-repetition rule listed sentence structure, key nouns, and sensation focus. A term of address is none of those, so nothing discouraged reusing it — and with it present in all three recent lines, it read as an established habit to continue rather than a rut to break. Terms of address are now named explicitly.

All five prompt locales updated to match.

## Description vs lore

**Both are read by the model, every reply.** They were doing different jobs without saying so. The editor now states it: the description is the character being played (manner, attitude, speech), lore is background fact the model stays consistent with.

## Verification

Live against the running app: 199 patterns relabelled, composed prompt **28,223 B / ~7,056 tokens** via `/api/diagnostics/prompt-composition`, both new editor hints present in the shipped bundle.

gofmt, `go vet`, golangci-lint (0 issues), full `go test ./...`, `CGO_ENABLED=0` build, tsc, 354 frontend tests, 1,330-key × 5-locale audit.

## Not verified

The persona wording changes are prompt-engineering judgement, not measurement — there is no way to prove the character lands better, or that the pet-name repetition stops, without running the local model against a real persona over several turns.

## Summary

Merges the exact upstream Buzz Desktop v0.5.3 release into the Kiingo fork while preserving the fork's Azure production, Blob media, canonical-host, and Kiingo ACP changes.

- Upstream release: https://github.com/block/buzz/releases/tag/desktop-v0.5.3

- Merge commit: `8f92b9d0699c8f973477185bbf57f4cc55fc0f89`
- Merge parents: Kiingo `c88656b932b469d455a0c29c87040204ee2a99f2`; upstream `3a96acea09b4a9e3f02c3a26cfb0607d2ccacf42`

Production deployment and live regression evidence will be recorded in the Kiingo implementation plan after this PR is merged.

> **Status: ready for review; device pass in progress.** The branch's history is
> mid-course-correction — the first three commits build a filter that the sixth deletes — so read the
> net diff, not the commits. Worth squashing before merge.

## What changed

When a rider taps a transit leg in the directions view, the map should show the vehicles that are
options for realizing that leg. It used to poll `trips-for-route` for the whole route and then
*reconstruct* which of those vehicles could be the rider's — a 50 m geometric projection per vehicle
per frame, plus per-route end-of-ride schedule bounds with an ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE/UNKNOWN tri-state.

The app already had the answer and was throwing it away. The leg card's ETA strip renders the board
stop's live arrivals for the planned route **and every interchangeable alternative**; every entry in
that list *is*, by definition, an option for realizing the leg, and each carries `tripId`, `routeId`
and a full `tripStatus`.

The old code half-admitted this: `focusedRideKeepsVehicle` exempted the tapped ETA pill outright
because "its pin is derived from the arrivals response's exact active-trip + GPS identity, while both
filters are reconstructed independently of it … and can still miss it." Exactly one trip got that
authority. Giving it to the whole queue leaves the reconstruction with nothing to decide.

**So the boarding stop's arrivals queue selects which trips belong to the ride; the existing 10 s
route poll only says where they are.** Positions, extrapolation, `TripState` and the poll cadence are
untouched — no freshness regression — and `filterToFocusedRide` becomes a hash-set membership test
over a selection computed once per poll.

```
admitted = (previously admitted, still running) + queued + continuations
visible  = admitted − (trips provably past the ride's alighting stop)
```

Admission comes from the queue, so the bound only has to answer "is this ride over yet": one stop,
one monotone rule where every unknown reads as *keep*. `RouteLegRef.alight` already carried that stop
and was being dropped at the map boundary.

## One poll, not two

The map and the leg card's ETA strip need the same arrivals, so HOME hoists **one session** for the
focused leg's boarding stop and hands it to that leg's Board row.

The session's lifetime has to be the *focus*, not a `LazyColumn` row's: the strip is created per Board
row inside the itinerary list, and `rememberClearedViewModelStoreOwner` cancels the poll when that row
scrolls out — which would make what the map draws depend on where the sheet is scrolled.
`DirectionsSubFocus.Route` carries the boarding stop for the same reason.

The row asks for its own session **unconditionally**, passing a null stop when one is hoisted (
`rememberArrivalsSession` returns null for a null stop). Putting the `remember`s on a branch that
flips with focus is precisely what Compose's slot table cannot follow — the first attempt did that and
produced a `ClassFormatError` in the generated facade class, caught by three unrelated tests.

## Interline continuity follows `nextTripId`, not `blockId`

Worth calling out, because the obvious answer is wrong and I checked the wire rather than assuming.

A rider staying aboard across an interline seam is on a *different* `tripId` afterwards, one that was
never in the board stop's queue. `blockId` looks like the continuity token, and it is populated — but
a block is a **service day, not a ride**: KCM block `1_8128824` (`trips-for-route/1_102574`) holds
**11 trips, all route 40** — one bus running back and forth all day. Admitting a vehicle's block would
keep it drawn for hours, and the alighting rule could *not* retire it, because the return trip serves
the opposite direction's stop ids and so never contains the alighting stop at all.

`isRouteContinuation` already documents the same trap: *"not 'does the block continue' (true at nearly
every trip boundary — almost every trip has a next trip)."*

So continuations follow `schedule.nextTripId`, **one hop per stay-aboard leg the plan contains** —
bounded by the ride rather than by the data. Everything needed is already cached: `nextTripId` rides
on `TripState.schedule` (backfilled by the poll we already pay for) and `resolveNeighborTrip` is
memoized in `NeighborTripCache`. **No `blockId` reader is introduced.** One deliberate difference from
`isRouteContinuation`: a *same-route* neighbour is accepted, because a self-interline rides one route
through two phases with the rider aboard.

## Also here

**The drawn approach** (`RouteApproach.kt`) clips each selected trip's own shape at the boarding
stop's `distanceAlongTrip`, instead of projecting the boarding point onto `stops-for-route` geometry.
That geometry is not always a set of complete alternative variants: route 3, direction "Summit
Downtown Seattle", returns the inbound run from Madrona and the outbound run to Summit as *separate
pieces*. A rider boarding downtown sits 80 m from the inbound piece and 7 m from the outbound one, so
the projection matched the piece the ride *leaves* on and drew its first 80 m as the "approach" — an
invisible stub where 4.9 km of inbound line belonged. Verified live on trip `1_675353060`: board
offset 5027.5 m, clip ends 7.0 m from the stop, **5027 m drawn against the old 80 m stub**.

**The block-end sentinel moved to the wire boundary.** OBA sends `""` rather than omitting
`nextTripId` at a block's ends (#2003); it is now blanked to null once in `toObaTripSchedule`, beside
the `activeTripId.ifBlank { null }` that was already there, so no consumer has to know it.

## Selection lives in its own collaborator

The queue, the admitted set, the continuation walk and the guards that keep all of it off the frame
loop are `RideSelectionController`, alongside `StopFocusController` and `RouteVehiclePoller` rather
than nine more fields on `RouteMapController`. It takes the trip-observation cache as the two lambdas
it actually calls, so every rule is reachable from a JVM test with no map host — the shape
`StopFocusController` already uses for its nearby-stops loader.

That extraction is what made the next part findable.

## A guard that drifted from its inputs (and #2149)

Found on device: an ETA pill showing the "vehicle on map" pin did nothing when tapped, then resolved
itself about a poll later.

`requestFocus` seeds the tapped trip and rebuilds the vehicle set in the same breath, with no new poll
in between. The selection's identity guard watched the polls and the queue but **not the seed**, so it
returned early, the seeded trip was never admitted, and `tryFocusVehicle` found no marker — and that
path drops *silently* rather than yanking the camera to the route extent (#1992). The next landed poll
opened the guard and the vehicle appeared unaided.

Adding a fifth clause would have left the same mistake available, and it had in fact already been made
a second time: a resolved stay-aboard continuation was also written asynchronously and also turned away
by the guard, so an interline vehicle waited a whole poll to be drawn.

So every guarded input now travels as one `RideSelectionInputs` value; the guard compares it whole and
the pass that follows reads its inputs from nowhere else. Adding an input is one field, and omitting
either half stops compiling. A tripwire test pins the field set so a new input arrives with an
invalidation test rather than without one.

Value equality throughout, not identity — required rather than incidental: `RideFocus` is rebuilt from
the controller's fields every frame, so an identity compare would never match and the guard would
recompute at 20 Hz.

**This shape recurs elsewhere in `RouteMapController`** (`refreshRouteColorMemo`, and `reframe`'s
change-detect), and it is the shape of the already-closed #1797. Surveyed and filed separately as
**#2149** rather than expanded into this PR.

## Deleted

`RideEligibility.kt` and its 246-line test in full; the tri-state; `focusedVehiclePathsByRou

body:
## Summary

Makes all three data surfaces live from SPD sources on data.seattle.gov:

- **Live Feed** — already live (SPD 911 Call Data `33kz-ixgy`, wired previously); unchanged.
- **Crime Map** — now plots the last 30 days of violent-crime reports (homicide, assault, robbery, kidnapping) from SPD's official **Crime Data: 2008-Present** dataset (`tazs-3rd5`), using SPD's 100-block coordinates, alongside the curated verified incidents. Pin popups label live records "SPD Open Data (live)".
- **Incidents list** — live SPD records are merged into the table, sorted by date, searchable/filterable like everything else, with a source note explaining verification status.

All queries run client-side (the Socrata API sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`), refresh on load / every 5 minutes / on Refresh, and fall back to the curated dataset with a visible "live layer unavailable" note if the portal is unreachable. Overview/Analytics statistics intentionally remain curated-only, so published counts stay verified.

## CI safety net

New `.github/workflows/verify-spd-data.yml` runs the exact Socrata queries `index.html` makes (both datasets: field list, filters, row availability) on every `index.html` change and weekly — a schema change at the city portal fails CI loudly instead of silently degrading the site. This sandbox cannot reach data.seattle.gov, so this workflow's first run on `main` is the verification of the query shape.

## Docs

`DEPLOYMENT.md` §4.5 rewritten to describe the live client-side feeds. Note: the live-SPD layer exists only in `index.html` (the deployed artifact), not the undeployed `client/` React app — recorded as drift per §1.

author: tnorlund
body:
## Outage

Last night the prod-facing Lambda MCP server (and the local `scripts/receipt_mcp_server.py` stdio server) started crashing on cold start. Root cause: **mcp 2.x removed the `@server.list_tools()` decorator API**, and our pins were unbounded, so any fresh dependency resolution (Lambda image rebuild, fresh venv) pulled 2.x and died at import/registration time. This took the remote MCP endpoint down.

## Fix

Bound every place `mcp` is resolved to `>=1.26.0,<2`:

- `receipt_logo/pyproject.toml` — `"mcp>=1.26.0"` → `"mcp>=1.26.0,<2"` (the only unbounded pin in any pyproject/requirements file, verified repo-wide)
- `infra/glyph_mcp_lambda/lambdas/Dockerfile` — bare `mcp` → `"mcp>=1.26.0,<2"`
- `infra/mcp_server_lambda/lambdas/Dockerfile` — added explicit `"mcp>=1.26.0,<2"` alongside `run-mcp-servers-with-aws-lambda==0.5.21`, which otherwise pulls `mcp` transitively with no upper bound

## Verification

Fresh venv (Python 3.14): `pip install "mcp>=1.26.0,<2"` resolves **mcp 1.29.0**, and `scripts/receipt_mcp_server.py` imports cleanly (module exec of the full file, all tool registrations included).

author: mclairewrazej-goatgirl
body:
## Summary
This PR adds extensive documentation for the Ultra Training mobile app and significantly enhances the dashboard, profile, and workout logging screens with new features including weekly goal tracking, nutrition logging, and improved activity metrics visualization.

## Key Changes

### Documentation
- **Added comprehensive README.md** (626 lines) covering:
  - Tech stack and prerequisites
  - Firebase and Google Cloud OAuth setup
  - Local development and EAS build configuration
  - Detailed troubleshooting and project structure guides
  - Firestore data model documentation

### Dashboard Screen Enhancements
- **Weekly goal tracking**: Display run/cross-training goals with min/max ranges for time, distance, and vertical gain
- **Multi-week navigation**: Added ability to view and compare stats across 12 weeks of history with week selector dropdown
- **Metric switching**: Toggle between distance, time, and vertical gain metrics
- **Enhanced chart visualization**: 
  - Stacked bar chart showing run vs. cross-training breakdown
  - Dynamic Y-axis with goal range boundaries
  - Proper scaling based on selected metric
- **Goal-aware stats**: Goals now vary by week and are fetched from `weeklyGoals` map in database

### Profile Screen Enhancements
- **Weekly goal editor**: Full UI for setting and editing weekly goals for running and cross-training
- **Per-metric toggles**: Enable/disable tracking for time, distance, and vertical gain independently
- **Min/max range inputs**: Set goal ranges for each enabled metric
- **Persistent storage**: Goals saved to Firestore under `weeklyGoals[weekKey]`
- **Real-time sync**: UI updates when goals change in database

### New Explore Screen
- **Activity breakdown by subtype**: Separate statistics for run types (easy, tempo, long, etc.) and cross-training types
- **Period filtering**: View stats for current week, month, or all-time
- **Metric selection**: Switch between time, distance, and vertical metrics
- **Percentage visualization**: Show each subtype's contribution to total
- **Average heart rate tracking**: Display average HR for activities with HR data

### Workout Logging Improvements
- **Moving time vs. elapsed time**: Added separate fields for moving time and elapsed time with toggle to choose which to use
- **Nutrition logging**: 
  - Add multiple nutrition items per workout with quantities
  - Automatic calculation of carbs/hour, hydration/hour, and sodium/hour
  - Nutrition entries saved with each activity
- **Enhanced data model**: Support for `movingTime`, `elapsedTime`, `useMovingTime`, and `nutritionEntries` fields

### Type System Updates
- **New types**: `NutritionItem`, `NutritionEntry`, `WeeklyGoal`, `GoalRange`
- **Extended activity types**: Added nutrition and time tracking fields to `RunEntry` and `CrossEntry`
- **Default goal structure**: Implemented `defaultWeeklyGoal` for consistent initialization

### Utility Functions
- Added helper functions for:
  - Week date calculations (`getMondayOfWeek`, `localDateKey`)
  - Goal retrieval with fallback logic (`getGoalForWeek`)
  - Effective duration calculation respecting moving/elapsed time preference
  - Metric formatting and axis scaling for charts

## Notable Implementation Details
- Goals are stored per week using ISO date keys (YYYY-MM-DD of Monday)
- Chart Y-axis intelligently includes both base ticks and goal boundary values
- Nutrition calculations only trigger when duration and items are present
- All goal changes trigger Firestore updates and parent component callbacks for real-time sync
- Dashboard stat cards always show current week while charts can view historical weeks

author: placek
body:
Trzydziesta pierwsza perykopa bazy — **domknięcie Księgi Znaków**: bilans narratora („tak wielkie znaki — a nie wierzyli") ugruntowany podwójnym cytatem Izajasza (53,1 znad pieśni o Słudze i 6,10 w twardej Janowej parafrazie), zwieńczony najśmielszym zdaniem chrystologicznym rozdziału — *Izajasz powiedział to, PONIEWAŻ ujrzał Jego chwałę*; kryptowierzący spośród archontów zważeni jedną frazą o dwóch chwałach; i **mowa bez sceny** — Jezus zawołał (ἔκραξεν) ponad zamkniętą narracją wprost do czytelnika: kondensat całej Ewangelii, od „kto mnie widzi, widzi Posyłającego" po ostatnie publiczne zdanie księgi: *przykazanie Jego JEST życiem wiecznym*. Rozszerza pokrycie do **J 1,1–12,50** — **cała Księga Znaków ukończona**.

## Tekst ze źródła prawdy

Greka wszystkich 14 wersetów złożona programowo z `db.sqlite` (tabela `words`, księga 500) i **zweryfikowana werset po wersecie** — 0 rozbieżności na 14.

Trzy noty tekstualne z rzeczywistego aparatu NA28 (tabela `commentaries`):
- **w. 40** — `ἐπώρωσεν` wobec `ἐπήρωσεν` P66 P75 ℵ: rzadki przypadek tekstu przyjętego przeciw trzem najstarszym świadkom;
- **w. 41** — `ὅτι/ὅτε`: jedna litera, na której wisi patrystyczny dowód preegzystencji („ponieważ ujrzał" vs „gdy ujrzał"), plus ostrożnościowe dodatki „chwałę Boga";
- **w. 47** — `μὴ φυλάξῃ` wobec bizantyjskiego `μὴ πιστεύσῃ`: letni słuchacz wygładzony na zwykłego niewierzącego.

## Zawartość

- **trzy bloki wersetowe** (37–43, 44–46, 47–50) z **dziewięcioma jednostkami analizy** — m.in. inkluzja z 1,11, Targumowe tło w. 41, portret kryptowierzących z Nikodemem i Józefem jako dojrzewającymi, koncentryczna budowa wołania
- sekcje: Izajasz jako „ewangelista przed Ewangelią", zatwardzenie od faraona po Jawne, kryptowierzący wobec aposynagogos, forma mowy bez sceny
- w tomizmie: **excaecatio jako subtractio gratiae** (S. Th. I-II, q. 79 — z Pawłowym „częściowa i czasowa"), *fides sine confessione*, *sermo iudex* (Augustynowe *Verbum quod contemnis, ipsum te iudicabit*) i *mandatum vita est*
- **katena sześciu głosów**: Chryzostom i Augustyn dwukrotnie (Tract. 53 o zatwardzeniu bez obwiniania Boga; Tract. 54 o słowie-sędzim), Cyryl (przezroczystość Obrazu), Beda (próg Księgi Chwały)
- dziewięć nowych leksemów (τυφλόω, πωρόω, ὁμολογέω, ἀθετέω, ῥῆμα, βραχίων, κράζω, ἐντολή, ἀκοή), terminy semickie זְרוֹעַ *zeroa* i שְׁמוּעָה *szemua*; nowy motyw przekrojowy **„δόξα — chwała Boża a chwała ludzka"**
- dwadzieścia odniesień (Rz 10,16 i 11,25-32 jako apostolskie paralele, Pwt 18,18-19 jako matryca słowa-sędziego)
- liturgia: środa 4. tygodnia wielkanocnego (12,44-50), Iz 53 w Wielki Piątek dokładnie w funkcji nadanej przez Jana, Sanctus przez w. 41
- status: `ukonczona`

## Weryfikacja

- `make build` przechodzi; pokrycie ww. 37–50 pełne, zero pustych treści
- desktop / mobile 390 px / tryb ciemny / tryb statyczny — zero błędów JS, bez poziomego przewijania
- interlinia: 241 słów (127 czerwienią jako *verba Christi*), 18 wpisów aparatu, Wulgata dla 14 wersetów

Następna perykopa otworzy **Księgę Chwały**: umycie nóg (J 13,1–20).

author: benkirk
body:
**Documentation only.** Adds `docs/plans/CHART_ARCHITECTURE.md`; no source is touched.

## Why

`src/webapp/dashboards/charts.py` has grown 701 → 1,069 → 1,717 → 2,011 lines in about three months, entirely by copy-paste. `generate_allocation_type_pie_chart_matplotlib` (`:1005-1043`) is `generate_facility_pie_chart_matplotlib` (`:958-996`) with two dict keys changed, and a 17-line `ax.pie(...)` block appears verbatim five times.

Two prior plans bound this work. `WEBAPP_OO_REFACTOR.md` § 1.3 deliberately scoped itself to the chart *figure lifecycle* and left the bodies alone — the bodies are what remains. `MOBILE_FRIENDLY.md` ruled charts out entirely ("*No chart refactors. SVG/matplotlib charts stay exactly as they are*"); that deferral is what this reopens.

Mobile and dark mode both need the same thing from charts: the ability to render the same data more than one way. The flat-function design cannot express that, which is the main reason to do this now.

## What the plan proposes

- **Three layers** — `BaseChart` → family (pie / stacked / histogram / dual-panel) → 16 concretes. The abstract-vs-matplotlib split is considered and rejected; the migration seam is bought instead with matplotlib-free modules (`series.py`, `links.py`) enforced by an AST test.
- **`layout` and `theme` as first-class render axes**, with `desktop`/`light` reproducing today's output exactly. Groundwork only — neither is wired to a client.
- **Drill-downs collapse to one structured scheme.** Nine ad-hoc sentinel prefixes plus a hardcoded `ROW_SENTINELS` table in `svg-chart-links.js` become `#sam/<action>/<args>`, so adding a drill-down chart stops requiring a JavaScript edit.
- **Caching preserved exactly** — unchanged cache names (they are Redis key prefixes), import-order registry population, and the `.cache_clear()` / `.cache_info()` surface that profiling and tests probe.
- **`charts.py` becomes a facade package**, so all 18 call sites and the existing ~56 chart tests are untouched.
- A 13-commit series where C1–C11 are **zero visual change**, with the one intentional byte-level change (the href scheme) isolated in a single reviewable commit.

## Two findings that shaped the design

- **`plt.rc_context()` cannot carry a per-request theme.** Gunicorn runs `gthread` with 4 threads (`gunicorn_config.py:69,73`), and `rc_context` mutates process-global rcParams with no thread isolation — concurrent light/dark renders would cross-contaminate. Theme is threaded explicitly and applied per-artist instead.
- **The cache decorator's default `key_fn` hashes only `args[0]`** (`caching/chart.py:116`). A `theme=` kwarg would be silently dropped and four charts would serve one theme to everyone — globally, since Redis is shared across pods. The key is composed once in the binder rather than in eleven hand-written functions.

Also documented: a latent bug where rcParams never sets `text.color`, so every legend label in every chart currently renders pure black rather than the intended space-blue. Invisible on white, fatal on dark. It is scheduled into the separate pixel-changing PR rather than smuggled into the refactor.

## Scope note

LOC reduction is **explicitly a non-goal** — the document says so and shows the arithmetic (executable lines come out roughly flat). The case is marginal cost: a new pie goes from ~70 lines of copy-paste to ~10.

Chart dark mode is blocked on app dark mode regardless — charts sit inside `.card`s hardcoded to `#fff`, and 81 hardcoded white values across the app CSS bypass the token layer. This lays groundwork only.

## Outcome
Investigation note explaining why dashboard cluster-detection missed a 2-brief near-duplicate pair, with a confirmed root cause and a recommended next route. No behavior change.

## Business or User Value
Prevents wasted future investigation time on the same question, and gives whoever picks up the follow-up (Route G) an accurate starting point instead of the brief's unverified hypotheses (minimum-cluster-size threshold, size-band bug — both ruled out).

## Route Selected
I — Investigation. Brief `20260731-171144-dashboard-cluster-detection-missed-a` asked why the cluster detector missed a specific 2-brief pair; root cause required reading code + running real data through it, not a code change.

## Epic / Feature / Specification
None — investigation note only, referencing `cluster_detect.py`'s existing REQ-011..014 (spec not present in this repo's history; ported in via the Phase 1c extraction commit `bf4a0fd`).

## Behavior Before
N/A — no behavior changed.

## Behavior After
N/A — no behavior changed. `docs/specs/research/cluster-detect-2brief-near-duplicate-miss.md` added.

## Scope
Investigate and document root cause; recommend next route. No code changes.

## Non-Goals
Fixing the threshold/gating (deferred — needs a spec-first product decision per the note's recommendation, Route G).

author: scouten
body:
Closes #152.

The parser already computes the time-dependent document attributes
(`docdate`/`doctime`/`docdatetime`/`docyear` and their `local*` siblings), but
they surfaced nowhere in `adoc`'s output, and neither an input file's
modification time nor `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` fed them. This wires them through the
renderer and the CLI.

## What changed

**`html5` library**
- Populate the standalone footer's `<div id="footer-text">`: the
  `{last-update-label} {docdatetime}` "Last updated" stamp and the
  `{version-label} {revnumber}` line, matching Asciidoctor's html5 footer.
- `reproducible` suppresses both the footer stamp and the volatile
  `<meta name="generator">`, so reproducible builds emit stable output.
- Add `Options::reference_time` / `Options::input_mtime`, threaded into the
  parser; re-export `ReferenceTime`.

**`adoc` CLI**
- Seed each file input's `doc*` attributes from its modification time
  (Asciidoctor's `input_mtime`).
- Resolve `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` up front: a valid value pins the whole clock
  (overriding the file mtime), an empty/unset value is ignored, and a
  **malformed value fails the run with exit 1** — the parser tolerates a bad
  value (no error channel), so the CLI validates it.

**Tests**
- Convert the tracked `invoker_test.rb` cases (docdate/doctime override and the
  three `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` cases) from `non_normative!` to real tests.
- Add `html5` renderer coverage: the footer stamp, `reproducible` suppression,
  the version line, and `input_mtime` precedence over the reference time.

## Verification

`cargo +nightly fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
--all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (all
green), and `(cd sdd && cargo run)` — the four converted `invoker_test.rb`
cases now report as verified.

## Known limitation

A local timezone *offset* derived from the system `TZ` is not implemented: this
toolchain carries no timezone database, so an unpinned clock reads as UTC. The
two `-d inline` timezone tests (which also need a doctype `adoc` rejects) stay
`non_normative!`.

## Test-plan snapshots

```
$ adoc doc.adoc -o - -a docdate=2015-01-01 -a doctime=10:00:00-0700
  <div id="footer-text">
  Last updated 2015-01-01 10:00:00-0700

$ SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1234123412 adoc doc.adoc -o -
  Last updated 2009-02-08 20:03:32 UTC

$ SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=aaaaaaaa adoc doc.adoc -o - ; echo $?
  adoc: malformed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH value 'aaaaaaaa': expected an integer count of seconds since the Unix epoch
  1
```

Henry reportó que el buscador no estaba en los módulos. **Tenía razón**, y el diagnóstico es incómodo: el código se inyectaba bien, pero dos decisiones mías —ninguna pedida— lo escondían justo donde él miró.

## Los dos defectos

| | Qué pasaba | Ahora |
|---|---|---|
| **Umbral de 3 filas** | agregó unos pocos vehículos; con 2 la caja no salía y el módulo parecía no tenerla | basta **1 fila** |

Las pruebas cubrían el **filtro** y ninguna la **inyección**, que es donde estaban los dos defectos. 1, 2 y 5 filas → sale; dos tablas → dos buscadores; Clientes conserva el suyo; filtra de verdad ("1 de 5") y al limpiar vuelven las 5 filas; y aparece **solo cuando el módulo repinta**, sin llamarlo a mano.

author: vitramir
body:
agyn-cli half of [2026-08-01-agent-default-thread](https://github.com/agynio/architecture/blob/main/changes/2026-08-01-agent-default-thread.md). Needs [threads#42](https://github.com/agynio/threads/pull/42).

`threads send` required `--thread` from everyone, and fell back to reading `THREAD_ID` when it was missing. Neither serves an agent instance.

- Omitting `--thread` leaves `thread_id` off the wire; Threads resolves it from the caller identity for an agent instance and refuses everyone else with the reason.
- **The `THREAD_ID` fallback goes.** A stale value in a long-lived container silently misroutes messages — that is exactly the objection that removed the variable, and reading it here reintroduced it.
- `--wait` takes the thread from the send response, which is where a caller that named none first learns it.

`agyn agents instantiate --default-thread` from the same change is not here: there is no `agyn agents` command group yet, which belongs with the CLI threads/agents alignment work.

author: maxfreedompollard
body:
Closes #75746.

`SessionDB` is 6,868 lines and 153 methods. It is already a mixin composition, so this adds the fourth alongside `hermes_state_search.py`, `hermes_state_schema.py` and `hermes_state_portability.py` rather than introducing a pattern:

```python
class SessionDB(
    SessionTelegramTopicsMixin,
    SessionSearchMixin,
    SessionSchemaMixin,
    SessionPortabilityMixin,
):
```

`hermes_state.py` goes 8,604 -> 8,107 lines. The class goes 6,868 -> 6,370 lines and 153 -> 142 methods.

## What moved

492 contiguous lines (7786-8287), 11 methods, all Telegram forum-topic support: the opt-in schema migration, the mode switch, and CRUD plus lookups over the chat-topic-to-session bindings that migration creates.

This is the only platform-specific code in `SessionDB`, which is otherwise a platform-neutral session store. None of it is reachable unless a user runs `/topic`, and the tables it queries do not exist until `apply_telegram_topic_migration` has run.

## Why it is safe

**1. The bodies are byte-identical.** A script parses the pre-refactor `hermes_state.py` out of git and the two post-refactor files, extracts each method's exact source span, and compares strings. All 11 match. The same script confirms exactly those 11 left `SessionDB`, that nothing was added, and that no other method in the class changed by a character. The only hand-written lines in the diff are the class declaration, one import, and the new module header.

**2. Method resolution is unchanged.** The new mixin is placed first, giving `SessionDB -> SessionTelegramTopicsMixin -> SessionSearchMixin -> SessionSchemaMixin -> SessionPortabilityMixin -> object`. First is the position that preserves the precedence these methods had when they were defined on `SessionDB` itself. I also checked the three existing mixins for any of these 11 names and there are none, so nothing was being shadowed in either direction and the ordering is belt-and-braces rather than load-bearing. Every method name defined on the old class still resolves.

**3. The module contract is respected.** Per the docstrings on the existing three, the new module does not import `hermes_state`, and takes `_PREVIEW_RAW_SELECT` and `_shape_preview` from `hermes_state_common`, which is where `hermes_state_portability.py` already gets them. No cycle.

`_execute_write` is the only `SessionDB` method the cluster calls; it stays where it is and resolves through the MRO unchanged.

On the one dependency that could have bitten: the moved code uses `sqlite3` in nine places, and five tests patch `hermes_state.sqlite3.connect`. That is an attribute patch on the shared `sqlite3` module object rather than a rebinding of the name, so it is visible from the new module too. Verified rather than assumed.

## Verification

Differential run against clean `upstream/main` at the same base commit, in two isolated worktrees, over the `hermes_state` suites, `tests/state`, `tests/gateway`, `tests/acp` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_session_recovery.py`:

| | clean main | with this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4688 | 4688 |
| failed | 11 | 11 |
| skipped | 35 | 35 |

The 11 failures are identical in both runs and pre-existing on `main` (Discord send, wecom callback, systemd notify, acp auth, session store prune). Set difference in both directions is empty.

No test file is modified by this PR.

author: vtlinh
body:
Three commits.

## 1. The real paused frame — and it caught two bugs

The screenshot proves the pixel analysis was aimed at the wrong thing. What it says:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| bar colour | `#FF0032`, not the `#FF0000` anyone would assume (JPEG walks it to `#EE0532`) |
| left inset | 9% of the width — YouTube clears the display cutout |
| bar height | 9px on a 1200px frame, **under 4dp** |
| below the bar | **217px, 18% of the player** — share, "More videos", the YouTube wordmark |

That last number broke two things that were shipped:

- **The capture was the bottom fifth.** The bar sits at 82%, so a fifth only just reached it. Now a third.
- **The plausibility check rejected any gap over a quarter of the captured strip** — which would have thrown this real frame away and silently fallen back to the constant. The limit is now passed in by the caller, the only thing that knows the player's full height.

**The margin you asked for.** Blocking flush under a 4dp line would make the one control the reveal exists to reach the one control nobody can hit. 20dp of the gap stays reachable. It has to fit: on that frame the chrome starts 58px below the bar, so this can't grow much — the test asserts both ends of that (`blockTop > 982` and `blockTop <= 1040`).

The fixture is your screenshot re-encoded at quality 0.65: 180KB instead of 950KB, identical bar rows, and one *fewer* false positive. Decoding goes through reflection — `javax.imageio` isn't on the Android unit-test compile classpath, since `android.jar` is the bootclasspath and Android's `java.*` has no `java.awt`. It's there at runtime. The alternatives were a hand-written JPEG decoder, a multi-megabyte pixel dump, or a second Gradle module.

One test worth calling out: the frame is *full* of red — a red-lit set behind the presenter with 300px runs two thirds across. `the red set behind the presenter is not mistaken for the bar` pins that the left-anchored constraint is what saves it.

## 2. Bottom bar, shorter status bar

Status bar: 24sp title with 14dp padding → 18sp with 6dp. Most of a tile row back on a phone.

The bar is on both of the child's screens (grid and About). Not on the player — fullscreen, and it doesn't need another thing to press mid-video — and not in parent mode, which is behind the gate and has its own bar; a way back to the child's screens from there would blur which side of the gate you're on.

**The Channels tab is read-only, and that's the design.** It lists what's approved, and tapping a row narrows the grid to that channel. It **cannot remove a channel and cannot open YouTube**.

I made that call rather than reusing the existing channel screen, because that screen's row tap returns a URL for `ParentActivity` to open — real YouTube — and its ✕ edits `ChannelStore`, which is the parental control. Putting either on the child's side of the gate would breach two things CLAUDE.md calls out by name. Both stay in `ApprovedChannelsActivity`, unchanged, behind the gate. **If you wanted the child's tab to be the management screen, say so and I'll wire it — but not silently.**

Narrowing the grid needed feeds kept per channel rather than flattened on the way out of `ChannelFeeds`, since a feed entry carries no channel id of its own. `flatten` and `forChannel` are in `Library`, pure and tested — including that an unknown channel gives an empty list, because a channel removed while its videos were on screen must not fall back to showing everything.

## 3. Auto-fix may edit tests

You asked, and it's done: `android/app/src/test/**` is off the hold list. Workflows stay on it — a model editing the workflow that judges it can switch off the judging, and nothing downstream would notice.

I'd raised this as the guard rail, so I want the trade recorded rather than buried. The mechanical check is gone; what's left is an instruction in the prompt, rewritten to draw the line where it actually is:

> updating an expected value because the behaviour legitimately changed is fine; relaxing a matcher, deleting a case, or widening an input set until the failure stops is not

**A run that quietly weakens an assertion will now merge itself**, and the unit tests are what stand between a bad video id and the player. Red merely stops; green publishes to every installed device. README and CLAUDE.md both say so, and note the guard is four lines away if it stops looking worth it.

Your reasoning holds, for the record: holding *every* PR whose fix touched a test stopped the loop on the ordinary case — a behaviour change has to change the test that pinned the old behaviour — rather than on the dangerous one.

## Testing

`gradle -p android testReleaseUnitTest assembleRelease` — **82 tests green** (70 before: +7 `ChromeTest`, +5 `LibraryTest`), release APK builds. The autofix workflow YAML parses; it can't be exercised until it's on `main`.

## Also answering your question

**`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`** is a Console API key — billed to Anthropic API credits, per token, independent of any Claude subscription. Create it at console.anthropic.com, works anywhere, no seat required.

**`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`** is a long-lived token minted from an existing Claude Pro/Max subscription (`claude setup-token` in the CLI). It draws on that subscription's usage limits rather than API credit.

For this repo either works — the workflow takes whichever is present. Practical difference: the OAuth token costs nothing extra if you already pay for Max but shares your personal rate limit with your own CLI use, so a busy CI day can eat into your interactive quota. The API key is separately metered and won't. For an auto-fixer that fires on failures, the API key is the more predictable choice.

author: armaxri
body:
## What & why

The same defect class has hit three times: a typed backend struct that mirrors a frontend TypeScript interface silently **drops** any field it does not explicitly model, because it deserializes at the IPC boundary with `#[serde(default, rename_all="camelCase")]` and no catch-all — so an unmodelled key vanishes on save and the user loses that setting on restart (#2261 `AppSettings`, #2309 `TerminalOptions`).

Closes #2311.

## Approach — (a) flatten catch-all + (b) drift test, combined

Both candidate approaches were evaluated; each is applied where it fits best.

**(a) `#[serde(flatten)] extra` catch-all** on the two IPC-boundary *settings-mirror* structs that actually got hit and are the exact recurrence pattern (a large TS interface mirrored field-by-field):

- `AppSettings` (`connection/settings.rs`)
- `TerminalOptions` (`connection/config.rs`)

Any field the frontend adds now round-trips verbatim instead of being dropped — **no data loss, no future backend change required**. The map is empty by default, so a flattened empty map contributes nothing to the serialized output (verified by test). Blast radius is trivial: all construction sites use `..Default::default()` (`TerminalOptions` derives `Default`; `AppSettings` has a manual `Default` that gained one line).

**(b) drift test** for the two *container* structs where flatten is the wrong tool:

- `ConnectionConfig` — `settings` is already opaque `serde_json::Value`, so it captures everything under `config`; it is immune to drift and only its two top-level keys need parity.
- `SavedConnection` — has ~44 full-literal construction sites (several in `*_projection` domains) and no `Default`, so a flatten field would be an invasive refactor touching unrelated code. Instead, a test reads the frontend TS interface (`include_str!`) and fails loudly if the frontend carries a field the backend neither models nor knowingly excludes.

This directly satisfies the issue's *Done when*: a newly-added frontend field is either **preserved** (flatten round-trip) or **fails a CI test** — no silent drop.

## Real drop found by the new guard

The drift test immediately surfaced a live instance: the frontend `SavedConnection.icon` (`src/types/connection.ts`) has no backend field, so it is dropped by `save_connection`. It is recorded as a documented known-gap so CI stays green, and tracked by follow-up #2316 to persist it properly (it needs an explicit field, not flatten, for the reason above).

## Tests

- `terminal_options_flatten_preserves_unknown_frontend_field` / `app_settings_flatten_preserves_unknown_frontend_field` — unknown key round-trips through the catch-all (would fail without the fix).
- `*_empty_extra_keeps_serialized_output_clean` — empty catch-all leaks no `extra` key.
- `saved_connection_no_silent_frontend_field_drop` / `connection_config_no_silent_frontend_field_drop` — TS-vs-backend drift guard.
- `drift_guard_flags_an_unmodelled_field` — proves the guard's red path (a synthetic unmodelled field is reported).
- `ts_field_extractor_ignores_comments_and_nested_blocks` — TS parser sanity.

All in the standard `cargo test` lane. `cargo test -p termihub --lib connection::` → 188 passed; `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, and `cargo build` all clean.

Note: clippy `large_enum_variant` fired on `ConnectionTreeNode` once `TerminalOptions` grew; resolved with a justified `#[allow]` (boxing would add heap indirection to every tree node for a short-lived (de)serialization type).

## Changelog

No changelog fragment — internal hardening with no user-visible feature change (the two previously-lost settings from #2261/#2309 are already fixed by their explicit fields).

author: johnriv
body:
The Devin CLI stores created_at and last_activity_at as Unix epoch seconds, but the parser treated them as milliseconds. This produced dates in 1970 that were discarded as invalid, leaving started_at and ended_at NULL for every Devin session.

Replace devinUnixMilli (time.UnixMilli) with devinUnixSec (time.Unix) and correct the FileMtime multiplier from 1e6 to 1e9. The same fix applies to message_nodes.created_at, which is also epoch seconds.

Rename variables and test helpers from the misleading MS/Millis suffixes to match the Devin DB column names. Update all test data from 13-digit millisecond values to 10-digit second values.

Add timestamp-unit evidence to the Devin provenance entry.

I tested this and confirmed it fixes #1199

💡 What: Replaces the chained `.map()` and `.findIndex()` calls with an early-exiting `for` loop using an O(1) `Set` lookup.
🎯 Why: The original logic caused O(N^2) operations on every boolean/join operation. Additionally, `Math.min(...selectedIndices)` risked throwing a "Maximum call stack size exceeded" error on large layer selections due to spreading a massive array into the arguments list.
📊 Impact: Transforms an O(N^2) search and allocation bottleneck into an O(N) loop with no new array allocations, significantly improving performance for boolean operations and path joining on large artboards.
🔬 Measurement: Verify by selecting 10,000+ paths and clicking the "Union" or "Join" tools. Before, this would lock the UI or crash the stack; now, the index calculation resolves instantly.

- Rutas eliminadas: `/dar` y `/voluntarios/gestionar/[id]`.
- Componentes y hooks: `ItemsForm`, `ListaLugares`, `Countdown`,
  `AccionesRecogidaVoluntario`, `useItemsRealtime`, `useRecogidasPendientes`.
- `api.ts`: salen `crearAporte`, `getAportesVoluntario`, `getItemsActivos`,
  `obtenerContacto`, `completarRecogida`, `liberarRecogida`, `confirmarEntrega`,
  `editarAporteItem`, `eliminarAporteItem` y `getZonasRescatePorEstado`.
- `types.ts`: 18 tipos sin consumidor (`Aporte`, `Recogida`, `ItemConCategoria`,
  `LugarConItems`…). `api.ts` queda en 931 líneas y `types.ts` en 578.
- `sw.js` precacheaba `/dar`: se retira de la shell y el cache sube a
  `panasayudan-v10`.

**Migración `0064`**

- Dropea las RPC del modelo viejo, todas sus sobrecargas, con el patrón
  defensivo de 0033/0059/0063.
- Saca `aportes`, `aporte_items` y `recogidas` de la publicación Realtime.
- Retira `cedulas_bloqueadas.recogida_id`: desde 0040 el bloqueo cuelga de
  `compromiso_id`. Las filas de cédulas bloqueadas se conservan.
- Renombra las tres tablas a `*_legacy`, les revoca todo permiso a
  `anon`/`authenticated` y deja RLS activa.

**Archiva, no borra.** Son datos de una emergencia real: dejan de ser
alcanzables desde la app pero siguen ahí para consultarlas con service role. Un
`DROP` definitivo, si se decide, va en otra migración y con respaldo previo.
`locations` se conserva: la referencian los nodos.

Este PR va sobre `issue-25`, así que hasta que se mergee el PR #147 su diff
incluye también aquellos cambios.

author: willow7737
body:
Lane 0's CertificateStore kept the finalized-event set, the epoch fence,
the counters, and the active validator set in memory only. A node restart
therefore lost every finalized event ID and reset the epoch to 0, violating
Lane 0's "once final, always final" guarantee: a previously-final event
could be re-acked or reported not-final, and a node restarting mid-rotation
could accept acks from a validator set it had already superseded.

Add a durable backend for the safety-critical subset of Lane 0 state:

- Lane0PersistentState: epoch, events_finalized, finalized event IDs (in
  order), and the current validator set as (pubkey, stake) pairs. Pending
  (not-yet-final) certificates are deliberately not persisted — re-acking
  is safe, so dropping them costs a little liveness, never safety.
- Lane0Store trait with a redb-backed implementation (RedbLane0Store,
  postcard-encoded) and an in-memory implementation for tests and
  Lane-0-disabled nodes.
- CertificateStore::with_store restores the persisted set/epoch/counters on
  boot; set_validators and the finalize/rotate paths persist atomically.
  A persist failure is logged loudly but does not unwind the in-memory
  update, so the hot ack path never drops live finality.

Wire it into the node: a new lane0_data_dir config field opens the redb
store, restores the validator set on startup, and init_lane0 persists the
boot set.

Regression tests cover finality surviving a drop-and-rebuild, epoch and
validator-set restoration, rejection of superseded-validator acks after a
mid-rotation restart, and redb round-trip / first-boot behaviour.

author: matraque
body:
## Root cause

ADK correctly emits and persists the single-turn note-taker child event. `@assistant-ui/react-google-adk` 0.0.17 currently converts every non-user text event into a visible assistant message, including `author=note_taker`.

## What changed

- filter only exact `author === "note_taker"` events before live Assistant UI accumulation
- filter the same private author from loaded session messages after refresh
- retain the parent tool call, function response, psychologist response, and every backend SQLite event
- keep all other authors and event ordering unchanged

## Privacy

The adapter never reads, serializes, or logs the private note-taker content, tool arguments, or tool result.

## Validation

- 47 frontend tests pass
- lint and production build pass
- real Assistant UI QA with an isolated synthetic user confirms the internal note-taker text is absent live and after refresh
- SQLite still contains the note-taker child event, parent function response, and psychologist final event

## Separate finding

The same QA uncovered a pre-existing note-taker false-success case where it returned text without a Filesystem MCP call. That is tracked separately and is not caused or hidden by this PR.

body:
Remediates the 2026-07 security audit. **Root cause:** the Supabase RLS lockdown was a one-time manual sweep, so tables/functions added afterward shipped anon-writable or anon-readable, and several routes trusted non-secret ids (`players.id`, `host-<code>`) as credentials.

All quality gates pass locally: **typecheck, 954 tests, lint, format, `next build`**.

## Critical
- **Spotify token theft** — `/api/spotify/{token,login}` now require a matching `hostToken` for `host-<CODE>` identities.
- **LiveKit voice IDOR** — `audio-token`/`audio-presence` authorize on the secret `resume_token` / `member_code` (service-role) and derive identity server-side; the anon-readable `players.id` is never trusted.
- **`restart_tournament`** — anon `EXECUTE` revoked; route switched from the anon to the service-role client.

## Database (migrations `20260803120000..120500`, defensive/idempotent)
- Revoke anon `EXECUTE` + pin `search_path` on `word_rush_add_score`, `codewords_process_guess`, `restart_tournament`, `rotate_player_resume_token`.
- Phase-6 anon-write lockdown → SELECT-only: `quiplash*`, `quick_draw*`, `memory_match*`, `ping_pong_sessions`, `tournaments*`, `anonymous_messages`, `anonymous_room_bans`; revoke `tournaments.host_token` column.
- Service-role-only: `jikan_*` cache (RLS was never enabled), `mafia_player_states`/`mafia_sessions`, `mahjong_player_state`, `landmine_round_mines`.
- `blog_posts` public read restricted to published + not-future.
- `avatars` storage bucket: anon write/delete removed (read-only).
- `resume_token` trigger → CSPRNG (`gen_random_uuid`, 16 hex) instead of `random()`.

## App
- Crypto-strength host/resume tokens; `/advance` force derived from a verified host token; anonymous-messages sender resolved via `resume_token`; `/api/library` auth + rate limit + zod + PostgREST-injection fix; admin login rate limit + constant-time compares + password-fingerprint session revocation + open-redirect guard; security headers + CSP; JSON-LD `<`-escaping; ai-questions/klipy rate limiting; rooms creator-token entropy; supply-chain tripwire restored.

## Regression guard
- `scripts/security-invariants.sql` (runtime assertions) + `scripts/check-migration-security.mjs` (static PR gate, wired into `ci.yml`).

## Before merge / follow-ups
- Run `scripts/security-invariants.sql` against the dev DB to confirm grant state.
- **Not included** (needs coordinated per-game rework + live playtest): card-hand / codewords / describe-it / two-truths / bingo tables are read directly by the browser and need server-side redaction. UNO reference in progress.
- `xlsx` CDN override (needs install+build verify); admin-layout server-side gate.

author: thorwhalen
body:
Gives the braidio MCP connector a proper front door and a document → script on-ramp.

## Guide (`_guide.py` — one SSOT)
- `INSTRUCTIONS`: the FastMCP server-level description (the doc→script→audio workflow, which tools cost money). `build_server` now passes `instructions=INSTRUCTIONS`.
- `capabilities()` backs a new **free** `help` tool, so a user can ask "what can you do?" and get the capability + tool catalog.

## Document ingestion (`_docs.py` + `ingest_document` tool)
Fetch a public URI **or** take pasted text, extract plaintext (HTML strip, PDF via `pypdf`, else UTF-8), and store it under the project so the model can analyze it into a Script.

Fetching is **SSRF-hardened** (it runs server-side on a shared production box):
- http/https only, on ports {80, 443};
- host must resolve to a **public** address (`ipaddress.is_global`, IPv4-mapped IPv6 canonicalized) — loopback/private/link-local/cloud-metadata refused;
- **redirects are NOT auto-followed** — every hop's `Location` is re-validated, so a public URL can't `302` to an internal host;
- the whole fetch is bounded by a wall-clock deadline, a redirect cap, and a chunked total-bytes cap; PDF extraction is page-capped (decompression-bomb guard).

## Authoring
- `save_script` links an authored Script into the project graph. It (and `weave_project`) now **reject Dialogue beats up front**, so an unsupported script fails cleanly instead of half-writing the graph.

## Wiring
- `FREE_TOOLS += help, ingest_document, save_script`; `pyproject [mcp]` adds `pypdf`.
- Tests: help served; HTML/plain/redirect-SSRF/port extraction guards; ingest requires-project-then-stores; save_script links narration + rejects dialogue. Full suite green, ruff + black clean.

Addresses the **ingest** half of #10 (remote-audio delivery still open).

author: jsboige
body:
Grain: MED/logic -- lane myia-po-2023:CoursIA -- prev: MED/smartcontracts #9107

See #8052 (claims↔outputs EPIC). The notebook self-contradicted on whether OWL 2 RL (owlrl) supports `someValuesFrom` classification.

## Summary

`SW-13-Python-Reasoners.ipynb` claimed owlrl (OWL 2 RL) "**ne supporte pas** la classification automatique par restrictions `someValuesFrom`" — but the notebook's **own worked solution** (code cell 68) prints `owlrl (RL) : pizza1 classifiee comme MeatPizza ? True` and explicitly names the responsible OWL 2 RL rule:

> Note : contrairement a une idee repandue, owlrl implemente la regle **cls-svf1** d'OWL 2 RL, ce qui lui permet ICI de deriver la classification via someValuesFrom.

The **lecture cell 69 already carried the correct reading**: "sur `someValuesFrom` [...], owlrl *reussit* la classification car cette construction-la *est* couverte par RL." So the notebook contradicted itself: solution (c68) + lecture (c69) = truth, but the exercise consigne (c84) + the Resume (c88) = stale (they predate the cls-svf1 note).

Aligned c84 + c88 to the truth the code already carries: **RL COVERS `someValuesFrom` (via cls-svf1); the genuine RL limit is `minCardinality` in super-class position** (cf. example 6's BigFamily part, where owlrl returns `False` and HermiT returns `True`).

## The defect (firsthand, G.1)

| Cell | Type | Claim (stale) | Contradicted by |
|------|------|---------------|-----------------|
| **c88** Resume | md | "le profil RL [...] **ne supporte pas** la classification automatique par restrictions `someValuesFrom`" | c68 output `owlrl (RL): pizza1 MeatPizza ? True` + c69 lecture |
| **c84** consigne 3 | md (exercise) | "la classification [...] via `someValuesFrom` **n'est PAS supportee** en profil RL standard" | c68 (True) |
| **c84** indice | md (exercise) | "verifier l'**absence** de l'inference `pizza1 a MeatPizza`" | c68 (inference IS present) |

The worked solution (c68) tests TWO constructions: `someValuesFrom` (MeatPizza) — both RL and DL return `True` (no difference); `minCardinality` (BigFamily min 2) — RL `False`, DL `True` (the real difference). The Resume/consigne located the RL/DL difference on the wrong construction.

## The fix (markdown-only, 5 elements)

- **c88[4] (Resume)**: "ne supporte pas someValuesFrom" → RL covers `someValuesFrom` via cls-svf1; its real limit is `minCardinality` in super-class position.
- **c84[2] (intro)**: reframe the exercise to explore `someValuesFrom` THEN `minCardinality` to localize where RL reaches its limit (matches what the solution actually demonstrates).
- **c84[9] (consigne 3)**: "n'est PAS supportee" → owlrl **supports** someValuesFrom (cls-svf1); the RL limit shows on `minCardinality` (BigFamily min 2).
- **c84[10] (consigne 4)**: "DL est necessaire pour la classification riche par restrictions" → RL suffices for someValuesFrom + subClassOf; DL needed for out-of-profile constructions (cardinalities, unions).
- **c84[15] (indice)**: "verifier l'**absence**" → "verifier la **presence**" (cls-svf1), then contrast with minCardinality that only HermiT derives.

No rewording of the worked solution (c68) or lecture (c69) — they were already correct; the drift was localized to the consigne + Resume that predated them.

## Diagnostic dérive (§D.5)

- **Cause (b) — claim antérieure stale.** The Resume (c88) and exercise consigne (c84) were written when the common belief was "RL does not support someValuesFrom". Later, the cls-svf1 note + corrected lecture (c68/c69) were added to the worked solution, but the Resume/consigne were not updated to match. The notebook accumulated an internal contradiction: the teaching (solution+lecture) evolved, the framing (consigne+Resume) did not.
- **Verdict: markdown-fix (deterministic LOGIC claim).** This is a factual/logical claim ("RL does/does not support someValuesFrom") grounded in a deterministic classification result (`True`/`False`), not a perf/timing/WER number. The §D.5 re-exec mandate (`claims-vs-outputs-d5-perf-number-reexec`) applies to perf/timing/cost numbers that move between kernel passes; it does **not** apply to a deterministic logical classification that reproduces identically (`True`) on every run. Markdown-align to the committed output is the honest and complete remedy.

## Acceptance criteria (verified firsthand)

- **Re-exec n/a**: deterministic logical claim, not a perf number. The grounding output (c68 `owlrl (RL): pizza1 MeatPizza ? True`) is deterministic and reproduces on every run.
- **Markdown-only**: 5 insertions / 5 deletions, 1 notebook file. 31 code cells + all outputs byte-identical (code_sha unchanged, verified). 0 code cell touched.
- **H.3**: 0 null execution_count, 0 errors (31 code cells).
- **content-loss guard**: findings=0 (md cells 58→58 stable; +503 normalized chars = content added, none lost).
- **rendering detector**: 0 violations (no frontmatter_supersize).
- **Twin parity**: SW-13 Reasoners [OK]. Invariant `git rev-parse HEAD:<nb>` == yaml `python_sha` (ffd32bd6) verified. C# sha unchanged.
- **Twin C# audited** (cf `twin-bugfix-propagate-cross-twin-audit`): SW-13-Reasoners-CSharp (23 cells, dotNetRDF) does **not** carry the someValuesFrom exercise → no cross-twin fix.
- **Catalogue byte-identical** to origin/main (untouched).

See #8052, #3801.

body:
## Summary

Implements two roadmap-open architecture items (`docs/roadmap.md`), both **opt-in and backward-compatible** — defaults leave existing presets, param counts, the `(logits, cache)` forward return, and the AdamW path unchanged.

### MTP heads — sequential, DeepSeek/K3-faithful (training-only)
- New `kimi_k3/mtp/heads.py::MTPHeads`: D chained modules teacher-forced on ground-truth future tokens, sharing the trunk `embed_tokens` + `lm_head`, each refined by a lightweight SiTU-GLU FFN (documented deviation from a full block, for CPU-testability).
- Config: `ModelConfig.num_nextn_predict_layers` (D) + `mtp_loss_weight` (λ), default `0`/disabled.
- `model.forward` gains an opt-in `return_mtp` flag → `generate()` and existing callers are unchanged.
- Weighted auxiliary loss (`mtp_loss`) wired into the minimal trainer and the HF adapter (training-only). No speculative decoding.

### Per-Head Muon — hybrid Muon + AdamW
- New `kimi_k3/training/muon.py`: batched quintic Newton–Schulz + `collect_muon_param_groups` (per-head split for KDA/MLA `w_q/w_k/w_v/w_o/…`; whole-matrix for MoE/FFN; embeddings/lm_head/norms/conv/router on AdamW).
- Single hybrid `Muon` optimizer (works with the manual schedule **and** HF `LambdaLR`).
- Opt-in via `TrainConfig.optimizer="muon"` and the pretraining `OptimizerConfig.name`; AdamW stays default.
- LR schedule refactored to scale Muon and AdamW base rates proportionally.

## Testing
- `pytest`: **139 passed, 1 skipped** (CUDA) — new `test_mtp.py` (12) + `test_muon.py` (11) + a pretraining Muon-path test. No regressions.
- `ruff` clean · `mypy` clean (39 files).
- Overfit gates: MTP(D=2)+AdamW → `0.0002`, Muon → `0.0001`, Muon + MTP composed → `0.0000`.

## Notes

author: codesjd
body:
## Summary
The previous fix (#9, already merged - scoping Quick Setup's domain lookups to the current child) did not resolve the reported redirect-loop-back-to-Quick-Setup after completing setup, confirmed by reproducing it on a genuinely fresh, single-child install - which rules out the child-scoping theory entirely (there's only one child to scope to on a fresh install).

I directly tested the caching layer's key-derivation (`redis_cache`'s own `get_args()`) against the exact call patterns used here and confirmed the existing cache-invalidation call in `set_hconfig()` (gated on `child_id == Child.current().id`) produces the same cache key as the plain `hconfig(key)` reads used everywhere - so the standard invalidation path should work correctly for the common single-child case, ruling out the most likely caching explanation too, at least generically.

Rather than ship a third unconfirmed guess, this PR only adds temporary diagnostic logging at the exact point the redirect fires in `Dashboard.py`, capturing: the cached `hconfig()` result, a cache-bypassing direct DB read of the same row, the resolved `child_id`, request host/proxy_path, and the authenticated account. This should make the next reproduction conclusive instead of another round of back-and-forth guessing.

**This is diagnostic-only, not a fix** - a follow-up PR will remove the logging once the root cause is confirmed from real log output.

## Test plan
- [ ] Reproduce the redirect loop on a fresh install.
- [ ] Pull `hiddify_panel.out.log`/`hiddify_panel.err.log` and find the `first_setup redirect fired: ...` line - this tells us definitively whether the DB value itself is `True` (something is resetting it) or `False` (it's the cached read serving a stale value).
- [ ] CI passes.
