author: robertoaraneda
body:
Closes #10.

`ValidateInProperty` only worked for units that canonicalize to a single base unit with exponent 1. For everything else `canonicalProperty` returned the canonical *unit string*, which the caller compared against a *property name* — so it could never match:

```
ValidateInProperty("N", "force")                 -> has property "g.m.s-2"
ValidateInProperty("L", "volume")                -> has property "m3"
ValidateInProperty("mol", "amount of substance") -> has property "dimensionless"
ValidateInProperty("mm[Hg]", "pressure")         -> has property "g.m-1.s-2"
```

Every unit above genuinely has the property asked for. The method is exported and had **0% coverage**, which is why it went unnoticed. The unused `_ *Model` parameter on `canonicalProperty` suggests it was left unfinished rather than gotten wrong.

## Properties are not derivable dimensionally

I measured this before choosing an approach, using the package's own canonicalizer over all 101 declared properties:

- **15 canonical forms are shared by more than one property.** `"1"` is claimed by 11, including both `amount of substance` and `fraction`. `"m"` is claimed by 4, including `length` and `height of horses`. `g.m-1.s-2` by `pressure` and `pressure level`.
- 92 of 101 properties are internally consistent (all their units share one canonical form). The 9 that are not are the arbitrary-unit properties — a direct consequence of #7 giving each arbitrary unit its own dimension, and correct.

So a purely dimensional check would accept `mol` as a `fraction`. That ruled out the obvious implementation.

## What it does now

- **An atomic unit is judged by its declared property, strictly**, with no dimensional fallback. Exact, and it is what rejects `mol`-as-`fraction` and `m`-as-`height of horses`.
- **A compound expression has no declared property**, so it is judged dimensionally against the canonical forms of the units that do declare the requested property. `m/s2` resolves as acceleration, `kg.m/s2` as force, `g/L` as mass concentration.
- An unknown property name is an error rather than a silent mismatch.

The residual ambiguity is documented on the method: for compound expressions whose canonical form is one of the 15 shared ones, the check cannot distinguish which property is meant. That is a limit of the definitions, not of the implementation, and atomic codes never take that path.

## Cost

The property index is built at construction from codes only — canonicalizing every unit up front would slow `New` for a feature many callers never use. The canonical forms behind a property are resolved on first use and memoised in a `sync.Map`.

`New` is unchanged: **1.537 vs 1.538 ms/op** over 400×5 iterations. (An earlier 300×2 run suggested a regression; it was noise.)

## Verification

- Coverage 86.3% → **88.1%**; the method itself 0% → 88.2%
- `-race` clean, lint clean, all 573 official cases pass
- `canonicalProperty` is deleted — it was the broken code, and nothing else called it
- Also removed a dead branch in a helper I had just added, of the kind listed in #11

body:
Increment 2 of the hexagon port (081KYXE4W8808QG0R0011X8S70). Increment 1 gave WSet the **comonoid**; this gives it the **trace** — FROZEN-CORE §A's "Four-Corner = Traced Monoidal Category = ZSet Retraction", now executable. `WSet.negate` + `FourCornerTrace` (Generator/Traced/start/delta/step/fold + `toFourCorner` packaging a turn as the literal `FourCornerOwnership`).

**Invariant:** after every step, `Emitted = consolidate (gen currentInterpretation history)` — the retraction *exactly* cancels the superseded output.

**11 tests (7 properties + 4 witnesses), 22/22 with increment 1.** Highlights: L1 retraction-cancels **+ an assertion the stored history is unmutated** (the honesty claim tested, not just documented); L5 the **C₄ witness over ℂ** — `i² = −1`, `i⁴ = 1` — the design doc's "quantum corner and retraction corner are two points of one phase" **as a ring identity**.

**A real bug the property caught:** `start` returned an empty `Emitted`, so turn zero's retraction was unmatched and the invariant was false. Fixed. A hand-picked example would have shipped it silently.

**Earned honesty note:** which corners admit the trace at all — retraction needs an additive inverse, so ℤ and ℂ do; normalized ℝ≥0 and Boolean are **inverse-free** semirings where the loop doesn't instantiate (type-level refusal via `IRing`) — correction there is re-normalisation, not retraction.

author: mauricio7x
body:
## El problema

La app mostraba **5 procesos** para Helder y 4 eran «AUNAR ESFUERZOS». Dos defectos concretos, más el instrumento que faltaba para no volver a diagnosticar a ciegas.

## 1 · Convenios fuera (`lib/filtros.es_convenio`)

«AUNAR ESFUERZOS TÉCNICOS, ADMINISTRATIVOS Y FINANCIEROS…» es la fórmula del **convenio interadministrativo / de asociación** (Ley 489/1998 art. 95-96): no hay pliego, no hay oferta, no se compite. Se colaban porque muchas entidades los publican bajo «Régimen Especial (con ofertas)», que sí es modalidad competitiva. Corre **antes** que cualquier otro filtro de objeto.

La regla es deliberadamente precisa para no llevarse obra real por delante:

| Patrón | Dónde descarta |
| --- | --- |
| `aunar esfuerzos` / `aunar recursos` | En cualquier parte del objeto (nunca es incidental) |
| `convenio interadministrativo/de asociación/de cooperación/marco`, `contrato interadministrativo` | **Solo si encabeza** el objeto |

Porque «construcción de placa huella **en el marco del** convenio interadministrativo 123» es obra legítima y **debe seguir apareciendo**. Hay prueba en las dos direcciones (8 convenios excluidos, 3 obras legítimas conservadas).

## 2 · UNSPSC por CLASE, no por producto — el defecto silencioso

UNSPSC es jerárquico: `SS-FF-CC-PP` (segmento, familia, clase, producto). Verificado sobre las listas del repo:

> **Los 393 códigos de los dos RUP terminan TODOS en `00`** — están inscritos a nivel de **clase**.

SECOP II, en cambio, publica muchas veces el **producto** concreto (`72141015`). La comparación era de igualdad exacta de 8 dígitos, así que **para casar hacía falta que la entidad hubiera publicado justo el `…00`**: todo lo demás se descartaba en silencio — y no solo al consultar, también en el **prefiltro de la sincronización**.

Ahora se comparan los 6 primeros dígitos. Es estrictamente más permisivo y nunca al revés: una clase ajena al RUP sigue fuera (probado).

⚠️ **Requiere relanzar `/api/sync?modo=full`**: lo que la regla vieja descartó nunca llegó a Redis, así que ampliarla no lo hace aparecer solo.

## 3 · `GET /api/diagnostico` (mismo token, solo lectura)

El instrumento para responder «¿por qué solo salen N?» con datos:

- **`embudo`** paso a paso en el orden real de la consulta, con las bajas de cada filtro.
- **`contrafactuales`**: cuántos se recuperan al relajar cada regla (UNSPSC exacto vs por clase, anticipo, capacidad, cerradas).
- **`distribuciones`**: los valores **reales** de `modalidad_de_contratacion`, `estado_del_procedimiento` y `fase` con sus conteos — lo que este repositorio nunca pudo muestrear en vivo — y qué término de la blacklist disparó cada baja.
- **`unspsc_cobertura`**: clases distintas en el corpus, cubiertas por clase vs exacto, y el top de **no** cubiertas.
- **`muestra`** de procesos visibles con su veredicto.

Dos invariantes probadas: los pasos **suman** el total (nadie desaparece sin motivo registrado) y `embudo.visibles` **==** el `total` que sirve `/api/oportunidades`.

## 4 · Anti-suministro

La regla ya exigía ausencia de verbo de obra para bloquear, así que «CONSTRUCCIÓN DE AULA INCLUYENDO SUMINISTRO DE MOBILIARIO» **ya pasaba** — no era el culpable. Se refuerza igualmente el vocabulario que ancla obra (`ejecución`, `reforzamiento`, `reposición`, `optimización`, `canalización`, `urbanismo`, `intervención`, `excavación`, `cimentación`…) y quedan cubiertos por prueba explícita los dos casos del encargo: ese pasa, «SUMINISTRO DE MOBILIARIO ESCOLAR» cae.

## 5 · UI

El mínimo de anticipo trae atajos (0/10/20/30) y aclara «0 = sin filtro · los sin dato nunca se excluyen»: ese filtro solo excluye anticipos **declarados**, que en `p6dx-8zbt` son minoría.

## Pruebas

`node tests/e2e.js` → **4/4 verdes**, con casos nuevos en el dataset sintético (por mes): dos convenios que no pueden salir, una obra que solo menciona uno y sí sale, y un proceso con UNSPSC de producto que antes era invisible.

body:
…board

Real symptom: Insights said "Ajnas O has 2 overdue items out of 2 open tasks" while the Health dashboard's Accountability drill-down showed only 1 overdue story for the same person, from the same snapshot.

Root cause: scripts/lib/overdue.mjs's accountability() is a hand-maintained mirror of dashboard/lib/health.ts's accountability(), documented as "a literal 1:1 mirror -- any semantic change to health.ts should be copied here too." On 2026-07-25 (commit 4988606) health.ts started excluding stories with no epic/parent link at all (parentId null, e.g. PXB1-6847/ 6848) from every accountability computation via a shared linkedStories() filter -- but overdue.mjs was never updated to match, so it kept counting those genuinely-unlinked stories. Whenever a person had an overdue story like that, the AI briefing (which reads overdue.mjs) would count it while Health's dashboard (which reads health.ts) silently excluded it, producing two different numbers for the same person from the same underlying data.

Fix: port health.ts's linkedStories() filter into overdue.mjs, applied at the same single point (accountability()'s stories list) health.ts applies it. Test fixtures updated to match dashboard/tests/health.test.ts's own expected values exactly (PXB1-6848/Sarika Agrawal now excluded from byPerson, same as the TS test), restoring the 1:1 mirror invariant.

author: marcodejongh
body:
Closes #4103

## Why the #3602 fix never took

`keychainAccessible` is applied when an item is **created**. On iOS, `setItemAsync` on a key that already exists returns `errSecDuplicateItem` and falls through to `update()`, whose update dictionary is `kSecValueData` only — `kSecAttrAccessible` is never sent, so the item keeps whatever class it was born with:

```swift
// expo-secure-store SecureStoreModule.swift:127-144
let updateDictionary = [kSecValueData as String: valueData]
let status = SecItemUpdate(query as CFDictionary, updateDictionary as CFDictionary)
```

Every credential written before 01bb11a9e is therefore still `WHEN_UNLOCKED`, and the failure is self-sustaining: the background read fails → the refresh that would rewrite the token never runs → the item is never rewritten. That is why the affected user count went **up** (183 → 283) after the fix shipped.

The obvious repair — read it back and write it again — is a no-op for exactly this reason. Delete-then-add is worse, because it can't be verified from JS: `deleteValueWithKeyAsync` (`SecureStoreModule.swift:43-51`) discards all three `SecItemDelete` statuses and never throws, so a silently failed delete degrades the re-add straight back into that same no-op `update()`, and the read-back looks identical either way. It would have reported success and changed nothing.

## What this does instead

Copy values into a keychain **service** we have never used, `boardsesh.v2`. A write there is a guaranteed-fresh `SecItemAdd`, which is the one path that applies `kSecAttrAccessible` (`SecureStoreModule.swift:98`).

Per key: read v2 → present means done. Else read legacy → null means nothing to move. Else write v2 and **read it back** before calling it migrated.

The presence of the v2 item *is* the completion record — per key, durable, nothing to keep in sync. A partial pass resumes by itself: keys that aborted still have no v2 item, keys that landed are skipped by the first read. It also stays honest after a restore onto a new device, where a version marker would arrive claiming work that never happened (`AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK` items travel in encrypted backups).

Nothing is ever destroyed, so every interruption leaves a key either legacy-only (retry later) or in both namespaces (v2 wins on read) — never neither, and with no orphan copy that could resurrect a signed-out session.

**Phase 1 (this PR).** Readers try v2 then legacy; writers write v2 and mirror to legacy best-effort; the auth keys migrate from `auth-store`'s own first read (inside the credential mutation queue, so it can't interleave with a sign-in or sign-out), and the other 16 from a root component. **Phase 2**, after this soaks: drop the mirror, delete the legacy copies, collapse the readers. Filed as #4128.

### One deliberate deviation from the agreed design

The adopted design said to delete the legacy copy after verifying the v2 write. **I did not**, because it contradicts phase 1's other stated requirement — rollback safety. JS that predates this change reads only the legacy namespace, so deleting the legacy copy would sign out anyone who lands back on an older bundle between the migration and their next token write. The verdict's own note that "legacy copy remaining is harmless — v2 wins on read" makes skipping it safe, and phase 2 already owns legacy cleanup. Flagging it explicitly rather than quietly choosing.

### Also fixed while in here

Sign-out now clears **both** namespaces and confirms the result by reading, instead of trusting a delete that cannot report failure. With two namespaces a half-completed delete is newly possible, and without the check the surviving legacy copy would be reachable through the read fallback. The tombstone is written to v2 and to legacy, so a credential that survives deletion is overwritten rather than merely shadowed.

## Changes since the first round of review

Rebased onto current `main` (clean, no conflicts). Four fixes on top:

**1. The sign-out tombstone can no longer land in neither namespace** (review issue 1). `writeSecureValue` writes v2 first and throws if that fails, which is right for a sign-in — `writeCredentialForGeneration` returns a boolean the caller trusts — but wrong for the tombstone, where a rejected v2 write skipped the legacy write entirely and left the surviving legacy credential readable through the fallback. `clearStoredCredential` now uses a second writer, `writeSecureValueToEitherNamespace`, which attempts both independently and fails only when both reject. The two writers differ deliberately and say so at both ends.

**2. A migration pass that failed outright no longer burns the process's one attempt.** `migrateSecureKeysToV2` never rejects — a locked keychain is an outcome it resolves, not an error — so the once-runner latched on a pass where every key came back `legacy-read-failed` and never tried again. That is precisely the shape of the events we're seeing: every BOARDSESH-C3 event carries `in_foreground: false`, i.e. a process cold-launched in the background on a locked phone. It would have given up before the user ever unlocked. The runner now takes a `Promise<boolean>` and latches only on a complete pass; auth retries through auth-provider's existing AppState `active` → `checkAuth` → `getAuthToken` path, and `KeychainNamespaceMigration` gets its own AppState `active` listener so the 16 preference keys retry the same way.

**3. The retry can't flood PostHog.** An incomplete pass is reported once per scope per process; the completing pass always reports, and clears the entry so a later regression is still visible.

**4. The migration key list can't silently lose a key to a platform fork.** `preference-secure-keys.ts` imported the two session keys from `./session-store`, which has a `session-store.web.ts` sibling that declared them privately — on the browser target Metro resolves to that fork and both imports come back `undefined`, punching holes in the list that `tsc` (which resolves the native file) cannot see. Both keys now live in a fork-free `session-store-keys.ts` that both forks read from. `LOCALE_OVERRIDE_KEY` moved out of `i18n/locale-preference.ts` for a related reason: that module reaches i18next, react-i18next and every catalog through `./config`, which is a lot of module graph to pull in for one string. A new test asserts the list has no `undefined` or duplicate entries.

Plus the missing `verify-mismatch` test (review issue 2) — the fake gained a hook that lets a write report success while nothing lands, which is the only physical shape that failure can take.

## Changes since the second round of review

The independent pass came back ready with two minor findings. Both fixed.

**5. The preference pass could undo a preference the user just changed.** `migrateKey` reads legacy, then writes that value into v2, and `readSecureValue` prefers v2 — so a store that clears or rewrites the same key inside that window gets silently reverted. Tap "Clear recents" while the pass sits between its legacy read and its write and the cleared pills come back permanently, because the legacy copy is gone and v2 is now the only one. The auth scope never had this problem: its pass runs inside the credential mutation queue. Nothing played that role for the 16 preference keys.

`secure-store-io` now keeps a set of keys this process has written or deleted. Every writer and the deleter mark their key **synchronously, before their first await**; `migrateKey` checks it as the **last statement before its write**. That ordering closes the window rather than narrowing it. If the app got in first, its mark is set before its first native call is even enqueued, so the migration stands down (new `superseded` outcome). If the app started after the check, its native call is queued behind the migration's write on expo-modules-core's serial `AsyncFunction` queue (`AsyncFunctionDefinition.swift:20` builds a plain non-concurrent `DispatchQueue`; `:161` dispatches every async module call

body:
PR 6 — the last of the compliance series.

**Infrastructure**: `make python-test` runs `pytest python/tests -q`; pytest added to the CI venv line and a `test` extra in pyproject. The `__main__` runner blocks are gone with the plain-script mode they served.

**The ordering hazard, killed structurally**: running pytest over the OLD files failed exactly 2 tests — the lazy-import guards, exposed by definition-order collection precisely as the audit predicted. Both are now fresh-interpreter subprocess checks: order-independent, and stronger (they cannot be satisfied by accident of what an earlier test imported).

**The split** (test count pinned at 83 through every phase):
- `test_bench.py` (546 lines, 12 source modules) → ten files under `tests/bench/` (synth with the GEN_DATA_GOLDENS moved verbatim, params, variants, spec, driver, runners, cli, metrics, runlog, lazy_imports).
- `test_bindings.py` (865 lines) → `test_estimators.py` / `test_compat.py` / `test_dataset.py` + `integration/test_cli_parity.py` (fixture-converted).
- `test_doc_snippets.py` and `test_xgb_compat.py` → `integration/` (the doc-snippets REPO depth fixed for the move). `test_device_and_grower_mapping` stays with xgb_compat rather than splitting — it depends on that file's fit helpers.
- `conftest.py`: shared csv loader, path constants, CH_PARAMS, session-scoped toy fixtures.
- All 20 try/except/else-raise sites → `pytest.raises` (message asserts via `exc_info.value`); encoding's duplicated `load`/`auc` locals hoisted. House adaptation kept: `np.testing.assert_allclose` for arrays.

**References updated**: CI comments, docs/feature_gap.md, guide 8's link (the frozen 2026-07-30 review doc left as-is per archive policy).

Verification: `make python-test` green (83 passed), `make docs-check` green, ruff clean. Three AST/regex mishaps during conversion were each caught by the parse/ruff/pytest gates and fixed before commit — nothing merged mid-flight.

- **`HANDOFF.md` 가 v0.5.0 시점에 멈춰 있었다** — `CLAUDE.md` 가 이 파일을 "현재 상태" 정본으로 지목하고 있어 새로 합류하는 사람·에이전트가 첫 진입에서 통째로 오도된다. 존재하지 않는 의존성 설치, 특정 개발자 머신 절대경로, 이미 완료된 "다음 작업" 이 그대로였다.
- **따라 하면 실패하는 how-to 2건** — `slack-notify.md` 는 없는 서브커맨드(`setup`·`off`·`on`)와 미지원 기능(bot token)을 안내했고, `confluence-sync.md` 는 존재하지 않는 인자 문법(`search "…"`)을 예시로 들었다.
- **issue 가 1급 work_mode 로 승격됐는데** `INDEX.md` 는 여전히 "사이클 없는 경량 모드" 라 적고 있었고, `workspace-layout.md` 는 STATE.md 를 `완료`·`보류` 로 갱신하라고 안내해 **preamble P2 계약과 정면 모순**이었다 (그대로 하면 다음 doctor `--fix` 가 지운다).

author: narenp12
body:
Stacked on #35, which is stacked on #34. Review the top commit only.

`get_window_extent` returns the axis-aligned bounding box of the *rotated* string. Measured, one 11pt label:

| rotation | bbox | area |
|---|---|---|
| 0° | 119.0 × 15.3 | 1818 |
| 45° | 94.9 × 94.9 | 9015 |
| 90° | 15.3 × 119.0 | 1818 |

Five times the ink at 45°, and the extra area is two right triangles nothing is drawn in. On `main`, two parallel 45° labels with clear page between them:

```
check_collisions -> (False, "overlapping: [('ascending label','parallel label')]")
glyph ink actually intersects: False
```

### Reconstructing the oriented box

No private API and no rebuilt transform. Rotating a rectangle about any point sends its centre to the centre of the result, so the centre of the rotated AABB **is** the centre of the oriented box; the unrotated extent supplies the side lengths. Turning the artist to 0° to read those is the one mutation and it is undone in a `finally`.

The derivation is checked rather than trusted: the AABB of the reconstructed corners has to come back as the AABB matplotlib reported, and anything that does not round-trip falls back to the axis-aligned corners. Across 0/15/30/45/60/90/120/-37 degrees the round-trip is exact to 0.00px and the oriented box holds a constant 1818px² while the AABB reaches 9015.

`_overlap` is now SAT over four edge normals. Exact for rectangles, and `test_separating_axis_agrees_with_the_old_test_on_upright_boxes` pins it against the previous min/max implementation over seven cases, so no verdict moves on a figure that draws no rotated text.

### One thing I got wrong when I proposed this

I claimed clipping was affected too. It is not, and `check_clipping` is unchanged. An AABB is the bounding box of the oriented box's own corners, so its extremes are attained by real corners of the label and a min/max test against the canvas gives the same answer on either shape. `test_clipping_is_unaffected_by_rotation` asserts the identity so the next reader does not "fix" that gate, and so a change to `_corners` that broke it is caught.

### Still on the axis-aligned box

`check_text_readability` samples a rectangular pixel block, so an oblique label's clutter fraction is measured partly over page it does not cover. Masking that block to the oriented box is a further change and is not in this one. `_box_distance` in `check_label_attribution` is the same story.

### Verification

Suite green at 1102 passed, 34 skipped. All seven gallery figures pass with no warnings.

author: atomchung
body:
## What this changes

This is a full refresh of the public product experience, not a small README patch around agent personality.

The three mirrored README surfaces now explain the complete journey in user order:

1. start with a live decision, transaction history, holdings screenshot, or fictional test drive;
2. let the deterministic engine establish facts before the agent interprets them;
3. answer only motive/context questions code cannot know;
4. receive the useful answer or complete review card visibly in the conversation;
5. retain the final action and choose at most one review rule, or skip;
6. return later with continuity from the prior rule, confirmed thesis, and recorded portfolio.

Changed together:

- `README.md`
- `README.zh-TW.md`
- `README.zh-CN.md`

## Product posture

PR #700 is merged. The README consumes its actual global authority rather than treating personality work as a dependency or as this PR's subject:

> FOMO Kernel is a direct, evidence-bound trading decision partner. Its job is to reduce the user's decision burden, not to make the decision.

The public opening states the deployment fact separately: the product runs locally.

## User before / after

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| First impression was primarily “upload trades and receive a review card.” | First screen exposes both core moments: before a trade and after trades. |
| A live decision had no visible first-use journey. | The README shows the minimum input, first useful outcome, and truth boundary for portfolio-aware and no-recorded-portfolio decisions. |
| Demo detail, persistence internals, and architecture appeared before the complete experience was clear. | Product journey first: plain-language entry → facts → questions → delivery → user-owned action → continuity. |
| Different inputs were explained in scattered sections. | One input/outcome map distinguishes contemplated trade, transaction history, snapshot, and test drive. |
| `profile.md` was advertised as working memory despite having no writer or reader. | The dead user path is removed; #619 retains the remaining registry decision. |
| Privacy copy could read as “nothing leaves the machine.” | The README separates local trade/state storage, public symbol/date lookups, the chosen AI host's terms, and the absence of a FOMO Kernel backend. |

## Scope boundary

- Documentation only: no engine, prompt, flow, schema, validator, state, card, demo asset, or routing change.
- No recommendation, forecast, broker execution, research ingestion, or M2 memory expansion.
- Weekly market-read remains an owner-approved prototype under #683 and is not advertised as an accepted core route.
- The existing synchronized demo values are retained inside a collapsed block, so the product journey remains first while README/HTML/image drift protection stays intact.

## Verification

- Exact PR head: `ac93df338fc6b749d5fccee4fdd60b5d8617c79f`.
- GitHub Actions run `30685713470` passed the complete offline suite on Python 3.11 and 3.12 against the merge tree with current `main@3b488007`.
- Only the three README files change.
- All locale-specific commands and the supported set `--language en|zh-TW|zh-CN` are explicit.
- README links, heading structure, bash commands, and synchronized demo `$` / `%` / `pp` values pass repository gates.
- `profile.md` no longer appears in any README variant.
- Public examples remain synthetic/generic.

This documentation refresh does not itself satisfy #610 owner-live product acceptance.

## Risk / recovery

Docs-only and fully reversible. No migration or stored-state compatibility change.

Closes #699. Refs #676, #475, #479, #597, #610, #619, #22, #46, #683.

author: brandon-coproduct
body:
## The defect

`export_prov_json` emitted two PROV relations inferred from observation **order**:

```rust
// wasDerivedFrom: link to previous entity (linear approx).
// used: activity used the previous entity.
```

Both are assertions that data actually flowed. Deriving them from sequence adjacency asserts flows that were never computed — a local file read followed by an unrelated web fetch became a derivation chain purely because one happened after the other.

The module header says it exists "for regulatory compliance." **In a document offered as evidence, a fabricated relation is worse than a missing one**: a missing relation is visibly absent; a fabricated one is indistinguishable from a real finding.

Nothing shipped wrong — the only caller is a test.

## The fix

Both relations removed. Nodes (`entity`/`activity`/`agent` with IFC labels) are untouched — those are direct renderings of things actually observed.

The relation **types** stay: the schema is right, only the data is unavailable. Worth noting for whoever picks this up — the signature `&[(u8, String, String)]` has **no field for a parent set**, so restoring real relations is an input-type change, not a change to the body.

## Tests

The two tests that asserted the fabrication (`sequential_entities_linked_by_derivation`, `activity_uses_preceding_entity`) are replaced by tests asserting its absence, named for the property rather than the mechanism. Plus a new one checking the **serialized** document omits the relation keys entirely — an empty relation object still reads to a consumer as "a graph with no findings."

**Perturbation-verified:** reinstating the sequence-order link REDs exactly those two, at the derivation assertions.

## Docs corrected in the same change

**The causal-ancestry claim.** The quickstart said *"the flow graph proves there is no model node in the causal ancestry of these values."* Nucleus's flow graph carries no derivation edges — nodes are recorded with no parents — so that predicate is **trivially true of every value**, including ones a model did produce.

The underlying guarantee is real, but it comes from somewhere else: content-addressed re-execution, which an auditor can verify without trusting us. The text now attributes it correctly and states explicitly what is *not* being claimed.

**The compliance table.** Listed `W3C PROV-DM | PROV-JSON export from flow graph` with no qualifier, directly below a CLI command marked "coming soon." Now states that nodes are exported, relations are not, and the CLI has not shipped.

## Gates

`clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` · `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo test` (933 portcullis-core tests) · `cargo hack check --each-feature --no-dev-deps` · `fmt --check` · `check-line-ratchet --strict` — all green.

Touches `portcullis-core/src/`, which is outside the Aeneas fence (`portcullis-core/lean/**`, `nucleus-ifc-kernel/src/**`).

author: fsantibanezleal
body:
The ADR-0071 UI floor put `height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden` on the WHOLE shell. That is right for the workbench route, where the instrument should own the viewport, and wrong for the prose routes, which are legitimately taller than the screen: `overflow: hidden` deleted the overflow instead of scrolling it, and no inner scroller existed to recover it. Verified with real gestures - mouse wheel and the End key both left `scrollY` at 0.

ADR-0071 rule 1 says scrolling belongs INSIDE the container that owns long content. The floor had implemented the "not on the document" half and skipped the "inside the container" half.

Fixed at source in `tools/ui-floor/apply_ui_floor.py` (now v2) so it cannot be reapplied wrong, and the reachability gate now sweeps EVERY route: its previous single-route check passed *because* the two document-scroll equalities it asserted are true when the shell clips. A page that hides what did not fit satisfies them.

## What

New plugin `plugins/skills-cookbook/` — a cookbook of 21 ready-to-paste example prompts that teach efficient use of the hub's skills, organized in 5 tracks (each a sub-skill):

| Track | Focus |
|---|---|
| `prompts-project-understanding` | cut cognitive load: architecture X-ray, project wiki, guided learning, spec grilling |
| `prompts-feedback-loops` | api-test-loop, chrome-qa-loop, error-fixer-loop, karpathy-loop + chaining rules |

| `prompts-design-frontend` | direction + design data + a11y, single-aesthetic rule, screenshot→code, redesign |

The root SKILL.md ships the teaching core: 6 combination rules, an 11-pair anti-pattern matrix (mutually exclusive aesthetics, hub duplicates, QA/image overlaps, pass/loop-driver conflicts) and 9 validated combos.

## Why

Skill catalog passed 150 plugins — picking and combining them is itself cognitive load. The cookbook turns that into recipes: exact skill names (better selector activation), `<placeholders>`, and a verifiable success criterion per prompt (Karpathy-style), plus explicit guidance on which skills stack and which are mutually exclusive or redundant.

receipt id**, so the glob on `rid[:8]` never matched and every publish fell through to
`cat` the newest file.

With two PRs evaluated back to back that's a coin flip on the second one — and the failure
mode is the worst available here: **one PR's signed receipt attached to another PR's
numbers**, with both looking properly attested.

Now matched on the id inside the file. Verified against the two receipts on the box:

```
"receipt_id": "11406ee45f84760a0d82849a2bc78159"   ← #25's payload
"receipt_id": "c13ebd1eef148351b4df14fcff7ac9ff"
```

author: jeshua29
body:
Descripción:
Este PR aplica correctamente la nueva estandarización del frontend al módulo de Siembra / Pre-Cría: separación de pantallas por operación CRUD (editar y detalle), manejo de errores centralizado vía ErrorContext, alerts con duración según el estándar, redirección al listado principal al registrar, y limpieza de código que ya no correspondía al módulo (service duplicado, console.error).

Cambios:

Se separa DetalleSiembraScreen en dos pantallas independientes, según el estándar de una ventana por operación CRUD (no se combina editar y detalle en un mismo screen):

DetalleSiembraScreen - ahora es solo lectura, sin lógica de edición.

EditarSiembraScreen (nueva) - formulario editable, con nueva ruta /siembra/editar.

Ambas pantallas comparten useDetalleSiembra.

Se conecta el ErrorContext/ModalError global para errores fuera de formulario.

Se agrega un helper mostrarMensaje (con useRef + setTimeout) en useNuevaSiembra, useDetalleSiembra y useCatalogoModal, que hace auto-dismiss del Alert a los 3 segundos si es éxito o 6 segundos si es error, según el estándar.

Al registrar una Siembra o Pre-Cría correctamente, ahora se redirige a la pantalla principal del módulo y el alert de éxito se muestra ahí (pasado por parámetro de navegación), en vez de quedarse en el formulario de Nueva Siembra.

Se elimina estanquePorFinca.service.js: no debía existir un service propio de Siembra envolviendo al de Estanque. Los 3 hooks (useNuevaSiembra, useDetalleSiembra, useSiembraList) ahora consumen estanqueService.getEstanques() directamente, filtrando por finca del lado del cliente.

Se quitan todos los console.error de los services del módulo (siembra, precria, lote, proveedorLarva, laboratorio, procedencia) - los errores ya se propagan y se manejan en la UI y no deben aparecer en consola.

Se corrige calcularProgresoCiclo (en siembraCalculos.js), que nunca calculaba el día real del ciclo y siempre devolvía 0. Ahora compara la fecha de inicio contra la fecha actual (nueva función diasTranscurridosDesde en dateUtils.js), respetando el formato dd/mm/aaaa del estándar de fechas del proyecto.

Se corrige un bug donde el formulario de Editar marcaba Registro actualizado correctamente aunque no se hubiera modificado ningún campo (un efecto que sincroniza areaHectareas del estanque actualizaba formData pero no el snapshot original siembra, haciendo que la comparación de cambios siempre diera distinto).

Nombre de botones ajustado al estándar [Ícono] [Verbo] [Valor]

PENDIENTE (no incluido en este PR): el filtro y la barra de búsqueda de SiembraListScreen hoy usan los componentes compartidos SearchBar/FilterPanel/FilterChip de shared/components, en reemplazo de los que se usaban de Inventarios. Según lo hablado con Brayan, va a crear una versión más ajustada de estos componentes compartidos; cuando esté lista, se hará el cambio correspondiente.

Pruebas:
Se probó manualmente contra el backend real.

Capturas de pantalla:
No hay.

Equipo #: 4

author: beardedparrott
body:
## Phase A: Grafana telemetry stack (v0.1.160)

Replaces SigNoz/ClickHouse with the Grafana stack — **Tempo** (traces), **Loki** (logs), **VictoriaMetrics** (metrics), **Grafana** (UI). This is the foundation for the single-container build: the telemetry plane drops from ~2.5GB resident to ~0.5-1GB, uses the industry-standard observability stack, and gives a far better (Datadog-like) exploration UI.

### What changed
- **otel-collector fan-out**: traces → Tempo (OTLP HTTP), logs → Loki (`:3100/otlp`), metrics → VictoriaMetrics (Prometheus remote write, `resource_to_telemetry_conversion` so `orchicon.tenant_id` becomes a series label). Collector image swapped to `otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib` (distroless).
- **`QueryClient`** (`internal/telemetry/grafana_client.go`) replaces `SigNozClient`: `QueryTraces` → Tempo `/api/search` (attribute tag filters), `QueryLogs` → Loki LogQL (tenant + `severity_number` filters, structured-metadata parsing for trace_id/span_id), `QueryMetrics` → VM PromQL `query_range`. Same result types + degraded-graceful semantics.
- **Grafana embedded same-origin under `/grafana`**: `serve_from_sub_path` + plain reverse proxy (no HTML rewriting — Grafana generates its own `/grafana` URLs). Frontend Telemetry page embeds kiosk-mode Grafana Explore deep-links per datasource.
- **Compose**: 7 services. Ports — Grafana :3002/:3003, Tempo :3200/:3201, Loki :3100/:3101, VM :8428/:8429. Grafana moved off :3000 (a `bun` dev server owns that port on this host).
- **Metric names kept canonical**: instruments dropped their units (the Prometheus exporter suffixes `_<unit>`).
- Removed `signoz-config.yaml`, `clickhouse-cluster.xml`, the `/signoz` HTML-rewriting proxy + tests.

### Verified
- `make ci` passes (buf lint, codegen, go vet/test, RLS gate).
- Stack: postgres/nats/tempo/loki/victoriametrics/grafana healthy, collector running (distroless, no healthcheck).
- Traces flow: `QueryTraces` RPC returns real Tempo spans (`api./healthz`, etc.).
- Logs flow: `QueryLogs` RPC returns control-plane records from Loki with tenant + severity.
- Metrics flow: `orchicon_outbox_lag` series in VM with the `orchicon_tenant_id` label; `QueryMetrics` RPC returns the series/point.
- `/grafana` proxy serves Grafana 200 (root + `/api/health`); explore deep-links resolve to the SPA shell.
- Frontend `tsc` + production build clean; `dev status` reports all endpoints OK.
- **Not verified in a browser**: Playwright MCP can't launch (no Chrome on this machine — `npx playwright install chrome` needs sudo). Embedding verified at the HTTP/bundle level instead.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Phase B: single container + supervisor (the reason this swap happened first).
- Consider Tempo/Grafana `localhost:8080/grafana` root_url when the plane isn't on :8080.

author: enesyilmazcode
body:
Closes #77.

Four places in this repo state that every HTML page carries a strict CSP: `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the comment at the top of `public/404.html`, and `PROJECT.md`. Three pages honoured it. `demo.html` did not, and it is the page where someone types a live Anthropic or OpenAI key.

It could not simply be pasted in, which is presumably why it stayed the exception: the page had an inline `<style>` block and a 114 line inline `<script>`, and `style-src 'self'` plus `script-src 'self'` would have blocked both. So the fix is the externalisation, and the policy follows.

- styles to `public/demo.css`
- script to `public/demo.js`
- the same meta CSP the other pages use

## Honest severity

Low. Nothing here was exploitable. There is no `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `document.write` or `eval` anywhere in `public/`, every output path is `textContent`, the page loads no third-party resources, and the raw provider key is cleared from the field after sealing and never persisted. What was actually wrong is defence in depth on the highest value page, plus a checkable claim that was false in four documented places. On a repo whose whole pitch is documented engineering judgment, the second half is the part that matters.

## Verification beyond a text match

`node --check public/demo.js` parses, and a script cross-referenced every `\id` lookup in `demo.js` against `demo.html`:

```
ids referenced by demo.js: 13 | missing in demo.html: 0
inline style/script left: none
csp present: true
```

So the split did not orphan a handler, which is the realistic way this change breaks.

Six assertions added to `smoke.mts`, covering all three pages: each carries the strict CSP, and each has no inline script or style for it to block. The pre-existing focus-ring assertion now reads `demo.css`, since that is where the rule lives.

`npm run check` green, `npm run test:e2e` green.

author: alpineobserver-cmd
body:
## What changed

- Require an account before entering the dashboard or claim workflow and remove the anonymous entry path.
- Refine the public and sign-in copy around Debrief's mission-intelligence purpose.
- Replace service-period free text with structured period and branch selectors plus calendar dates.
- Make unresolved claim and package reviews visibly actionable and provide exactly one package-level priority action.
- Add a deterministic 90-persona next-action guidance simulation.
- Add a feature-gated Google authentication-strength check with audit and enforcement rollout modes.

## Why

Initial testing showed that anonymous entry, prefilled-feeling states, and competing calls to action made it unclear where a veteran should begin or what to resolve next. This change starts new users with a clean, saved account and makes each next action explicit.

Email is not used as a second factor because it would rely on the same Google account. The stronger-authentication gate instead accepts Google's MFA, passkey, or hardware-key authentication signals. Enforcement remains disabled until Google Security Bundle configuration and a Staging audit are complete.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run test:release`
- `npm run test:browser` (27/27)
- 90 modeled users receive one specific next action

author: keishis
body:
## 目的

Closes #219

ノートのheaderへ書ける文書属性のうち、Marginalis独自のものは`tags`だけで、残る`sectnums`、
`toc`、`toclevels`、`stem`、`source-language`はAsciiDocの組込み属性でした。名前を見ても区別が
付かず、本文を他のAsciiDoc処理系へ移したときに`tags`だけが意味を失うことを、書いた人が事前に
判断できませんでした。

引用スタイルを指定する属性を加える #220 で独自属性が増えるため、増える前に命名の規則を
決めます。

## 主な差分

### 命名規則と改名

Marginalis独自の文書属性は`marginalis-`で始める規則を定め、`tags`を`marginalis-tags`へ
改名しました。接頭辞と属性名の正本は`marginalis-domain`の`NOTE_POLICY`へ置き、入力検査と
`get_note_profile`の広告が同じ値から導かれる状態を保っています。

- `crates/marginalis-domain/src/policy.rs` `DOCUMENT_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX`と
  `TAGS_DOCUMENT_ATTRIBUTE`を追加
- `crates/marginalis-asciidoc/src/analysis.rs` 属性値の読み取りを正本から導出

### archiveの移行

改名すると、既存の本文にある`:tags:`が未対応の属性として拒否され、タグを持つノートが
すべて移行できなくなります。`migrate_previous_archive`が、文書headerに並ぶ`:tags:`、
`:tags!:`、`:!tags:`を新しい名前へ書き換えてから現行の規則で再検証するようにしました。

書き換えるのは題名の行から最初の空行までの範囲だけです。本文に現れた同じ並びは属性の操作では
ないため触りません。

移行元として`("marginalis-archive-13", "0.23.0", 4)`を受理契約へ加え、archiveの
`note_profile_version`を4から5へ上げました。

### 版の更新

- `get_note_profile`の`profile_version`を11から12へ（公開するprofileの形が変わるため）
- archiveの`note_profile_version`を4から5へ（受理する入力の範囲が変わるため）

Issue本文には前者だけを書いていましたが、今回は受理する入力が実際に変わるため、後者も
上げる必要がありました。

### 文書

`docs/architecture.md`へ命名規則とその理由を記載し、`docs/rest-api.md`、`docs/mcp.md`、

body:
## Objective
Pass `-usb` in QEMU invocation when attaching `$SEED_ISO_PATH` via `-device usb-storage`.

## Root Cause
When attaching a USB storage device (`-device usb-storage,drive=seeddrive`) without explicitly enabling a USB controller, QEMU throws `No usb-bus bus found for device usb-storage` and terminates QEMU process startup immediately. Adding `-usb` initializes the standard QEMU USB bus controller, allowing the seed storage device to attach cleanly.

## Solution
- Add `-usb` to `qemu_args` in `run-qemu.sh` when `$SEED_ISO_PATH` is specified.

## Validation
- All 17 local test suites pass 100% cleanly.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

The repo had no automated tests: every module measured 0% statement coverage (`test_env_manual.py` is an interactive walkthrough, not a test), and CI verified only the two end-to-end training runs, which take minutes and can only tell you the audit's final exit code. This adds 103 unit tests in `tests/` — no training, ~10s for the whole suite — bringing every module to 100% except one `sys.path` guard line.

| module | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gridworld_env.py` | 0% | 100% |
| `q_learning.py` | 0% | 100% |
| `audit.py` | 0% | 100% |
| `train.py` | 0% | 100% |
| `compare_rewards.py` | 0% | 100% |
| `test_env_manual.py` | 0% | 100% |
| `inspect_eval/reward_hacking_task.py` | 0% | 99% |

What the tests actually pin down, beyond line coverage:

- **`gridworld_env`** — the exact reward arithmetic in both modes, including the occupancy payout the exploit depends on (standing on `D` and bumping the wall pays `+0.95` *every* step, not just on re-entry), and the `shaped` mode's `step_penalty + gamma*Phi(s') - Phi(s)` against a recomputed potential at gamma != 0.99. Also the episode-level claim itself: camping earns 27.50 vs 9.60 for solving under `rigged`, and the ordering flips under `shaped`.
  - One thing worth knowing: a wall bump at the start under `shaped` nets `+0.03`, not a loss — the residual `(gamma-1)*Phi(s)` is `+0.08` at Manhattan distance 8, larger than the `-0.05` step penalty. Harmless (real progress pays ~`+1`), but it means "camping always costs something" isn't true as stated in the module docstring, so the test asserts `|residual| < 0.1 * progress` instead.
- **`audit`** — the invariant in all three cases, not just the failing one: hacking policy flagged, task-solving policy passed, *and* an honestly-bad policy (low reward, low success) passed, which is what makes the signal divergence rather than "low success". `REWARD_BAR` is monkeypatched to confirm the check is an AND of both bars. Exit codes are checked through a subprocess run of the CLI, since that's what CI gates on.
- **`train`** — `run_episode`/`evaluate` are driven with a `ScriptedAgent` stub so the assertions are on exact rewards and on which transitions `update()` saw (terminated only on the goal step). `main()` is covered by stubbing `train_module.train`; `N_EPISODES` can't be monkeypatched for it because it's bound as a default argument.
- **`inspect_eval`** — the solver and scorer are plain async callables over `state.metadata`/`state.store`, so they're driven directly with a `FakeStore`, no Inspect runner or model. Includes bar-boundary parametrization and a test asserting the ported `REWARD_BAR`/`SUCCESS_BAR` still equal `audit.py`'s, which is the property that would silently break if either file drifted.

Also adds a `unit-tests` CI job (`pytest --cov`) that runs before the training jobs, `requirements-dev.txt`, `pytest.ini`, `.coveragerc`, and a README section.

author: lahma
body:
`AGENTS.md` gave exactly one citation URL form, `https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-...`, and told implementers to "read the TC39 spec section" without saying *which* document that is.

That is wrong for a large part of this engine. Jint ships 17 features that are still proposals, and the code already cites `tc39.es/proposal-*` across 22 distinct ones — so the written guidance did not describe the practice it was meant to describe. It also never mentioned ECMA-402, despite essentially every test262 exclusion being intl402.

## What changes

- **Three documents, and when each owns a feature** — the living ECMA-262 for merged features (not a dated snapshot, not MDN, not a compat table), the proposal's own spec for stage 2.7/3, ECMA-402 for i18n.
- **Anchors get renamed on merge.** A proposal's citations need re-pointing when it lands in ECMA-262 — `sec-iteratorprototype.take` became `sec-iterator.prototype.take` — otherwise they silently rot.
- **test262 at the pinned SHA is the arbiter** where prose and tests disagree. The repository already relied on this, but only stated it as "never fix these tests" under a test-project description. Also points at a test's `info:` block as the fastest way to read a normative change, since it usually quotes the numbered algorithm verbatim.
- **A suite bump is a code change, not a pin change.** New "Updating the test262 suite" section covering regeneration, and `ExcludedFeatures` as the place an unimplemented feature parks until the PR implementing it removes the entry.
- Notes that proposal-stage built-ins are registered unconditionally, since `Options.ExperimentalFeatures` reads like a feature gate but is about CLR interop.

Documentation only — no code, no test impact.

author: easonsusu
body:
## Motivation

Phase 12.0 remains a documentation-only contract review. This follow-up closes the rollback-retention transition, import-source lifecycle and authority, complete adapter-byte purge, provenance-language, and model-free static-validation gaps without implementing the adapter registry.

## Status

- Phase 11: completed.
- Phase 12: under review; Phase 12.0 remains documentation and contract work only.
- Phase 12.1 through 12.4: not started.
- Phase 13: not started.
- PR remains draft and must not be merged by this change.

## Contract clarifications

- A rollback-retention reference can be removed before byte purge through a reviewed same-department system_admin or department_admin mutation when the adapter is not active and no conflicting operation is active. The mutation requires exact expected-reference/version checks and records an immutable mutation audit plus deployment-governance event.
- Releasing Phase 10 and Phase 11 retention dependencies is a separate post-purge transition. It requires no active deployment or rollback reference, no active intake/evaluation/review/promotion/rollback/reconciliation/purge operation, committed purge of the registry final and every bound source copy, and committed adapter state `purged`. Historical metadata and audit history remain.
- Import-source state is separate from adapter state: `staging`, `committed`, `claimed`, `consumed`, `rejected`, `abandoned`, `purge_pending`, and `purged`.
- One committed source bundle may be consumed by at most one exact adapter version. It cannot create sibling adapters; failed attempts and retries remain bound to the same adapter and source.
- Successful registry publication plus PostgreSQL authority transitions the source to `consumed`; the immutable registry becomes adapter authority. The source is never runtime, evaluation, promotion, or rollback authority.
- DeptSLM generates a closed, content-free `intake_manifest.json` binding department ID, source-bundle ID, import publication-attempt ID, positive attempt number, safe internal uploader/request references, both payload digests and positive sizes, intake contract version, and code revision. Host paths, original filenames, bytes, tensor values, arbitrary operator text, external manifests, and credentials are never authority or persisted.
- Source publication requires private attempt-scoped staging, retained descriptor-relative no-follow handles, complete allowlist and identity checks, same-filesystem no-replace rename, parent fsync, post-rename rehash, and final PostgreSQL authority commit.
- Source reconciliation and purge are separate from registry cleanup. They are dry-run by default, bounded, administrator-only, exact-attempt owned, descriptor-relative/no-follow, tombstone-bound, crash-resumable, and operation-audited. They cannot delete an active intake/retry source, registry artifacts through source cleanup, or any Phase 10/11 artifact.
- Registry purge removes the authoritative registry artifact; source purge removes each exact bound immutable import source. Registry-only deletion cannot mark an adapter purged while an import copy remains. A consumed source may be purged before the registry only after independent registry verification and no active intake retry/reconciliation requires it; the adapter may remain active because the registry is authority.
- The registry records verified governance lineage, declared external training association, and verified artifact compatibility. It does not prove exact Phase 11 bundle or Phase 10 dataset use, declared LlamaFactory execution, declared training steps, or unmodified weight production. Operator attestations remain untrusted; stronger provenance requires a separately reviewed trusted-execution, signing, or remote-attestation design.
- Phase 12.1 must use a reviewed, source-controlled, model-free static adapter schema. Before implementation it must pin compatible PEFT/safetensors/Transformers interface versions, the closed config and tensor-key grammar, target modules, rank/shape/dtype rules, required/prohibited groups, and numeric limits. Phase 12.0 invents none and loads no model or tokenizer.

Documentation only:

- `AGENTS.md`
- `README.md`
- `docs/adapter-registry.md`
- `docs/api.md`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `docs/deployment.md`
- `docs/product-spec.md`
- `docs/roadmap.md`
- `docs/sft-dataset-builder.md`
- `docs/storage-policy.md`
- `docs/training-job-generation.md`

No files under `apps/`, `services/`, `packages/`, `alembic/`, `.github/workflows/`, `scripts/`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, dependency manifests, or lockfiles changed.

Local checks on commit `7034345`:

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Documentation-only scope check — passed; only the 11 files above changed.

author: lack435
body:
Follow-up to #99, which left `is_test_file` classified one way in `deps` and another way everywhere else. Investigating that turned up a larger defect underneath it.

## The defect

`is_test_file` matched all three of its markers as substrings of the **whole path**, so the directories *above* a project decided the answer for everything inside it. A checkout at `~/app.spec.v2/` classified every file in it as a test.

The fix is to match each marker where it actually means something:

- `.test.` / `.spec.` are **file name** conventions — `auth.test.ts`, `parser.spec.js`. Nothing about a *directory* called `app.test.stuff` says its contents are tests.
- `__tests__` is a **directory** convention, matched as a whole path component. That also fixes it on Windows, where the embedded forward slash in `"__tests__/"` meant it never matched at all — the same tree classified one way per platform.

`__tests__` is a directory name, so an ancestor called `__tests__` is still indistinguishable from a local one without a root. Four of the five callers have a scope and now strip it (`rank`, `grok`, `blast`, `deps`); `read::outline` has none and passes what it was given. That is the chip's option (a), and it resolves the split #99 left.

## Measured

Pre- and post-change release builds, not asserted:

| case | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| scope spanning `app.spec.v2/` and `plain/` | `plain\src\b.ts`, then `app.spec.v2\src\a.ts` | **reversed** |
| tainted checkout containing a real test file | `auth.test.ts`, then `zprod.ts` | **reversed** |

In the first, `a.ts` was docked `search::rank`'s 120-point penalty for its *parent directory's* name. In the second, the prod file was docked the same penalty as the genuine test file beside it, so the test sorted first; now it doesn't.

A tainted checkout containing **no** genuine test file does not reorder — the penalty is uniform there, and `BoundedRetain` caps by count rather than by an absolute score, so neither order nor the retained set moves.

The non-comparative effects are the grouping ones: `grok`, `blast` and `deps` file every row under their "tests" heading, and `read::outline` switches rendering mode for a file that also parses as tests.

On Windows, every file under a `__tests__` directory now takes the ranking penalty and the test grouping where before it took neither. That is the intended parity with Linux.

## Review

Found a regression, a miscount and a false claim, all in the second commit:

- **A regression this branch introduced.** The first commit deleted #97's scope-relative guard in `deps` as "unnecessary". It wasn't: a project at `<tmp>/__tests__/proj` classified both dependents as tests — worse than *either* prior state. Fixed by generalising the guard to all four scope-bearing callers rather than deleting it.
- **"Two of the five callers have no scope"** named `blast`, which uses its `scope` two lines below each call. It's one.
- **"Within a single tainted checkout, nothing reorders" was false.** The premise holds only when the checkout contains no genuine test file. That's the second row of the table above, and it's my own measurement now.
- **The `__tests__` half was guarded on Windows only.** The test helper joins with the platform separator, so on the Linux runner the component match could be reverted with the whole suite green. The partial-component test now carries a forward-slash literal — the one spelling under which reverting it fails on both platforms. That test had also been written with two cases that never distinguished the spellings, since `contains("__tests__/")` required a trailing separator.

Cleared: no directory-level `.test.`/`.spec.` convention exists in this repo or the benchmark fixtures, so the narrowing produces no false negatives — `test/`, `tests/`, `_test.go`, `test_*.py` are handled by a separate detector (`facets::is_test_match`) that is unchanged. `components()` cannot match a prefix or root component. `overview.rs` already used component-matching for `__tests__` and file-name matching for `.test.`, so this aligns the crate with its own precedent.

## Verification

- **Tripwire, four-cell matrix.** Full revert fails 2 of 5 tests here and 1 on Linux-shaped paths; reverting *only* the `__tests__` half fails the partial-component test on both. The module records which tests are tripwires, on which platform, and which are regression guards.
- 903 tests passing, failure set unchanged at the documented 14-test Windows-local baseline. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean.

author: bestdan
body:
Makes `opx` the documented default for **interactive/agent** invocations of the Linear GraphQL fast-path scripts, replacing the ambient `op signin` session model. Unattended runs are unchanged.

Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-01-opx-key-resolution-design.md`.

## Why

An `op signin` session is ambient — `op` holds it in a per-user cache daemon, so for roughly 30 minutes *every* process the machine spawns can read the key without the user seeing anything. That key is a Linear **personal API key**: a full-account bearer token.

[`opx`](https://github.com/bestdan/opx) wraps `op` to force a native approval dialog on each read and invalidate the session afterwards. No window, no cached credential between invocations.

## The selection rule

`linear-common.md` → "Key resolution" is the single source of truth. Step 3 is now a two-way branch:

- Key already in the environment → invoke plainly. Unchanged. (Headless `$OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` + `$LINEAR_API_KEY_REF`, and the launching-terminal export.)
- Config has `linear.api_key_ref` and `opx` is on `PATH` → `opx run --env 'LINEAR_API_KEY=<ref>' -- python3 <script>.py …`
- Config has a ref but no `opx` → today's `LINEAR_API_KEY_REF='<ref>' python3 …` prefix form.
- No ref anywhere → invoke bare, exit non-zero, floor.

**The five `commands/handlers/assets/linear-*.py` scripts are untouched.** They already prefer `$LINEAR_API_KEY` over `$LINEAR_API_KEY_REF`, so under `opx run` they never invoke `op` or `opx` themselves — which is exactly what makes a caller-side wrapper work.

## Why not swap `op read` → `opx` inside the scripts

Rejected, and recorded as such in the decision-record addendum. `get_key()` is shared verbatim across the family and used unattended as well as interactively. `opx` fails **closed** with no UI to approve (exit 3), so every headless read would break — and because a non-zero exit *is* the fallback trigger, with no `[ -n "$LINEAR_API_KEY" ]` pre-check, that breakage would be **silent**: a correctly-configured cron run would floor indistinguishably from "no key configured at all."

## What it costs

One dialog per **script invocation**. `/reconcile-tasks` row 2 invokes `linear-scan.py` once per resolved scope, so a turn can raise several; `/sweep-for-complete` batches into one call. Documented rather than hidden.

## Security boundary

Unchanged in substance, tighter in practice. A cloud checkout has no `opx`, no `op` session, and no `.task-config.local.yml`, so it floors to the OAuth-scoped MCP path exactly as before — and even with an `opx` binary present, no-UI means exit 3, which is itself a floor. No new route for a key into a cloud sandbox.

## `/doctor`

The linear check used to prove the key by resolving `op read "<ref>" >/dev/null`. Under `opx` that would pop a dialog on every `/doctor` run *and* tear down any `op` session the user had. The probe is now gated: `op read` only when `$OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` is set; when `opx` is present, report the ref as configured-but-not-probed instead. Also adds an `opx` presence line. Status vocabulary stays `PASS`/`WARN`/`FAIL`.

## Files

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `commands/handlers/linear-common.md` | Source of truth — selection rule, failure legibility split by cause, cost note, security-boundary addendum |
| `commands/doctor.md` | `opx` presence check; resolution probe gated |
| `commands/handlers/linear-config.md` | "Archive key" documents both mechanisms |
| `commands/handlers/linear-archive.md` | Interactive path → `opx`; the cron section stays on `op` |
| `commands/handlers/linear-claim.md`, `linear-false-closures.md` | Re-pointed for consistency |
| `skills/auto-pilot/references/launch-preflight.md` | One sentence: `opx` unusable unattended |
| `dev_docs/decisions/linear_read_fastpaths.md` | Addendum; original decision untouched |

`linear-reoptimize.md`, `linear-reconcile.md`, and `linear-sweep-complete.md` needed no change — they reference `linear-common.md` rather than restating the mechanism.

## Verification

- `dprint check --incremental=false` clean.
- Two `scripts/check.sh` steps fail in this worktree for environment reasons unrelated to the change, both confirmed green on the main checkout: `lint-shell`/`test-shell` (bats submodules not initialized in a fresh worktree) and one `test-task-scan` fixture (sandbox blocks `git init` writing `.git/hooks/*` in a temp dir).
- The `opx run` invocation was field-tested against real Linear with the Python scripts unchanged, per the spec.

## No version bump

Per `CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Versioning", CI bumps from the merged commit's Conventional Commit type and `docs:` maps to no release. No `SKILL.md` in this repo carries a `version:` field.

author: krystophny
body:
Closes #2887.

## Preserved compiler invariant
A USE statement may only access entities the named module makes available (F2023 14.2.2). Operator and assignment generic specs were not even represented before this change: the only-list parser stopped at `operator(` and silently dropped the entry.

## Change
- `parser_import_resolution`: parse `OPERATOR(op)` / `ASSIGNMENT(=)` in USE ONLY lists **and** in renames (`operator(.a.) => operator(.b.)`), stored in one canonical spec form.
- New `generic_spec_names`: the single canonical spelling for generic specs, folding the two spellings of the relational operators (`.eq.`/`==`, ...) onto one form. The private copy of that folding inside `parser_interface_block_headers_module` is **retired** in favour of it - exactly one convention survives.
- New `semantic_use_export_validation`: rejects an accessed generic spec that the module - when defined in the same source and when its export list is fully understood - does not export. A module that itself USEs another module, or that holds a construct the analyzer does not model, is skipped: missing knowledge means silence, never a rejection. Plain names are deliberately not checked (their export set depends on common blocks, enumerators and other constructs not modelled here); that restriction was derived from the rejection gate, which showed 12 valid corpus files falsely rejected by a name-based check.

## Red evidence (unmodified main, `frontend_probe`)
All four negative fixtures compiled clean: `use_9`, `use_19`, `operator_6`, `interface_operator_3` -> `parse_ok:true, semantic_ok:true, diagnostic_text:""`.

## Green evidence
- `use_9` -> `Generic spec 'operator(.func.)' referenced in USE ONLY is not found in module 'test'`; `use_19` -> `operator(/)`; `operator_6` -> `operator(.none.)`; `interface_operator_3` -> `operator(/=)` (accepted under both spellings `==`/`.eq.`).
- All four corrected neighbours still accepted; each fixture pair verified against `gfortran -fsyntax-only` as the oracle.
- `fo test test_reject_use_01_diagnostics` PASS; full `fo` pipeline green (483 tests, lint OK, fmt clean for touched-by-me files).

## Rejection-work gate
- `make check-rejection-gate`: OK, no newly rejected corpus file.
- Full gfortran.dg sweep (7857 files) against a baseline built from unmodified `origin/main`: exactly 4 newly rejected files - `interface_operator_3.f90`, `operator_6.f90`, `use_19.f90`, `use_9.f90` - all of which gfortran itself rejects. **Zero valid files newly rejected.**

## Scope note
Issue #2887 lists further USE-family fixtures (`use_15`, `use_16`, `use_rename_5`, `use_rename_11`, `use_iso_c_binding`, `function_kinds_2`) whose rules are different constraint families (program-unit name conflicts, host/rename collisions, intrinsic-module symbol tables). They need separate mechanisms and are left to follow-up work.

author: marielletheguzman
body:
Step 5 of M1a. The parser resolves extracted phrases against a **closed set** of slugs and may never invent one, so without a populated `skills` table there is nothing to parse against.

30 skills, 107 aliases, one career row. **Reference data, not a migration** — migrations are immutable once applied, and this is expected to be *replaced* by real ingestion rather than amended forever by a chain of `INSERT` migrations.

## The provenance decision

Every row is **`source_tier: 3`, `basis: 'curated'`, `retrieved_at: NULL`**. I made this call rather than defer it, and the reasoning is in `seeds/README.md`:

- **Not tier 1 or 2** — those require a source that was actually consulted. These were curated by hand, and claiming ESCO or O\*NET without having ingested them would be a provenance lie. Provenance is not cuttable.
- **Not tier 4** — tier 4 is *anecdotal*: forums, self-reported experience. A curated taxonomy is not that.
- **`retrieved_at` stays NULL** because nothing was retrieved. `source_url` points at canonical documentation so the claim is *checkable*, not because that page was fetched.

**The consequence is the intended one:** tier 3 maps to `low` confidence, so anything computed from these rows is low-confidence until superseded. A hand-seeded registry should not produce confident answers. An integration test asserts the tier — a row quietly claiming tier 1 fails the build.

## No edges

`requires` edges and `career_skills` are M1b and need a real method with recorded support. An edge asserted without evidence makes every learning path a guess presented as a sequence. A test asserts `skill_edges`, `career_skills`, and `career_edges` still do not exist.

## Verified against live PostgreSQL

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | reports 30/107/1, database untouched — `0\|0\|0` |
| apply | 30 skills, 107 aliases, 1 career |
| re-apply | 0 inserted, 0 aliases — idempotent |

author: vjsingh1984
body:
## What
Second application of the **TD-DECOMP-1 decomposition recipe** (after the `rank_metrics` pilot, #1366). Extracts the cluster RPC **abstraction layer** — `src/cluster/rpc/{error,types,traits,retry}` (~2.6K LOC, **37 inline tests**) → `proximadb-runtime` (platform tier). Behavior-neutral.

## Why
Continuing the root-monolith decomposition (850K-LOC root lib binary bundles 9,538 inline tests → OOMs the 16 GB runner → `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`). After the `rank_metrics` pilot, I researched observability/catalog/cluster for the next clean leaf: observability's and catalog's remaining residue is cross-coupled to layering-forbidden tiers (modality/query), but **cluster `rpc/`** is a fully self-contained abstraction layer — deps only `serde`/`async-trait`/`futures`/`rand` + foundation `proximadb-distance-types`, **zero `crate::` climb-out**. Platform tier may host it (may depend on every layer except root/app/binding).

## Change
- `git mv src/cluster/rpc/{error,types,traits,retry}.rs` → `proximadb-runtime/src/cluster_rpc/` (verbatim; `super::` sibling refs stay valid).
- Runtime: `pub mod cluster_rpc;` + deps `futures`/`rand`/`proximadb-distance-types` (workspace; `serde`/`async-trait` already present).
- Root `src/cluster/rpc/mod.rs`: `pub mod {error,types,traits,retry};` → `pub use proximadb_runtime::cluster_rpc::{error, retry, traits, types};` — the root-side tonic impl (`connection`, `grpc_client`, `grpc_server`) and the ~7 external `crate::cluster::rpc::*` / `proximadb::cluster::rpc::*` callers resolve unchanged.

## Verification (quiet machine)
| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo check -p proximadb` | ✅ |
| `nextest -p proximadb-runtime` | ✅ **54 passed** (17→54: +37 cluster_rpc tests moved in) |
| `check_workspace_boundaries.py` | ✅ no findings |
| `check-layering.sh` | ✅ |
| `cargo build -p proximadb-server` | ✅ |
| `cargo clippy --lib --bins -D warnings` | ✅ |
| `cargo fmt --check` + `make work-commit-check` + td-unique | ✅ |

**Payoff:** 37 tests out of the root lib binary (now in the runtime's own process).

## Follow-ups (TD-DECOMP-3)
Move the tonic/proto-backed RPC impl (`connection`, `grpc_client`, `grpc_server`) once `proximadb-runtime` gains `tonic`/`proximadb-proto`. Then the rest of `src/cluster/` (consensus/replication/sharding/distributed_ops — 273 tests total) submodule-by-submodule — cluster is layering-legal to host in platform wholesale, the richest remaining test-payoff target.

author: jakechampion
body:
> Stacked on #5969 → #5970. Those commits drop out as they merge.

## What

Every remaining driver site routes IR-or-error. **`asm.fern` and `asm_arm64.fern` now have no callers outside their own files**, so the deletion (slice-5 step 5) is unblocked.

| driver | sites |
|---|---|
| `asm_ir_run` | x86, `-target arm64`, `-target arm64-darwin` |
| `asm_load_run` | x86 last resort (after the per-module concat rescue), arm64 |
| `asm_modload_run` | same, both targets |

`asm_ir_run` drops its `./asm` and `./asm_arm64` imports entirely; `asm_load_run` gains `./asm_arm64_ir` for the mirror.

## Three test consequences, each pre-authorised rather than incidental

**The AST-vs-IR differential loses its comparison.** Once `asm_ir_run` has no AST leg, its `-ir`-on and `-ir`-off runs are the *same emitter* — so `TestSelfHostAsmIRPath`'s assertion was **vacuous, not merely redundant**. Slice-5 step 4 says "DELETE, do not re-point", and re-pointing is genuinely unavailable: the cases are in the driver dialect (`parser.module_with_builtins` injects `map_new` / `__alloc` / casts) that native `-interp` rejects, so there is no independent oracle to swap in.

Its **~930 cases are kept** as an eligibility + assembly guard — each must compile through the IR path, assemble, link and run, which is the largest such guard in the suite and exactly what keeps slice 5 green. The cost, stated plainly in the test header: a wrong exit code now passes there. The dedicated `*_ir_test.go` corpora carry the oracle role (each checks values, most against `fern -interp`).

**The env-gated merged fixpoints are deleted** — `TestSelfHostModloadFixpointX86_64` and `TestSelfHostFixpointArm64`. Both headers already said they stay *"until slice 5 deletes `asm.fern`, at which point it goes with it"*, and this reroute forces the moment: they compile the whole compiler through the merged bundle, which now refuses. Routine coverage is the per-module whole-compiler tests on both targets, with byte-identity in the env-gated `TestSelfHostPerModuleEmitAllFixpointX86_64`.

**The x86 `std/string` test** moved to the loader driver in #5969, because that module stopped being self-contained.

## Verification

All three `asm_ir_run` targets emit correctly for an eligible program — x86 `movq`, arm64 `ldr x0`, arm64-darwin `@PAGE` / `_main` (192 and 19 occurrences) — and `cmp` confirms the x86 and arm64 outputs genuinely differ, so the `-target` dispatch is live rather than silently defaulting.

Both refusal paths work: an over-budget module exits 1 with `not IR-eligible` on x86 **and** on arm64. The `-ir`-off leg on an eligible program still emits (27314 bytes), confirming the flag now selects a fast path rather than an emitter.

## What's left for the deletion PR

`asm.fern` + `asm_arm64.fern` + the 512-function budget, plus sweeping `"asm.fern"` / `"asm_arm64.fern"` out of the **~221** Go harness copy-lists — atomic with the file removal, since those tests read the sources to build their project dirs.

author: chrisdusyk
body:
Turns the Aspire starter page into the admin console shell: navigation, an environment switcher, and a placeholder screen for each feature that is coming.

## The design

**Thesis.** In a flag console the most consequential fact on screen isn't a flag, it's *which environment you're about to change*. So the shell gives that permanent chrome: the selected environment holds a full-height band of its own colour down the edge of the window, labelled in vertical mono caps, and that band is also the switcher. Everything else stays quiet.

**Palette — "Enamel & Signal".** Dark enamelled evergreen (`#08201B`) for chrome, a cool bone workspace (`#F0F2EE`), graphite text, live amber (`#E4671B`). Environment tones are cool for the safe places and hot for the real one: development teal, staging violet, production amber. The opinionated bit: **on ≠ good, on = live**, so heat marks what is live rather than what is healthy — green never means "safe" here, and red stays reserved for destructive actions.

**Type.** Archivo Variable for display, actually using its width axis (`wdth 118%`) for a nameplate feel; Public Sans for body; JetBrains Mono for flag keys and micro-labels, since a key is a literal code identifier. Text-only navigation, no icon set.

## Structure

Screens mirror the backend's slice layout — `src/features/{aggregate}/{Screen}Page.tsx` owns a page and its copy, `src/shell/` owns the chrome they share, and navigation is declared once in `src/shell/navigation.ts` for both the rail and the overview.

Routes: Overview, Flags, Segments, Rules, and Organization (Members, Environments, Settings), plus a not-found screen. Every unbuilt screen uses `<Unbuilt>`, which states what will live there instead of dressing an empty page up as a finished one. **No screen invents data** — there are no fake flag counts or placeholder users anywhere.

Environments are hard-coded in `src/shell/environment.ts` until the backend owns them; the selection persists to `localStorage` and defaults to development, the safest place to land.

## Also here

- `app.MapFallbackToFile("index.html")` — `UseFileServer` answered `/flags` with a 404 once the SPA is published into `wwwroot`, so deep links and reloads broke outside development.
- Frontend conventions documented in `CLAUDE.md`.
- Starter assets removed (`App.tsx`, `App.css`, `Aspire.png`, `github.svg`). The `/api/weatherforecast` endpoint is left alone — nothing calls it now, but removing it wasn't in scope.

## Checks

- `pnpm build` (tsc + vite) and `pnpm lint` pass.
- `dotnet test FeatureFlags.sln` — 82 passed, 0 failed.
- Reviewed in a real browser at 1440px and 390px: the rail collapses to a drawer, the spine becomes a top band, keyboard focus is visible on the spine and nav, and `prefers-reduced-motion` is respected.

body:
## Summary

- add atomic heartbeat execution claims and execution-ID fencing to the public task-store contract
- recover tasks interrupted by a prior single-host process generation before scheduler polling begins
- preserve checkpoints and run history, suppress stale late completions, and surface recovery metadata/events to operators
- document the single-process file-adapter boundary and the CAS/lease requirements for hosted stores

## Durability boundary

The built-in file adapter provides restart recovery for one Node.js process owning a state root. Multi-process and replica deployments still need a remote `HeartbeatTaskStore` with compare-and-swap, transactions, or leases. Recovery does not roll back external domain effects, so host mutations must remain idempotent.

author: wwoosshh
body:
아사히에게 스킬·MCP·커넥터가 없던 문제의 첫 조각이다. **우리가 SKILL.md 를 써서 넣는 것이 아니라, 남이 만든 스킬을 받아들이는 통로**를 만든다 — 전자는 하네스가 아니라 문서 추가일 뿐이고 그 방향으로는 공식 스킬도 서드파티 스킬도 영원히 못 쓴다.

앞으로 스킬 추가는 **폴더를 그대로 복사해 커밋**하면 끝이다. 첫 스킬로 `frontend-design` 이 들어 있다.

## 만든 게 별로 없다

SDK 0.3.207 이 이미 스킬을 지원한다. `plugins: [{type:'local', path}]` 로 폴더를 넘기면 그 안의 `skills/<이름>/SKILL.md` 가 등록된다. 실제 배포 형식도 `plugin.json` 3항목 + frontmatter 2필드라 **변환이 필요 없다.**

그래서 이 브랜치의 코드는 순수 함수 셋과 `query()` 옵션 두 줄이 전부다. 나머지는 전부 "어떻게 조용히 실패하는가"를 찾아낸 기록이다.

## 조용히 실패하는 함정 셋을 잡았다

이 기능의 실패는 전부 **"스킬이 그냥 안 보임"으로만 나타나고 로그를 한 줄도 남기지 않는다.** 셋 다 배포 후에야, 그것도 원인 불명으로 드러났을 것이다.

**1. `tools: []` 가 `Skill` 도구까지 닫는다.** 봇은 SDK 내장 도구를 의도적으로 전부 닫아 두는데(파일·셸은 워커에서 원격 실행), 그게 `Skill` 까지 닫는다. `skills: 'all'` 로도 되살아나지 않고 `tools` 배열에 `"Skill"` 이 있어야 산다.

계획의 첫 태스크를 코드가 아니라 **실험**으로 잡아 배선 전에 확정했다(`agent/src/scripts/skillProbe.ts`). 세 조합을 재고 판정 표대로 갈랐다. 그래서 켜고 끄는 스위치가 `skills` 옵션이 아니라 `builtinTools` 멤버십이 됐다 — WebSearch 와 같은 축이라 오히려 단순해졌다.

`skills: []` 가 실제로 끄는지는 증명되지 않았으므로(프로브의 C 갈래가 `tools: []` 와 겹쳐 분리되지 않았다 — 구현자 지적) 그 경로에 차단을 걸지 않았다. `skills` 는 항상 `"all"` 이다.

**2. SDK 는 `<플러그인 루트>/skills/<이름>/SKILL.md` 를 스캔한다.** 첫 구현은 루트 바로 밑에 스킬을 뒀고, 그러면 **플러그인은 에러 없이 로드되는데 스킬이 0개**다. 태스크 리뷰가 잡았고 실측으로 확정했다 — 같은 루트에 평면·중첩을 동시에 두고 물었더니 중첩만 발견됐고, 평면 쪽 질문에서 모델이 "그건 없지만 중첩된 그 스킬은 있다"고 답해 한 번 더 확인됐다.

**3. `.gitignore` 의 `*.txt`·`data/` 가 새 스킬의 파일을 조용히 떨어뜨린다.** 이 브랜치의 계약이 "폴더째 복사해 커밋"인데 그 계약을 리포 설정이 깨고 있었다. `git add` 는 경고 한 줄 없이 종료 코드 0으로 파일을 빠뜨린다. 지금 `LICENSE.txt` 가 들어 있는 유일한 이유가 `git add -f` 로 강제한 것이었고, 그 사실은 커밋되지 않는 파일에만 적혀 있었다. 배포되는 스킬은 `references/`·`assets/`·`data/` 를 흔히 동봉한다.

## 검증

`npm test` 973 통과 / 3 skip (49 파일), `npm run typecheck` 클린, `node scripts/check-docs.mjs` 통과.

`frontend-design` 이 실제로 로드되는 것은 배포 전에 확인했다 — **모델이 `SKILL.md` 본문 문장을 그대로 인용하게 해서** 판정했다. "스킬 있어"라는 자기 보고는 증거로 쓰지 않았다.

태스크마다 개별 리뷰를 거쳤고 마지막에 브랜치 전체 리뷰를 한 번 더 했다. 그 과정에서 **내가 앞서 "실재한다"고 적었던 `.dockerignore` 함정이 실은 없었다는 것도 정정됐다** — `.dockerignore` 는 gitignore 가 아니라 Go `filepath.Match` 라 `*` 가 `/` 를 넘지 못한다. 예외 줄은 방어적으로 남기되(누가 `**/*.md` 로 넓히면 그때 실제로 지켜준다) 틀린 단정을 주석과 스모크에서 걷어냈다.

`capability-model.md` 의 `builtinTools` 서술 세 곳도 이 브랜치로 거짓이 돼 함께 고쳤다 — 보안 불변식을 적는 자리라 특히 중요하다. `check-docs.mjs` 는 이 종류를 구조적으로 못 잡는다.

## 남은 것

**도커 빌드가 미검증이다**(작업 기계에 데몬이 없다). `deploy/smoke-test.md` 의 스킬 항목 둘이 유일한 방어선이고, 컨테이너 안 파일을 직접 보는 절차로 적었다.

로드맵상 다음 단계:

1. ~~스킬 로딩 하네스~~ (이 PR)
2. **스크립트 브리지** — 스킬 문서는 봇에, 파일·셸 실행은 워커에 있다. 이 비대칭 때문에 지금은 문서형 스킬만 동작한다. 미니PC 는 `update-worker.ps1` 로 같은 `agent/skill-plugin/` 을 이미 받고 있어서, 다음 단계는 파일을 나르는 문제가 아니라 경로 규약 문제다
3. 외부 스킬 신뢰 정책 — 스킬은 아사히가 따르는 지시문 + 미니PC 에서 도는 스크립트라 공급망 표면이다
4. MCP·커넥터
