author: pyricau
body:
## The name on a rectangle is now the way to reach it

A rectangle's children cover every pixel of it, so the name the map writes on a child of the current root is the one piece of that rectangle still showing — and reading the map is reading those names. Pointing at one answered with whichever descendant happened to be under the lettering, which is a question nobody asked.

The translucent plate under a name is now a hit target of its own:

- **Hovering it** describes the rectangle it names, in the chain beside the view and in the card at the pointer.
- **Clicking it** walks into that rectangle, rather than jumping to the bottom of the map.

Everywhere else the innermost rectangle still wins, and a container is still pressed by its outline (`edgeGrab`) too — this is one more way in, not a replacement.

The plate is measured once, into a new `MeasuredLabel`, so the rectangle painted and the rectangle pointed at are literally the same value. It is clamped to the cell it names: a name on a rectangle barely a line of text tall would otherwise overhang, and the overhang would both be drawn on the sibling below it and answer the pointer for it. The lettering can still overflow, as it always could; what stands for the rectangle can't reach outside it.

`namedCellAt` lives in `shark-explorer-app` rather than in `core` because only Compose can measure text.

## And a pile of objects gets to say what it is

A rectangle has room for `400 × Sibling` or `300 smaller objects` and no more, so the fully qualified class name — or which rectangle a leftover pile was left out of — fits nowhere but the card at the pointer. That card was drawn for `Selection.Object` alone, which meant pointing at the one kind of cell whose name is *incomplete* answered nothing at all.

`PointerCard` now takes a `Selection` and says its piece for all three kinds:

| What's under the pointer | What the card says |
| --- | --- |
| One object | unchanged |
| Every instance of one class, or the uncollected garbage | the title, the **qualified class name**, how it's held, what it retains, and that it isn't one object — click it to reach them |
| The children a subdivision had no room for | how many, which rectangle holds them, what they retain, and that they're too small or too many to draw one by one |

Those last two lines are separate constants on purpose: a pile of one class is a node of the tree, so clicking it goes into it and the objects are there, while a leftover pile has nothing to go into. Promising otherwise would be a lie.

Clicking needed no change for either: a class group is already a tree node with a path, and a leftover group already becomes the selection in place.

## Testing

- `TreemapViewTest` — two tests pressing and hovering a name over a child that covers its parent entirely.
- `MapNamesTest` — four window-level tests: a name reports and opens what it names rather than the array drawn inside it, a class pile gives up its qualified name, and a leftover pile says what it is. New file rather than more of `ExplorerAppTest`, which is at detekt's `LargeClass` limit.

Both halves were checked by removal: dropping `namedCellAt` from the hit test fails the two view tests, and filtering the card back to `Selection.Object` fails the two pile tests.

`:shark:shark-explorer:shark-explorer-app:check` and `:shark:shark-explorer:shark-explorer-core:test` are green, detekt included. Notes updated in `notes/treemap-rendering.md` and `notes/decisions.md`. No changelog entry — the explorer modules aren't published.

💡 **What:**
Computed the count of `HingeBasisFunction` in `self.current_basis_functions` before the loop inside `_find_best_candidate_addition`, rather than recalculating it on each iteration.

🎯 **Why:**
This loop iterates over many candidate additions. Re-calculating the sum over `self.current_basis_functions` in every iteration caused unnecessary runtime overhead and CPU usage.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
For a targeted test with 15 features and `max_terms=20`, this small change reduces time from ~66.1 seconds to ~64.0 seconds for the forward pass, and the method execution profile in cProfile shows notable speedup for smaller runs (reduced primitive call count and execution time) since the method was called repeatedly on a growing basis function list.

body:
**Part of #156 (US-004 — Historial de archivos cargados).** PR 1/3 de la cadena `feature-branch-chain` — base: rama tracker `feat/us-004-historial-ingestas`.

## Qué entrega (Slice 1: backend core + migración)

- **Schema**: `Ingesta.accountId`/`banco` → nullable, nueva columna `userId` NOT NULL (FK `ON DELETE RESTRICT`) + CHECK `PROCESADA ⟹ accountId NOT NULL` (SQL crudo). Migración en dos fases con backfill fail-closed.
- **Registro de todos los fallos**: cada salida terminal del pipeline (incl. fallos tempranos sin cuenta) ahora persiste una fila `FALLIDA` con `motivoFallo`, vía un `registrarFallo` never-throw en el borde del orquestador.
- **Persistencia colapsada**: `createPending → commit → markFailed` → un único `persistirProcesada` atómico (create anidado). Puerto de escritura colapsado + puerto angosto `IRegistrarIngestaFallidaWriter`.
- **`GET /api/ingestas`** ampliado: quita el filtro `PROCESADA`-only, aísla por `userId` directo, DTO con `nombreArchivo`/`estado`/`motivoFallo`. Enum de Prisma narrowed a union literal `IngestaEstado` en el borde infra (ADR-005: application sin `@prisma/client`).
- **demo-cleanup** borra `Ingesta` por `userId` directo (fila FALLIDA sin cuenta ya no rompe el teardown).
- **eliminar-ingesta (US-018)** endurecido: gate explícito `userId` directo + `estado: PROCESADA` (FALLIDA no borrable por decisión, no por accidente del join).

## Verificación

- `pnpm api test` → **927/927 verde**; int-specs contra Postgres local (atomicidad, aislamiento multi-tenant, FALLIDA-no-borrable) verdes.
- Diseño aprobado tras **2 rondas de Judgment Day** (adversarial dual) + **revisión 4R** (risk/reliability/resilience/readability) del diff.

## ⚠️ CI roja esperada en este PR

Este PR es el Slice 1 de una cadena. La migración `userId NOT NULL` rompe **16 archivos de test** (fixtures sin `userId` + specs que dependen del ciclo viejo) que **arregla el Slice 2** (PR 2/3). Por eso `tsc`/CI van rojos acá a propósito — solo la rama tracker mergea a `main` en verde una vez integrados los 3 slices. Ver `openspec/changes/us-004-historial-ingestas/design.md` §10.5.

author: carlos-verdes
body:
## Summary

Closes #159

Stacks on #158 (both touch `authoritative_reconcile` and the same call sites in `app.rs`, per this repo's git-workflow guidance on not parallelising PRs that edit the same hot file) \u2014 base this PR against `feat/refresh-error-banner-157`, not `main`, until #158 merges.

Found while re-verifying the board after #157/#158: a manual Refresh eventually picked up correct data (a merged PR disappearing from the board), but only **after** the spinner had already stopped and gone back to the idle icon \u2014 the update looked like it came out of nowhere, well after the UI had signalled "done."

## Root cause

The two-phase refresh (`delta_refresh` then `authoritative_reconcile`, #126/#149) is deliberate: the fast delta paints first and clears `board_refreshing` (the spinner flag) right away, then the slower authoritative reconcile runs silently afterwards to catch drift the delta window can't see \u2014 exactly the kind of change (a PR that just closed/merged an issue) most likely to matter. Nothing in the UI reflected that second phase, so the spinner stopping communicated "fully refreshed" while the more important half was often still running.

## What Changed

- Added a `syncing: Signal<bool>`, set true at the start of `authoritative_reconcile` and false at the end, for every source (auto-revalidate-on-open, the periodic reconcile loop, manual Refresh) \u2014 centralized in the one function all three call, so no call site needs its own bookkeeping.
- Folded it into the existing `refreshing` computation the Refresh button's spinner already watches (alongside `board_refreshing`), so the icon now spans the whole two-phase refresh instead of going idle after just the delta half.
- `on_refresh`'s early-return guard also checks `syncing()`, so a second click while a reconcile is still running (even one an automatic source kicked off) is a no-op, same as the existing `board_refreshing` guard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The Refresh button's spinner stays active for the full duration of an authoritative reconcile triggered by any source (manual or automatic), not just the delta phase
- [x] A second manual Refresh click while one is already syncing is a no-op

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace` (pre-push `make check` gate, all green)

author: rbellatinf
body:
## Root cause

The deployed `ghcr.io/spree/spree:5.4.0` image configures Active Job to use Sidekiq. The current Blueprint sets `SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA`, which this image does not use, and provides no `REDIS_URL`.

A valid publishable API key reaches Spree authentication, which enqueues its usage-tracking job. Without Redis, Sidekiq cannot enqueue the job and the Store API responds with HTTP 500. Missing or invalid keys correctly return HTTP 401.

## Changes

- provision a free, private Render Key Value instance named `rumbo1-redis`
- inject its internal connection string into the Spree web service as `REDIS_URL`
- remove the ineffective `SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA` setting
- use the `noeviction` policy for the job queue
- document the free-tier job-processing limitation and the production worker requirement

## Impact

After the Blueprint is synced, authenticated Store API reads can enqueue Sidekiq jobs instead of failing before the controller response. The no-cost setup remains intended for catalog and integration testing; a dedicated paid worker is required before enabling job-dependent production flows.

## Validation

- parsed the updated `render.yaml` successfully
- checked the Key Value and `fromService.connectionString` fields against Render's current Blueprint schema
- verified the exact Spree 5.4.0 image source revision configures `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq`
- reproduced HTTP 401 for missing/invalid keys and HTTP 500 only for the valid publishable key

body:
## Summary
- Root-cause fix for premature logouts: proxies `/api/*` through the frontend's own origin (Next.js rewrite) instead of calling the Render backend directly from the browser. The refresh cookie was cross-site (vercel.app → onrender.com), which browser ITP/third-party-cookie policies purge within days regardless of `SameSite=None`. Same-origin, it's first-party and persists like Instagram/YouTube sessions until explicit logout.
- Adds optional two-step verification (TOTP/authenticator app), with backup codes, gating login behind a short-lived challenge token when enabled. New Settings entry + dismissible onboarding nudge.

## Test plan (done locally against a real account, see conversation)
- [x] `npx next build` clean
- [x] Rewrite proxy verified: `/api/health` and `/api/login` through the frontend origin correctly reach the backend, refresh cookie arrives scoped to the frontend's own origin
- [x] 2FA: setup → QR/secret → confirm with real generated TOTP code → enabled
- [x] Login with 2FA on returns `requires2FA` + challenge token, wrong code rejected, correct TOTP accepted
- [x] Backup code accepted once, rejected on reuse
- [x] Disable 2FA (password-gated), login no longer requires a second step

author: alexreinking
body:
The signed round-toward-negative-infinity branch of `fast_integer_divide` rewrites `numerator` in place (`numerator = xsign ^ numerator`) to fold in the sign, but the `denominator == 1` special case then returned that bit-flipped value instead of the original. So `fast_integer_divide(n, 1)` returned `~n` for negative signed `n` (e.g. int8 `-128` -> `127`, `-5` -> `4`, `0` -> `-1`).

Capture the original numerator before the branch and use it in the `denominator == 1` select. The unsigned and round-to-zero branches never reassigned `numerator`, so they are unaffected.

Adds `test/correctness/fast_integer_divide.cpp`, which compares `fast_integer_divide`/`fast_integer_modulo` against floor division over u8/u16/u32/s8/s16/s32; it exercises the signed denominator == 1 case that previously went uncovered.

## Breaking changes

`fast_integer_divide` now returns `0` with a zero denominator. `fast_integer_modulo` now returns `0` with a `0` modulus.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (not required for docs, CI config, or typo fixes)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if public API changed)
- [ ] Python bindings updated (if public API changed)
- [ ] Benchmarks are included here if the change is intended to affect performance.
- [x] Commits include AI attribution where applicable (see Code of Conduct)

author: eddiefiggie
body:
## What & why

The priority-picker autocomplete users rank stats in was polluted — **520 distinct affix names, ~159 used ≤2×**, riddled with build-time parse garbage (`Bal`, `INT`, `Class Required: Wizard, Sorcerer, Bard (UMD`, `Improved Deception +17 (Bug: ...`, `Penalty Balance +`). Root cause: for the ~8,000 gear-planner-sourced items, the harvest **flattened** the dump's already-structured affixes (`{name, type, value}`) into free-text `enhancements[]` strings, which `affix_parser.py` then re-inferred — badly.

This makes `gearplanner_items.json` the **single source of truth for item affixes** (as `gearplanner_sets.json` already is for sets): the build reads it directly and maps its separate `affixes`/`sets`/`crafting` keys onto records with structured affixes — no free-text round-trip.

## Results

- Distinct affix stats in the dataset: **520 → 352**
- Priority-picker autocomplete: **520 → 208 clean names** (verified live in-browser — zero garbage)
- Item-record affix schema unchanged → solver / `model.js` / `results.js` untouched
- **Python 297 + Node 302 tests pass**

## Implementation units

- **U1** — structured-affix ingest path in `variants.py` (bypasses the parser; wiki-only shards still fall back to it, characterized)
- **U2** — `vocab.map_gearplanner_type` reconciles the dump's actual `type` tokens to canonical bonus types; null-typed procs quarantined by default with a verified allowlist (**KTD6**); leaves the parser's `BONUS_TYPES` untouched to avoid wiki-parse regressions
- **U3** — new `src/planner_items.py` reader; retires the flattened `enriched_planner_ml29.json` shard. Appended **last** so base-seed and existing wiki-enriched shards win name collisions (**KTD5**); net-new items gated by `verify`; `Sealed in X` seal hosts recovered from `crafting`
- **U4** — build emits `metadata.rankable_affixes`; the wizard/browse datalists gate on it (solver still accepts any typed affix)
- **U5** — regression + coverage hardening

## Decisions (settled with the maintainer)

- **KTD5** — own the roster growth: existing shards win collisions, net-new items are `verify`-gated (no dropped names; 0 of the retired shard's 6,195 names lost)
- **KTD6** — null-typed affixes (weapon procs/banes) quarantined by default (solve-neutral) with a small verified allowlist

## Code review

A multi-agent review caught a **P1** (independently confirmed, with reproduction): the reader re-introduced the documented KTD6 **double-listing trap** — the 8 Dinosaur Bone hosts that `dino_blanks` generates post-dedup got a colliding gear-planner body (duplicate `variant_id`). Fixed by excluding host-pipeline names from the reader (0 duplicates now). Also fixed: a vacuous double-listing test guard, leaked malformed datalist names (`Invisibility (Protection`, single-item procs), and reverted a change to dead code (`query.js`).

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-07-31-001-refactor-structured-affix-sourcing-plan.md`

author: pradeep0153
body:
Closes #487.

### Description
This PR executes a foundational architectural refactoring of the global presentation layer. It systematically eradicates a severe code quality degradation caused by developers aggressively hardcoding raw hex colors directly into the UI components, which was actively blocking our ability to scale the brand's visual identity.

### Changes Made
- **Codebase Audit:** Profiled the React component tree and discovered thousands of instances where raw hex values (e.g., `color: '#E2E8F0'` or `backgroundColor: '#1A202C'`) were hardcoded directly into styled-components, inline styles, and CSS modules.
- **Hex Eradication:** Systematically ripped out all hardcoded hex values across the entire frontend repository.
- **Design Token Architecture:** Implemented a strict, centralized Design Token architecture utilizing a global Tailwind CSS configuration (e.g., `tailwind.config.js`).
- **Component Refactoring:** Refactored all components to strictly consume these semantic design tokens (e.g., replacing `#1A202C` with the Tailwind utility class `text-primary-dark` or `bg-slate-900`).

### Impact
- **Developer Velocity & Theming:** Hardcoding hex colors makes it mathematically impossible to execute a sitewide rebranding, seamlessly support Dark Mode, or globally ensure accessible WCAG contrast ratios without executing a massive, error-prone manual find-and-replace operation across thousands of files. By engineering this strict Design System architecture, we mathematically guarantee stylistic consistency. We completely decouple the UI from arbitrary values, drastically accelerate developer velocity when building new features, and pave the way for seamless, dynamic theming across the entire Furnix platform.

author: mrcoder
body:
## What

The OpenAPI viewer (`forge-swagger-ui.ts`) and editor (`forge-swagger-editor.ts`) now resolve, recover, and open their document through one shared pipeline — `openDocument()` + an OpenAPI `TargetSpec` in the new `src/utils/documentOpening/`. Both files' inline resolution/recovery orchestration is deleted in this same PR (the spec's delivery gate: no framework-only PRs).

Slice 1 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-content-opening-unification-design.md`; plan in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-01-slice1-openapi-pipeline.md`. Follows Slice 0 (#432), which unified the save-time writeback decision this slice feeds.

## Why

Seven-plus independent content-opening implementations exist across the app. This slice collapses OpenAPI's two (viewer `loadDiagram` + editor `mountEditorDocument`'s block) into one pipeline call plus one declarative target spec, with **zero family branches inside the pipeline** — every OpenAPI-specific rule (uuid-title fallback, `onMiss`, default doc) lives in `targets/openApiTarget.ts`.

## Ledger (the spec's acceptance criteria)

| Criterion | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAPI content-opening implementations | 2 | 1 pipeline + 1 TargetSpec |
| Copy-scan modes | ad hoc per call site | policy-derived (`read` → cross-page-only, `write` → full) |
| Fail-closed save protection | 1 family (Graph) | 2 (Graph, OpenAPI) |
| Family branches inside the pipeline | — | 0 |

## Behavior changes (accepted in the spec)

1. **Editor, brand-new macro:** `window.diagram`/`store.state.diagram` become `NULL_DIAGRAM` instead of `undefined`. No visible change (`doc?.code || OpenApiExample` resolves the same), and it fixes a latent `exit()` dirty-check inconsistency.
2. **Editor, existing macro whose content load fails indeterminately** (403/5xx/malformed — content may still exist): mounts with `legacyLoadBlocked`, so Publish is refused with a toast rather than silently overwriting the real document with a blank template. This extends Graph's existing data-loss guard (`Persistence.ts`, already family-generic) to OpenAPI. A **clean, confirmed 404** still self-heals exactly as before — a fresh save creates a replacement and repoints the macro (on submittable surfaces).
3. **Viewer, total resolution failure:** shows a terminal "This diagram isn't available." instead of silently rendering the Petstore sample spec. No retry button, no support link, no new analytics — the spec's no-polish constraint.

## Bugs found and fixed along the way

- **uuid-recovery regression** (`cdb1dfc0`): the first cut of `openDocument` returned `failed` before trying `legacyFallbacks` whenever no `customContentId` resolved — which broke recovery for Connect-era macros copy-pasted to a new page (params carry `{uuid, updatedAt}` only, and the uuid-title lookup is the only way back). Caught while migrating the viewer against the old code's actual behavior.
- **shared-singleton mutation** (`a7afb9ae`): `defaultDoc: () => NULL_DIAGRAM` returned the module singleton, which the editor's save handler then mutated in place via `Object.assign`. Now returns a fresh copy, with the contract documented on `TargetSpec.defaultDoc`.
- **over-broad fail-closed guard** (`a7afb9ae`): the guard initially fired on every failed outcome including a clean 404, which would have permanently bricked a macro whose content was simply deleted. Narrowed to indeterminate failures only, matching Graph's precedent; toast wording corrected (OpenAPI never used legacy content properties, so Graph's "legacy diagram content" wording was false here).
- **`loadError` persistence trap** (`6956d92f`): added to `sanitizeCustomContentBody`'s strip list. No live path persists it today, but Slice 4 wires `forgeIndex.ts`, which views *and* edits over one shared `store.state.diagram` that it saves — a failed load would otherwise persist the error and trap the macro in the error UI permanently.

## Writeback-derivation cross-check (plan Task 5, Step 3 — the mandated gate)

The editor's `origin` → `derivationInput` mapping is the highest-blast-radius change here; `forge-*-editor.ts` entry files have no unit-test harness in this repo, so the plan made a line-by-line trace the gate. Each field, old → new:

| Field | Old source | New source | Equivalent? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sourceId` | `window.diagram?.id` before save | unchanged | yes — untouched |
| `originalCustomContentId` | module var, set unconditionally to `configId \|\| modalId` at editor open | `origin.originalCustomContentId` = `resolved?.contentId`, which `resolveOpenApiId` computes as `configId \|\| modalId`, set unconditionally | yes, including modal-sourced (dashboard-edit) ids — `source` is recorded separately and does not gate it |
| `docSource` | `window.diagram?.source` | unchanged | yes — untouched |
| `recoveredFromOrphan` | read off `window.diagram.recoveredFromOrphan` at save | `origin.recoveredFromOrphan`, captured at mount | yes — set under the identical two conditions (orphan-sibling hit, or any `legacyFallbacks` hit), and the doc object is still stamped as before, so other readers are unaffected |

On the `failed`/indeterminate path, `saveToPlatform` throws before `derivationInput` is ever read (traced: sentinel → spread → `Object.assign` → throw → catch → return), and `dashboardEditDocLoaded` stays `false` because `NULL_DIAGRAM.code` is `''`.

## Verification

- **Unit:** 184 files / 2123 tests green. 24 new tests across `openDocument.spec.ts`, `openApiTarget.spec.ts`, `viewerBootstrap.spec.ts`, `OpenApiViewer.spec.ts`, all red-first.
- **Typecheck:** `tsc --noEmit` diffed error-for-error against a clean `main` checkout — zero new errors. (`vue-tsc` crashes in this environment on a pre-existing tooling bug unrelated to this branch.)
- **Lint:** 0 errors on all changed files.
- **Build:** `build:lite` succeeds.
- **E2E:** `writeback-gate-non-submittable.spec.ts` passed against deployed staging. `openapi-create`/`openapi-edit` hit an ace-editor click flake locally (same failure across 3 attempts, in a helper this branch never touches, against a deployed site this worktree cannot affect) — CI's `pull_request` run is the authoritative check.
- **Review:** each task got a spec+quality review; the branch got a whole-branch review plus a scoped re-review of the fix wave.

## Carry-forward for Slice 2 (Graph)

Two contract gaps the final review surfaced, deliberately **not** fixed here because Slice 1 cannot exercise either (adding unused capability would be the framework-only work the spec forbids). Slice 2 should open with them:

1. **`LegacyFallback` cannot report an indeterminate failure.** Its return type is `Promise<Diagram | undefined>`, but Graph's `legacyLoadBlocked` originates *entirely* from that channel (five sites in `forge-graph-editor.ts`, cleared when a later fallback succeeds). Slice 2 cannot preserve Graph's existing data-loss protection without widening it.
2. **`DocumentOrigin` omits `legacyLoadBlocked`/`isCopy`/`copyReason`** (all declared in spec §3), so the fail-closed synthesis currently sits at the call site as a three-branch block each editor would otherwise copy. Collapsing it into the pipeline is expressible purely as read-vs-write policy — no family branch.

## Supersedes

PR #196 (`feat/error-panel`, draft since June, unmerged) — its `ViewerLoadDiagramResult`/`loadError` contract is replaced by this slice's `OpenError`, scoped down per the spec's no-polish constraint (no retry button, no support link, no diagnostic bundle, no new events). #196 should close once this merges.

author: aslafy-z
body:
The effective per-litre price used a linear model — price × (1 + burnt/tank)
— which understates long detours and prices stations a full tank cannot even
reach: a 1.53 EUR/L station 157 km away outranked 2.20 EUR/L next door in
the Favorites' recommended sort, and stations 400-1200 km out ranked on
meaningless finite numbers.

The trip burns part of the tank being bought, so the litres kept cost
price × tank / (tank − burnt), and a round trip past the tank's range has
no effective price at all (Infinity) — those rows sink below every
reachable station, closest first, alongside the priceless ones.

selectRecommended learns the matching fallback: a zone where no round trip
fits the tank crowns its nearest station instead of reading as empty
(Infinity − Infinity is NaN, which satisfied no tie test).

author: ciobotaruandrei
body:
## Ce face

Motorul care decide **daca** un raid incepe, peste pragurile din PR #931. Interventia propriu-zisa (lockdown, sanctiuni, restaurare) vine in PR-ul urmator.

Cele cinci tipuri din specificatie, fiecare cu fereastra lui glisanta:

| Tip | Cum se grupeaza |
|---|---|
| Mesaje identice sau aproape identice | per autor **si** text normalizat |
| Spam cu taguri | per autor, dupa **numarul de mentiuni** |
| Servere, invitatii, reclame | per autor |
| Linkuri sau atasamente | per autor |
| Canale sau roluri fara autorizatie | per autor |

## Detalii care schimba rezultatul

**Pragul de taguri se masoara pe mentiuni, nu pe mesaje.** Specificatia spune „mai mult de 3 mențiuni, adică minimum 4, în maximum 10 secunde". Un singur mesaj cu patru mentiuni il atinge, la fel ca patru mesaje cu cate una. Daca se numarau mesajele, un `@everyone` + trei roluri intr-un mesaj ar fi trecut nesanctionat.

**Normalizarea acopera „aproape identice".** Linkurile, mentiunile si punctuatia sunt scoase, textul e trecut la litere mici si spatiile colapsate, deci `Castiga bani ACUM!!!` si `castiga   bani acum` cad in acelasi cos. Fara asta, un spammer scapa schimband semnele de exclamare.

**Invitatiile sunt recunoscute pe mai multe domenii** — `discord.gg`, `discord.com/invite`, `discordapp.com/invite`, `discord.me`, `dsc.gg`, `invite.gg` — nu doar pe cel evident.

**Atasamentele conteaza la pragul de linkuri chiar fara text**, fiindca patru fisiere la rand sunt exact la fel de mult spam ca patru linkuri.

## Doua fals-pozitive evitate deliberat

1. **Trei persoane care spun acelasi lucru nu sunt un raid.** Mesajele identice se grupeaza per **autor** si text; altfel, trei membri care raspund „da" intr-o conversatie ar fi declansat lockdown.
2. **Un membru care doar vorbea in acelasi timp nu devine participant.** Un incident coordonat cere ca fiecare participant sa aiba **repetitie** in fereastra, nu un singur mesaj. Fara regula asta, oricine scria in canal in timpul unui atac ar fi fost sanctionat impreuna cu atacatorii — exact ce interzice specificatia cand spune ca botul nu sanctioneaza o persoana aleasa la intamplare.

Semnalele din afara celei mai lungi ferestre sunt curatate la fiecare observatie, plus un plafon absolut, deci memoria nu creste la nesfarsit intr-un atac lung.

## Teste

15 teste noi: normalizarea, pragul atins si neatins, fereastra expirata, mesaje diferite de la acelasi autor, mesaje identice de la autori diferiti, pragul de mentiuni pe ambele cai (un mesaj cu 4 vs. patru mesaje cu 1), invitatiile pe trei domenii, atasamentele fara text, structura, coordonarea cu doi participanti, membrul nevinovat exclus, mai multe tipuri simultan, curatarea memoriei, pragurile stramte ale ownerului, si `reset`.

`npm run check`: exit 0, 2593 teste.

- [x] **Documentatie**: `CHANGELOG.md` (comportamentul detectiei); pragurile si comenzile sunt deja documentate in `docs/Comenzi Functionalitate.md` prin PR #931, iar acest PR nu adauga comenzi noi
- [x] **Teste**: 15 teste noi pentru detectie, grupare, coordonare si curatarea memoriei
- [x] Comentarii: niciun comentariu adaugat in fisierele cu cod (regula 1)
- [x] **Benchmark**: nu se aplica inca — motorul e pur si plafonat la 2000 de semnale, cu curatare la fiecare observatie; masurarea sub incarcare reala are sens dupa ce se cableaza pe `messageCreate`, in PR-ul de interventie
- [x] Conflict cu situatia curenta din repo: verificat; PR #930 si #931 sunt MERGEABLE cu toate check-urile SUCCESS, iar acest branch porneste de pe #931

author: minhtridinh-kayden
body:
The moat was one sixth built.

## What was wrong

`_ENTRIES` held **12** of the **74** mappings TCVN3 needs — the `a` vowel family plus
`đ`. Everything present was correct; the table simply stopped there, as its own
docstring said it would until the source column could be validated.

Real output, before:

```
QuyÕt đÞnh
cña Bé trëng Bé Tài chÝnh sè 1141-TC/Q§/C§KT
```

Missing by vowel family: `o=19  e=12  u=12  a=8  i=5  y=5  đ=1`.

Measured against ten hand-transcribed government documents: **32.8% diacritic
recovery**.

## Provenance of the new entries

No authoritative charset file was available, which is what the docstring said blocked
this. The bytes were instead derived from **31 real TCVN3 documents** published by
Vietnamese government bodies 1998–2009, by aligning byte sequences against the fixed
phrases such documents always carry — `Cộng hoà xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam`,
`Độc lập - Tự do - Hạnh phúc`, `Căn cứ Nghị định số`.

Every entry but one is backed by an observed occurrence. `0xA5` → `Ơ` is inferred from
its block and **marked inline as inferred**.

The derivation explains why the old table stopped where it did: **`0xA1`–`0xA7` are
the uppercase base vowels** `Ă Â Ê Ô Ơ Ư Đ` and `0xA8`–`0xAE` their lowercase forms.
The bytes immediately below the accented ranges are not accented letters at all — a
shape invisible unless the whole block is laid out together. An earlier attempt of
mine guessed at four of them and got all four wrong.

## Tests

Twelve real-document phrases, because **the existing per-entry tests all passed while
the table was one sixth complete** — each of the twelve entries was individually
correct. Only running text shows what is absent.

Plus a residue test: no unmapped Latin-1 byte may survive conversion, excluding the
Vietnamese letters that legitimately live in that range (`à á â ã è é ê ì í ò ó ô õ ù
ú ý`).

## One existing test changed, and why

`test_detects_viscii_by_content` now uses a sentence instead of a six-word phrase.

This is not cosmetic. Content-frequency detection separates candidates by margin, and
a **complete** TCVN3 table trial-converts VISCII bytes into something Vietnamese-shaped
enough to score within **0.011** of the correct reading. At that margin the detector
returns `None` — which is the right behaviour, not a bug. Over a full sentence the gap
widens to **~0.09** and VISCII wins outright.

Worth knowing on its own: completing one table narrows detection margins against the
others, which is a further argument for content detection staying opt-in.

## What this PR does not prove

Re-running the benchmark after this change gives **1.000**, and that number is
worthless. The ground truth was produced with this same table, so the benchmark now
asks whether the table equals itself. It is kept only as a check that the change
transferred completely.

The table’s correctness rests on its derivation and on a human reading the output as
Vietnamese. Measuring TCVN3 accuracy independently again needs a transcript typed by a
person reading the rendered document.

author: jiawoget
body:
## Summary

**Milestone v1.2: Release Assurance & Workflow Closure**

This PR retains the approved secure quick-recording ID behavior, fixes the existing pre-commit hook's Node/npm eligibility selection without adding another runtime wrapper, restores the two local PDF fixtures to their committed bytes, and brings the real implementation through Native OpenGSD research, checked planning, execution, verification, milestone audit, and same-branch archival.

**Current status:** Native Phase 2 verification and the Native milestone audit passed. The v1.2 archive and retrospective are committed on this PR. Frozen-head review found four actionable launcher/interpreter boundaries across `#!/usr/bin/env node`, `npm.cmd`, extensionless `npm`, and fixed Node shebangs. The direct-route repair binds both probe and invocation to one explicit, verified Node + npm CLI pair and conservatively falls back for every unproved launcher. Later exact-head reviews correctly found stale Native-report provenance, a shadowable bare PowerShell host, nested non-root `engines` metadata that could authorize direct execution, and version output whose embedded CR/LF bytes could be deleted into an apparently compatible value. body:
## What this deletes

`frontend/src/workbench/` — the pre-channel block canvas — became a
self-referential island once #1283 made channels the only agent conversation
surface. Nothing outside the directory imported it; its entire live audience
was the test suite written to guard it.

**Frontend sources — 24 files, 5,571 lines**

`BlockHost.tsx`, `WorkbenchCanvas.tsx`, `WorkbenchBlockCreateDialog.tsx`,
`CustomBlockProposalPreview.tsx`, `block-registry.ts`,
`block-create-helpers.ts`, all seven renderers under `blocks/`
(`artifact`, `custom`, `custom-templates`, `file`, `markdown`, `terminal`,
`work-context`), and their CSS.

**Tests — 7 files fully deleted, 2,178 lines**

| File | Lines |
| --- | ---: |
| `test/workbench-block-renderers.test.ts` | 837 |
| `test/workbench-block-registry.test.ts` | 433 |
| `test/file-block-editor-reseed.test.ts` | 358 |
| `test/components/WorkbenchBlockEnvPicker.test.ts` | 265 |
| `test/degraded-ui/block-host-degraded.test.ts` | 162 |
| `test/degraded-ui/block-create-dialog-fallback.test.ts` | 94 |
| `test/e2e/components/AddWorkspaceDialog.spec.ts` | 29 |

**Trimmed, not deleted** — two mixed suites also cover the server REST surface,
so only their frontend source-assertion sections came out:
`test/workbench-custom-blocks.test.ts` (−256), `test/workbench-layout.test.ts`
(−103). `test/tsconfig.json` dropped two now-missing `include` entries.

**Also deleted in the review pass**: `shared/workbench-capability-utils.ts`
(46 lines). Review caught that the slice orphaned it — its only consumers were
the deleted `BlockHost` and the deleted tests. It stayed typecheck-green only
because `test/tsconfig.json` compiles `shared/**/*.ts` wholesale, so no gate
could have flagged it.

Branch total: **43 files changed, +118 / −8,176**.

## What deliberately stays

No route or verb changes here. `shared/workbench-*` types, `server/workbench-*`
routers, and the `/workbench/*` REST surface are untouched and still tested —
what they now lack is a UI consumer. That is a scope boundary, and it is now
recorded in-tree (`shared/workbench-custom-blocks.ts` header) rather than left
for the next hygiene pass to rediscover: the proposal REST surface plus its
five `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` client functions have zero `.tsx` callers and
are held for a channel-era renderer.

## #1223 extension note

This slice extends #1223 ("Delete zero-reference frontend remnants") rather
than closing it. #1223's enumerated delete-safe scope — `ToolCard`,
`FileChangeRow`, `view-tree.ts` + its four implementation-internal tests,
`SessionHistoryPanel` — all landed earlier (verified gone on this head). The
workbench island was **not** in that list: at the time #1223 was written,
`frontend/src/workbench/` still had a reachable path. #1283 removed it. Same
thesis (delete what reachability analysis disproves, leave the live
compatibility surface alone), new evidence, so it ships under #1287 slice 0
and refs #1223 for lineage.

## Docs close-outs

- `docs/federated-relay.md` — the `#616` FileBlock/Edit-mode sections describe
  a renderer that no longer exists. Marked historical **by name**, per section.
- `docs/LEARNINGS.md` — `L-20260801-derived-topics-are-all-or-nothing`
  corrected and extended (see below).
- Stale present-tense pointers to deleted components swept out of
  `shared/workbench-custom-blocks.ts`, `shared/workbench-block-types.ts`, and
  `shared/workbench-layout-types.ts`.

## Review trail

One adversarial review returned **concern** with 8 findings. All valid ones
applied in `12af938b`:

| # | Sev | Finding | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | P2 | `federated-relay.md` banner scoped positionally ("the next two sections"), marking the **live** `PromptAttachment` contract historical while leaving the genuinely-dead "Edit mode" section unmarked | Fixed — scoping is now by section name, with an explicit carve-out for `PromptAttachment` |
| 2 | P2 | The all-or-nothing derived-topic comment's justification does not hold at its own boundary | Fixed — see below |
| 3 | P2 | `shared/workbench-capability-utils.ts` orphaned by this very branch | Fixed — deleted |
| 5 | P3 | Five sibling stale pointers survived in a file edited to kill stale pointers | Fixed — all past-tense |
| 6 | P3 | Retained-without-consumer REST surface unrecorded | Fixed — recorded in-tree |
| 7 | P3 | Test header docblock listed sections 1–6; file runs 11 banners | Fixed — header covers 1–11 |
| 4 | P3 | Commit `1ac128ca`'s deletion rationale is false | **Corrected below** + #1298 |
| 8 | P3 | "Fixture does not exist" criterion applies to 56 other specs | **Corrected below** + #1299 |

### Finding 1 detail

`shared/prompt-attachment.ts` is a live wire contract — imported by
`server/protocol-adapter-v2.ts`, `shared/agent-chat-protocol-v2.ts`,
`shared/context-packet.ts`, and parsed at runtime by `server/ws.ts` via
`parsePromptAttachmentList`. The banner had marked it historical while the
actually-dead "Edit mode (#616 slice 4)" section, which describes the deleted
`blocks/file.tsx` in present tense, sat outside the window with no marker at
all. Both halves were wrong in one sentence.

### Finding 2 detail

`server/workspace-topics.ts` stated the rule unconditionally, but `persisted`
is fetched with `includeArchived` and the store filters `status != 'archived'`.
So the guard is really **"one UNARCHIVED persisted row hides every derived
row"**. Archive every channel in a workspace and `persisted.length === 0`
fires the derived branch, resurfacing exactly the archived WorkContexts the
rule exists to suppress — derived rows key on `derived-<contextId>`, so they
neither dedupe against the archived rows nor inherit the archive filter.

Recorded as **accepted debt** with the closing fix named (gate on the
unfiltered count) rather than silently changing what an all-archived workspace
renders — that is a product call, not a hygiene-pass call. Mirrored into
`docs/LEARNINGS.md`.

### Corrected rationale for the AddWorkspaceDialog spec deletion

Commit `1ac128ca` justified deleting `test/e2e/components/AddWorkspaceDialog.spec.ts`
with "`test/topic-sidebar-shell.test.ts` covers those controls as components".
**That is false** — the commit message is immutable, so the correction lives here:

```
$ grep -c "Add Workspace\|add-workspace\|addWorkspace\|Browse for folders" test/topic-sidebar-shell.test.ts
0
$ grep -rln "AddWorkspaceDialog" test/
(no matches)
```

The accurate rationale: **deleting it loses nothing because the spec never
ran** — it navigated to `/test-add-workspace-dialog.html`, which does not exist
and is not registered in `frontend/vite.config.ts`'s `includeE2eFixtures` map.
Its copy was also stale (it asserted the title "Add Workspace"; the dialog says
"add project"). But `AddWorkspaceDialog.tsx` is live — imported by `App.tsx`,
`lib/actions/definitions/workspace.ts`, and `lib/bulk-add-lanes.ts` — and now
has **zero** coverage. Filed as **#1298**.

Second correction: the "fixture page does not exist" criterion is not unique to
this spec. **56 of the 65** distinct `/test-*.html` targets referenced under
`test/e2e/` are missing. Deleting one of 57 equally-dead specs was arbitrary —
it was simply the one the #1287 audit surfaced while auditing the workspace-add
path. The full sweep is filed as **#1299**, with a suggested build-time gate so
no-op specs fail loudly instead of reading as coverage.

## Verification

Exact head `12af938b`, Node v22.22.3:

- `npm run check` → **0 errors**, 219 warnings (all pre-existing `sonarjs`
  style warnings, none in changed lines)
- Targeted vitest → **204 passed / 0 failed**:
  `workbench-custom-blocks`, `workspace-topics`, `workbench-layout`,
  `workbench-block-types`, `workspace-topic-room-api`, `workbench-prompt-hooks`
- `npm run build` → **exit 0**, `dist/frontend/index.html` emitted; the
  frontend still builds after the deletions
- Reference scan on head: `grep -rn "workbench-capability-utils"` → zero hits
  repo-wide (excluding `node_modules`/`.

body:
[impl agent, opus-4.8]

## Summary

Adds one new non-gated cross-backend parity row, `fadvise_hints`, the
file-backed analog of the existing `memory_advice` (madvise) row. It issues the
five standard `POSIX_FADV_*` hints — `NORMAL`, `SEQUENTIAL`, `WILLNEED`,
`DONTNEED`, `RANDOM` — against a temporary file and requires each to be
deterministically accepted (`posix_fadvise` returns 0 on success or a positive
errno directly). Advice is a pure hint with no observable effect on file
contents.

The fixture deliberately omits the invalid-advice edge case: native Linux
returns `EINVAL` for a bogus advice value, but all three Hermit backends
consistently accept it instead. That refusal behavior is a backend modeling
choice rather than a cross-backend contract, so the row asserts only the five
well-defined valid hints, on which all three backends agree.

Test-only change: new fixture + `run_matrix.py` source/case wiring + `matrix.tsv`
row + `README.md`. No product-source, backend, or determinization change; the
hermit binary is unchanged.

## Determinism

The only observable is whether each of the five standard file hints is accepted.
`posix_fadvise` mutates no file contents and returns a fixed status for a valid
hint on a valid fd, with no host-derived, timing, or cross-thread input, so the
result is identical across ptrace, DBI, and KVM. The fixture prints a single
`fadvise ok=5` line; identical bytes across repeated `--strict` runs and a
byte-identical `--strict --verify` guest-memory hash witness the determinism.

## Validation

Flags: `--base-env=minimal --max-timeslice=disabled --tmp=/tmp`.

- ratchet `--check`: exit 0 — ptrace 24/24, DBI 23/24, KVM 23/24
- `run_matrix.py --backend ptrace --strict`: `PASS ptrace/fadvise_hints: 3/3`
- `run_matrix.py --backend dbi --strict`: `PASS dbi/fadvise_hints: 3/3`
- `run_matrix.py --backend kvm`: `PASS kvm/fadvise_hints: 3/3`
- DBI L2 (`run --backend dbi --strict --verify`): `Determinism verified.`,
  guest-memory hash `2925569d808f77d4` (identical both observations)
- golden stdout `fadvise ok=5` (sha256 prefix `af59c583cff4ad38`)

The one unrelated `FAIL kvm/process_wait_accounting` observed locally is the
known pre-existing intermittent KVM `waitid`/`ECHILD` child-sync flake, not
introduced or touched by this row.

## Relationship to gVisor

Not applicable: no KVM backend code changes; `fadvise_hints` passes on all three
backends and adds no KVM gap.

## Human Review Required

None. This is a test-only fixture + matrix + README addition. It adds no new
syscall support (posix_fadvise is already handled), no Reverie API or
core-abstraction change, no new determinization strategy, and no DetCore
scheduling change — none of the four post-facto-human-review triggers apply.

author: sparlane
body:
## Description

The loop slept `command_poll_ms` and derived every other cadence from a tick counter: `tick_counter % ticks_per_sec` for the per-second tasks, `% send_config_period_ticks` for the 15 s broadcast. But the loop period is the sleep *plus* whatever the body took — `sendCommand()` fans out over every client, and once a second `cleanupRemovableClients()` joins the recv threads of departing clients — and `usleep` returns early on a signal, since the handlers install with `sa_flags = 0` and the CRL reload depends on that. So the counter drifted in both directions and "every second" meant "every tenth iteration, whenever those happened".

Each task now carries its own deadline, advanced by its own period after it fires, so skew cannot accumulate. This is the shape `examples/fake_client.cpp:236` already uses, and that file's comment explains the same failure mode for its own intervals.

Three details worth naming:

- A sleep cut short by a signal now rounds the loop instead of falling through to the body. The top of the loop is where a SIGHUP's CRL reload and a SIGTERM's shutdown are noticed, and whatever remains of the period is slept on the next pass — so a signal no longer shortens a tick, it just makes the loop notice things sooner.
- Which tasks a pass owns is decided before the body runs, so a slow body cannot pull the next period's work into this one.
- On overrun the missed slots are skipped rather than fired back to back. A catch-up burst would redispatch the same command repeatedly and hand the fail-safe a run of zero-length seconds — the same drift this commit removes, from the other side.

The previous commit made the fail-safe measure its own thresholds, so it no longer depends on this. What this fixes is everything else on the per-second schedule that still trusts the caller: `checkTimeouts()` — which decides when a client is declared gone — and `sendRTTRequest()`, whose replies feed the client-clock offset that the position staleness gate uses.

`ticks_per_sec` and `send_config_period_ticks` stay: the command poller is a separate thread with its own `sleep_for` and its own counter, and it is not touched here.

Verified: 439 unit cases green; check-code.sh clean; the **full** e2e suite (35 tests, 7m13s) passes, including the four that pin fail-safe timing, the sub-second command latency check, and the frozen-database case that asserts the main loop does not stall.

## Summary by Sourcery

Replace the main server loop’s tick-counter-based scheduling with monotonic, deadline-driven timing to ensure periodic tasks run at correct real-time intervals and avoid drift under signals or slow iterations.

Enhancements:
- Introduce a monotonic clock and per-task deadlines in the main loop to drive command polling, per-second maintenance, and configuration broadcasts.
- Ensure signals only cause the loop to re-round and do not shorten effective periods, and prevent slow iterations from pulling future-period work into the current pass.
- Skip overrun slots instead of firing missed periodic tasks back-to-back to avoid command bursts and distorted fail-safe timing.

body:
## 📝 Pull Request Description

### Related Issue
Closes #714

### Summary
`AIResponsePreview` declared `useState` **after** the `if (!content) return null;` early return — a Rules-of-Hooks violation. When `content` flips from falsy to truthy across renders (exactly what happens as an AI answer loads/streams in), the hook count changes between renders and React throws *"Rendered more hooks than during the previous render"*, crashing the component (caught by the ErrorBoundary). ESLint also flagged it as `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks`.

Fix is a one-line reorder: declare the hook at the top of the component, then keep the `if (!content) return null;` guard below it, so hooks always run unconditionally.

Verified with `npx eslint` on the file — the `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` error is gone.

author: bunsdev
body:
Closes cave-j54fz — `acquisition does not return success after its final audit outlives the lease`, failing ~1 run in 6.

## Why the bead's suggested fix doesn't work

The test needs the lease **alive at the promotion checkpoint** (which reports a plain `expired`) and **dead at the final ownership audit** (the only checkpoint that reports `expired-before-return`). It arranged that with `ttlMs: 100` plus a 200ms sleep injected into the `gate-acquired` audit append — so both sides depended on winning a wall-clock race.

The bead suggested raising `ttlMs`. I tried it: **1000 still failed 1 in 8**, with the identical `'expired'`.

The measurement explains why. Failed runs leave their tmpdir behind, so their `audit.jsonl` gives the real timeline — the gap between gate creation (`gate-draining`) and the promotion checkpoint (`acquire-rejected`):

```
1289 ms   1501 ms   2937 ms   4421 ms
```

Acquisition's own file I/O is what varies, by more than 3×. Any fixed `ttlMs` only relocates the boundary, because the sleep then has to outlast the larger ttl as well — the two constraints chase each other, and the test gets slower at every step.

## What this does instead

Stop racing the clock. Give the lease a 60s ttl no setup delay can plausibly exhaust, and expire it *exactly where this test means to*: backdate the gate timestamps as the `gate-acquired` line is written — after promotion, before the final audit.

That's sound because `gateExpired()` is a plain `heartbeatAt + ttlMs` comparison and `clockRegressed()` only fires on **future** heartbeats, so a backdated gate reads as unambiguously expired rather than merely late.

`acquiredAt` shifts with `heartbeatAt`: `validateGate` requires `heartbeatAt >= acquiredAt`, so moving the heartbeat alone makes the gate *malformed* instead of expired and the rejection path's cleanup then fails with `gate-cleanup-failed` — observed **10/10** before the timestamps were shifted together. This mirrors the file's existing `expireGate()` helper, which can't be called directly because the shim runs inside the spawned child.

## Verification

- **12/12 runs green** (was ~1 in 6 failing).
- The test drops from **~3–7s to ~0.8s**, since nothing sleeps any more.
- **Mutation-checked that it still discriminates**: removing the `expired → expired-before-return` remap in `maintenance-gate.mjs` makes it fail with `actual: 'expired'`, exactly as it should. So the race was removed without hollowing out the assertion.
- Full file: 22/23. The one remaining failure is a **different, pre-existing** test — `concurrent multi-process acquisition: exactly one winner`. I measured it on an unmodified `origin/main` copy of the file (1/6 failures) versus this branch (2/6), so it is not caused by this change; filed as **cave-uadm8**.

`scripts/maintenance-gate.mjs` is untouched — this is a test-only change.

### Note on a neighbouring bead

cave-nseb2 tracks a *different* race in this same file, and a fix for it is sitting uncommitted in the primary checkout as another session's live work. I left that alone; this PR touches only the one test function, so the two shouldn't conflict beyond a trivial rebase.

author: stebo85
body:
`builder/check_version.py` opened an issue such as #2947 for every recipe whose upstream had a newer release. Nothing consumed those issues — `process-issues.yml` only reacts to `[CONTRIBUTION]` issues — so each one was manual work that had to be repeated by hand.

This makes the weekly job apply the bump and open the pull request itself.

### What changed
- `builder/check_version.py` rewrites the recipe's top-level `version` (preserving its original quoting), commits it on `auto-update/<name>-<version>`, and opens a PR. Any existing legacy "may update to" issue for that recipe is closed by the PR body.
- Recipes that build from a pinned commit get their `revision` repointed at the commit the new tag resolves to (annotated tags are dereferenced). Without this, a bump of `niimath` would relabel the container while rebuilding the identical source.
- Cases a human has to judge still become issues: unsupported/missing `auto_update` fields, versions `packaging` cannot compare, tags that do not map onto a recipe version, and any bump the script cannot apply cleanly.
- Duplicate suppression now checks for an existing branch or PR for the target version instead of an open issue.
- `--dry-run` (or `AUTO_UPDATE_DRY_RUN=1`) reports what would change without touching git or opening anything, and `workflow_dispatch` exposes it as an input.
- `.github/workflows/auto-update.yml` gains `contents: write` / `pull-requests: write` and checks out with `NEURODESK_GITHUB_TOKEN_ISSUE_AUTOMATION`, because pull requests pushed with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger the recipe CI workflows.

### Scope
Three recipes currently opt in with an `auto_update` block — `niimath`, `mede` and `emuses` — out of 237. Recipes without the block are never checked or bumped.

### Verification
Dry run against live upstream data resolved `mede` and `emuses` as up to date and produced the `niimath` bump, including the correct commit for `v1.0.20260720`. The resulting recipe passes `python3 builder/validation.py recipes/niimath/build.yaml`. That bump is #2986.

author: maxlemoar
body:
Everything here comes out of reading the two emails a real customer received after the first live order.

## The legal form was wrong

The site described the operator as a sole trader — "Animals of Cologne", "Inhaber: Maximilian Marowsky" — in the Impressum, the Datenschutz controller block, the JSON-LD and the order-confirmation footer. It is a **GbR** with three partners.

That is not a wording nicety: a GbR has no proprietor, § 5 DDG wants the legal form in the name and the partners authorised to represent it, liability differs, and the withdrawal declarations customers send are addressed to this entity. `site.operator` now carries `partners`, and all five consumers follow from that one record.

For the structured data the three are `member` of the Organization rather than `founder` — founding is a claim about history that nothing here sources, and the old `founder` node carried the *company* name on a Person, which was a bug in its own right.

## A promise we could not keep

The confirmation email, the AGB and the withdrawal page all stated that payment before 14:30 on a working day means printing the same day. Nobody could source that number, and the first real order contradicted it: paid at 21:58, handed to print at 22:00 the same day.

Replaced everywhere with what the flow actually guarantees — the letter goes to print immediately after payment, and neither the print nor the delivery day is owed. On `/widerruf` the timing was load-bearing, because it explained when the service counts as completely performed and the withdrawal right lapses under § 356 Abs. 4 BGB; that statement is kept and now anchored to completion of the print steps rather than to a clock.

## The supplier stopped emailing the customer

`NotificationMail` on the eBrief job was the tenant's address, so two minutes after our own confirmation the buyer received an unbranded B2B "Auftragseingang" from a company they never contracted with, carrying our eBrief customer number, our name under "Kundeninformationen" and eBrief's internal article numbers. It reads like a data leak and tells the buyer nothing they need. It goes to the operator now.

## The confirmation was written for the file, not the buyer

Same content, different weight. Purchase, price, order number and order date first; what happens next second; the full legal block last and visually subordinate under a heading that says what it is. Nothing legal was removed — the Widerrufsbelehrung, the Muster-Widerrufsformular, the § 356 Abs. 4 confirmation (itself mandatory under § 312f Abs. 3 BGB), the § 19 UStG note and the VSBG statement are all still there.

Two smaller repairs in the same pass: the customer-facing reference was a 66-character `cs_live_…` Stripe session id and is now the eBrief job number, which is also what a support request would be searched by; and the order date is stated, because the withdrawal form asks the customer to fill in "Bestellt am" and the email carrying that form did not tell them.

## Guards

None of these four defects would have failed an existing check, so each got one: the mail check now rejects any clock time presented as a promise and any `cs_live_`/`cs_test_` reaching the customer, and asserts section order; a new Playwright test rejects `HH:MM Uhr` on the two legal pages and requires `/widerruf` to keep both "§ 356 Abs. 4 BGB" and "Vollständig erbracht", so dropping the timing again cannot silently drop the legal statement with it; `legal.spec.ts` asserts the GbR suffix and all three partners.

## Verification

`npm run verify`: 145 passed, 1 flaky, 2 skipped. `grep -rn "Inhaber" src/` and `grep -rn "14:30" src/` both empty.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: edbertchan
body:
## Summary

Forking a workflow creates a real new workflow. The renderer's workflow map was never told about it.

The prior slice's harness caught this: the `fork-workflow` scenario failed with `workflow-metadata-publish-never-triggered`, the same class of gap that made a real detach not show up in the graph.

The cause: `headlessForkWorkflow` never called `requestWorkflowMetadataPublish`, unlike `detach-workflow` and every other workflow-metadata mutation next to it.

`HeadlessDeps` had no field for this at all -- it is only meaningful on the shared-owner dispatch path, where a live renderer exists to notify.

## Review Claim

Approve a new optional `requestWorkflowMetadataPublish` field on `HeadlessDeps`, wired through `executeHeadlessExec`, and one new call from `headlessForkWorkflow` with reason `'fork-workflow'`.

## Review Lane

behavior

## Review Unit

activation-surface

## Safety Invariant

The new field is optional and unset in standalone/owner-serve mode (no live window there), matching every other optional callback on `HeadlessDeps`. The one call site uses `deps.requestWorkflowMetadataPublish?.(...)`, a no-op when absent. Nothing else on the fork-workflow path changes.

## Slice Rationale

A focused follow-up to the harness that found this: the harness proved the bug, this slice is the fix, kept separate per this repo's proof-before-fix ordering.

## Non-goals

Does not fix the same class of gap for `set workflow` / `set task` / `set gate-policy`, which share the same missing-field root cause but are out of scope for this fork-workflow-specific fix.

## Test Plan

<details>
<summary>Test Plan</summary>

- [ ] `pnpm --filter app test`
- [ ] `pnpm --filter app build && pnpm --filter @invoker/ui build`
- [ ] `cd packages/app && npx playwright test e2e/drift/drift-single-op.spec.ts -g "fork-workflow" --reporter=list` (fails before this change with `workflow-metadata-publish-never-triggered`, passes after)
- [ ] `cd packages/app && npx playwright test e2e/drift/drift-single-op.spec.ts --reporter=list` (all 29 scenarios pass)

</details>

## Visual Proof

Not path-flagged as UI-impacting by this repo's tooling, but included because the fix is directly about what reaches the renderer. Real captured output, unpatched vs. patched, same real e2e harness and scenario.

![fork-workflow: unpatched (workflow-metadata-publish-never-triggered) vs. patched (renderer receives wf-test-2)](https://pub-cf646cda2bd945d683792ee19b5f9d98.r2.dev/pr-images/20260801-f96c21/fork-workflow-fix.png)

author: wiwiwilliam
body:
## Summary

Adds the baseline open-source governance documents this repository was missing, so external contributors have a real entry point:

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — the multi-repository layout (17+ independent repos, `NimoOS-Build`'s `clone_all.sh` for cloning the whole workspace), the `NimoOS-Common` local `replace` dependency and why siblings must be kept up to date, cross-repository feature PRs (including why the `NimoOS-MessageBus` checkout has to be present as a sibling — several other services' `go generate` reads its hand-authored, git-tracked `api/message_bus/openapi.yaml` directly; there's no ordering requirement to run its own generate first), build prerequisites (CGO matrix, pinned Go/echo versions, **never run `go mod tidy`**), the `NimoOS-UI` pnpm commands, the DCO sign-off requirement and rationale, PR conventions (squash merge, English, test evidence), and pointers to `SECURITY.md`/`ROADMAP.md` for the known multi-user isolation gap.
- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — rewritten from scratch against the official Contributor Covenant v2.1 text (the previous file in this repo was the CasaOS-era v2.0 text); enforcement contact is `nimonas@yeaher.com`.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` and `feature_request.yml` — GitHub issue forms, replacing the superseded CasaOS-era freeform `bug_report.md`/`feature_request.md` templates (removed, so the chooser doesn't show duplicate bug-report options). The bug report form includes a component dropdown (Files/Photos/Search/AI/AppStore/Terminal/UI/Gateway/Other) that nudges cross-repo reports to their own repository, and reminds reporters to grab logs with `sudo journalctl -u <service> -f`. `alpha_bug_report.yml` is kept as-is (distinct alpha-testing purpose). The existing `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` already pointed at Discussions and Discord with `blank_issues_enabled: false`, so it wasn't touched.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — change description, test-evidence checklist, DCO sign-off reminder, and an explicit "did not run `go mod tidy`" checkbox.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — added a `[1.9.4-alpha1]` entry as the starting point for NimoOS as its own project (the file's existing history is CasaOS-era and stops at `0.4.3`; left untouched). The entry summarizes currently shipped capability (AI agent, RAG search, knowledge layer, web terminal, snapshots/Time Machine, RAID, photo library, app store compatibility) consistent with `ROADMAP.md`, and explicitly calls out the multi-user isolation gap so it doesn't contradict `SECURITY.md`.

Aside from the `.md` template removals noted above, this doesn't touch any other existing file in the repository.

## Follow-up (not done here, by design)

- The DCO GitHub App (the bot that blocks unsigned-off PRs) is an org-level install and needs an org admin to add it to this repository — the PR checklist mentions sign-off, but nothing currently *enforces* it. Whoever has org admin should install <https://github.com/apps/dco> and enable it for `NimoOS`.
- Linking the other 16+ NimoOS repositories' READMEs back to this repo's `CONTRIBUTING.md`/`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` is deliberately out of scope here — that's a separate pass across each repo.

## Test plan

- [x] `git diff --stat` against `main` touches only the files listed above (5 added/modified, 2 removed)
- [x] All added/modified content scanned for CJK characters (`grep -P '[\p{Han}]'`) — none found
- [x] The remaining issue-template YAML files (`bug_report.yml`, `feature_request.yml`, `alpha_bug_report.yml`, and the untouched `config.yml`) parse cleanly with `yaml.safe_load`
- [x] The `NimoOS-MessageBus` generate-order claim was independently verified against the actual `go:generate` directives in this repo and other service repos (they read MessageBus's committed OpenAPI spec directly, not generated output) before writing the corrected text

### Issue for this PR

Closes #39902

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

Runtime MCP mutations publish a tool-change event, but the asynchronous subscriber can update the tool registry after the HTTP response returns. This exposes the existing location-scoped reconciliation effect and awaits it after add, remove, connect, and disconnect mutations. Because event-driven and explicit reconciliation share the same semaphore, the endpoint waits for any in-flight refresh and then reads the current MCP catalog before returning. Other event publishers remain asynchronous.

author: epetrowork-oss
body:
Lands all 7 hydration-nutrition diagrams and sources the strand. **The first fully clean delivery since batch 15** — nothing held, nothing reconciled. Coverage goes to **128/139** (154/165 image slots).

## Images (7/7)

Correct filenames, correct dimensions across three aspect ratios, 30–40 KB throughout, true alpha on `hyponatremia-vs-dehydration`, no slivers.

**All three flagged reversals came back correct, including the one that was a genuine safety issue rather than an accuracy one:**

- **`hyponatremia-vs-dehydration`** carries the required banner — *"More water makes this WORSE, not better"* — and nothing in that panel shows or implies drinking more water. The two panels read as **different problems**, not mild-vs-severe versions of one. This was the batch's real risk: an image implying "drink more" for confusion plus a worsening headache after hours of plain water would have taught something harmful.
- **`fuel-crossover-graph`** has fat oxidation starting high and falling, carbohydrate starting low and rising, crossing at a marked crossover point — and the easy-to-miss part, **neither line reaches zero**, so fat is never shown as fully switched off.
- **`urine-color-chart`** puts the checkmark at the pale end and the warning at the dark end, as an abstract gradient bar with no realistic imagery.

`fueling-timeline` uses the exact windows (3–4 hours / 1–2 hours / 30–60 minutes after) in left-to-right order around a practice icon.

**The no-branding rule held.** The lesson names Gatorade, Red Bull, and Monster in its *text*, so the brief required generic containers — putting a red X over a recognisable can would depict a real product as harmful. The delivery uses a plain "WATER" bottle, an unlabelled orange sports drink, and a generic dark "ENERGY DRINK" can, with no logos or recognisable trade dress anywhere including the granola bar and duffel.

## Sources — scoped by content, not by the earmark

`docs/HANDOFF.md` had two NATA statements earmarked for this strand. Checking them against the units showed they don't both apply everywhere:

| Source | Bands | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Fluid Replacement for the Physically Active** (2017;52(9):877–895, `10.4085/1062-6050-52.9.02`) | all three | backs the urine-colour check, the >2% body-weight-loss threshold, the pre/post weigh-in sweat-rate protocol, and hyponatremia |
| **Safe Weight Loss and Maintenance Practices in Sport and Exercise** (2011;46(3):322–336) | **11-12 only** | the one band with a "Body composition, weight-class sports, and knowing when to refer" section and RED-S content |

Attaching the second statement to the 7-8 and 9-10 units would have pointed a weight-practices source at lessons that never discuss making weight. It's cited without a URL because the earmark carried no DOI. Both were originally supplied by the repo owner, so unlike the warmup strand there's no provenance gap.

## Gates

- `npm run validate:content` — 54 files, 0 errors
- `npm run build` — clean
- Playwright against `npm run preview`: all 7 diagrams render at correct natural dimensions, 0 placeholders, and both sources confirmed rendering in the Sources panel — including the un-linked 2011 entry, checked by expanding the `<details>` element rather than counting anchors

## Remaining

Two strands after this: **skin-conditions (6)** and **sports-psychology (5)**, both carrying safety-sensitive content flags whose framing will be written into their briefs — contagious-condition scope (recognize / cover / refer, never diagnose or treat), and recognize/support/refer only with no depiction of self-harm or crisis imagery.

author: pfbyjy
body:
## What this does
Puts the whole drawer state in the URL, down to line level. Copying the URL reproduces the exact view: layout, open tab, open files in both panes, and highlighted lines.

Stacked on #1035 (#1026 → #1034 → #1035 below it).

## URL params
- `tab=` — trial pane tab (written for every tab, including summary)
- `file=` / `lines=L12-L20` — trial pane file and line range
- `taskFile=` / `taskLines=` — task-definition pane file and line range
- `drawer=task`, `version=` — task page drawer and version

## Changes
- The file panels report which file is open, so `?file=` / `?taskFile=` stay current while browsing. Switching files drops the old line range.
- The task page (`/tasks/[task_id]`) drawer is now in the URL too. Before, it wasn't addressable at all.
- Drawer panes keep stable identities, so switching layout no longer remounts the trial pane. One segmented control (task / split / trial) replaces the old hide/show buttons.
- Deep links that use a short file name (like `instruction.md`) match the real path without dropping the line range.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01ATstGyewJhEw45PQhXdPLc

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large client-side URL synchronization surface with hydration race guards; mistakes could drop or corrupt share links but changes stay in frontend navigation state, not auth or data APIs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Makes task and experiment drawer views **shareable via the URL**: open trial/task drawers, trial tab (`tab=`), trial file/lines (`file=` / `lines=`), and task-definition pane file/lines (`taskFile=` / `taskLines=`). Copying the link should reproduce layout, tabs, files, and highlighted line ranges.
> 
> On the **task detail page**, the drawer is now hydrated from and synced back to the query string (including unresolved `?trial=` across versions and guards so `replaceState` does not strip params before hydration commits). **Experiment detail** gains the same independent task-pane addressing and clears it when switching tasks or closing the drawer.
> 
> **`TaskFilesPanel`** bubbles selected file and line range to parents for URL sync, skips default file auto-select when a deep-linked path is pending, and passes selection into **`FileRenderer`**. **`TrialDetailPanel`** reads/writes the live `window.location` search (not `useSearchParams`) and drops line anchors when the file or trial changes. New **`sameFilePath`** treats short deep-link paths and canonical tree paths as the same file so line ranges are not cleared on resolve.
> 
> **`UnifiedDrawerWrapper`** replaces paired hide/show toggles with a **task / split / trial** segmented control and keeps resizable panes mounted with stable keys so toggling layout no longer resets trial tab, file, or scroll position.
>

author: tayfunates10
body:
## 1. Harita kapsayıcıdan taşıyordu

Gerçek cihaz ekran görüntülerinde görüldü: harita iki yandan da kesiliyordu.

Görsel bilerek büyütülüyordu — masaüstünde `width: 112%` + `translateX(-2%)`, 720 px altında ayrıca `.coverage-map { width: 118%; margin-left: -9% }`. Amaç tam genişlik etkisiydi ama sonuç **Türkiye'nin batı ucunu — yani Edremit'in bulunduğu yeri — ve doğu ucunu kırpmaktı**. Taşmayı `body { overflow-x: hidden }` yuttuğu için sayfa kaymıyor, kara parçası görünmez oluyordu.

Her iki kural da kaldırıldı. 12 genişlikte ölçüldü (320 → 2560 px): görselin viewport dışına taşan piksel **0**, kapsayıcı dışına taşan **0**, yatay kaydırma yok.

## 2. Edremit işareti yanlış konumdaydı

Halka, Edremit'in **216 px doğusunda ve 50 px güneyinde** duruyordu — kabaca Afyon/Kütahya hizası.

Konum ölçülerek bulundu: Türkiye anakarasının uç koordinatları (26,0°–44,8° boylam · 35,8°–42,1° enlem) taban görselin kara sınırına oturtuldu; Edremit (27,024°D · 39,596°K) görselin **%8,0 solunda, %42,3 üstünde** çıkıyor.

İşaret görselin içine gömülü olduğu için CSS ile taşınamıyordu. `tools/harita.py` eklendi:

- `tools/harita-taban.webp` — halka ve güzergâhlar silinmiş taban (kara parçası + şehir noktaları). Silme maskesi genişletilerek yapıldı; ilk denemede kenar yumuşatma pikselleri kalıp **hayalet halka** bırakmıştı.
- Betik her çalıştığında işareti ve üç kesikli güzergâhı doğru konumdan yeniden çizer, 1300 ve 900 px WebP üretir. Konum değişirse görsel elle rötuşlanmaz — koordinat değiştirilip betik yeniden çalıştırılır.

Edremit kıyıda olduğu için işaretin bir kısmı denize (sarı zemine) taşıyor; sarı halka orada kaybolurdu. Altına kara rengiyle aynı koyu disk konuldu — karada görünmez, denizin üstünde rozet gibi okunur.

HTML'deki "EDREMİT" etiketi de yeni halkaya taşındı (`top: 55%`, `left: 8%`). Halka sol kenara yakın olduğu için etiket **ortalanmıyor**; ortalansaydı görselin sol kenarından taşardı. Sol kenarı halkanın merkezine oturur, sağa doğru uzar — haritacılıkta alışılmış yerleşim.

## 3. Boş galeri kaynak klasöründe iş akışını düşürme

PR #11 ile eklenen "Galeri çerçevesi" iş akışı ilk çalışmasında kırmızıya düştü ([run 30690939321](https://github.com/tayfunates10/okur-nakliyat/actions/runs/30690939321)): `galeri-kaynak/` klasörü aynı PR'da oluşturuldu, içinde henüz fotoğraf yok, betik `1` döndürüyordu.

Boş kaynak klasörü hata değil — normal bir başlangıç durumu. Artık `0` dönüyor. Gerçek hata sayılan iki durum kaldı: klasörün kendisi yoksa ve komut satırında adı verilen dosya bulunamıyorsa `1`.

## Doğrulama

- 19 senaryoda `scrollWidth == clientWidth`.
- **Kapsayıcı dışına taşan öğe 0** — önceki turda 320–667 px'te 1'di (harita).
- Gutter simetrisi 0,0 px, 44 px altı dokunma hedefi 0, görsel oran bozulması 0.
- Harita 390 / 980 / 1440 px'te tek tek incelendi: batı ve doğu uçları tam görünür, işaret Ege kıyısında.

`?v=15` → `?v=16`.

author: ryo3191007-bit
body:
### Motivation

- 現行の `user_fishing_spot_detail_values` は地点×項目の最新スナップショットのみを保持しており、調査単位の履歴を残せないため、履歴を追加して過去の検査記録を蓄積できるようにする必要があった。 
- 履歴追加と現在値の更新は原子的に行う必要があり、owner-scoped な RLS と認証付き RPC を用いて安全に実装する方針とした。 
- 既存データ互換性を保ちつつ既存スナップショットを削除・変更せずに履歴へ backfill することで既存ユーザーのデータを失わないようにする。

### Description

- 新規 forward-only migration `supabase/migrations/20260801090000_issue_395_field_report_history.sql` を追加し、親テーブル `user_fishing_spot_field_reports` と子テーブル `user_fishing_spot_field_report_values`、インデックス、RLS ポリシー、制約、`snapshot_backfill` を含む backfill 処理を実装した。 
- 認証済みのみ実行できる `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC `save_my_user_fishing_spot_field_report` を追加し、空配列拒否、重複 `item_key` 拒否、所有者不一致拒否、履歴追加と `user_fishing_spot_detail_values` への upsert を同一トランザクションで実行するようにした。 
- 既存の `create_my_user_fishing_spot_with_details` を改定して初期詳細を履歴（`initial_details`）として保存する流れを追加し、既存の署名・互換性を保ったまま履歴化を行うようにした。
