author: lancekrogers
body:
## Why

`camp machine` listed the fleet but had no way into it. The only pointer to `camp switch <id>:<campaign>` lived in the `?` overlay, so an operator who opened the screen looking for a way onto a machine found the fleet, the socket state, a connection tester, and no door.

## What

`enter` on a machine row opens a campaign picker for that machine and hops there.

```
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Hop to buildbox                                                     │
│  From the last snapshot; press r to ask the machine now.             │
│                                                                      │
│  › notes                                                             │
│    obey-campaign                                                     │
│    platform                                                          │
│                                                                      │
│  j/k move · enter hop · r refresh · esc cancel                       │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

**Nothing about the hop is new.** The screen writes `ssh-hop:<machine>:<campaign>` to `--path-output` and the shell wrapper turns that into `camp switch <sel> --shell-connect` — byte-for-byte the path `camp list`'s picker already takes. The far machine's own registry still resolves the root; no remote resolution is duplicated here.

Campaign names come from the completion snapshot first, which is what makes the picker open without dialing. `r` refreshes live; a cold cache pays for one fetch, and that fetch warms the cache so the next open is instant.

## Decisions worth reviewing

**`enter` was bound to test-connection.** It now hops; `t` keeps the tester. This is the one user-visible regression in the set — anyone with muscle memory on `enter`-to-test gets a campaign picker instead. `enter` is the universal "go there" and the footer already led with `t test connection`, so this seemed the right way round, but it is a live rebinding and worth a second opinion.

**Hopping needs the wrapper, and says so when it is missing.** No subprocess can replace the shell that launched it. Without `--path-output` the key reports `hop needs shell integration: run eval "$(camp shell-init <shell>)"` rather than appearing to work — the same shape `camp list` uses for the same reason.

**Refusals happen before the list opens, not after a choice.** `local` (this computer) and password-auth machines are rejected at `enter`, so no picker ever leads nowhere.

**Unreachable ≠ empty.** A failed fetch shows the error and points at `camp machine diagnose <id>`. An empty list would read as "this machine has no campaigns", which is a different and wrong claim.

## Verification

Green tests do not verify a TUI, so this was driven in a real pty (`pyte`) against a fixture `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, reading the rendered screen:

- fleet screen renders, footer reads `enter hop · t test connection · …`
- `enter` on `local` → `✗ local is this computer; use 'camp list' to open a campaign here`
- `enter` on `buildbox` → picker above, from the snapshot, no ssh dialed
- `down down` + `enter` → `--path-output` file contains exactly `ssh-hop:buildbox:platform`
- without `--path-output` → `✗ hop needs shell integration: run eval "$(camp shell-init <shell>)"`

Wrapper arms driven end-to-end in a pty with a stub `camp` on PATH:

| invocation | zsh | bash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `camp machine` | hops via switch | hops via switch |
| `camp machine list` | passthrough | passthrough |
| `camp machine add devbox --host x` | passthrough | passthrough |
| `camp machine diagnose devbox` | passthrough | passthrough |
| `camp machine --help` | passthrough | passthrough |

`just gate`: 4080 dev + 4035 stable tests pass, lint clean. `just docs` regenerated only the two machine reference files.

## Gaps

- **fish is asserted but not executed.** fish is not installed on this machine, so its arm is covered by the generator test and shape-matched against the existing `list` arm, not run. `TestGenerateFish_ValidSyntax` skips for the same reason and will cover it on a box that has fish.
- **No integration test performs a real hop.** The seam is `camp switch`, which is already covered; this PR tests up to the payload and the wrapper's handling of it.

## Note for reviewers

The first version of the wrapper test file was named `machine_arm_test.go`, which Go silently excluded from the package — `_arm` reads as a `GOARCH=arm` build constraint. It reported `ok` with zero tests running. Renamed to `machine_wrapper_test.go`. Worth knowing generally: a `_test.go` file whose name ends in `_<goarch>` or `_<goos>` disappears without warning.

author: alexbelgium
body:
## Problem

The updater writes the raw upstream tag into each add-on's `config.yaml` `version:`. Home Assistant orders add-on versions with [`awesomeversion`](https://github.com/ludeeus/awesomeversion), and the update entity (`homeassistant/components/update/__init__.py`) returns `STATE_OFF` whenever the two versions **can** be compared and the new one is not strictly newer. Verified against `awesomeversion==25.8.0`, the version the Supervisor pins:

| current | new upstream tag | result |
|---|---|---|
| `1.2.3` | `1.2.3-2` | semver pre-release → **older**, update hidden |
| `1.2.3` | `1.2.3+4` | build metadata ignored → **equal**, update hidden |
| `1.2.3-2026-07-25` | `1.2.3-2026-08-01` | not newer, update hidden (this is what `dockerhub_by_date` produces) |
| `version-bf9e0b4f`, `ubuntu-2026-06-01`, `v26.2-ls255`, `4.16-r0-ls93` | — | `AwesomeVersionStrategy.UNKNOWN`, no ordering at all |

About 15 add-ons in the repo currently carry a version Home Assistant cannot order.

## Fix

A new helper, `addons_updater/rootfs/usr/bin/ha_version.py`, derives the version to publish from the upstream tag using the same library Home Assistant uses:

1. a tag that Home Assistant can order and that is newer is used unchanged (the usual case, nothing changes);
2. `1.2.3-4` and `1.2.3+4` become `1.2.3.4`, matching the `X.Y.Z.N` convention in `CLAUDE.md`;
3. for a tag it cannot order, the release number inside the tag is used (`v26.3-ls256` → `26.3`);
4. else the add-on number moves on (`1.37` → `1.38`, `26.3` → `26.3.1`);
5. else the date is used (`2026.08.01`, then `2026.08.01.1` for a second update the same day).

Every returned version is checked to be recognisable by `awesomeversion` and never older or equal to what is installed.

`updater.json` keeps the **raw** upstream tag, so the next run still compares upstream with upstream and a single upstream release never triggers two add-on updates. The raw tag also stays in the `Dockerfile`/`build.*` files and is named in the changelog entry and the commit message.

Existing add-ons migrate on their next upstream bump; nothing is rewritten in bulk here.

## Also in this change

- the raw tag is escaped before being used in `sed`, so dots no longer match any character and `&` or `/` in a tag can no longer corrupt a `Dockerfile`;
- `config.json`/`config.yaml` are removed from the raw-tag replacement loop (no add-on references its upstream tag there) and their `version` field is written explicitly, anchored on `^version:`;
- if the helper fails, the config version cannot be read, or the write does not land, the add-on is skipped (and reverted) instead of committing a version Home Assistant would not offer;
- `updater.json` is rewritten from a validated `jq` result instead of `jq | sponge`, which truncates the file when `jq` fails;
- the `+`→`-` comparison hack is gone: the upstream comparison is now exact.

## Testing

- `python3 /usr/bin/ha_version.py --selftest` — 34 cases covering the histories of the add-ons in this repo (LinuxServer tags, nightlies, date tags, `dockerhub_by_date`, plain semver, scheme switches, same-day updates, future-dated versions); all pass.
- The `99-run.sh` helpers (`config_version`, `sed_pattern`, `sed_replacement`) and the whole update block were replayed on fake add-on folders for five upstream scenarios; `config.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, `updater.json` and `CHANGELOG.md` all end up as expected.
- `shellcheck -x`, `hadolint`, `flake8` clean.

The plan and the implementation were also reviewed by GPT-5.6-Codex; its findings on the acceptance rule, the failure policy, the `sed` escaping and the `jq | sponge` truncation are folded in.

author: yadavbalbir
body:
## Summary

The super admin dashboard was a flat grid of numbers. This PR turns it into an interactive, charted UI (using **recharts**, themed to the indigo brand) across the **Dashboard**, **Tenants**, and **Support Inbox** pages.

## What changed

### Dashboard (`pages/Dashboard.jsx`)
- **KPI strip** — Total Tenants, Users, Courses, Active (with context sub-labels).
- **Tenant Status donut** (Active / Inactive / Suspended).
- **User Composition donut** (Students / Faculty / Admins).
- **Plan Distribution bar** (Trial / Starter / Growth / Enterprise).
- **Tenant Growth area chart** — cumulative tenants over the last 6 months, derived client-side from `created_at`.
- **Top Tenants by Students** — horizontal ranking.
- Kept **Needs Attention** and **Recent Tenants**, restyled.

### Tenants (`pages/Tenants.jsx`)
- Summary snapshot above the table — loaded from a **full unfiltered fetch** so the search box doesn't move the charts.
- Mini stats (Total Tenants, Total Students, Total Courses, Avg Students/Tenant) + Status donut, Plan bar, Top-by-Students chart.

### Support Inbox (`pages/Support.jsx`)
- Mini stats (Total Leads, Demo Requests, Job Applications, Awaiting Response).
- **Leads by Type** and **Leads by Status** donuts.

### Shared
- New reusable chart primitives in `components/charts.jsx`: `ChartCard`, `MiniStat`, `DonutChart`, `BarChartCompact`, `HBarChart`, `GrowthAreaChart`.

### Backend (`core/superadmin_views.py`)
- `LeadListView` now returns `counts.by_status` (`new` / `contacted` / `closed`) to power the Support status donut. **Backward-compatible** — the frontend falls back gracefully if absent; the donut becomes fully accurate once the backend is deployed.

## Data sources
All charts read from existing endpoints (`/superadmin/stats/`, `/superadmin/tenants/`, `/superadmin/leads/`) plus the small additive `by_status` field. No schema/migration changes.

## Testing
- `npm run build` (superadmin-frontend) passes.
- `manage.py check` passes; `superadmin_views.py` compiles clean.
- Previewed locally against the live API.

## Deploy note
The frontend auto-deploys via Netlify. The `by_status` field needs the **backend redeployed** for the Support status donut to be exact (it shows New accurately and 0s for contacted/closed until then).

## Summary by Sourcery

Improve the top tab manager UI behavior and robustness, align configuration defaults and naming, and document and enforce tab visibility/order behavior and editor formatting rules.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix misaligned custom settings left column and dynamically align the right-column tab manager title with the first left-column control.

- Ensure tab visibility/order fallback behavior consistently chooses the first visible functional tab, with a robust fallback to "other" when needed.
- Correct tab manager hit-testing to include the new highlight layer so clicks and drags behave as expected.
- Fix initial custom category rendering so tab rows are not all highlighted when the category is first shown.

Enhancements:
- Refactor tab ordering and fallback selection into shared helpers to remove duplicate logic and make future tab additions safer.
- Rename the top-tab layout method to `LayoutTopTabs` for clearer intent and future maintainability.
- Improve the tab manager eye icon behavior by using a single reliable MDL2 glyph and color to distinguish visible vs hidden states.
- Clarify the "other" tab label by changing the suffix text from "fixed" to "cannot be hidden".

author: diegoglozano
body:
Three separate things were wrong.

**build-setup.yml failed on every push.** It is a list of steps that dist
injects into the generated release workflow, not a workflow itself, but it
lived in .github/workflows/ — where GitHub parses every .yml as a workflow.
It failed that parse each time, hanging a red X on main with zero jobs. Move
it to .github/build-setup.yml and reach it with `../` from
github-build-setup, which is resolved relative to .github/workflows/.
Verified with `dist generate --check`: the generated release.yml is
unchanged, and a probe step added to the relocated file does show up in it,
so dist is genuinely reading the new path.

**The v0.2.0 release failed.** The tag was pushed while every crate still
read 0.1.0, so dist's plan job refused the whole run: "This workspace doesn't
have anything for dist to Release ... --tag=v0.1.0 will Announce: skein".
Bump the `skein` package to 0.2.0; `dist plan --tag=v0.2.0` now succeeds.
The existing v0.2.0 tag points at the commit before this one and has to be
re-pointed for the release to go through.

**The web job took 4m49s of a 4m52s CI run**, and 3m49s of that was the
Playwright suite:

- Stop running the M0 cosmos.gl spike. It is a measurement, not a check; D7
  already decided on its evidence, nothing in the app imports cosmos.gl any
  more, and under CI's SwiftShader its numbers may not be cited for anything
  (D3/D5). It cost ~53s per run to produce a file no one may use. It is now
  opt-in via `npm run spike -w tests`, which also drops the dev server from
  the default webServer list. The spike-metrics artifact goes with it — it
  was uploading the 25 committed files in bench/results/ every run.
- Run the rest in parallel. Every test drives its own page from `goto('/')`
  and OPFS is per-context, so there was no shared state behind `workers: 1` —
  only the spike's timing, which is now serialised on its own.

Fixing the parallelism exposed a latent flake, so fix its cause too: the app
declared no icon, so Chromium fell back to `GET /favicon.ico` and the 404
landed in the console, tripping explore.spec's zero-console-error assertion
whenever a run was slow enough for the lazy fetch to arrive mid-test. It
failed 3/3 parallel runs before and 14/14 tests pass after. index.html now
carries an inline data: SVG icon, which both CSP copies already permit under
`img-src 'self' data:` and which keeps §7 intact — no request at all.

Measured on a 4-core container, spike excluded from both: 226s serial vs
194s at two workers. CI should see rather more, since the ~53s spike comes
off the top there as well.

body:
💡 What: Replaced the O(N*M) nested `Array.prototype.filter()` operation inside the `generateLiveStatus` interval loop with a precomputed O(1) Map (`SCHEDULES_BY_TRAIN`).

🎯 Why: The original implementation iterated over all schedules for *every* train on every tick to find the relevant route stops. By caching this globally at the module level, we remove an extremely expensive loop from a function that runs on an interval to compute live locations.

📊 Impact: Converts an O(N * M) lookup (where N is the number of trains, and M is the total number of scheduled stops) into an O(N) pass with an O(1) inner map fetch.

🔬 Measurement: Check the CPU usage profile for the main thread when navigating to the Train Status page; the 1-minute interval `generateLiveStatus` recalculation overhead will be drastically reduced.

<details>
<summary>konflux-ci/build-pipeline-tasks (quay.io/konflux-ci/tekton-catalog/task-buildah)</summary>

### [`v0.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/konflux-ci/build-pipeline-tasks/blob/HEAD/task/buildah/CHANGELOG.md#0110)

##### Changed

- When scanning the built image with Syft, scans the image filesystem as
  a directory instead of scanning the the image as an OCI archive. This improves
  the scanning time, disk usage and may improve memory usage. More details in
  [konflux-build-cli/docs/design/syft-image-scanning.md].
- The remote variants of this task now push the built image to the registry directly
  from the build VM instead of rsyncing the image back to the cluster first.
  For large images, this significantly reduces the time spent on network transfers.

##### Removed

- BREAKING: Removed the `sbom-syft-generate` step, SBOM generation now happens
  in the `build` step.
- BREAKING: Removed the `push` step, the push now happens in the `build` step.
- If you have step overrides configured for either of the two removed steps,
  the pipeline will fail with `invalid StepOverride`. See the migration guidance below.

##### Migration guidance

Buildah v0.11.0 comes with a migration script that will attempt to automatically
fix the step overrides in your PipelineRuns. In most cases, no manual action will
be needed. But there are cases that the script cannot handle:

1. Your PipelineRun references an external Pipeline. In this case, the migration
   script will never get a chance to run on the PipelineRun.
2. Your PipelineRun is multi-platform, SBOM generation needs more resources
   than the build itself and the remote VMs do not have sufficient resources.

If the migration script doesn't solve the problem, please follow the procedure below.

##### Manual procedure

If you have `sbom-syft-generate` or `push` step overrides in the `.spec.taskRunSpecs`
section in your PipelineRun, please remove them. In most cases, this should be all.

However, if you were previously requesting more resources for SBOM generation
than for the build step itself, there is a chance that the build will fail.
In this case, move the relevant overrides to the build step. The same technically
applies for the push step, but it's highly unlikely that pushing would require
more resources than the build.

For example:

```diff
 spec:
   taskRunSpecs:
     - pipelineTaskName: build-container
       stepSpecs:
-        - name: sbom-syft-generate
+        - name: build
           computeResources:
             requests:
               memory: 16Gi
             limits:
               memory: 16Gi
```

This will work for build steps that run in-cluster - single-platform builds
and typically also the amd64 builds in a multi-platform build setup.

For build steps that run on remote VMs, the overrides have no effect. In case
the build fails, please switch to a larger VM flavo

author: manugh
body:
## What changed

- Add hysteresis and a starvation hold to automatic playback-profile selection.
- Tune HLS buffering and retry behavior for constrained links.
- Restart reaped sessions safely and retry bounded `/intents` lease conflicts.
- Detect failed heartbeat reachability and recover through a bounded network watchdog.
- Stabilize mobile network probing and preserve the recovery budget across restarts.

## Why

Moving mobile links can briefly disappear without `navigator.onLine` changing. The old flow repeatedly re-probed, selected an aggressive profile, started new transcodes, and could leave playback stranded after the link returned.

## Validation

- `npm --prefix apps/webui run type-check`
- Targeted player and recovery tests (99 tests passed)
- Complete Web UI suite (132 files, 672 tests passed)

author: gasizdat
body:
Three improvements to the `refactor-sweep` skill, one commit each.

Supersedes #224 (closed - it proposed the single-sentence version of rule 2; GitHub closing keywords do not close PRs, hence no `Closes` here).

## 1. Bundle categories into one PR per boundary

The skill forced **one consistency-issue category per branch and per PR**. #222 and #225 are the *same* category — #225 exists only because #222's survey missed sites — yet the rule required two separate PRs.

Categories now bundle by default: they are behaviour-preserving and mechanical, so several in one PR stays reviewable.

**Unchanged:** the production/test boundary split. A production regression and a test regression must never be able to land in the same change, and that rationale is independent of the category axis.

**Strengthened, not relaxed:** commit granularity. With several categories in one PR, the commit list is what keeps review tractable, so each category's commits must stay contiguous.

**Scope discipline becomes the pressure valve:** a category whose canonical pattern is a judgment call (a naming scheme) still gets its own PR, so it can be rejected without blocking the mechanical ones. The cost of bundling is that squash merge makes a sweep a single revert unit on `master` — acceptable for mechanical categories, which is exactly why contestable ones are held back.

## 2. Enumerate sites with the code model, not grep

The investigation stage said to survey with Grep/Glob and file "the full list of non-conforming sites". Text search cannot do that job. A category is a *shape* — a return type, a member kind, a mutation — and grep matches tokens, so every spelling it did not anticipate is a silent miss.

The receipt is in this repo: **#222's grep survey found 3 of the 16 real sites**, missing tuple-embedded returns, `Task<(...)>`-wrapped returns, and a local function. #225 exists only to mop up the 13.

**The rule:** grep may *propose* a category; only the code model may *enumerate* its sites. Grep/Glob stays legal for open-ended discovery of which inconsistencies exist, where a miss just waits for the next sweep. Not a blanket ban.

Also added: a completeness assertion (a semantic query over a compilation with unresolved references returns *fewer* sites and looks exactly like a clean run — the same failure as the grep it replaced), the `GT4.Core.Utils` multi-target double-count trap, and a post-pass re-run of the query as the regression check that would have prevented #225.

### Verified by running it

A syntax-model walk over the pre-refactor (`origin/master`) versions of the three files enumerates **all three sites #225 lists, at the exact line numbers the issue records**:

```
GedcomComparer.cs:530  method BuildBuckets
    -> List<(List<Individual> Left, List<Individual> Right)>
GedcomComparer.cs:534  local function Bucket
    -> (List<Individual> Left, List<Individual> Right)
GedcomExporter.cs:442  method PartitionResidue
    -> (Dictionary<string, GedcomNode> Owned, List<GedcomNode> Other)
TreeWalker.cs:45       method WalkAsync
    -> Task<(IReadOnlyList<TreeNode> Nodes, IReadOnlyList<TreeIssue> Issues)>
```

A plausible grep pattern over the same three files finds **one** of those four — only the plain `IReadOnlyList<GedcomNode>` return on `GedcomExporter.Residual`. The 3-of-16 failure, reproduced live.

Running it also corrected two things in the draft: the completeness assertion now applies only to semantic-model queries (the syntax-only walk was complete with no compilation at all), and the walk is documented as deliberately over-enumerating, so a future agent does not mistake extra hits for a broken query.

## 3. Comment hygiene as a category, and the trivia trap

Comment hygiene is now listed as a legitimate consistency category.

Enumerating it has a trap worth recording: **comments are trivia, not nodes.** A `DescendantNodes()` walk finds none of them and reports a clean zero rather than failing — so an agent sweeping comments that way concludes the codebase has none. Measured on `Core/`: **0 comments via `DescendantNodes()` across 174 files, 604 via `DescendantTrivia()`** (468 `SingleLineCommentTrivia`, 136 `SingleLineDocumentationCommentTrivia`).

The classification rules for what survives a comment sweep (history / narration / behavioural claim / contract / durable rationale — only the last two survive) live in `surgical-change`, where the per-edit rules belong. This skill only points at them. `surgical-change` is git-excluded in this repo, so that half is not part of this PR.

## Notes

- Documentation only — no product source touched, so no build or test run.
- Under these rules, **#222 + #225 are one PR, not two** - that is now #223, which carries all six conversions and closes both.

author: tosinfamzy
body:
## Context

Follow-up to the driven-pass finding: `POST /games/:id/start-with-teams` is **dead and broken**.

**Broken:** it auto-forms teams via `TeamFormationService.createTeamsForGame` then sets the game `IN_PROGRESS`, but the formed teams are persisted with `gameId = NULL`. The score service requires the team to be in the game's own `teams` relation, so every score submit against a start-with-teams game fails with `Team is not part of this game`. It could never be scored.

**Dead:** confirmed no caller anywhere —
- Frontend: zero references (it uses `POST /games/:id/start` with pre-made team ids).
- Backend: `startGameWithTeams` was invoked only by its own controller route.
- Only other trace was the auto-generated `openapi.json` snapshot.

Its capability (auto-form teams + start in one call) is fully covered by the real frontend flow: `create-teams` → `/start` with team ids, which links teams to the game (`team.game`) and scores correctly. That path stays and is well-tested (happy-path e2e).

## Change

- Remove the `@Post(':id/start-with-teams')` controller route.
- Remove `startGameWithTeams` from `game.service.ts`.
- Delete `StartGameWithTeamsDto` and the now-orphaned imports (`StartGameWithTeamsDto`, `CreateTeamsDto`).
- Drop the stale path + schema from `docs/api/openapi.json`.
- `createTeamsForGame` (team service) is untouched — the team controller's `create-teams` endpoint still uses it.

## Verification

- `tsc` + eslint clean; full suite green (393 tests, 31 suites).
- **Driven live:** `start-with-teams` now returns `404 Cannot POST`; the canonical `POST /games/:id/start` still routes (hits auth as expected). No behavior change to the working scoring path.

body:
## What changed

### Labels and localization
- add a shared fallback that detects blank translations and EasyStore's untranslated-key response
- fix Buy Now, purchase-limit, search, filter, product-card, customer-order, and store-locator labels
- escape fallback output used in HTML attributes
- JSON-encode every Liquid translation embedded in JavaScript
- centralize safely encoded Flatpickr day and month labels
- localize quantity-limit reason text
- read quick-view errors from the correct translation object

### Runtime hardening
- cancel superseded collection-filter requests so stale responses cannot replace current results
- check collection-tab response status and restore the prior tab after failures
- guard optional EasyStore currency conversion and inserted DOM nodes
- scope featured-product IDs to the section instance
- make featured-product and quick-view variant callbacks null-safe

### Regression coverage
- prohibit the broken `t | default` translation pattern
- require JSON encoding for translations inside scripts
- enforce safe attribute fallback output
- enforce request cancellation and collection-tab recovery
- enforce section-scoped IDs and null-safe quick-view behavior

## Root causes

EasyStore returns missing translation keys as non-empty strings, so Liquid's standard `default` filter cannot detect them. The wider review also found translations interpolated directly into JavaScript, unsequenced asynchronous section requests, fixed IDs in repeatable sections, and unguarded optional platform data.

## User impact

Internal translation keys no longer appear in the storefront. Localized strings cannot break inline scripts, rapid filter changes cannot render stale products, failed collection tabs recover cleanly, and multiple featured-product sections no longer collide.

## Validation

- `python scripts/theme_ci.py check theme`
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — 35 tests passed
- `node --check` for every runtime and editor JavaScript asset
- runtime/editor asset parity check
- `git diff --check`
- theme-wide scan: zero raw Liquid translations inside JavaScript
- theme-wide scan: zero `t | default` translation fallbacks

### [`v0.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/konflux-ci/build-pipeline-tasks/blob/HEAD/task/buildah/CHANGELOG.md#0110)

##### Changed

- When scanning the built image with Syft, scans the image filesystem as
  a directory instead of scanning the the image as an OCI archive. This improves
  the scanning time, disk usage and may improve memory usage. More details in
  [konflux-build-cli/docs/design/syft-image-scanning.md].
- The remote variants of this task now push the built image to the registry directly
  from the build VM instead of rsyncing the image back to the cluster first.
  For large images, this significantly reduces the time spent on network transfers.

##### Removed

- BREAKING: Removed the `sbom-syft-generate` step, SBOM generation now happens
  in the `build` step.
- BREAKING: Removed the `push` step, the push now happens in the `build` step.
- If you have step overrides configured for either of the two removed steps,
  the pipeline will fail with `invalid StepOverride`. See the migration guidance below.

##### Migration guidance

Buildah v0.11.0 comes with a migration script that will attempt to automatically
fix the step overrides in your PipelineRuns. In most cases, no manual action will
be needed. But there are cases that the script cannot handle:

1. Your PipelineRun references an external Pipeline. In this case, the migration
   script will never get a chance to run on the PipelineRun.
2. Your PipelineRun is multi-platform, SBOM generation needs more resources
   than the build itself and the remote VMs do not have sufficient resources.

If the migration script doesn't solve the problem, please follow the procedure below.

##### Manual procedure

If you have `sbom-syft-generate` or `push` step overrides in the `.spec.taskRunSpecs`
section in your PipelineRun, please remove them. In most cases, this should be all.

However, if you were previously requesting more resources for SBOM generation
than for the build step itself, there is a chance that the build will fail.
In this case, move the relevant overrides to the build step. The same technically
applies for the push step, but it's highly unlikely that pushing would require
more resources than the build.

For example:

```diff
 spec:
   taskRunSpecs:
     - pipelineTaskName: build-container
       stepSpecs:
-        - name: sbom-syft-generate
+        - name: build
           computeResources:
             requests:
               memory: 16Gi
             limits:
               memory: 16Gi
```

This will work for build steps that run in-cluster - single-platform builds
and typically also the amd64 builds in a multi-platform build setup.

For build steps that run on remote VMs, the overrides have no effect. In case
the build fails, please switch to a larger VM flavo

author: enzo-wego
body:
## The bug this started from

The dashboard's Gateway Status panel showed `unavailable`. The panel was a red herring — it was already proxied through the worker, so removing it would have fixed nothing.

Real cause: the VPS worker env sets

```
HTTP_PROXY=http://172.18.0.1:8888
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,postgres      ← gateway host absent
```

Go's default transport honours `HTTP_PROXY`, so every request to `http://172.18.0.1:8750` was routed to the :8888 relay, which drops it. A fresh container on the same network reaches the gateway fine; the worker could not.

**This broke every LLM call, not just health** — generation, cheap judge, describe, and all embeddings. It was invisible only because `processing_paused = true`. Unpausing would have failed 100% of LLM work, each after burning the full 200s client timeout.

### Fix

Gateway HTTP clients now use a cloned transport with `Proxy = nil` — a same-host bridge address is never legitimately proxied, and inheriting ambient proxy env is exactly how this went unnoticed. Applied in `internal/llmgateway/client.go`, `internal/worker/gateway_handlers.go`, `internal/worker/usage_handlers.go`. Verified with a regression test run under a deliberately dead proxy (`HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9`) — all calls go direct.

Not fixed by widening timeouts or adding retries: it was a routing bug, not slowness.

## Embedding Dimensions is now read-only

It cannot move to llm-gateway — agent-mem has **two** widths and both are properties of its own schema (`observations.embedding` `vector(768)`, `graph.artifact_index.embedding` `halfvec(3072)`). One gateway setting cannot serve both.

But it should never have been a dropdown: the graph width is a Go constant while the flat one was editable, and changing it re-embeds nothing — it just makes every observation insert fail with `expected 768 dimensions, not 3072`, which reads like a schema fault. Now displayed as `768 (flat) / 3072 (graph)`.

## Editable gateway configuration

The gateway remains the owner; agent-mem is a client UI that stores nothing:

```
dashboard -> agent-mem GET/PUT /api/llm-gateway/config -> llm-gateway GET/PUT /config
              (pure proxy)                                 (owns + persists)
```

A copy in agent-mem would be a second source of truth that drifts, and Claude-Code-Remote shares this gateway.

Two guards worth calling out, both verified in the pushed code:
- **`GET /config` uses an allowlist**, not a denylist — 12 non-secret keys. `API_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` cannot leak by omission when a future secret is added.
- **`PUT` rejects `CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_S >= 200`**, preserving `gateway 180 < client 200 < lease 240`. A longer gateway timeout would let leases expire mid-call, and the janitor would hand the same job to a second worker — duplicate LLM calls, the amplification shape already paid for once.

Pairs with llm-gateway `cd832f3`.

## Verified

```
go build ./...        clean
go vet ./...          clean
go test ./...         21 packages pass
grep http.DefaultClient on gateway paths   -> nothing
npx tsc --noEmit      clean
```

4 failures in `internal/hooks` / `internal/skills` are pre-existing on `main`, filed P3.

## Follow-up (config, not code)

`NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,postgres,172.18.0.1` on the VPS as defence in depth — tracked as `agent-mem-oar`. The code fix alone is sufficient.

They will fail with `ERR_PNPM_SUDO_NOT_SUPPORTED` in pnpm v12. Read-only global commands (such as `pnpm bin --global`) are unaffected.

##### Patch Changes

- Fixed pnpm failing to start under asynchronous Node.js module loaders when no `.pnpmfile.mjs` exists [pnpm/pnpm#11701](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11701).

- Fixed `minimumReleaseAge` fallback for custom dist-tags so the selected version does not exceed the registry’s original tag target.

- Removing a dependency from `package.json` and reinstalling no longer re-resolves the dependency graph. The importer's entry is dropped from `pnpm-lock.yaml`, anything it made unreachable is pruned, and a catalog entry that loses its last referent is removed — all without registry access. Installs still fall back to a full resolution when a package that stays resolves a peer dependency through the removed one, since that would change the surviving package's entry rather than only prune.

- Changing a catalog entry to a different exact version no longer re-resolves the dependency graph. The package is replaced in `pnpm-lock.yaml` directly, reusing the same check the `pnpm.overrides` fast path applies: every locked dependency of the package must still satisfy the new version's manifest. Installs fall back to a full resolution when anything other than the catalog reaches the package — an importer that depends on it directly, or another package that depends on it — since the graph would then need both versions.

- Fixed a CI regression where `github:owner/repo` dependencies (and other shorthand Git specifiers) would fail to install with `Permission denied (publickey)` on CI runners that lack SSH keys. The Git resolver no longer records an SSH URL unless the user explicitly wrote one (e.g. `git+ssh://` or `git@host:...`):

  - The repository visibility probe (an HTTP HEAD request) now retries transient failures such as `429 Too Many Requests`, so host throttling of CI runners is no longer mistaken for a private repository.
  - For non-SSH specifiers, anonymous HTTPS `git ls-remote` access is now tried before SSH, so a public repository whose visibility probe fails still resolves to a portable HTTPS URL instead of an SSH URL that only works where SSH keys are configured.
  - When every probe fails, the resolver falls back to HTTPS for shorthand and HTTPS-style specifiers, and only guesses SSH when the user explicitly provided an SSH URL.
  - A repository that could not be confirmed public is no longer resolved to the host's anonymous archive URL (e.g. `codeload.github.com`, which would fail to download for a private repository); it stays a regular `git` resolution so installs can use ambient Git credentials such as credential helpers and tokens.

  Note that a private repository that is reachable both over authenticated HTTPS and over SSH now resolves to its HTTPS URL, where previous versions recorded the SSH URL.

  Fixes [pnpm/pnpm#13276](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13276).

  <!-- cspell:ignore publickey -->

- `ng build` and `nuxt build` now work under the global virtual store: pnpm's built-in compatibility extensions add the `tslib` dependency that `@angular/build` uses without declaring and the `unplugin` dependency that `@nuxt/vite-builder` v4 uses without declaring.

- Fixed `link:` dependencies under `enableGlobalVirtualStore` so linked children are materialized and slots remain isolated by their resolved link targets.

- An install that skips resolution because `pnpm-lock.yaml` is already up to date now reacts fully to packages the lockfile removed — for example after pulling a lockfile in which a dependency was deleted. The hoist layer is recomputed, so a package that became hoistable when a direct dependency was removed is hoisted, and `pendingBuilds` entries for removed packages are dropped instead of staying pending forever.

- The held-back-update warning printed by `pnpm update` no longer fires when `minimumReleaseAge` is the actual reason a newer version was not picked. The warning's baseline now applies the same maturity cutoff as the pick itself, so it no longer wrongly attributes the hold-back to "your manifests and already installed dependencies" or recommends an override that would defeat the age gate. See [#​13071](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13071).

- Checking whether `ignoredOptionalDependencies` is up to date no longer reorders the configured patterns. The check sorted them in place, which could move an `!` exclusion ahead of the pattern it excludes from and flip which optional dependencies were ignored.

- Changing `autoInstallPeers`, `dedupePeers`, `peersSuffixMaxLength`, `excludeLinksFromLockfile`, or `injectWorkspacePackages` no longer re-resolves the dependency graph when the lockfile proves the setting cannot affect it: no package or project declares a peer dependency for the peer settings, and no project depends on a directory or on another workspace project for the link and injection settings. The new setting is recorded in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the install proceeds from the existing resolution. Every other case still falls back to a full resolution.

- Adding, editing, or removing an entry in `patchedDependencies` no longer re-resolves the dependency graph. Resolution never reads a patch — it only records the patch file's hash against the package it matches — so the install now rewrites the affected entries in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and materializes the patched package from the store instead. Installs still fall back to a full resolution when the patched package is reachable as a peer dependency, and when the new configuration would leave a patch unused while `allowUnusedPatches` is off, so `ERR_PNPM_UNUSED_PATCH` is still reported.

- Resolving a private git repository no longer blocks on an interactive credential prompt: `git ls-remote` now fails fast with an authentication error when git has no credentials for the repository [#​13522](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13522).

- Lockfile verification now honors offline mode by using cached registry metadata instead of reaching the registry. When the required metadata is not available locally, verification reports the same `ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_META` condition used by offline resolution.

- POSIX shell shims now follow symbolic links before computing `basedir`, preventing execution failures when a shim is invoked via an external symlink on `PATH` [#​13405](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13405).

- The automatic `packageManager` version switch works again on registries whose tarball URLs point at a different host than the registr

author: pfbyjy
body:
## What this does
Adds an `oddish link` command that prints dashboard URLs, so scripts and agents can link to an exact place (a trial, a file, a line range) without building the URL by hand.

Stacked on #1032. The artifacts tab URL support moved to #1038 (on top of this).

## Examples
```
$ oddish link trial <trial-id> --tab files --file verifier/test-stdout.txt --lines 40-52
https://www.oddish.app/tasks/<task>?trial=<trial-id>&tab=files&file=verifier%2Ftest-stdout.txt&lines=L40-L52

$ oddish link trial <trial-id> --experiment leg-d897144a32c2
$ oddish link task <task-id> --version 3 --file instruction.md --lines 8-14
```

## Changes
- New module `oddish.links` builds the URLs and rejects bad input: `lines` needs `file`, `file` needs the files or artifacts tab, and a version number like `3` becomes the full id `task-v3` (what the page matches on).
- New CLI commands `oddish link task` and `oddish link trial`. Use `--base-url` or `ODDISH_DASHBOARD_URL` to target a preview. Output is plain text.
- 34 unit tests in `tests/test_links.py`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01ATstGyewJhEw45PQhXdPLc

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Additive CLI and URL helpers with validation tests; no changes to auth, APIs, or runtime eval behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **`oddish link`** (`link task` / `link trial`) so the CLI prints **canonical dashboard URLs** instead of hand-built query strings. Base URL comes from **`--base-url`** or **`ODDISH_DASHBOARD_URL`** via existing `get_dashboard_url`; output is plain text for piping.
> 
> Adds **`oddish.links`** as the shared Python builders for the dashboard URL grammar (task vs experiment routes, trial drawer, tabs, files, **`L*`** line ranges, task-definition pane params, version ids like `{task_id}-v3`). Invalid combinations raise **`ValueError`** (e.g. `lines` without `file`, trial-pane params without `trial_id`).
> 
> Wires the new Typer app into the root CLI and adds **unit tests** for `format_lines`, `trial_task_id`, `task_url`, and `experiment_url`.

author: alandtse
body:
## Summary
- Replaces `ShadowDemandCS`'s single per-tile depth tap (a stochastic
  sample that could miss thin or off-center geometry, the root cause
  of visible flicker in an earlier tap-count experiment) with a
  deterministic MIN/MAX depth reduction over every texel in the
  tile, via a new `ShadowDemandPyramidCS` pass.
- Every downstream consumer (cluster lookup, distance falloff, the
  C++ readback ring, the EMA, the scheduler tiebreaker landed in
  #372) is untouched -- this only swaps the depth source feeding the
  existing per-tile representative position.
- Builds on #372 (`feat/scm-vsm-demand-instrumentation`) -- targets
  the same base and should land after it.

## Design notes
- Reduces directly to the existing 64x64 cluster-tile granularity
  rather than building a full mip pyramid, since lights are already
  binned at that granularity elsewhere in this pipeline. This also
  sidesteps per-light sphere-to-screen projection and its near-plane
  degeneracy case, since occlusion is still evaluated through the
  existing per-tile representative-position path rather than a
  per-light screen-space test.
- Non-VR only, matching the existing scope of `ShadowDemandCS.hlsl`.
- **Reduces both MIN and MAX depth, not MAX alone.** A MAX-only
  reduction always scores a tile's demand against its farthest
  surface -- a light illuminating only near geometry (e.g. behind a
  foreground pillar, against a distant background) would always
  evaluate at the far surface and read as permanently absent,
  deterministically, so it would never self-correct the way a
  stochastic tap eventually would by chance. `ShadowDemandCS` now
  evaluates demand at both representative depths per tile, skipping
  the near pass when it lands in the same cluster Z-slice as the far
  pass (same light list, so evaluating it twice would only
  double-count). Found and required by the adversarial-review/rebuttal
  pass on the follow-up zero-demand-skip design built on top of this
  producer -- a persistent false-zero here would have looped a
  skipped light through a forced backstop redraw that re-evaluates
  the same missed point and immediately re-skips, reading as a
  permanent stutter rather than bounded staleness.

## Does this need a Phase 2 to be worth it?
Yes -- **on its own this PR does not reduce CPU cost**, only signal
accuracy. #372's `EnableShadowDemandRedraw` tiebreak is a bounded
score nudge among already-competing candidates; it never skips a
redraw, so the actual CPU bottleneck
(`SCM::RenderScheduledShadowLights`, ~7.4-7.8ms in this A/B, dominated
by the portal-graph visibility walk) is untouched by either #372 or
this PR. Confirmed by the A/B below: that pass's cost was the same
order of magnitude on both builds.

The "trade GPU for CPU" payoff this line of work is ultimately after
requires a Phase 2 that genuinely skips/demotes a low-demand light's
CPU-side scheduling work -- the `SkipZeroDemandRedraw`/Stage-B
mechanism explored (and rejected, for visible flicker) earlier with
the noisy single-tap producer. This PR exists to give that future
mechanism a trustworthy, noise-free signal to build on; it is not, by
itself, a performance improvement. Treat it as infrastructure with a
small (~5-6us) fixed cost, not a perf PR.

**Phase 2 is now #377**, built on this producer. Same-session A/B
against `origin/dev` (`chosen=117/excess=0` matching exactly on both)
shows a real redraw and estimated-pass-cost reduction with the skip
on -- see #377 for the full economics-gate writeup. That confirms
this producer's signal is usable for a real hard-skip consumer, not
just the soft tiebreak in #372.

## Review fixes (this round)
Two of three CodeRabbit findings fixed and their threads resolved:
- The shadow-demand staging buffers were created with
  `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_BUFFER_STRUCTURED` + a `StructureByteStride`,
  which requires a shader-resource/UAV bind flag a `BindFlags=0`
  staging buffer cannot have. Zeroed both -- no functional change,
  staging is only ever `Map()`'d for CPU readback.
- The "Prioritize Redraws by Screen Demand" tooltip claimed the
  instrumentation checkbox sits "below" (it's a different panel) and
  omitted that the setting has no effect in VR. Corrected.

**One finding left open, blocking merge under this repo's
all-threads-resolved ruleset:** `ShadowCasterManager::ResetSession`'s
copy of the demand EMA is cleared on reset, but `LightLimitFix` keeps
its own separate copy that isn't told about a reset reached through
`ScheduleShadowCasters`' pending-teardown path (as opposed to
`OnSceneTransitionReset`, which already clears both correctly). A new
light landing on a reused pool slot can inherit the previous
occupant's stale demand for one push cycle. Not a quick fix -- the
correct repair needs a way for `ShadowCasterManager`'s teardown path
to reach across into `LightLimitFix`'s own state, and no such
callback exists yet. Deliberately left unfixed rather than rushed;
tracked, not blocking functionality today (the natural per-frame
reconciliation in `ScheduleShadowCasters` self-corrects within a few
frames), but does block merge until resolved.

## Test plan
- [x] `BuildDevFast.bat` clean build
- [x] Live smoke test on SE: both shaders compile at runtime with
      zero errors; `EnableShadowDemandRedraw` toggled on live via
      devbench, game stayed responsive for ~2500 frames afterward
- [x] Live A/B via devbench `inspect kind=profiler`, same save/scene,
      before/after this PR's build (MAX-only version; the later
      MIN/MAX fix adds one more evaluation pass per tile at
      comparable cost):

  | Build | Pass | avg GPU cost |
  |---|---|---|
  | Legacy (single tap, pre-#373) | `LightLimitFix::ShadowDemand` | ~8.6us |
  | Hi-Z (MAX-only) | `LightLimitFix::ShadowDemandPyramid` | ~7.5us |
  | Hi-Z (MAX-only) | `LightLimitFix::ShadowDemand` | ~6.4us |
  | Hi-Z combined | both passes | ~13.9us |

  Net: Hi-Z costs ~+5.3us over the legacy tap (~0.08% of a 60fps
  frame budget), for a deterministic instead of stochastic signal.
  Single-scene sample (one Whiterun-exterior save), not a
  multi-scene sweep -- treat as a sanity check on cost, not a
  rigorous benchmark. Not re-measured after the MIN/MAX fix; expect
  a small additional cost from the second per-tile evaluation pass.
- [ ] VR runtime test (feature is non-VR only, no VR-specific
      behavior to verify yet)
- [ ] Flicker-rate comparison against the pre-Hi-Z tap (the original
      motivation) -- not yet measured; requires the same
      live-observation protocol used to falsify the K=4/N=90
      tap-count variant earlier in this line of work
- [ ] EMA reset-ownership fix (see Review fixes above) -- blocking
      merge under the repo's review-thread-resolution ruleset

author: chrisrackauckas-claude
body:
## Problem

`SciMLTesting.run_qa` runs ExplicitImports' checks, and ExplicitImports *does* know
about extensions — it reads the `[extensions]` table out of `Project.toml` — but it
skips any extension whose module does not exist:

```julia
ext_mod = Base.get_extension(mod, Symbol(ext))
ext_mod === nothing && continue
```

An extension module only exists once its trigger weakdep is loaded, and the QA
environment loaded none. So today **none of ADTypes' three extensions are scanned by
QA at all** — `ext/` is entirely outside the ExplicitImports checks.

## Fix

Add the weakdeps to `test/qa/Project.toml` (with `[compat]` mirroring the root
package's bounds) and `using` them in `test/qa/qa.jl` before `run_qa`.

**Extensions now scanned: all three.** ChainRulesCore, ConstructionBase and EnzymeCore
are lightweight, pure-Julia and co-resolve without trouble, so there is no partial
coverage here and nothing left out.

Verified the extension modules really do materialize in the QA environment:

```
ADTypesChainRulesCoreExt => ADTypesChainRulesCoreExt
ADTypesConstructionBaseExt => ADTypesConstructionBaseExt
ADTypesEnzymeCoreExt => ADTypesEnzymeCoreExt
```

## What the new coverage found

Exactly one finding, in `all_qualified_accesses_are_public`:

```
Module `ADTypesEnzymeCoreExt` has explicit imports of names from modules in which they are not public:
- `ForwardMode` is not public in `EnzymeCore` but it was imported from `EnzymeCore` at ext/ADTypesEnzymeCoreExt.jl:6:54
- `ReverseMode` is not public in `EnzymeCore` but it was imported from `EnzymeCore` at ext/ADTypesEnzymeCoreExt.jl:7:54
```

`ADTypesEnzymeCoreExt` needs these to dispatch `ADTypes.mode(::AutoEnzyme{M})` on the
mode type parameter. EnzymeCore v0.8.21 exports only mode *instances* —
`Forward`, `Reverse`, `ReverseWithPrimal`, ... — and neither `ForwardMode`,
`ReverseMode`, nor their supertype `Mode` is exported or declared `public`
(`Base.ispublic(EnzymeCore, :ForwardMode) == false`). Each exported instance is one
specific parameterization, so there is no public spelling of "any forward mode" to
constrain `M` with. This is the "owner package has not declared the name public yet"
case, so it is ignored with a comment naming the owner and the reason.

### Ignore entries added

| Symbol | Owner | Justification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:ForwardMode` | EnzymeCore | Mode type needed to constrain `AutoEnzyme{M}`; EnzymeCore exports only mode instances, no public supertype spelling exists. |
| `:ReverseMode` | EnzymeCore | Same. |

(The pre-existing `:broadcastable` / `:depwarn` `Base` ignores are unchanged.) No check
was disabled, nothing was marked `@test_broken`, and the ChainRulesCore and
ConstructionBase extensions pass every ExplicitImports check unignored — no extension
source needed changing.

Worth a follow-up upstream: asking EnzymeCore to declare `Mode`/`ForwardMode`/`ReverseMode`
public would let both ignores be dropped, since dispatching on AD mode is the obvious
intended use of those types.

## Local QA result

Ran `GROUP=QA julia --project=. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test()'` on this branch (Julia 1.12):

```
Test Summary: | Pass  Total   Time
QA            |   20     20  43.4s
     Testing ADTypes tests passed
```

Before adding the ignores, the same command failed with the EnzymeCore finding above
(`19 passed, 0 failed, 1 errored`), which is the direct confirmation that the extensions
really are being scanned now rather than silently skipped.

author: marinofaggiana
body:
## Summary

Improve remote video playback reliability and prevent VLC lifecycle races when changing or closing videos.

## Changes

- Replace the AVFoundation status observation with an async playability check.
- Fall back to VLC when the AVFoundation probe fails or exceeds 8 seconds.
- Cancel obsolete playback probes when the selected video changes.
- Wait for VLC to stop completely before detaching its drawable, dismissing the player, or changing video.
- Recover the SwiftUI playback state when VLC presentation is rejected, allowing a new playback attempt.
- Forward the configured user agent to remote playback.
- Add privacy-safe VLC diagnostics for presentation, playback requests, and state changes. Direct URL paths, queries, and tokens are never logged.
- Update the app version to 34.1.1.

## Motivation

Remote videos could remain indefinitely in the loading state when the AVFoundation probe did not complete or when a VLC presentation request was rejected during a transition.

VLC could also continue accessing its rendering view while the player was being dismissed or another video was selected, potentially triggering an Auto Layout operation outside the main thread.

## Testing

- Nextcloud scheme builds successfully in Xcode.
- Verified cancellation and fallback paths compile correctly.
- Verified VLC shutdown completes before the drawable and controller are released.
- Verified rejected presentations reset the playback state and can be retried.

author: bsj-k-hioki
body:
Claude Code の OpenTelemetry 出力を受けて **実際の作業量(WP)** を計測し、それを燃料にした**製造プロトタイプ**と、使い方を可視化する**業務スコアカード**を追加します。

## できること

| | |
|---|---|
| 🏭 **製造** | 抽出機に原材料をセット → 実WPが50溜まるごとに製品が完成 → 📖図鑑を埋める |
| 📊 **メトリクス** (`/metrics`) | Claude Code から届く全メトリクス/イベントの一覧と WP の内訳 |
| 🏆 **リーダーボード** | 効率・PR・コミット・Skill・Agent・委譲率など9軸で並べ替え |

## セットアップ

`http/json` が使えるので **OTel Collector は不要**です。`otel.mjs` が素の Node で OTLP を直接受けます（依存ゼロを維持）。

各自の `~/.claude/settings.json` の `env` に設定を入れて、**新しい** claude セッションを開始してください（詳細は README）。プロンプト本文・ツール入力・API本文は送らない設定にしています（既定でも無効ですが、自己文書化のため明示的に `0`）。

```
Claude Code ──OTLP/JSON──▶ :4318 /v1/metrics, /v1/logs   ← otel.mjs（受信 + 集計）
                                    │  生ログを ~/.claude/factory/otel-raw.jsonl に追記
                                    ▼
                           :4321 /api/otel ──▶ /metrics ・ ゲーム画面
```

生ログを残しているので、`otel.mjs` の重みを書き換えて再起動すれば**過去データを自動リプレイして再集計**できます。

## UI の変更

- 上中央に **今日の労働量ボード**（今日のWP / 今日の製造数）と**製造パネル**を横並びで配置（幅が足りなければ上下に折り返し）
- 上部のタブ群を **☰ ハンバーガーメニュー**に格納
- **レイアウト編集**は右下に常時表示
- 左下の稼働/休憩を **Claude君の絵**に（稼働=作業ポーズ+✨ / 休憩=座り+☕）
- **ガチャを削除**。あわせて ⚙️(生産P) の概念も撤去し、💰はショップ内でのみ残高表示
- 💰は**製品のレア度に応じた売上**として、完成品一覧を開いたときに加算

## 実測でわかった OTel の仕様差異

ドキュメント通りに書くと動かない箇所があったので記録しています（README / WP.md）。

| 項目 | 実際 |
|---|---|
| イベント名 | `event.name` は `claude_code.` プレフィックス**無し**（docs 通りだと WP が全部 0 になる） |
| 識別属性 | `user.email` / `session.id` は resource ではなく**各 datapoint / logRecord の attributes 側** |
| 未記載イベント | `subagent_completed`（`total_tool_uses` / `is_async` つき）、`skill_activated`、`hook_*` |
| `event.timestamp` | 数値ではなく ISO8601 文字列 |
| `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` | OTel 送信はブロックされない（併存可） |

## 指標としての注意

**ゲーム用WPと業務スコアカードは目的が違うので分離しています。**

ゲーム用WPは「活動量」であって「パフォーマンス」ではなく、**人と人の比較には使えません**。実測で `Skill` 1.2% / `Agent` 0.9% しか占めず、単一の合計値で並べると **Bash を大量に叩く人が1位になります**。使い方を見るためのスコアカードは単一の合計値を作らず、多軸のまま並べています。

較正データ・重みの根拠・限界は [WP.md](https://github.com/bsj-yoshijima/Claude_factory/blob/feat/otel-metrics/WP.md) にまとめました。

## 残っている調整

- **`CRAFT_WP` は 50 のまま**です。動作確認しやすい値にしてあるので、実運用のペース（1日1個なら5,000前後）に合わせて要調整
- 機械のレベルアップは ⚙️ 撤去に伴い効果がありません
- スコアカードは全期間の累計です（週次リセットは未実装）

author: jacksonbai
body:
Closes ESS-42

## 改了什么

**1. 统一 WatchLog 设施**（`Watch/WatchLog.swift` + `Shared/ClientLog.swift`）
- `os.Logger`：subsystem `beer.workspace.wristagent`，按模块分 category（lifecycle / welcome / player / recorder / transport / wcsession / turn / watchlog）；
- 应用容器 JSONL 滚动日志（`ClientLogStore`）：单文件 ≤2MB、chunk 最多保留 3 个，超限丢最旧并写 `chunks_dropped` 留痕；每条 `ts / request_id / module / event / detail / error{code, description}`，与服务端 trace 同构；只记元数据，不落音频与凭据。

**2. 交互全链覆盖**
- 生命周期：冷启动（版本号）、scenePhase 前后台、welcome 去重判定结果；
- 欢迎语：每次尝试生成 `welcome-<uuidv7>` 关联 id——资源查找（bundle 路径/字节数）→ AVAudioSession 激活结果+当前音频路由 → player 创建/play() 返回值 → 完成/解码错误/系统中断回调，全部同 id 串链；
- 录音：开始（会话配置/权限）、结束（时长/字节）、空录音/失败原因、取消；
- WCSession：激活状态与错误、isReachable 变化、transferFile 入队/回执（成败+原因）、didReceive 文件与消息（类型/字节/request_id）；
- 结果下行：收到音频（字节）→ sha256 校验 → 落盘/入加密仓结果 → 会话激活/路由 → 播放开始/结束/error；
- 状态机：每个状态事件落 `state / applied / failure_stage / detail`（乱序被拒事件也留痕）。

**3. 日志回传，Mac 侧可读**
- Watch：`WatchLogShipper` 在 WCSession 激活、进前后台、回合终态、欢迎语走完时把 chunk 经 `transferFile`（系统托管队列）送 iPhone；成功回执才删本地副本，通道不可用时 chunk 留存（模拟器已验证 `ship_skipped` 后日志仍在）；
- iPhone：`ClientLogUplink` 落盘排队 → `POST /v1/client-logs`（HMAC 签名，chunk_id 作 request_id）；退避重试、App 重启续传、稳定 4xx 视为毒 chunk 丢弃、积压超 32 个丢最旧；
- Bridge：新增 `POST /v1/client-logs`——协议版本/chunk_id/签名校验，chunk_id 幂等去重（重传不刷屏），客户端字段白名单+截断后逐行落 bridge.log：

```
grep watch_client_log bridge.log | grep <request_id>
```

## 如何验证

- `Scripts/verify.sh` 全绿：79 Swift tests（含新增 `ClientLogStoreTests` 5 个：JSONL 契约键、顺序、2MB 滚动、保留 3 上限+丢弃留痕、chunk 删除白名单）+ iOS/watchOS 双 target 构建；
- Bridge `npm test` 40/40（新增 `test/ess42-client-logs.test.mjs`：签名必需、逐行 `evt=watch_client_log` 按 request_id 可查、坏行留痕、超长字段截断、chunk 幂等、稳定错误码）；
- watchOS 26.5 模拟器实测：冷启动完整日志链（cold_start → greet_start → resource_found → session_activated(route=Speaker) → play_started → playback_completed，同一 welcome id）；把 bundle 里 WelcomeSpeech.m4a 改名后重启，日志明确给出 `resource_missing` + `ERR_WELCOME_ASSET_MISSING` 与降级决策。

## 已知限制

- Bridge 的 chunk 幂等集是进程内 LRU（512 个）：Bridge 重启后极端情况下同一 chunk 可能重复落一次日志（内容相同，grep 无害），换持久化不值得复杂度；
- iPhone 端 chunk 明文暂存（Watch 侧已保证只有元数据）；
- 与 PR #14（iPhone→Watch 下行可靠投递）相邻：本 PR 基于当前 main（#15 之后），未动下行投递路径，如 #14 先合入按需 rebase。

author: ivohofland
body:
Closes #10.

## What this fixes

`scripts/archive.ts` had no tests and **could not have any**. `main()` ran at module scope, so importing the file launched Chromium and started hitting the network, and `captureNode` was not exported. That mattered because `captureNode` is the single path every provider source and every reference document archives through — the routine that writes the `.sha256` sidecar the whole evidentiary chain reads.

This branch opens the seam. It is **infrastructure only: no behaviour change**.

## The seam

`captureNode(node, dir, deps)` now takes its dependencies explicitly instead of reading module-scope constants and calling Playwright directly.

Injecting the **capture function** rather than faking a browser was the design decision, and three things fall out of it:

- **The `browser` parameter disappears.** It existed only to reach `saveLocalCopy`, so Playwright is now closed over by `main()`'s single production call site rather than threaded through the module. Verified: importing the module returns in under a second, exports `captureNode`, launches no browser.
- **`today` needs no clock seam.** Only `saveLocalCopy` uses it, and a fake capture picks its own filenames.
- **A test can make the capture fail on demand** — which #6 needs, and which a fake browser makes nearly impossible, since `page.pdf()` only fails on non-headless Chromium.

`pauseMs` is injected too. `captureNode` sleeps 10–30s after a Wayback submission because archive.org throttles hard; without this, any test reaching that branch blocks for half a minute.

## Killing the hidden global

`failedCaptures` was module-level mutable state that `captureNode` pushed into — not assertable, and invisible to anyone reading the signature. It returns a `CaptureResult { changed, failedCapture }` now, accumulated by `main()` and by `archiveReferences`, whose `Promise<void>` signature previously hid that failures were even possible.

## The entrypoint guard is itself pinned

The guard is the branch's new single point of failure: all archiving is now conditional on a filename match. If it stopped matching, `npm run archive` would become a **silent no-op that exits 0** while the suite stayed green — a researcher believing evidence was captured when none was. The final review caught this; the wiring test now asserts the guard names this file. Also `endsWith(path.sep + "archive.ts")`, since the bare suffix also matched `sync-archive.ts`.

## Tests: 285 → 293

Eight tests, no browser and no network, all injecting `capture` and `submitWayback`:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| no `url` is skipped, and says so | silence made an unarchivable source look captured |
| existing snapshot **on disk** is skipped | "already archived" = the file exists, not that the YAML declares a path |
| `--force` re-captures | the escape hatch actually escapes |
| a failed capture is reported, not swallowed | `failedCapture` returns the id; `local_snapshot` is never set |
| Wayback-pointless URL is never submitted | injected `submitWayback` **throws**, so it is enforced, not observed |
| `--skip-wayback` suppresses submission | |
| `dir` is threaded through, not hardcoded | a provider source and a reference write to their own directory |
| wiring: both loops route through `captureNode`, and the guard names this file | mirrors `sync-archive.test.ts` |

Every one has a named source mutation that reddens it — checked, not assumed.

## Verification

- `npm test` and `npm run test:ci` — **293/293**, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` exit 0
- **No behaviour change**, verified by extracting every `console.*` / `process.stdout.write` / `exit` statement from `34ef0b6:scripts/archive.ts` and the current file and diffing them: only indentation differs. Dutch strings, their order, throttle values, exit codes and per-source write timing are unchanged.
- Smoke run against the real archiver: `npm run archive -- _references --no-sync` captures nothing (every reference already has a snapshot on disk) and leaves the tree clean.
- `scripts/archive.ts` has been byte-frozen since the second commit apart from comments and the one guard line.

## Known open item

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-01-archive-testability-design.md:42` still says Playwright *"is closed over by the default"*. There is no default — `CaptureDeps.capture` is required, and `archive.ts`'s matching docblock was corrected to say so. The spec therefore contradicts the code it describes. One sentence; blocks nothing; flagged here rather than quietly carried.

## Process

Spec → plan → four TDD tasks, each implemented by a fresh subagent and reviewed independently. Two fix rounds fired, both on Important findings, and **both traced to the plan text rather than to any implementer**: a false claim about `archiveReferences` that had reached a commit message, and a tautological `deepEqual` whose comment overclaimed what it pinned. Both are recorded as dated corrections in the spec and plan rather than silently amended.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-01-archive-testability-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-01-archive-testability.md`

## Unblocks

**#6** (archiver names a file it did not write) — its fixes need exactly this seam to be written test-first. Sequencing is **#10 → #13 → #6**: #6's first fix starts declaring `.png` in `local_snapshot`, and until #13 lands a held `.png` classifies as "body not in this checkout".

author: rameerez
body:
Both spellings publish today, and one of them is a typo:

    Softail          fi,gb,lu,nl,nz,ua
    Softtail         nl,nz               <- typo
    Softail Custom   fi,nl,nz
    Softtail Custom  nl,nz               <- typo

Harley spells it **Softail** — [the family page](https://www.harley-davidson.com/us/en/motorcycles/softail.html) and every model page (`softail-standard`, `softail-custom`, `softail-deluxe`). This is a **correction, not a naming choice**; there is no argument for the other spelling.

Build: **exit 0, zero gate failures.** Both typos folded, survivors keep their availability, 0 chains across 4,111 aliases.

### Context — this is the small piece of a larger finding

A read-only dossier over Harley's 633 records produced three results I am deliberately **not** acting on tonight (written up in NEGOTIATION Turn 218):

1. **My one-child filter has good precision and bad recall.** Six of the 65 bases have children the regex cannot see, and the 51 many-child bases I skipped hold *more* genuine duplicate mass than the 65 I kept.
2. **`flstc` is thirteen records for one motorcycle** — `flstc`, `flstc-heritage`, `flstc-heritage-classic`, `flstc-heritage-softail`, `flstc-heritage-softail-cl`, `flstc-heritage-softail-classic`, `flstc-softail-classic`, `flstci`, … That is the real prize and it needs a cluster pass, not a pair pass.
3. **The disjoint-availability signal is dead on this make.** It identified exactly the right pairs on Honda; here `nl_rdw` covers 622 of 633 records, so all 65 pairs intersect and it fired **zero** times. A heuristic's usefulness depends on source coverage, not just on the make.

All three verified against the catalog before being written down.

## Summary

직전 PR(#22)에서 넣은 "여러 장 선택"이 아이폰에서 동작하지 않던 문제입니다.

파일 입력을 `hidden`(=`display: none`)으로 숨겨 두었는데, **아이폰 사파리는 이렇게 숨긴 파일 입력에서 사진첩을 열지 않는 경우가 있습니다.** 같은 파일의 `ImageUpload` 는 투명하게 덮어 두는 방식(`absolute inset-0 opacity-0`)을 쓰고 있고 그건 정상 동작하는데, 새로 넣은 쪽만 다른 방식을 쓴 것이 원인이었습니다.

- `hidden` → `absolute inset-0 opacity-0` (`label` 에 `relative` 추가)
- 작은 안내 글씨 `10px` → `11px`

author: shinjiro0126
body:
## 症状

第2週に入っても、記録タブ上部の「あなたの道のり」が1週目と同じ「スタートの岸+立て札」レイアウトのまま表示される。

## 原因

`src/app/(tabs)/progress.tsx` の coldStart 判定が「開始から14日未満」(`MIN_INSIGHT_DAYS = 14`)になっていた。意図は「コールドスタート表示は第1週だけ」。

14日にしてあったのは、通常レイアウトの `journeyDays`(`src/lib/insight-stats.ts`)が「直近14日」の窓を無条件に埋めるため、開始8日目に切り替えると目標開始前の日が「欠け(missed)」のグレー石として表示されてしまうから。

## 修正方針(案B: journeyDays が開始日を認識する)

- `journeyDays` に目標開始日 `startKey` を後方互換な任意引数として追加し、`dateKey < startKey` の日は新状態 `'beforeStart'` にする(missed にしない)
- `journey-stones.tsx` の `StoneShape` は `beforeStart` の日に石を一切描かない(水面のまま。点線の `future` とも区別)。S字2段の座標計算は既存の14要素前提のまま
- coldStart 判定を「開始から7日未満」(第1週内)に変更。判定式は `isJourneyColdStart(startKey, today)` として `src/lib/insight-stats.ts` に切り出し、テスト可能にした
- `journeySummaryLabel` の集計(歩いた日・報告した日・おやすみ)に `beforeStart` が数えられないことをテストで保証

## 見た目の変化

- 第1週: 従来どおり「スタートの岸+立て札」レイアウト
- 第2週から: 通常の14日S字レイアウトに切り替わり、目標開始前の期間は石のない水面として表示される(グレーの「欠け」石は出ない)

## テスト

`src/lib/__tests__/insight-stats.test.ts` に5件追加(計145件、全通過):

- 開始前の日が `beforeStart` になる(missed にならない)
- `startKey` を渡しても開始日以降の状態判定は変わらない
- `startKey` 未指定では従来挙動のまま(後方互換)
- 境界: 開始7日目(diffDays=6)はコールドスタート、8日目(diffDays=7)は通常レイアウト
- `journeySummaryLabel` が `beforeStart` を各カウントに数えない

## 検証

- `npm run typecheck` 通過
- `npm run lint` 通過
- `npm test` 145件全通過

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>konflux-ci/build-pipeline-tasks (quay.io/konflux-ci/tekton-catalog/task-buildah)</summary>

### [`v0.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/konflux-ci/build-pipeline-tasks/blob/HEAD/task/buildah/CHANGELOG.md#0110)

##### Changed

- When scanning the built image with Syft, scans the image filesystem as
  a directory instead of scanning the the image as an OCI archive. This improves
  the scanning time, disk usage and may improve memory usage. More details in
  [konflux-build-cli/docs/design/syft-image-scanning.md].
- The remote variants of this task now push the built image to the registry directly
  from the build VM instead of rsyncing the image back to the cluster first.
  For large images, this significantly reduces the time spent on network transfers.

##### Removed

- BREAKING: Removed the `sbom-syft-generate` step, SBOM generation now happens
  in the `build` step.
- BREAKING: Removed the `push` step, the push now happens in the `build` step.
- If you have step overrides configured for either of the two removed steps,
  the pipeline will fail with `invalid StepOverride`. See the migration guidance below.

##### Migration guidance

Buildah v0.11.0 comes with a migration script that will attempt to automatically
fix the step overrides in your PipelineRuns. In most cases, no manual action will
be needed. But there are cases that the script cannot handle:

1. Your PipelineRun references an external Pipeline. In this case, the migration
   script will never get a chance to run on the PipelineRun.
2. Your PipelineRun is multi-platform, SBOM generation needs more resources
   than the build itself and the remote VMs do not have sufficient resources.

If the migration script doesn't solve the problem, please follow the procedure below.

##### Manual procedure

If you have `sbom-syft-generate` or `push` step overrides in the `.spec.taskRunSpecs`
section in your PipelineRun, please remove them. In most cases, this should be all.

However, if you were previously requesting more resources for SBOM generation
than for the build step itself, there is a chance that the build will fail.
In this case, move the relevant overrides to the build step. The same technically
applies for the push step, but it's highly unlikely that pushing would require
more resources than the build.

For example:

```diff
 spec:
   taskRunSpecs:
     - pipelineTaskName: build-container
       stepSpecs:
-        - name: sbom-syft-generate
+        - name: build
           computeResources:
             requests:
               memory: 16Gi
             limits:
               memory: 16Gi
```

This will work for build steps that run in-cluster - single-platform builds
and typically also the amd64 builds in a multi-platform build setup.

For build steps that run on remote VMs, the overrides have no effect. In case
the build fails, please switch to a larger VM flavo

author: dattamks
body:
Follow-up to the merged PR #8.

Railway refuses to build a Dockerfile that declares `VOLUME` ("VOLUME ... is not supported, use Railway Volumes"). `Dockerfile.standalone` had `VOLUME ["/data"]`, which blocked the Railway build.

### Change
Removes the `VOLUME ["/data"]` instruction (one line). It was only a Docker hint that auto-created an *anonymous* volume; real persistence is provided at runtime and is unaffected:
- `docker run -v floppydata:/data …`
- the named volume in `docker-compose.standalone.yml`
- a Railway Volume mounted at `/data`

So this changes nothing for existing local/compose users and unblocks the Railway build.

### After merging, to deploy on Railway
- Build with **`Dockerfile.standalone`** (Dockerfile builder).
- Attach a **Railway Volume at `/data`** (replaces the removed VOLUME hint) — or set the `R2_*` vars to store files in Cloudflare R2 instead.

author: mwelwa-cyber
body:
Fixes the P1 from the Codex review of #2077.

The buffering heartbeat fired every **24 tokens**, so a slow or sparse token stream — notably a long first-token latency — could go 30s without emitting one, tripping the client's `AI_CHAT_STREAM_STALL_MS` (30s) stall watchdog and aborting an otherwise-healthy request (the endpoint allows 60s).

**Fix:** replace the per-token counter with a `setInterval` that writes a `: keepalive` SSE comment every `CHAT_HEARTBEAT_MS` (10s) throughout generation **and** the output-moderation call, cleared in `finally` (both success and error paths). The interval is declared outside the `try` so `finally` can always clear it.

## Verification
`npx eslint functions/index.js` — clean; `npm run build` — pass. (The moderation-windowing behaviour is covered by `contentModeration.test.js` from #2077; this change is the heartbeat scheduling only.)
