Close #4

## Customer Summary

- Keeps modulo calculations available through the `calc` command alongside addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
- Preserves existing calculator behavior with no migration or compatibility changes required.

## Technical Summary

- Defines the supported operator values once and derives the TypeScript `Operator` type from that shared list.
- Reuses the shared list for Commander argument validation so runtime choices and compile-time types cannot drift apart.
- Moves automatically run calculator and CLI tests under `test/unit` and keeps modulo coverage on the real CLI subprocess path.
- Removes narrower modulo assertions that duplicated the CLI behavior test.

## Why

- The operator union and CLI choices previously repeated the same values, making future operator additions easy to implement inconsistently.
- A single source of truth keeps modulo support consistent across calculation typing and CLI validation while retaining broad behavioral coverage.

## Testing

- `bun test`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

author: vsolano9
body:
## What & why The directory-picker save path de-duped filenames only against the other files in the same batch, then called `getFileHandle(name, { create: true })`. A file already sitting in the chosen folder was overwritten silently, so receiving a second `report.pdf` destroyed the first. `uniqueName` now probes the folder as well as the batch: the existing file keeps its name and the incoming one becomes `report (1).pdf`. The probe stays cheap — a single `getFileHandle` for the exact candidate, never a directory scan. `existsInDir` reports three states rather than two. `NotFoundError` means the slot is free; any other failure is `"unknown"`, and on that we stop probing and return the current candidate so the real `create: true` write surfaces the real error. Treating an unreadable directory as free would overwrite a file we cannot see, and treating it as taken would spin forever looking for a free slot. The `dir` argument is optional, so the single-file `showSaveFilePicker` path and the in-memory tray keep their existing behaviour. One note on the acceptance criteria: **in-batch de-duplication already worked** before this change — three same-named files in one batch already became `a.txt`, `a (1).txt`, `a (2).txt`. Only the on-disk case was broken. That criterion now has a regression check so it stays working, but it isn't a behaviour change. Closes #133 ## Type - [ ] feat - [x] fix - [ ] docs / chore / refactor / test / perf ## Checklist - [x] `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck` pass locally - [x] `pnpm --filter @warp/web build` is green (web changes) - [x] Engine changes: the relevant `web/src/lib/warp/*.check.mjs` harness passes (and covers the new behaviour) - [x] Design tokens + inline-style component style respected (no drive-by restyling) This is a web-only, two-file engine change, so per the template's "delete lines that genuinely don't apply" I've dropped the server-test and mobile-width rows: the diff contains no `server/` files and no UI. ### Hard constraints - [x] No new recurring-cost infrastructure — no TURN, database, storage, or paid API - [x] Still STUN-only — no relay in the file path - [x] The signaling server still never reads, stores, or understands file contents - [x] `SEND_HIGH_WATER` in `peer.ts` untouched — `peer.ts` is not in this diff at all - [x] Transient network drops still recover — accept/resume logic untouched ## Testing `useWarpTransfer.check.mjs` gains 13 collision cases (50 checks pass in total): the on-disk collision, three-in-one-batch, the no-collision case, combined disk + batch, probe cost, an inconclusive probe, dotfiles, and extensionless names. Because that harness uses a fake directory handle, it proves the algorithm but not the API contract. So the behaviour was also verified against the real File System Access API through OPFS in Chrome: - a probe for an absent name throws exactly `NotFoundError` — the assumption the whole fix rests on - three `report.pdf` receives into a folder that already holds one leave **four** files with the original intact - `.env` becomes `.env (1)` As a control, the pre-fix code exercised the same way leaves **one** file with the original's contents replaced — the bug reproduced as real data loss. ## Known gaps, deliberately out of scope - `DefaultReceiveHost` in `peer.ts` carries a second copy of the same in-memory-only de-dupe. It is not the app's path — `useWarpTransfer` injects its own `ReceiveHost` at both `new WarpPeer` sites — but a library consumer who doesn't inject one would still overwrite. Happy to fix in a follow-up if you'd like it in scope. - Concurrent receives are not made atomic. Names resolve when the offer is accepted while handles are created lazily, so two simultaneous accepts could still pick the same free name. `getFileHandle` has no exclusive-create option, and `createWritable()` defaults to `mode: "siloed"`, so the last writer can win. `createWritable({ mode: "exclusive" })` would instead surface the clash as `NoModificationAllowedError` and could drive a retry under a fresh name, but that needs a wider `FsFileHandle` type, a change to the write path, and updated mocks, so it is a separate follow-up rather than part of this naming fix. This is pre-existing behaviour and unchanged here. - `useWarpTransfer.check.mjs` isn't wired into `pnpm test` (`web` has no `test` script), so it has to be run explicitly, as its own header says. - I could not drive a real `showDirectoryPicker` — it needs a user gesture and an OS dialog. OPFS exercises the same `getFileHandle` interface and is the closest substitute, which is why the control above matters. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Prevented directory-based transfers from overwriting existing files. * Improved filename handling for duplicate files, including dotfiles and extensionless names. * Added safeguards for collisions between files transferred in the same batch. * Improved error handling when the destination cannot be checked reliably.

Greptile Summary

 This PR fixes a silent data-loss bug (#133) where receiving a file into a folder that already contained a same-named file would overwrite it. `uniqueName` is promoted to async and extended to probe the chosen directory with a single cheap `getFileHandle` call per candidate, so the existing file keeps its name and the incoming file steps aside. - `existsInDir` introduces a three-state return (`true` / `false` / `\"unknown\"`) so an unreadable directory neither causes infinite looping nor silently overwrites an invisible file — an inconclusive probe returns the current candidate immediately, deferring the real error to the subsequent `create: true` write. - The `accept` callback in `useWarpTransfer.ts` was already async, so the addition of `await uniqueName(…, dir)` fits naturally into the existing flow. - Nine new scenarios in `useWarpTransfer.check.mjs` cover on-disk collision, pure in-batch deduplication, combined disk+batch, the \"unknown\" probe path, probe cost, dotfiles, and extensionless names.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — the overwrite bug is correctly fixed, all edge cases are covered, and the async change fits naturally into an already-async accept callback. The algorithm is correct and well-documented. The only concern is that the test helpers in the .check.mjs file are manually duplicated from the production TypeScript, meaning a future algorithm change won't automatically be reflected in the tests unless the test file is also updated. **Files Needing Attention:** web/src/lib/warp/useWarpTransfer.check.mjs — the hand-copied existsInDir and uniqueName helpers need to stay in sync with their counterparts in useWarpTransfer.ts.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | web/src/lib/warp/useWarpTransfer.ts | Refactors uniqueName from sync to async, adds existsInDir helper, and threads dir probe into accept()'s folder-target path. Logic is correct: unknown probe state defers to the real write, used-set tracks in-batch deduplication, and the dotfile/extensionless edge cases are handled. | | web/src/lib/warp/useWarpTransfer.check.mjs | Adds 9 well-structured test scenarios covering on-disk collision, in-batch deduplication, combined disk+batch, the unknown probe path, dotfiles, and extensionless names. The existsInDir and uniqueName helpers are hand-copied from the .ts source rather than imported, which creates a drift risk if the production algorithm is updated without also updating the test file. |

author: patali
body:
Two changes to the extension. They're in one PR because they have the same
root cause: the popup was both the UI *and* the owner of in-flight work.

## Remove "Send via email"

It rendered on the server but handed the file to Mail.app through a
native-messaging host each user had to install per machine — more setup than
the feature was worth. Removed from the popup, the settings toggles, and the
docs. The `nativeMessaging` permission and `extension/native-host/` go with
it, since nothing can reach them once the UI is gone.

`/convert` still returns the rendered file, so the capability can come back if
it earns its keep. Restore the helper with:
`git checkout 9fba815 -- extension/native-host`

## Keep job state outside the popup

A browser popup closes the moment you click the page behind it — that part is
not fixable. The problem was that closing it tore down the message channel
carrying the conversion result, so a send still in flight simply vanished:
reopening showed no trace of it, and there was no way to learn whether it
succeeded.

Conversions are now jobs written to `storage.local` by the service worker and
only *read* by the popup. The popup shows what's running plus any outcome it
hasn't displayed yet, then clears it. Settings gains a **Recent conversions**
list, since that's now the only place to look a past conversion up.

Three details that are easy to get wrong, all covered by the harnesses below:

- **Concurrent writes.** Mutations go through a single promise chain. Two
  conversions doing read-modify-write on one storage key otherwise lose an
  update, and running two at once is the normal case.
- **Orphaned jobs.** A service worker restart proves nothing is driving those
  fetches, so anything left `running` is marked interrupted. Otherwise it
  spins in the popup forever.
- **Results vanishing as you watch.** The popup keeps rendering a job it has
  already shown, so an outcome landing while the popup is open doesn't
  disappear from under the user. `seen` only takes effect on the next open.

## Verification

Ran the real `background.js` under mocked Chrome APIs (27 checks): job
completion, server and extraction failures recorded rather than lost,
seen-once clearing, running jobs never hidden, three concurrent jobs all
surviving the mutex, stale-job recovery, the 50-job cap, and the removed
`mail` mode now rejected.

Ran the real `popup.js` in a fake DOM to confirm a job finishing while the
popup is open stays on screen, that `markSeen` doesn't re-enter itself
forever, and that the job is gone on the next open.

Rendered both pages in headless Chrome to confirm they draw without errors —
the popup shows two buttons and the running/done/error rows; settings shows
the history with linked titles and relative times. Also confirmed the served
`/extension.zip` no longer contains `native-host/` and the install page no
longer mentions Mail.app.

author: liuh886
body:
## Goal

Refine RhythmCoach's lightweight spoken-word DSP without adding speech recognition, cloud processing, or complex audio controls.

## Research basis

The parameter strategy combines Web Audio / MediaRecorder specifications with conservative spoken-word practices from OBS documentation and audio community discussions. There is no universal cross-device preset, so this PR avoids aggressive makeup gain and uses stable, testable defaults.

## Changes

- Separate the pre-DSP analyser path from the recording-style path so Natural, Podcast, and Crisp cannot change speaking-time or pause metrics.
- Disable browser automatic gain control to avoid double compression and pumping.
- Refine Podcast and Crisp with conservative high-pass filtering, presence EQ, soft-knee compression, and a -3 dB safety limiter.
- Keep Natural free of custom EQ, compression, and limiting; rename the UI label from Raw to Natural.
- Target 128 kbps MediaRecorder audio with a constructor fallback.
- Add live guidance for low, good, hot, and noisy input conditions.
- Add DSP parameter and input-level tests.
- Document exact presets, design boundaries, and consulted references.

## Important boundaries

- No speech-content recognition.
- No makeup gain, multiband compression, AI denoising, or microphone emulation.
- A limiter cannot repair clipping that already occurred in the microphone or OS input stage; the input warning addresses that risk.
- Final tonal validation still requires listening tests on representative devices.

## Validation

- `npm ci`
- session metrics tests
- training focus tests
- DSP preset and input-level tests
- TypeScript/Vite production build

author: stevemcqueenz
body:
Follow-up on #1. After the Northrend zone-name fix the reporter confirmed Northrend works, but flagged three **[78] Icecrown** quests whose objectives still showed nothing:

- **13118** The Purging Of Scourgeholme
- **13110** The Restless Dead
- **13122** The Scourgestone

## Cause

Their quest **givers** rendered fine — only the **objectives** were blank. Those mobs have zero spawn coordinates in *every* public source:

| mob | pfQuest | Questie | Questie-AC |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30543 Forgotten Depths High Priest | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 30541 Forgotten Depths Underking | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 30202 Reanimated Crusader | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 30482 Wrathstrike Gargoyle | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 30546 (Restless Soul) | 0 | 0 | 0 |

So there was nothing to import from Questie. They **do** exist in the maintainer's own `acore_world` dump (AzerothCore rev `13e8857b515d`, mod-playerbots fork) — the authoritative source for the server these players are on.

## Coordinate conversion

World (x,y) → map percentage was **not** taken from DBC bounds. It was fitted empirically from **143 NPCs** appearing both in `acore_world` (map 571) and in pfQuest zone 210 with a single unambiguous spawn:

```
pctX = -0.01592986 * worldY +  86.80283     mean residual 0.043%
pctY = -0.02394430 * worldX + 225.67845     mean residual 0.052%
```

**Independent cross-check:** the derived clusters land immediately beside the known quest-giver coordinates (Ebon Watcher 83.0/73.0, Father Gustav 82.9/72.8) — neither of which was part of the fit.

NPC **30546 is summoned** and has no creature row at all, so its nodes come from that quest's own `quest_poi` polygon — the exact area the client itself highlights. The file labels it as such rather than passing it off as a spawn.

## Result

```
quest 13110  0 -> 12 renderable nodes
quest 13118  0 -> 67
quest 13122  0 -> 74
```

Entries are emitted whole (`patchtable` replaces keys outright), but all five had empty coord tables so nothing is overwritten; `lvl`/`fac` carried over. `luac5.1 -p` clean.

QA: pick up the three quests in Icecrown and confirm objective dots appear around Scourgeholme, east of the Argent Vanguard.

author: ygd58
body:
## Context

Supersedes #75611 per @teknium1's review -- two real issues.

## Fixes

1. **Indentation-match too strict.** The whole-response scan required the closer's leading whitespace to exactly match the opener's, but CommonMark permits 0-3 leading spaces on each independently. Removed the equality requirement.
2. **Final buffer unprotected.** `_flush_stream()`'s final partial-line flush (content with no trailing newline) unconditionally stripped it, without checking `_in_stream_code_fence` -- a response cut off mid-code-block could have its last line corrupted. Guarded it the same way the main loop already is.

## Verification

Added both requested regression tests. Verified each fix independently by reverting it and confirming the corresponding test fails with the exact reported symptom.

28/28 pass in the full test file; 49/49 across two more dependent test files (no regression).

body:
## Summary

Visual redesign of the two top Home-screen cards (Varaaja, Lämpimät suihkut) per the attached mockup, adding the weekly-minimum inlet temperature to the Varaaja card. Colors, borders, gradients, and the rest of the home screen (price card, heating plan, chart) are untouched.

**Before/after screenshots**: GitHub's MCP tooling available in this session has no image-upload endpoint and I didn't want to commit test screenshots into the repo, so I've sent the before/after images directly in the chat session instead of embedding them here.

## Varaaja card (`components/home/temperature-card.tsx`)

- `"Päivitetty X min sitten"` moved from the card's bottom to a fixed-height slot right under the title, so its length never shifts the temperatures below it (verified with both a short and an artificially long string, e.g. `"Päivitetty 123456 min sitten"`, without breaking layout). Same warning/normal coloring as before.
- Third reading added: the weekly-minimum inlet temperature, in blue (`#40d9ff`), below the bottom-tank reading with a small gap. All three readings are now centered on one vertical line within the space left of the temperature bar (previously right-aligned/offset), so the bar never skews them.
- Missing weekly minimum renders a bare `"--"` (no degree sign) rather than falling back to a default or the latest raw `inlet_temp` reading — see `formatWeeklyMinimumInletTemperatureLabel` below.

## Lämpimät suihkut card (`components/home/warm-water-card.tsx`)

- Removed the small 🚿 icon under the left scale.
- Tank graphic nudged down slightly.
- The secondary temperature reading (`"58°"`) moved from below the tank into the tank graphic itself, horizontally centered near the bottom, clear of the primary showers-left value's box and the tank's edge.
- `metricCard` `paddingVertical` and `cardLabelRow` `minHeight` now match `temperature-card.tsx` exactly, so both card titles land on the same vertical level with identical typography (they already shared the same font size/weight).

## Data layer (`lib/temperaturePresentation.ts`, `app/(tabs)/index.tsx`)

- New pure `formatWeeklyMinimumInletTemperatureLabel()`: `null` → `"--"`, otherwise rounded value + degree sign. Extracted so the placeholder rule is unit-tested rather than inline in the screen.
- Presentation only — `lib/inletTemperature.ts` (from the prior data-layer PR) still owns the actual 7-day-window filtering/computation; the component does not recompute anything.
- Home screen passes the already-computed `weeklyMinimumInletTemperature` state through this formatter into `TemperatureCard`'s new `inletTempLabel` prop.

Shower/forecast/heating-optimization calculations are unchanged.

## Testing

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` passes
- [x] `npm test` passes, including new cases in `lib/temperaturePresentation.test.ts` for `formatWeeklyMinimumInletTemperatureLabel` (missing → placeholder, rounding, `0` not treated as missing)
- [x] Visually verified by running `expo start --web` in this sandbox and rendering the actual Home screen with a locally-injected fake Supabase session (real backend calls fail in this network-restricted sandbox, so this only proves the redesigned components render, lay out, and don't crash — not that they render *correctly against live production data*). This confirmed: the third blue inlet reading renders in the right place with the right color, the shower icon is gone, `"58°"` sits inside the tank without covering the showers-left value, both card titles align, and the fixed update-text slot survives both a normal and an extreme-length string, at both a 360px and 430px viewport width.

### Not verified

- **Not tested on a real device or against live production Supabase data** — this sandbox's network policy blocks the real backend, so the screenshots above use injected mock state, not a real fetch.
- Several of the requested test bullets are inherently visual/rendering checks (icon absence, exact pixel position, typography match) that this repo's test suite cannot express — it's plain TypeScript unit tests run via `tsc` + `node`, with no React Testing Library / Jest / component renderer installed. I did not add one for this PR (out of scope, would be a meaningful infrastructure change) — those specific requirements were verified via the screenshots above and manual code/style review instead of an automated test.

author: arumes31
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The `ServeSetupUI` handler was using `text/template` instead of `html/template` to render the setup page. This allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) because variables are not contextually escaped. The `BaseURL` being passed into the template incorporates `r.Host`, which can be user-controlled.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could potentially manipulate the Host header to inject malicious scripts into the setup page, leading to XSS.
🔧 Fix: Changed the import from `"text/template"` to `"html/template"`. The `html/template` package provides the same interface but automatically escapes output contextually.
✅ Verification: Ran `go test ./...` in the server directory and reviewed the code to ensure `html/template` is used for rendering the `setup.html` page.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>konflux-ci/build-pipeline-tasks (quay.io/konflux-ci/tekton-catalog/task-buildah)</summary>

### [`v0.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/konflux-ci/build-pipeline-tasks/blob/HEAD/task/buildah/CHANGELOG.md#0110)

##### Changed

- When scanning the built image with Syft, scans the image filesystem as
  a directory instead of scanning the the image as an OCI archive. This improves
  the scanning time, disk usage and may improve memory usage. More details in
  [konflux-build-cli/docs/design/syft-image-scanning.md].
- The remote variants of this task now push the built image to the registry directly
  from the build VM instead of rsyncing the image back to the cluster first.
  For large images, this significantly reduces the time spent on network transfers.

##### Removed

- BREAKING: Removed the `sbom-syft-generate` step, SBOM generation now happens
  in the `build` step.
- BREAKING: Removed the `push` step, the push now happens in the `build` step.
- If you have step overrides configured for either of the two removed steps,
  the pipeline will fail with `invalid StepOverride`. See the migration guidance below.

##### Migration guidance

Buildah v0.11.0 comes with a migration script that will attempt to automatically
fix the step overrides in your PipelineRuns. In most cases, no manual action will
be needed. But there are cases that the script cannot handle:

1. Your PipelineRun references an external Pipeline. In this case, the migration
   script will never get a chance to run on the PipelineRun.
2. Your PipelineRun is multi-platform, SBOM generation needs more resources
   than the build itself and the remote VMs do not have sufficient resources.

If the migration script doesn't solve the problem, please follow the procedure below.

##### Manual procedure

If you have `sbom-syft-generate` or `push` step overrides in the `.spec.taskRunSpecs`
section in your PipelineRun, please remove them. In most cases, this should be all.

However, if you were previously requesting more resources for SBOM generation
than for the build step itself, there is a chance that the build will fail.
In this case, move the relevant overrides to the build step. The same technically
applies for the push step, but it's highly unlikely that pushing would require
more resources than the build.

For example:

```diff
 spec:
   taskRunSpecs:
     - pipelineTaskName: build-container
       stepSpecs:
-        - name: sbom-syft-generate
+        - name: build
           computeResources:
             requests:
               memory: 16Gi
             limits:
               memory: 16Gi
```

This will work for build steps that run in-cluster - single-platform builds
and typically also the amd64 builds in a multi-platform build setup.

For build steps that run on remote VMs, the overrides have no effect. In case
the build fails, please switch to a larger VM flavo

## Summary
PR #25 of the capability-registry roadmap. Introduces the **agentOS ↔ MCP capability registry** schema so the runtime can reason about tools as capabilities (stable name + one or more providers) instead of hard-coding integrations.

Adds a new package `@cerebro/capability-registry`:
- `src/schema.ts` — Zod schemas + inferred types: `CapabilityDefinition`, `CapabilityProviderSpec`, `CapabilityPolicy`, `ToolOperation`, `RiskLevel`, `AuthRequirement`, `TrustTier`, and the `CapabilityRegistryDocument`.
- `src/registry.ts` — `validateCapabilityRegistry`, `buildCapabilityIndex` (dedupe by capability id), `resolveProvider` (preferred → first), `listOperations`, and a minimal deny-wins `isOperationAllowed` **precursor** to the PR #27 policy engine.
- `src/registry.test.ts` — 13 vitest tests (validation rejects, index/resolve, policy precursor).
- `examples/registry.example.yaml` — instance aligned to the PR #24 Hermes MCP stack (source-control/design-context/workflow-automation/database-query).
- `README.md` — maps PR #24 `.hermes/policies.yaml` → `CapabilityPolicy`, and lays out the #25–#29 roadmap.

## Alignment with existing repo
- `provider.kind` mirrors `shared-types` `implementation: builtin | http | mcp`.
- `lifecycle` / `status` mirror `packages/capability-core` `CapabilityMetadata`.
- `provider.trustTier` (catalog | manual | internal) maps to PR #24 `policies.yaml` trust tiers.
- No secrets in the registry — only env-var **names** via `connectionEnv` (resolved from `~/.hermes/.env`), per PR #24.

## Scope discipline
- ✅ Schema, validation, indexing, provider resolution, minimal policy precursor.
- ❌ No file/HTTP IO (PR #26 loader), no risk gating/approvals/scopes (PR #27 engine).

- example YAML structurally validated (kebab-case ids, non-empty providers, valid kinds/trust)

## Depends on
PR #24 (Hermes MCP docs + template + policy) — kept as draft; this PR builds the platform-level counterpart to its dev-side policy layer.

## Follow-ups
- PR #26: runtime registry loader (file/HTTP + agentOS wiring)
- PR #27: policy evaluation engine (risk gating, approvals, scopes)
- PR #28: runtime capability discovery
- PR #29: marketplace / provider abstraction

```
  ┌───────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

```
Basically this look at parser code gives visible code size advantages using 2 main tecniques:

body:
## Razorpay Payment Integration

Implemented a complete Razorpay Test Mode payment and product-booking workflow across the backend and frontend.

### Backend

Added authenticated payment endpoints:

- `POST /api/v1/web/payments/orders/`
  - Accepts cart items and quantities
  - Retrieves authoritative prices from the database
  - Converts USD catalog prices to INR
  - Creates a Razorpay Test Mode order
  - Saves a pending local booking

- `POST /api/v1/web/payments/verify/`
  - Verifies the Razorpay HMAC-SHA256 signature
  - Rejects invalid or manipulated responses
  - Marks verified bookings as paid
  - Stores the Razorpay payment ID and payment time
  - Supports idempotent verification

- `GET /api/v1/web/payments/bookings/`
  - Returns the authenticated customer’s booking history
  - Includes products, quantities, totals, payment IDs, and booking status

### Database

Added:

- `orders` table
- `order_items` table
- Product price and quantity snapshots
- Pending and paid booking statuses
- Razorpay order and payment references
- Receipt and local booking numbers
- Payment timestamps

Migration added and applied:

```text
ab71e849c203_create_orders_and_order_items
```

Current database migration head:

```text
ab71e849c203
```

### Payment Security

- Razorpay secret remains backend-only.
- Browser-provided prices are never trusted.
- Order totals are recalculated using database product prices.
- Payment signatures use secure HMAC comparison.
- Invalid signatures do not confirm bookings.
- Users can only verify and view their own orders.
- Razorpay credentials are stored in the ignored backend `.env`.
- No Razorpay secrets are present in tracked files.

### Currency Handling

Configured Razorpay payments in INR:


Existing USD catalog prices are converted to INR before the Razorpay order is created.

### Frontend

author: subenoeva
body:
Forces a release so the Qt prune from #17 actually reaches users.

That work landed as `build:`, which release-please does not bump on, so the 77MB executable would sit on master until some unrelated `feat:`/`fix:` happened to ship it. A download dropping from **185MB to 77MB** is worth a release of its own.

It is also the first time the pruned **Linux AppImage** gets built — `release-build.yml` only runs on `release: published`, so `ci.yml` has never exercised the Linux spec change. If that build fails, the release publishes without binaries and therefore without `SHA256SUMS`; the updater already treats a missing manifest as "not ready yet" (`updater/feed.py`), so nothing breaks for existing users while it is fixed and rebuilt.

Empty commit carrying the `Release-As: 0.4.1` footer — **merge with squash so the footer survives into master**, or release-please will not see it.

author: ai-tachiuchia
body:
## What

Two related changes to the e-mail OTP error path.

**1. Recovers `d95cd7e`, stranded after PR #108.**

`auth-js` throws `AuthRetryableFetchError` for 5xx **before** parsing the response body (`fetch.ts` `handleError`), so `message` degrades to `JSON.stringify(Response)` === `"{}"` and `code` is undefined. The mapping keyed off message/code only, so during the 2026-07-09 SMTP outage (Resend rejected the configured credentials with 535, every OTP send died as an opaque 500) the Konto panel literally displayed `{}`.

Now keyed off `status` first — send path `>= 500` → the actionable "SMTP-Konfiguration prüfen" copy; verify path `>= 500` → a server-error message instead of blaming the user's code; `AuthRetryableFetchError` with no status (offline/DNS) → the network copy.

**2. Makes that mapping reachable at all** (Codex P1, `880f139`).

`throwForSupabaseError` discarded the Supabase error and threw a generic `AuthProviderActionError`, and `AccountPanel` renders that wrapper's message verbatim:

```ts
error instanceof AuthProviderActionError ? error.message : describeOtpSendError(error)
```

so the mapper fallback was unreachable for every real OTP failure — `describeOtpSendError`/`describeOtpVerifyError` were dead code in production.

`throwForSupabaseError(error, describe?)` now takes an optional mapper. The two OTP call sites pass the send/verify mappers; every other call site keeps the identical generic copy via the default parameter. `AccountPanel` is unchanged. No `cause` plumbing — that would change a shared constructor used at 8+ call sites for debugging metadata nothing here reads.

**This second defect is pre-existing** — it arrived with the provider-adapter layer, not with the cherry-picked commit. It's fixed here rather than deferred because without it change 1 has no runtime effect.

## Why change 1 was missing

Not a dropped merge. PR #108 merged at `2026-07-09T21:51Z` with head `f8094cf`; these commits were authored between `22:18Z` and `23:45Z` — work continued on a branch whose PR had already closed, and was never re-PR'd. Found while pruning stale local branches (`git cherry` plus a file-level diff against `main`).

Four further docs/skills commits are still stranded on `fix/auth-otp-handoff-and-error-copy` (including unshipped `supabase-live-debug` and `repo-catchup` skills); they need review against what has landed since and are deliberately **not** here.

## Tests

`authErrors.test.ts` covers the mapping; `authProviders.test.ts` adds both OTP paths through the adapter, the expired-code path (must not regress to the server-error copy), and one asserting a non-OTP call site still yields the exact pre-existing wording — that last one guards the default parameter, since a silently-generic default is how this bug stayed invisible. Mutation-checked: reverting the send call site fails the SMTP assertion.

**Not reproducible locally:** the live SMTP-outage path itself. It's covered by a unit fixture of the real `AuthRetryableFetchError` shape, not end to end.

## Gates

- `npx vitest run` — 963 passed, 1 skipped (documented baseline)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- `npm run lint` — 21 errors / 0 warnings (exact pre-existing baseline)
- `npx next build` — clean, all routes emitted

Closes the four open Dependabot alerts against `integration/`:

| Alert | Package | Severity |

author: keishis
body:
## 目的

Zed拡張の導入ロックに所有権の確認がなく、二つの処理が互いのロックを消す問題（#398）を
修正します。

## 現在の動作・結果

```
1. 処理Aがロックを取得し、ダウンロードに15分以上かかる。
2. 処理Bが古いロックとみなしてAのロックを消し、自分のロックを作る。
3. Aが終了し、Dropがロックを消す。これはBのロックである。
4. 三つ目の処理がロック無しとみなし、Bと同時に導入を始める。
```

`editors/zed/src/lib.rs`は、15分を過ぎたロックを所有者の確認なしに削除し、`Drop`も同じpathを
確認なしに削除していました。ロックの内容は作成時刻だけで、所有者を識別する値がありません。

## 期待する動作・結果

ロックを削除できるのは、そのロックを作った処理だけです。追い越された処理が終了しても、
後続のロックは残ります。

## 変更内容

- ロックへ書く行全体（作成時刻と一意な操作ID）を所有tokenとする
- `remove_lock_owned_by`が削除の直前に内容を照合する
- `Drop`が自分のtokenと一致する場合だけ削除する
- `stale_lock`を`lock_owner`へ置き換え、古いロックの所有者を返す
- 所有権の照合を固定するtestを2件追加

## 影響範囲

- [x] Language Server・Zed拡張

## 互換性と安全性

author: alex-morozov84
body:
First PR of the i18n/error-localization track. This is the **backend/shared half**: it makes English the base locale and removes the RU-centric starter defaults. `apps/web` still hardcodes Russian and is handled in follow-up PRs.

Russian remains a fully supported locale — `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` is unchanged apart from ordering, and a user who registers with `Accept-Language: ru` or an explicit `locale: "ru"` still gets Russian, as do all their emails and notifications.

## The actual problem

The default locale was re-declared in **six** places, so changing it in one would silently leave the others Russian:

| Location | Form |
|---|---|
| `packages/shared/src/constants/index.ts` | `DEFAULT_LOCALE` — the intended source of truth |
| `core/notifications/notifications.service.ts` | a local `const DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'ru'` shadowing it |
| `infrastructure/email/email.schema.ts` | a hardcoded `z.enum(['ru', 'en'])` |
| `core/organizations/invite.service.ts` | a `'ru'`-defaulting ternary |
| `notifications/channels/{email,telegram}-*.deliverer.ts` | two **verbatim copies** of a `toLocale()` helper |
| `core/auth/auth.service.ts` (x4) | inline `as 'ru' \| 'en'` casts |

Plus an unchecked `as SupportedLocale` cast in `notification-feed.service.ts` that blessed any stored string.

All now derive from `SUPPORTED_LOCALES`/`DEFAULT_LOCALE` via a new exported **`coerceSupportedLocale()`** — the non-throwing counterpart to the existing `parseSupportedLocale()`. The distinction matters: `parseSupportedLocale()` throws by design so bad stored data surfaces, but email/notification dispatch paths are best-effort and swallow errors, so using it there would have silently dropped invite emails on a locale anomaly.

## Defaults flipped

- `DEFAULT_LOCALE`: `ru` → `en`
- `User.locale` default: `ru` → `en`
- `User.timezone` default: `Europe/Moscow` → `UTC` — same reasoning; an English-base starter shouldn't assume Moscow time.

### Migration: no backfill, deliberately

The migration is `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DEFAULT` only. **Existing rows keep their stored values.** A stored value cannot be distinguished from a preference the user actually chose, so rewriting it would silently override real preferences. Recorded in the migration SQL and as a `CHANGELOG.md` upgrade note for forks with existing users.

Verified against the dev database after applying: column defaults now `'en'`/`'UTC'`, pre-existing row still `ru`/`Europe/Moscow`.

## Behavior change

An organization invite sent to an email with **no AMCore account** now renders in the base locale instead of always Russian. The recipient has expressed no preference; inheriting the inviter's locale would be a product setting, not a starter default.

## Test fix worth calling out

`email-verification.integration.spec.ts` was a **false green**. It was named "should render in Russian by default" but asserted only `'Александр'` and `'24 часа'` — both interpolated props, which render identically in every locale. It never verified the locale it claimed to, and would have stayed green under any default. It now asserts translated chrome in both directions, with a comment recording why props-only assertions are insufficient.

Other email specs had their default/explicit-locale tests swapped rather than deleted, preserving two-language coverage.

## Verification

typecheck · lint · build (467 files, 0 issues) · **2170** api unit · **40** email · **44** web unit · `auth` + `oauth` e2e (**107** tests) — all green.

Full local `test:e2e` was not run — it is documented as flaky under `--runInBand` locally; CI is the authoritative gate. The two suites whose assertions this touches were run in isolation.

## Not in scope

Left for a later PR in this track: the inline `7 days`/`7 дней` translation in `invite.service.ts` (bypasses the message catalogue, and `дней` is wrong for numbers like 2 or 21), and the stale `welcome.intro` backend email copy still advertising fitness/finance/subscriptions.

body:
Stacked on #190. Final sweep — answers "is anything left to remove?"

The live chat agent exposes **six** tools. Everything below was imported into `agents/tools/__init__.py` and referenced nowhere else, in production or tests:

| removed | why |
|---|---|
| `agents/tools/farmer_cached.py` (whole module) | `get_farmer_profile`, `get_herd_summary`, `list_animal_tags` — imported, never in `TOOLS`, zero test references |
| `search_videos` | never registered; only mentions were the import and a commented-out `Tool()` entry |
| `search_terms` | same |
| commented-out `Tool()` blocks and imports | `get_animal_by_tag`, `get_cvcc_health_details`, `get_farmer_by_mobile` |

### Kept, and why

- **`agents/tools/{animal,cvcc,farmer}.py`** stay. Their *tool wrappers* were commented out, but their *data* functions are live — `get_animal_data_by_tag` and `get_cvcc_health_data_by_tag` are called from `agents/farmer_context.py:7-8`. Only the unregistered wrappers went.
- **`agents/tools/terms.py`** stays. `get_ambiguity_hints_for_query` is on the chat path twice — the agent's dynamic system prompt and the pretranslation glossary — and is now covered by `tests/test_ambiguity_hints.py`.

### Verification

Live tool set is **identical before and after**: `check_loan_eligibility`, `create_ai_call`, `create_health_call`, `get_farmer_milk_collection_details`, `get_union_scheme_data`, `search_documents`.

**666 passed**, `import main` clean.

### What remains, deliberately

`app/services/translation.py`'s voice **channel mode** (`_is_voice_channel`, `VOICE_GU_PREFERRED_TRANSLATION_RULES`, the branches in `_post_normalize_gu_translation`). Verified working end to end, not a dangling fragment — but it is inline branching inside functions chat executes every turn, so removing it edits hot chat code rather than deleting dead code. Awaiting a decision on whether this repo should carry zero voice anything.

author: gdb3rys
body:
같은 질문("이 broadcast 를 누가 받나")을 두 코드가 따로 답하고 있었다.

    팀장님 @all    → `ownerDecision.broadcastTargets`   → 정식·활성 9명
    팀원 방 발언   → `inbox/messages.ts` 팬아웃         → `SELECT id FROM agent` = 11명

`agent` 표에는 `team_official_member`·`enabled` 컬럼이 **없다**. 그래서 팬아웃 쪽은 규칙을 적용할 방법 자체가 없었고, 두 값이 갈렸다. 꺼둔(`enabled:false`) 팀원에게도 수신행이 생겼다.

그리고 더 위층에 문제가 하나 더 있었다. **방 게시와 팀원 전달이 `broadcast` 한 단어에 묶여 있었다.** 팀원이 방에서 무슨 말을 하든 팀원 전원의 inbox 에 행이 생겼다.

## 무엇을 바꿨나

| 발신 | 방·슬랙 게시 | 팀원 inbox 전달 |
|---|---|---|
| `source=user` (팀장님) | 그대로 | **그대로 — 규칙에서 제외** |
| `source=system` (장애 통지 등) | 그대로 | **그대로 — 규칙에서 제외** |
| 팀원 방 발언 + `@all` | 그대로 | 정식·활성 팀원 전원 |
| 팀원 방 발언 (그 외) | **그대로** | **없음** |

팀에서 멘션·답장·sticky 사다리는 **팀장님 메시지에 답할 담당을 가리는 규칙**이고, 팀원끼리는 팀버스(`--to <id>`)로 한다. 방에서 팀원끼리 주고받는 일이 없으므로 팀원 방 발언의 예외는 `@all` 하나뿐이다.

수신자 판정은 `broadcastRecipientIds` 한 함수로 모았다. `@all` 마커 판정은 라우터의 기존 정본(`BROADCAST_MARKER_RE`)을 재사용한다 — 여기서 정규식을 새로 쓰면 그게 두 번째 판정이 되고, 그게 이 결함의 원인이었다.

## 효과 — 줄어드는 것은 깨움이 아니라 inbox 행이다

`wakeDispatcher` 에는 이미 "마커 없는 broadcast 는 inbox-only, 깨우지 않음" 게이트가 있다(2026-05-27). **멘션 없는 방 발언은 원래도 깨움이 0회였다.** 이 변경이 실제로 줄이는 깨움은 `@all` 의 11 → 9 뿐이다.

바뀌는 것은 **수신행**이다. 오늘 방 broadcast 82건 기준 902행 중 대부분이 사라진다 — 아무도 읽지 않던 행이다(오늘 방 broadcast 전체에서 `read_at` 이 채워진 것이 사실상 없다).

멘션 없는 방 발언 51건 중 **답이 달린 것은 0건**이었다. 이 축으로 잘라도 끊기는 대화가 없다. 다만 그 51건 중 상당수가 그날의 게이트 테스트 응답이라 평소보다 부풀어 있다 — 성격은 같지만 비율은 그날 특유다.

## 못 받게 되는 사람

`@all` 대상에서 `brief`(`enabled:false`) · `dex` · `forin` — 명부에서 정식 팀원이 아니다. 의도된 상태다.

**명부만 고치면 전 경로가 따라온다.** 코드도, 사람에게 묻는 것도 없다.

## 검증

- 전체 시험 실패는 **main 기준선과 동일**(신규 0). 절대 개수는 환경마다 달라 적지 않는다 — 실제로 두 검증자가 서로 다른 기준선 숫자를 봤다.
- 타입체크 신규 오류 0 (기존 7건은 이 변경과 무관한 `personaTemplates`·`inbox.ts` — main 에서도 같은 7건)
- 뮤턴트로 확인: 규칙을 DB 전원으로 되돌리기 · 슬랙 분기 제거 · 전달 통째 끄기 — 각각 시험이 잡는다

### 경계를 지키는 시험

`source=user`·`system` 은 이 변경에서 제외한다. **한 번 그 경계를 잘못 그어 4경로가 바뀌었다** — 주석에는 "안 건드린다" 고 써 있는데 슬랙 분기와 빈 배열 분기가 발신자를 보기 전에 걸렸다. 그중 **슬랙 스레드의 시스템 장애 통지가 0명**이 되는 것이 가장 나빴다.

지금은 분기 자체를 발신자별로 가르고, 그 네 경로를 시험으로 고정했다(기대값은 DB 에서 다시 계산 — 이름·숫자를 적지 않는다). **주석이 지키던 것을 이제 시험이 지킨다.**

### 검증 조건을 밝혀둔다

`agents.json` 은 gitignore 라 새 clone·워크트리·CI 에 **파일이 없다**. 그 상태에서는 이 변경의 결함이 **보이지 않는다** — 처음 두 번의 "신규 실패 0건" 보고가 그래서 틀렸다. 검수자가 파일이 있는 환경에서 돌려 14건 실패를 찾았다.

**위 수치는 `agents.json` 이 있는 상태에서 잰 것이다.** CI 만으로는 이 경로를 검증할 수 없다.

### 되돌아갈 자리를 시험으로 고정했다

- 팀원 방 발언에 멘션이 없으면 수신행 0, 그러나 **메시지는 저장된다**(두 축을 따로 잰다 — 겉보기가 같다)
- `@all` → 정식·활성 전원 · 명부 플래그를 켜면 팬아웃이 따라온다(판정이 둘이면 한쪽만 따라온다)
- **명부 파일이 없을 때** → `@all` 은 DB 로 되돌아가되 나머지는 0명(폴백이 판정 축을 삼키지 않는다)
- **플래그가 빈 명부**(공개 설치) → 전원
- 슬랙 스레드 → 수신행 0 (본문을 `@all` 로 두어 "슬랙이라서 0" 을 재게 했다)
- 팀원 경로가 0명이어도 **팀장님 메시지의 sticky 경로는 그대로 동작한다**
- wake allowlist 를 좁혀도 `@all` 대상이 안 바뀐다

마지막 두 개는 설계 논의 중 실제로 섞였던 지점이다.

### FK 위반을 막는다 — 0.3초짜리 창

명부(`agents.json`)가 정본이고 `agent` 표는 사본이다. 파일이 바뀌면 `watchRegistry` 가 300ms 뒤 동기화하므로 **어긋나는 창은 약 0.3초**다. 그 창에서 명부에만 있는 id 를 `message_recipient` 에 넣으면 FK 가 걸려 `insertMessage` 가 던지고, `acceptInbound` 에 try/catch 가 없어 그 요청이 500 이 된다.

드문 창이지만 교집합 한 줄로 닫히므로 닫았다 — 명부 id 를 DB 존재분과 교집합한다. (테스트에서 보이던 FK 실패는 실환경이 아니라 워크트리에 `agents.json` 이 없던 환경 문제였다.)

### 이번에 옮기지 않은 것

`broadcastAudience` 는 `lib/teamRouter/ownerDecision.ts` 에 있고, `db/inbox/messages.ts` 가 그것을 부른다. 순환은 없지만(정적·런타임 확인) **순환 없음은 경계가 맞다는 증거가 아니다** — 영속 계층이 라우터 모듈을 알게 된다. 중립 정책 모듈로 분리하는 편이 낫다는 검수 의견에 동의하나, 이번 범위("잘못된 DB 입력을 고치는 것")를 넘어 **후속 별건으로 남긴다.**

### 이번에 재지 않은 축

**실제 슬랙 POST·텔레그램 그룹 게시를 지나는 시험은 넣지 않았다.** 네트워크 경로 stub 설계가 필요해 이 PR 범위를 넘는다. 이 변경은 `message_recipient` 행만 건드리고 게시 경로는 `message_recipient` 에 의존하지 않는다(코드로 확인). 다만 **"수신자 0명" 과 "발송 실패" 는 겉보기가 같으므로**, 그 축을 자동으로 지키는 시험은 아직 없다 — 별건으로 남긴다.

## Summary

Registering a stdio MCP client via the management API causes Bifrost to exec an operator-supplied command as a subprocess of the gateway process. When dashboard authentication is disabled or unconfigured, requests to the management API are let through without any credential check — meaning this endpoint would otherwise allow unauthenticated remote code execution. This PR blocks stdio client registration in that state while leaving all other management endpoints unaffected, preserving the zero-config experience for non-dangerous operations.

## Changes

- Introduces a new context key `BifrostContextKeyAuthBypassed` that is set exclusively when a request is passed through because dashboard auth is unconfigured or disabled — distinct from `IsLocalAdminContextKey`, which is also set on genuinely authenticated sessions.
- The auth middleware now sets `BifrostContextKeyAuthBypassed = true` alongside `IsLocalAdminContextKey = true` in the unauthenticated bypass path.
- The `addMCPClient` handler checks this flag and returns `403 Forbidden` when `connection_type` is `stdio` and the request was not genuinely authenticated.
- The OpenAPI spec is updated to document the new `403` response on the client creation endpoint.
- Documentation clarifies that registering a stdio client requires an authenticated admin session, that immutable fields (`connection_type`, `stdio_config`, `auth_type`, `connection_string`) are ignored on edit, and adds the required `Authorization` header to curl examples.
- Tests cover that `BifrostContextKeyAuthBypassed` is set only when auth is nil or disabled, and is never set when auth is enabled but credentials are missing.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [x] Docs

## How to test

```sh
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/handlers/... -run TestAuthMiddleware_AuthBypassedFlag_SetOnlyWhenAuthUnconfiguredOrDisabled
go test ./...
```

**Manual validation:**

1. Start Bifrost with dashboard auth disabled or unconfigured.
2. Attempt to register a stdio MCP client via `POST /api/mcp/client` with `connection_type: "stdio"` — expect `403 Forbidden`.
3. Attempt to register an HTTP or SSE MCP client in the same state — expect success.
4. Enable dashboard auth, obtain a valid session token, and repeat step 2 — expect success.

## Breaking changes

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

`POST /api/mcp/client` with `connection_type: "stdio"` now returns `403` when dashboard authentication is disabled or unconfigured. Callers relying on registering stdio clients without authentication must either enable dashboard auth or provision the client via `config.json`.

## Security considerations

This change closes an unauthenticated remote code execution vector: without it, any network-reachable client could register a stdio MCP client and cause the gateway to exec an arbitrary command when dashboard auth is not configured. The fix is intentionally scoped to stdio only, preserving the zero-config management API experience for all other client types. The new `BifrostContextKeyAuthBypassed` context key provides a reusable signal for future handlers that need to gate similarly dangerous capabilities.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [x] I updated documentation where needed
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)
- [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

## Screenshots

**Der Platz am Marktpreis** – Angebot und Nachfrage im Gleichgewicht, 94 % Auslastung, 0,19 €/s.

![Übersicht](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paranerd/parking-sim/7f303df3f27c9e8b43120c8c288d9987265af717/docs/screenshots/01-uebersicht.png)

**Derselbe Platz, nur der Preis geändert** – links 1,20 €: 172 % Nachfrage, 42 % der Gäste werden abgewiesen, die Bewertung ist schon auf 3.7 gefallen. Rechts 4,50 €: die Nachfrage bricht auf 24 % ein, Plätze bleiben leer. Beide bringen mit 0,12 bzw. 0,11 €/s weniger als die 0,19 €/s am Marktpreis.

| Preis unter dem Marktpreis | Preis über dem Marktpreis |
|---|---|
| ![zu niedrig](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paranerd/parking-sim/7f303df3f27c9e8b43120c8c288d9987265af717/docs/screenshots/02-preis-zu-niedrig.png) | ![zu hoch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paranerd/parking-sim/7f303df3f27c9e8b43120c8c288d9987265af717/docs/screenshots/03-preis-zu-hoch.png) |

**Upgrades in drei Kategorien** – Kapazität, Nachfrage, Erlös; das Kassensystem nennt die aktuelle und die nächste Stufe.

![Upgrades](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paranerd/parking-sim/7f303df3f27c9e8b43120c8c288d9987265af717/docs/screenshots/04-upgrades.png)

**Neustart** und **Mobil**:

| Neustart-Dialog | Mobil |
|---|---|
| ![Neustart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paranerd/parking-sim/7f303df3f27c9e8b43120c8c288d9987265af717/docs/screenshots/05-neustart.png) | ![Mobil](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paranerd/parking-sim/7f303df3f27c9e8b43120c8c288d9987265af717/docs/screenshots/06-mobil.png) |

## Wirtschaftsmodell: Angebot, Nachfrage, Preis und Zahlungsbereitschaft

Der Parkplatz verfolgt keine einzelnen belegten Plätze mehr. Die Auslastung ist ein kontinuierlicher Anteil der Kapazität, der zu seinem Zielwert gleitet — der Gewinn fließt also, statt einem Zufallslauf aus An- und Abfahrten zu folgen.

```
Erlös/Std. = Kapazität × Auslastung × Preis × Zahlungsquote
Nachfrage  = Attraktivität × Tageszeit × Ruf × (Zahlungsbereitschaft / Preis) ^ 1,7
Auslastung = min(1, Nachfrage / Kapazität)
```

- **Preis senkt die Nachfrage** elastisch in beide Richtungen, begrenzt durch das Einzugsgebiet (`MAX_DEMAND_FACTOR`) — auch gratis kommen nur die Gäste, die vorbeifahren.
- **Stellplätze sind das Angebot** und deckeln die Auslastung.
- **Nachfrage-Upgrades**: LED-Beleuchtung, Reinigungsdienst und Werbung (unbegrenzt steigerbar, das Gegenstück zur Kapazität).
- **Zahlungsbereitschaft/Erlös**: Das Kassensystem beginnt bei der *Kasse des Vertrauens* (55 % zahlen) und geht über *Kassierer* und *Kassenautomat* bis zur *Kennzeichenerkennung* (99 %); die Überdachung hebt den Tarif, den Gäste akzeptieren.
- **Dauerhaft voll kostet Bewertungen**: Der abgewiesene Anteil drückt den Ziel-Ruf, der Ruf wirkt zurück auf die Nachfrage — mit langer Zeitkonstante, damit wirklich nur ein *dauerhaft* volles Haus schadet.
- **Der optimale Preis ist der Marktpreis**, bei dem Nachfrage auf Kapazität trifft: `W × (Attraktivität / Plätze) ^ (1/1,7)`. Er sinkt mit jedem gebauten Platz und steigt mit jedem Nachfrage- oder Komfort-Upgrade — kein fester Wert mehr.

Im Seitenpanel stehen jetzt Auslastung, Nachfrage, Zahlungsbereitschaft und Zahlungsquote sowie ein Hinweis, welcher Faktor gerade der Engpass ist.

**Balance:** Ein Testlauf über eine Spielstunde mit vernünftiger Strategie war zunächst nach ~15 Minuten am Ende — Kapazität allein bringt nichts, sobald das Einzugsgebiet ausgeschöpft ist. Deshalb ist Werbung unbegrenzt steigerbar und die Upgrade-Kosten sind neu justiert; jetzt wächst das Einkommen über die Stunde von 0,09 auf 0,45 €/s und alle drei Hebel werden gebraucht. Der Verlauf ist als Regressionstest festgehalten (`src/balance.test.ts`).

## Kontinuierlicher Gewinn

`advanceTime(seconds)` bucht alle stetigen Größen für beliebige Zeitscheiben (Uhr, Auslastung, Erlös, Ruf, Verschleiß) und läuft pro Animationsframe; `simulateTick()` würfelt nur noch einmal pro Sekunde Störungen aus. Abgerechnet wird die mittlere Auslastung der Scheibe, damit das Ergebnis nicht von der Schrittweite abhängt.

## Alte Spielstände

`loadGame()` baut den Zustand explizit aus bekannten Feldern auf und migriert dabei: umbenannte Upgrades (`restroom` → `cleaning`, `automation` → `payment`, `gate` → `shelter`), diskrete `occupied`-Plätze → kontinuierliche `occupancy`, unbekannte Schlüssel fallen weg.

## Test

- `npm test`: 36/36 grün — Nachfrage/Preis/Marktpreis, Kapazitätsgrenze, Bewertungs-Rückkopplung, Upgrade-Ketten, Offline-Ertrag und der Balance-Lauf.
- `tsc --noEmit` und `vite build` sauber.
- Im Chromium geprüft: Cash fließt sichtbar, der Preis steuert Nachfrage und Auslastung wie in den Screenshots, dazu Upgrade-Ketten, Filter, Neustart-Dialog und die Migration eines alten Spielstands.

`CLAUDE.md` hält die Arbeitsweise fest: Screenshots der relevanten Änderungen gehören immer in den PR.

body:
## Summary
`app/core/db.py`'s `_cfg()` does `yaml.safe_load(...)["database"]`, but `config.yaml` had no `database:` key at all — a hard `KeyError` at runtime, blocking `app/agents/agent_registry.py` (and anything else using `app.core.db.get_conn()`) from ever connecting.

- Adds a `database:` section to `config.yaml` (host/port/name/user/pool settings only — **no password**, since this file is committed to git)
- Adds a `_password()` helper in `db.py` that resolves the password from the `DATABASE_PASSWORD` env var (falling back to a `password:` key in config for local dev convenience), and raises a clear `RuntimeError` if neither is set
- `get_pool()` now calls `_password(cfg)` instead of the old `cfg["password"]` lookup
- Appends `DATABASE_PASSWORD=` (empty) to `.env.example`

## Verification (run locally)
- **Baseline confirmed first:** `_cfg()` raised `KeyError: 'database'`, and exactly 3 tests in `test_agent_mode.py` failed because of it, before any change was made
- After the fix:
  - `_cfg()` returns the parsed database config, no KeyError
  - `_password(cfg)` raises a clear `RuntimeError` ("Database password not configured...") when no password is set anywhere
  - `DATABASE_PASSWORD=testpass123` correctly resolves via the env var
  - The same 3 previously-KeyError-failing tests in `test_agent_mode.py` now fail with `psycopg2.OperationalError: connection ... Connection refused` instead — expected, since there's no live Postgres server in the CI/sandbox environment. That change in failure mode is the intended outcome of this PR, not a remaining bug.
- `py_compile app/core/db.py`: OK
- `ruff check app/core/db.py`: 6 style findings (import order, `SIM117` nested `with`, etc.) — same 6 already present on `main`'s version of this file, no new debt
- `config.yaml` still parses as valid YAML; `app/agents/agent_registry.py` still compiles
- Confirmed no real password was committed anywhere in `config.yaml` or `.env.example`

## Out of scope (intentionally not touched)
- `test_self_trainer.py`'s 3 failures: separate pre-existing issue (test still asserts against raw `sqlite3.connect()`, a leftover from before migrating to Postgres)
- `test_skill_forge.py`'s 5 failures: `chromadb` not installed in some sandboxes, unrelated to this fix

A live Postgres instance is still needed for `test_agent_mode.py`'s 3 DB-backed tests to actually pass end-to-end — that's outside this PR.

body:
## Breaking change

None.

## Proposed change

The gateway connection in `zhong-hong-hvac` can die silently: a status frame with an undefined fan speed value (`0x00`, observed after an indoor unit is switched off) crashes the library listener thread, and nothing restarts it. Entities then keep showing stale state forever with no health signal.

The library fix is in `zhong-hong-hvac` 1.0.16, bumped separately in #178412 (merged). This PR adds the component-side handling:

- polls every entity every 60 s so state self-heals even when the gateway stops pushing
- marks entities unavailable when the gateway connection is unhealthy (via `ZhongHongGateway.connected`)
- raises a translated `HomeAssistantError` when a control command cannot be sent, so a service call or automation no longer reports success for a command that never reached the gateway
- stops sending an invalid fan mode to the library when an unsupported value is requested

Rebased onto `dev` now that #178412 is merged, so this PR no longer touches the manifest or `requirements_all.txt` — the diff is the component change plus its tests.

## Type of change

- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] New integration (thank you!)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)
- [ ] Deprecation (breaking change to happen in the future)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Suggested changelog entry

`zhong_hong` entities are now marked unavailable when the gateway connection is unhealthy, are polled every 60 seconds, and raise an error when a command cannot be sent to the gateway.

## Testing

- SDK changes covered by unit tests in `crhan/ZhongHongHVAC` (12 passed, 1 skipped hardware test) and published as `zhong-hong-hvac` 1.0.16 on PyPI.
- Component test suite added (`tests/components/zhong_hong/`, 13 tests): setup, availability, scheduled polling, command-failure errors, unsupported fan mode.
- This component version has been running on a production Home Assistant 2026.7.2 container since 2026-08-01: entities report fresh status, fan modes map to HA standard values, and the connection self-recovers.
- `ruff`/`mypy`/`pylint` pass locally.

author: mcereal
body:
## Summary

- Channels created inside a `routine { }` are registered with the enclosing nursery and reclaimed at `sfn_nursery_exit`, closing a per-channel leak of a `pthread_mutex_t`, two `pthread_cond_t`, the ring buffer, and the handle.
- Fixes an `E0838` false positive that made **nested routines uncompilable** for both `Task<T>` and `Channel` handles — a live regression on `main`, not introduced by this branch.
- `sfn_nursery_exit` now closes a channel before destroying it, honoring the precondition `sfn_channel_destroy` documents.

Fixes SFN-688
Fixes SFN-696

## The leak (SFN-688)

`sfn_channel_destroy` was complete and correct but unreachable — nothing called it. Reclamation now hangs off the nursery, which already joins every child before returning, so teardown runs when no thread can still hold the handle.

Measured, fixture creating N nursery-scoped channels:

| fixture | channels | before | after | per-channel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| create + send + recv | 2k → 50k | 4,128 → 19,908 KB | 3,668 → 5,792 KB | 336 B → 44 B |
| create only | 2k → 50k | — | 3,528 → 3,616 KB | **1.8 B** |

The create-only fixture is flat across a 25× increase, so the handle, mutex, both condvars, and ring buffer are fully reclaimed. The residual in the send fixture is the pre-existing boxed-int channel-element leak, which predates this surface.

## Why the escape check is part of this PR

Reclamation is only sound if no handle outlives its nursery. Without that guarantee this change converts a bounded leak into a use-after-free — reproduced on an earlier revision of this branch as a segfault. SFN-694 landed the check on `main`; this PR fixes the false positive that shipped with it, and only then is the reclamation safe.

Concretely: because an escaping handle is now a compile error, unconditional registration at `sfn_channel_create` is sound **by construction**.

## The false positive (SFN-696)

`_sweep_nursery_escapes` flagged every parent-prefix binding carrying nursery provenance without asking *which* nursery bound it. A handle declared in an enclosing routine sits in an inner nursery's parent prefix as a matter of course, so any handle declaration followed by a nested `routine { }` falsely raised `E0838`.

| # | Shape | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | single routine, handle used locally | ok | ok |
| B | handle decl → nested routine (inner has a handle) | **E0838** | ok |
| C | handle decl → nested routine (inner has no handle) | **E0838** | ok |
| D | nested routine → handle decl (reverse order) | ok | ok |
| E | sibling non-nested routines | ok | ok |

The inner block's contents were irrelevant (C failed) and reversing the order silently passed (D), which is what made this easy to miss.

It affected **both** handle kinds. The `Task<T>` half came from SFN-446 and is live on `main` — `let h = spawn work(); routine { … } await h;` is rejected today. The fix snapshots parent-prefix provenance when a routine opens and sweeps only bindings that acquire it inside that routine. Genuine escapes are unaffected because a handle stored into a parent binding is flagged at the store site, not by the sweep.

## Recorded decision: unscoped channels

A channel created outside any `routine` — notably a module global, the idiomatic way to share one across tasks — is deliberately **not** reclaimed and lives until process exit. It is constructed before any nursery exists, so no scope end proves that no thread still holds it. Recorded in `sfn_nursery_register_channel`'s doc comment rather than left implicit.

## Scope notes

Two claims in the original issue did not survive contact with the tree:

- **AC1 ("registered and emitted")** assumed a lowering-side design. `sfn_channel_destroy` is reached runtime-internally via `sfn_nursery_exit`, so no `registry_services.sfn` row was added — one would be dead surface with no emitter. The intent (reachable, actually called) is met.
- **AC4 (ASAN leg)** asked for coverage alongside `concurrency_ownedbuf_asan_interleave_test.sfn`, but that leg runs `detect_leaks=0` and its own comment lists "a module-global `channel` is never destroyed" among the leaks that suppression exists to tolerate — it is structurally incapable of catching this. Replaced with a leak-**growth** comparison between a low-N and high-N run, so the known fixed leaks cancel out.

## Known limitation

A spawned task cannot currently reach a routine-scoped channel — capturing one checks green but fails to lower (`E1007`), and module globals are never registered. So the "destroy strictly after the joins" ordering is **defensive rather than load-bearing today**, and is not covered by a test, because no fixture can currently violate it. It becomes load-bearing as soon as capture lands, which is why the ordering and the close-before-destroy call are kept and commented.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `make compile` (self-host) | pass |
| `sfn fmt --check` on all touched files | clean |
| `channel_nursery_escape_test.sfn` | 6/6 |
| `channel_nursery_reclaim_test.sfn` | 2/2 (ASAN leg skips without compiler-rt) |
| `ownership_checker_test.sfn` | 124/124 |
| `task_join_all_test.sfn` | 22/22 — E0836/E0837/E0838 negatives still fire |
| 14 further concurrency/channel files | all pass |
| Total | **18 files, 203 cases, 0 failures** |

Genuine escapes verified still rejected after the fix (module-global reassignment, and the aliased `let ch = channel(4); g_ch = ch;` form) — a fix that over-corrected would look green on the false positives while silently dropping real escapes.

## Files Changed

- `runtime/sfn/concurrency/nursery.sfn` — channel registry on `Nursery` (104 → 128 B), `sfn_nursery_register_channel`, close+destroy after the join barrier
- `runtime/sfn/concurrency/channel.sfn` — register the handle with the current nursery at creation
- `compiler/src/ownership_checker.sfn` — scope the escape sweep to the binding's own nursery
- `compiler/tests/e2e/channel_nursery_escape_test.sfn` — nested-routine regression cases for both handle kinds
- `compiler/tests/e2e/channel_nursery_reclaim_test.sfn` — churn + leak-growth coverage
- `docs/status.md` — `channel()` row: reclamation, the escape gate, the module-global carve-out, and the `sfn_channel_create` ABI (third `owned` param was missing)

## Unrelated failure

The advisory `linux-arm64` self-host leg fails on corrupted IR emission in `http.sfn` (a stray `U+FF47` at line 3891 of the generated `.ll`). Present before this branch and untouched by it.

author: zechengz
body:
## What

`commands/spec/builtins.ts` held all 93 command specs in one 1,189-line table, while Python splits the same specs across nine family modules. TypeScript now mirrors that layout.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `builtins.ts` | 1,189 lines, all 93 specs | 29 lines, façade only |
| `builtin_specs/` | — | 9 family modules + aggregator |

Families match Python one for one: `archive`, `fs_mutate`, `hashing`, `listing`, `net`, `runtime`, `search`, `text_proc`, `viewing`. The aggregator raises on a duplicate name the same way Python's `__init__` does, and `builtins.ts` still exports `specOf` and `BUILTIN_SPECS`, so no caller changes.

The command-to-family assignment was taken by importing Python's modules rather than reassigned by hand. The two key sets already agreed exactly at 93 names, with nothing on either side alone.

## This is a pure move, and that is checked rather than asserted

Regenerating the spec dump from the split code produces **byte-identical JSON** for all 93 commands in both the node and browser outputs. Zero drift.

That is the parity gate from #666 doing the job it was built for, and it is not vacuous: deleting a single spec fails generation with `no builtin spec: wget`.

Preserved deliberately: the null-prototype freeze on `BUILTIN_SPECS`, so a script-controlled name like `toString` still misses instead of resolving an `Object.prototype` member.

## Verification

- spec regeneration: byte-identical, zero drift
- spec parity gate: 93 commands match
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- core: 541 files / 5,703 tests
- node: 202 files / 1,853 tests
- browser: 44 files / 181 tests
- pre-commit: exit 0

- Adds `contracts/nft-contract/examples/mint-from-backend.ts`, a runnable reference implementation for preparing a ClipCash NFT mint transaction from a Node.js backend context. Takes `--clip-id`, `--wallet`, and `--source` (the admin account, since the contract's `mint` requires `admin.require_auth()` on-chain — see `src/lib.rs`), and prints the unsigned transaction XDR to stdout.

The existing `mint()` stub is left untouched for callers that just want a mock boolean.
- References the script from `POST /nfts/prepare-mint`'s Swagger description, for developers integrating outside the REST API.

**Note:** stacked on #714 (repairs build-breaking merge corruption already on `main`). Includes that diff until it merges — the #694-specific work is `contracts/nft-contract/bindings/clips-nft-contract.ts`, `contracts/nft-contract/examples/mint-from-backend.ts` (new file), and one description line in `src/nft/nft.controller.ts`.

## Summary
- Added `Group.closedAt DateTime?` (migration `20260801112214_add_group_closed_at`) and an owner-only `closeGroup` command.
- Closing stops new check-ins from counting toward the crew's leaderboard from that point on — `scoreCrew`/`getCrewBoard` now take `closedAt` as an upper-bound cutoff, mirroring the existing per-member `joinedAt` lower bound.
- Closing also blocks new members from joining via the invite code (`joinGroup` now rejects non-members when `closedAt` is set), per the issue's own recommendation.
- Existing stats/members are untouched; members keep logging normally everywhere else in the app.
- UI: a "Close crew" action for the owner (confirmation via `window.confirm`, consistent with the #157 leave-crew pattern), and a "Closed" badge replacing "Live" on both the crew list and detail page.

**Note:** this branch and #157 (leave-crew UI) both independently add an `ownerId` field to `CrewDetail` in `lib/queries/groupQueries.ts` and touch the same crew detail page — expect a trivial merge conflict between them (one addition collapses into the other) depending on merge order.

## Summary
- Root-caused a brief (~300ms) flash of the real Google/email sign-in form on cold app open for an already-logged-in user (reported with PIN disabled, but unrelated to PIN — it's a Firebase-Auth-session-check timing issue). `js/auth.js`'s `onAuthStateChanged` handler unconditionally removed the `lock-screen-checking` class (which keeps `.auth-card` masked with `display:none` while the persisted-session check resolves) before branching on signed-in vs signed-out.

# Summary

完成 Part 02 第三章《Prompt Builder》（TASK-0009，draft）——回答"Runtime 为什么需要 Prompt Builder"。**不是 Prompt Engineering**（零技巧 / Few-shot / CoT 内容）。

## 整章主线

> Prompt Builder 是 Runtime 的一个组件，不是 Prompt 技巧。它负责把 Runtime 中各种输入稳定组装成一次模型调用的最终 Model Context。

## 章节结构（4.1 ~ 4.9）

- 4.1 Runtime 为什么需要 Prompt Builder（Q1/Q2：组装是每轮高频多源动作；散落代码=不可版本/测试/审计；Demo 为隐式实现的诚实标注）
- 4.2 Prompt Builder 输入（Q6：七输入表；**Policy / Runtime Configuration 决定，Builder 执行**）
- 4.3 Prompt Builder 输出（Q7：产出可发送的输入结构——Prompt Instance / messages / request payload；从架构语义看构成 Model Context，可能含 tool definitions / call configuration / policy metadata；不锁死为单一对象）
- 4.4 Prompt Template（Q8：Template → Instance → 语义上的 Context 三阶段）
- 4.5 Prompt Version（Q3/Q5：Prompt 是行为配置/行为契约的一部分，不等同 State Schema 数据契约；Version / Rollback / Review / Regression / Audit；**Builder unit test 与 Prompt regression test 分离**；最小审计元数据集合）
- 4.6 Prompt Builder 属于 Runtime（Q9：执行清单 vs 不能清单——不制定策略、不拥有权限治理判断权、版本由配置/发布策略选定）
- 4.7 Prompt Builder 与未来能力（Q10：挂载点表；RAG 收窄——Retrieve/Rank/Filter 不属于 Builder，只接收筛选后的 retrieved context）
- 4.8 常见误区（6 条）
- 4.9 总结（Q1-Q10 答案表 + 验收标准 + 边界）

## 新增 Mermaid（4 张）

1. Builder 在 Runtime 中的位置（Control Plane 内，策略层约束）
2. Builder 输入来源（七输入）
3. Template → Instance → 语义上的 Model Context
4. Prompt Version 生命周期（v1 → 变更 → Review → Regression → v2 → 回滚）

## 写作约束落实

- 零 Prompt Engineering / Memory / Checkpoint / Interrupt / Reducer / LangGraph API / RAG / MCP / A2A / Observability / Evaluation
- 显式标注推论：Demo 无显式 Builder（Runtime 逻辑抽象，隐式实现）
- 零新增代码；统一引用 Ch01/02/03 与 architecture-map，不复制定义

- 新增：ch04-prompt-builder.md、TASK-0009
- 修改：mkdocs.yml、Part 02 index、ROADMAP、content-map、current.md

- `mkdocs build --strict` ✅
- `pytest` ✅（数量以最新 CI 为准）
- `ruff check .` ✅
- Working tree clean ✅

## Remaining

- Architecture Review（重点：Builder 输出表述 / Policy-Builder 边界 / 行为契约与数据契约区分 / 两类测试分离 / 审计最小集合 / RAG 挂载点）

author: munix26
body:
## Summary

The drop list on the item detail panel only named the creature and where it lives, which said nothing about whether the item was actually reachable. Each row now also carries:

- **HP**
- **Bestiary difficulty**, colour-coded Harmless → Challenging
- **Level of the spawns** the creature appears in

Levels are derived from the hunting places that list the creature, shown as a **range** when it spans areas of different difficulty — Blightwalker reads `100–300` because it lives in both Pits of Inferno and Roshamuul Prison. A single number means every spawn it appears in agrees. 830 of the 1,304 indexed creatures resolve to a level; the rest are bosses and raid creatures belonging to no hunting place, shown as `—`.

## Why not estimate the missing ones

I fitted level against HP over the 770 known pairs (`level ≈ 1.13 × hp^0.565`) and it lands at **44% median error, 75% at p75** — Werelion would read 100 instead of 250. A number that wrong reads as data while being noise, so the gap is left visible instead.

Also fixed: using `min()` across spawns made Demon look like a level-35 creature because it appears in one low-level mixed spawn. The range makes that spread visible rather than hiding it behind a misleading single value.

## Verified in a browser

Demonic Essence opens with all 79 sources; the table shows Hellgorak 25,850 HP lvl 100, Blightwalker 8,100 HP Hard lvl 100–300, Bones 9,500 HP lvl — (raid creature, no spawn). No JS errors.
