author: ziagl888
body:
## Summary

Two hygiene follow-ups from the z-code-reviewer verdict on T-185 (PR #170). **Both parts are delivered.** Part 1 (the name guard) is unchanged and already reviewed; Part 2 was added in a follow-up commit, which also **corrects a factual claim** the earlier version of this PR made about why Part 2 was skipped — see below.

| | |
|---|---|
| Task | T-2026-KYT-9050-057 |
| Live effect | none — no register flip, no artifact promoted, `core/shadow_gate.py` untouched |
| New | `tools/promotion_guard.py`, `backtest/test_promotion_guard.py` (24 tests), `tools/retag_artifact.py`, `backtest/test_epd3_artifact_model_id.py` (4 tests) |
| Touched | `tools/bot_variants/index.py` (+1 accessor), `tools/verify_staging_artifacts.py` (check 8), `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `docs/STAGING_VERIFICATION.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `AUDIT_TODO.md`, `staging_models/epd3_model_SHORT.pkl` (re-dumped) |

## Part 1 — challenger promotion name guard (done)

A challenger promotion is two steps: flip the register line in `core/shadow_gate.py` from `SHADOW` to `LIVE`, and copy the artifact into the repo root. `shadow_artifact_path` returns the **bare root filename** for a LIVE leg, and `SHADOW_ARTIFACTS` historically carries the retrain *generation* filename rather than the tag's own:

```python
"RUB3": {"LONG": "rub2_model_LONG.pkl"}   # tag RUB3, file rub2_*
```

Promoting such a leg drops the challenger file into exactly the slot the **legacy loader** reads — both tags then score the same model and post it twice (hard rule 4, real money). That was live for **EPD3-SHORT** on 2026-07-21 (`epd2_model_SHORT.pkl` is bot 10's `EPD2_ARTIFACT_PATHS["SHORT"]`) and was averted **by hand** with the challenger-distinct name `epd3_model_SHORT.pkl`; the same handwork was repeated for **EPD3-LONG** in T-037.

`tools/promotion_guard.py` automates that handwork. For every leg in `SHADOW_ARTIFACTS` it checks whether the promotion target is challenger-distinct, and otherwise names the foreign owner plus the rename to apply (`RUB3 → rub3_model_LONG.pkl`).

**Why this shape (the brief offered two options — guard vs. naming convention):** both, but with different jobs. The *ownership* check is the hard evidence (another loader really does read that slot); the *tag-prefix* convention is the second, independent criterion that also catches a loader missing from any registry, and it is what generates the concrete rename suggestion. Together they reproduce the T-037 decision mechanically instead of relying on somebody remembering it.

**Severity comes from the lifecycle, not from the filename:**

| Case | Severity |
|---|---|
| leg is **LIVE** and the filename belongs to a foreign tag | **FAIL** (exit 1, promotion stop) |
| leg is SHADOW/SILENT/RETIRED, name not challenger-distinct | WARN — latent blocker before the next flip |
| a staging **file** is claimed by >1 tag | WARN per file (intent is not readable from a filename) |

So the guard is green today and turns red exactly when someone flips a leg to LIVE without the rename. Today's only finding: `RUB3-LONG` (WARN), parked on SHADOW since T-037.

**Wired in three places:** pre-commit hook `kythera-promotion-name-guard` (blocks that commit), check 8 in `tools/verify_staging_artifacts.py` (register scan at the end + per-file WARN), and the CLI.

**Shared-code discipline (hard rule 7):** `core/shadow_gate.py` is **not** modified. It is imported by the bots *and* by trainer/replay; changing what `shadow_artifact_path` returns would move serving behaviour on both sides. The guard reads the register, it never writes to it (pinned by a test). Every caller was enumerated before deciding this — `load_shadow_artifact` in bots 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 and 31, plus `tools/bot_variants/index.py`; none of them see a behaviour change.

The tag→filename bridge is **reused** from `tools/bot_variants/index.py` via a new public `legacy_artifact_slots()` accessor instead of curating a second registry that would drift. The diff to that file is purely additive (one function, `build_index`/`render_markdown` untouched), so the generated index output is unchanged by this PR. Separately: `python -m tools.bot_variants.index --check` **already** reports drift in `docs/bot_variants_index.md` / `model_archive/index.json` — verified identical against the pristine `index.py` at `HEAD~1`, i.e. pre-existing (artifacts moved root↔staging since the last regeneration). Not regenerated here to keep this diff to the guard.

## Part 2 — EPD3-SHORT `model_id` re-dump (delivered) + a correction

**First, the correction.** The earlier version of this PR argued Part 2 could not be done here because *"the embedded `IsotonicRegression` was pickled with scikit-learn 1.9.0, while the Fleet-Python 3.13 environment on this host has 1.7.1"*. That is **inverted relative to the actual measurement**. Re-measured on this host:

| | |
|---|---|
| `py -3.13` (fleet) | sklearn **1.7.1**, xgboost 3.1.2 |
| `py -3.14` | sklearn **1.9.0** |
| `epd3_model_SHORT.pkl` embedded `_sklearn_version` | **1.7.1** |
| `joblib.load(...)` under py 3.13 | **zero warnings** — no `InconsistentVersionWarning`, no skew |

That artifact was pickled *with* the fleet version. A re-dump under `py -3.13` is a **same-version round-trip**, not a downgrade. The file that really carries 1.9.0 is **`epd3_model_LONG.pkl`** (dumped in the 3.14 env during T-037) — the argument was true, but about the other artifact. The second half of the old reasoning (a real retrain needs DB + replay labels + CPU) is correct, but answers a question the task did not ask: the task says *"rebuild ONLY with Fleet-Python 3.13 (not 3.14, else dump-version mismatch)"*, which is a statement about **re-serialisation**, not about retraining.

**What was delivered.** `tools/retag_artifact.py` loads a format-A dict artifact, sets **only** `meta.model_id`, and writes into `staging_models/`. Two guards, neither of them optional:

1. **Hard rule 2** — the target must resolve inside STAGING. Promoting into the repo root is Michi's decision, never part of a tool run. A `--out` pointing anywhere else aborts.
2. **Version parity** — the artifact must load *warning-free* under the running interpreter. sklearn reports a serialisation skew itself: `InconsistentVersionWarning` carries `original_sklearn_version`. On a hit the tool refuses and names the interpreter under which the re-dump would be clean. This is precisely the guard that would have prevented the inverted claim above, and it **fires on `epd3_model_LONG.pkl`** (refused: *"pickled with sklearn 1.9.0, this interpreter runs 1.7.1"*).

After writing, the tool re-loads the result and diffs it against the source — `predict_proba` on a fixed probe matrix, the isotonic calibrator curve over a 101-point grid, feature list, threshold, full meta — and reports success only for **exactly one** difference. Re-running it produces a byte-identical file.

```
python 3.13.12 · sklearn 1.7.1 · xgboost 3.1.2
  staging_models\epd3_model_SHORT.pkl  (meta.model_id 'EPD2' -> 'EPD3')
  Verifiziert: genau EIN Unterschied zur Quelle — meta.model_id: 'EPD2' -> 'EPD3'
```

**The promoted root artifact `epd3_model_SHORT.pkl` is untouched** — hash unchanged in this worktree and in the live checkout. The root promote stays an operator decision (hard rule 2) and was never part of this task.

**Why this matters even though it is inert live:** bot 10 loads EPD3 through `shadow_gate.load_shadow_artifact`, which normalises to `{model, features, threshold}` and never reads `model_id`. But `core.model_artifacts.build_contract` — the loader the *live* bots use — takes the posting tag **only** from `meta.model_id`, and `tools/verify_staging_artifacts.py` checks exactly that field (check 3, HR-6). Anything going through the shared loader would have attributed this artifact to the previous generation.

### Two remainders, stated rather than papered over

- **`epd3_model_LONG.pkl` has the same tag defect and is not re-dumpable here.** Pickled with sklearn 1.9.0

author: thpoll83
body:
Establishes `perf/baselines/split72.json` so perf runs stop saying *"No baseline recorded yet"* and start producing a comparison table.

Source: `workflow_dispatch` run [30697375539](https://github.com/thpoll83/qmk_firmware/actions/runs/30697375539) on `PolyKybd` (fw 0.9.84). The **exact** `perf-report.json`, unedited, as `perf/baselines/README.md` requires.

## Validated before adopting

Per the new `measure-firmware-perf` skill — a bad run must never become the reference:

- `timing.ready_gate_ok` **and** `timing.settled` both true → it did not measure the master's boot-time busy window.
- `ovl_iters == reports` in both bursts (48==48, 8==8) → one bulk overlay report produced exactly one tagged iteration, so the instrumentation is sound.
- `console_tail` lines are **complete** — which doubles as the on-hardware confirmation that the console-reassembly fix (#48) works:
  ```
  LoopProf: iters=3329 ovl=8 worst=3ms(ovl br=2ms rn=0ms)
    ovltot wall=16ms bridge=2ms render=0ms rest=14ms
  ```

## Reproducibility

Against the previous run on a *different build* (0.9.83):

| metric | run 1 | run 2 | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| plain worst iteration | 36.99 ms | 36.84 ms | −0.4% |
| plain overlay wall | 261.25 ms | 263.01 ms | +0.7% |
| plain render | 166.40 ms | 166.29 ms | −0.1% |
| plain bridge | 12.17 ms | 12.15 ms | −0.2% |
| HID p50 | 3.97 ms | 3.91 ms | −1.5% |
| idle loop rate | 1109.3 /s | 1115.7 /s | +0.6% |

Sub-1% on every headline metric across two separate flashes. That is what makes these worth freezing, and it suggests the ±15% tolerance is comfortably generous.

## ⚠️ One known false-positive risk

`idle.worst_iter_ms` moved **2.85 → 3.48 ms (+22%)** between these two otherwise-identical runs. It is a **single-sample maximum over a 3 s window** — the noisiest statistic in the report — and it *is* in `TRACKED_METRICS`, so it will occasionally report a spurious regression at the 15% tolerance.

`long_iters_ge_10ms` (0 in both runs) is the better idle-health signal: it counts every iteration long enough to swallow a key tap, rather than reporting one outlier.

I've documented this in the commit rather than changing the metric set unilaterally — dropping `idle.worst_iter_ms` from `TRACKED_METRICS` (or replacing it with the long-iteration count) is a one-line change if you'd like it. Worth deciding before the first spurious ⚠️ trains people to ignore the table.

body:
## 概要 (What)

ビジュアル設計器が**自分の出力で図種を誤判定され、別図種のデザイナーへルーティングされる**問題を修正します。アプリ全体課題監査で確定した **HIGH の 4 件目**です。

## 目的・背景 (Why)

図種はテキスト内容だけで判定していましたが、**要素を削るほど判定材料が減り**、残ったキーワードが他図種と綴りを共有すると持ち主を決められません。Design タブを開き直しただけで別の設計器が現れ、**自分の図が編集できなくなる**（未対応ロック）か、**黙って別図種として編集が続く**状態でした。実測された誤ルーティング:

| 図 | 残った内容 | 誤判定先 |
|---|---|---|
| 配置図 | `database` ノードだけ | SEQUENCE |
| 配置図 | `component` ノードを含む | COMPONENT（`node` があっても先取りされる） |
| 配置図 | `rectangle`/`folder`/`frame` だけ | CLASS（既定へ脱落） |
| ユースケース図 | アクターだけ | SEQUENCE |
| ER 図 | 列なしエンティティだけ | SEQUENCE |
| どの図種でも | 全要素を削除 | CLASS |

- [x] バグ修正 (Bug fix)
- [ ] 新機能 (Feature)
- [ ] 破壊的変更 (Breaking change)

- [ ] ドキュメント (Docs)

## 変更内容の詳細

**2 層で防ぎます。テキスト形式は一切変えていません。**

1. **`SketchPane.resolveType`（主軸）**: **いま表示中の設計器でそのテキストを完全に扱える（未対応行ゼロ）なら図種を維持**し、扱えないときだけ内容判定へ委ねます。`component X` は配置図とコンポーネント図で完全に同一、空の図は手がかりゼロ — **内容だけでは原理的に判別できないケース**をこれで救います。本当に別図種へ書き換えた場合は現在のコーデックが未対応を報告するため、意図どおり切り替わります。

author: kateinoigakukun
body:
`WASIHostFunction` stored its implementation as a closure taking
`any GuestMemory`. Embedded Swift cannot specialize the generic guest-memory
accessors through an existential, so all 42 preview1 implementations failed to
compile there.

Parameterize `WASIHostFunction` and `WASIHostModule` on the memory type instead.
Callers already know it statically: `WasmKitWASI` resolves the guest's `memory`
export, which is always `WasmKit.Memory`.

The generic parameter needs `SendableMetatype` as well as `GuestMemory`,
otherwise the `@Sendable` implementation closures fail on capturing `M.Type`.

With this, `Sources/WASI` compiles for `riscv32-none-none-eabi`.

## Stack

Reviewable in order; each PR targets the one above it. Merge bottom-up.

1. #404 Decouple WASIFile from GuestMemory
1. #406 Make the WASI host module table generic over guest memory **← this PR**
1. #407 Allow linking a subset of the WASI preview1 surface
1. #408 Decouple WASIDir from its associated iterator type
1. #409 Cover WASI in the embedded check and strip unused code
1. #410 Run a WASI guest on emulated hardware in the ESP32 example

#401, #402 and #403 were the first three layers and are merged.

One more branch continues this locally: running the GDB stub on emulated
hardware and driving it with a real lldb. It will be opened once these land.

Unrelated but worth landing first: #405 fixes a debugger crash that makes
`CLICommandsTests` fail intermittently on Linux. It is the cause of the red
runs these PRs will otherwise keep hitting.

GitHub's native stacked PRs are not yet available for this repository, so the
chain is expressed through base branches instead.

author: kateinoigakukun
body:
The host module table built all 42 implementations from a single dictionary
literal, so every one stayed referenced and no linker could drop the unused ones.
On a device with a couple of hundred KB of RAM, that means paying for all of WASI just
to write to stdout.

Split the table into capability groups and represent a capability as a value
carrying its own registrar. An `OptionSet` would not work: its dispatch function
has to test every case, so it references every registrar and defeats stripping
just as thoroughly.

```swift
bridge.link(to: &imports, store: store, capabilities: [.stdio, .clocks, .random])
```

Guests import a fixed list regardless of what they call at runtime, so linking a
subset would otherwise fail to instantiate on an import the guest never uses.
`stubUnlinked` fills the gaps from a table of names and types that references no
implementation, and defaults to on.

`link(to:store:)` keeps its previous behaviour: all capabilities, plus the stubs
that were previously always defined.

Stripping also needs `-Xfrontend -function-sections`, which arrives later in the
stack along with the measurements.

## Stack

Reviewable in order; each PR targets the one above it. Merge bottom-up.

1. #404 Decouple WASIFile from GuestMemory
1. #406 Make the WASI host module table generic over guest memory
1. #407 Allow linking a subset of the WASI preview1 surface **← this PR**
1. #408 Decouple WASIDir from its associated iterator type
1. #409 Cover WASI in the embedded check and strip unused code
1. #410 Run a WASI guest on emulated hardware in the ESP32 example

#401, #402 and #403 were the first three layers and are merged.

One more branch continues this locally: running the GDB stub on emulated
hardware and driving it with a real lldb. It will be opened once these land.

Unrelated but worth landing first: #405 fixes a debugger crash that makes
`CLICommandsTests` fail intermittently on Linux. It is the cause of the red
runs these PRs will otherwise keep hitting.

author: kent-tokyo
body:
## Summary

Audit-only Wave 2C follow-up to PR #229 (Wave 2B), which split the 18 pinned `EZ_SHARED_CANDIDATE_BOND_RESIDUALS` fixtures (`crates/chematic-smiles/src/canonical.rs`) into 10 `EZ_SHARED_CARRIER_FULLY_RESOLVED` and 8 `EZ_SHARED_CARRIER_RING_CONSTRAINED_RESIDUALS`. This PR **empirically tests** the hypothesis documented above the latter constant — that every residual's coupled component includes an alkene end whose own double bond is *endocyclic* in a small ring — and measures the corpus-wide blast radius of 3 candidate production gating rules.

**No production code was changed.** Only a new read-only Rust example, a new Python diagnosis script, a new doc, and their generated `validation/results/*` output.

## What was built

- `crates/chematic-smiles/examples/ez_ring_constrained_residual_audit.rs` — read-only example emitting one JSON row per stereo-alkene end (coupled and singleton), with ring membership, endocyclic-vs-exocyclic classification, and whether canonicalization placed a directional marker. Atom correspondence across the canonicalize→reparse round trip is recovered via composition of the public `canonical_atom_order` API (verified per molecule, never assumed — 6/1,387 rows fail verification and are flagged `null`, not guessed).
- `scripts/ez_ring_constrained_residual_diagnosis.py` — drives the Rust example via `cargo run`, cross-checks every row against a live RDKit 2026.03.3 oracle (`FindPotentialStereo`, `AssignStereochemistry`), with explicit atom-index-correspondence verification before trusting any RDKit verdict (0/1,387 failures). Self-test included (`--self-test`), including a positive control reproducing the fixture-1 culprit/partner RDKit split.
- `docs/ez_ring_constrained_residual_audit.md` — full write-up, cross-referenced from `docs/canonical_smiles_residual_rfc.md`'s issue-#149 section and `validation/README.md` (per issue #216's convention).
- `validation/results/ez_ring_constrained_residual_audit.jsonl` (1,387 rows) + `..._summary.json`, generated from `scripts/descriptor_census_corpus.smi` (committed corpus, no external download).

## Classification of the 8 residual fixtures (individual, never pooled)

All 8/8 confirmed: each has a coupled pair where one end's own double bond is endocyclic (RDKit independently reports `STEREONONE`, absent from `FindPotentialStereo`) and the other is genuinely, independently stereogenic (real `STEREOE`/`STEREOZ`). 7 of 8 have a 6-membered culprit ring; fixture 8 (`CCO/C(O)=C(\C1=NCCN1)c1nnc(N)s1`) has a 5-membered imidazoline culprit with a fully acyclic (not just exocyclic) partner — a structurally distinct shape, called out explicitly.

**A real, non-overclaimed finding**: the identical endocyclic-culprit shape is *also* present in 5 of the 10 already-`EZ_SHARED_CARRIER_FULLY_RESOLVED` fixtures — the hypothesis is **necessary but not sufficient**. An unidentified second factor governs why those 5 still converge while the 8 don't (checked for an ortho/meta/para phenyl-symmetry pattern; none found). The other 5 of the 10 resolved fixtures use a completely different, unrelated coupling mechanism (both ends genuinely stereogenic — `hypothesis_holds = False`).

## Blast-radius table (5,000-mol corpus, 1,387 stereo-alkene ends, 995 molecules, 62 coupled ends / 31 coupling components)

Each rule measured independently, never combined:

| Rule | Ends excluded | % | Excl. & marked (confirmed / incl. unknown*) | Excl. & coupled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a1) end atom in ring size < 7 | 901 | 65.0% | 62 / 68 | 52 |
| (a1) end atom in ring size < 8 | 959 | 69.1% | 62 / 68 | 52 |
| (a2) **double bond endocyclic** in ring size < 7 | 783 | 56.5% | 10 / 16 | 6 |
| (a2) **double bond endocyclic** in ring size < 8 | 837 | 60.3% | 10 / 16 | 6 |
| (b) RDKit: bond absent from `FindPotentialStereo` | 933 | 67.3% | 10 / 16 | 6 |
| (c) (b) restricted to endocyclic bonds | 837 | 60.3% | 10 / 16 | 6 |

\* "incl. unknown" credits 6 rows where chematic's own atom-correspondence check failed (marker status genuinely unknown, not assumed unmarked) — reported as a range, not a single possibly-too-low number.

Key findings, each verified directly:
- **Rule (a1)** ("atom merely sits in a small ring") is badly over-inclusive (65–69% of the whole corpus) — ring membership of the *atom* is the wrong predicate; ring membership of the *double bond itself* (endocyclic) is what matters.
- **Rule (a2) at threshold 8 and rule (c) agree on every single row of the corpus (0/1,387 mismatches)** — strong support for "ring size < 8," though the corpus has a real data gap (observed endocyclic ring sizes: `{4,5,6,7,16,21,24,29}`, nothing 8–15) — the exact cutover point beyond "≤7 excluded, ≥16 included" also relies on a hand-built cyclooctene control, not corpus data alone.
- **Rule (b) is genuinely broader than rule (c)** (933 vs 837, a real 96-end difference, spot-verified as unrelated symmetric-substituent exclusions like guanidine, not a ring effect) — they do **not** coincide.
- Only **6 of the corpus's 62 coupled ends (3 of 31 coupling components)** are excluded by the recommended rule — a structurally *different* shape than the fixtures (both ends endocyclic in a fused polycyclic cage family, not one-endocyclic-one-free). The ring-endocyclic mechanism explains all 8 pinned fixtures individually but only ~10% of this corpus's general coupled-end population — issue #149 covers more than this one mechanism.
- 5 of the 18 pinned fixtures (all from the unrelated "both-real" family) are literally present in the corpus, verified via exact-string set intersection — not fully disjoint sample sets as an earlier draft of this audit assumed.

## Recommended predicate (NOT implemented — specification only)

```text
exclude a stereo-alkene end when: some SSSR ring contains BOTH atoms of its
own C=X double bond (endocyclic), AND the smallest such ring has < 8 atoms
```

## Verdict: CONDITIONAL GO

Confirmed for all 8 residuals individually, with unusually clean RDKit agreement (0/1,387 row-level mismatches) supporting the concrete threshold. **Not an unconditional GO** for three reasons:
1. The predicate is necessary, not sufficient — 5 already-resolved fixtures share the shape and would have a currently-marked end excluded; a future implementation must re-verify permutation-invariance for all 18 fixtures, not just the 8.
2. ~90% of the corpus's general coupled-end population (28/31 components) is untouched by this predicate — issue #149 should stay open after this ships.
3. The unidentified second factor governing the 5-vs-8 split means a correct implementation might still leave some fixtures non-convergent for a different reason.

Full reasoning, per-fixture tables, and RDKit oracle notes (including that RDKit 2026.03.3 has no `NOT_POSSIBLE` `StereoSpecified` value — confirmed by direct enum dump) are in `docs/ez_ring_constrained_residual_audit.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo build -p chematic-smiles --release --examples` — clean
- [x] `bash scripts/check.sh` — all green (fmt/clippy/tests/deny/publish-graph/version-consistency)
- [x] `.venv/bin/python3 scripts/ez_ring_constrained_residual_diagnosis.py --self-test` — passes, including a positive control reproducing the fixture-1 RDKit culprit/partner split
- [x] No `crates/*/src/` files touched (verified via `git diff --name-only`)
- [x] Independent review round caught and fixed 3 measurement gaps (marker-unknown undercounting, fixture/corpus overlap claim, threshold data-gap disclosure) before opening this PR — see the second commit

Refs #149

author: copilot
body:
GitHub Pages deployment was failing due to a non-discoverable workflow file, install/build mismatches, and artifact/output assumptions that did not match this TanStack Start app. This PR aligns build output, routing base path, and Actions workflow semantics so Pages can publish reliably from GitHub Actions.

- **Deployment workflow corrections**
  - Renamed the Pages workflow to a valid discoverable filename: `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`.
  - Switched to current Pages-recommended actions flow:
    - `actions/configure-pages@v5`
    - `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3`
    - `actions/deploy-pages@v4`
  - Kept required permissions explicit: `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`.

- **Build/output alignment for GitHub Pages**
  - Replaced `npm ci` with `npm install` (repo did not carry a lockfile suitable for CI install).
  - Updated artifact source to `dist/client` (actual static output for this app after build).
  - Added explicit output guard (`dist/client/index.html`) before artifact upload.

- **Static export + project-pages base path support**
  - In `vite.config.ts`:
    - disabled Nitro deployment output (`nitro: false`) for Pages static hosting,
    - enabled TanStack prerender with explicit routes (`/`, `/contact`, `/returns`, `/shipping`, `/sitemap.xml`),
    - wired `vite.base` from `GITHUB_PAGES_BASE_PATH` so assets resolve under `/gak-homepage/` on project pages.

- **Route link base-path safety**
  - Replaced hardcoded root-relative anchors with router-aware links where needed (`Link to="/"`, `Link to="/shipping"`, etc.) so generated URLs respect configured base path.

- **Repository setting dependency (one-time)**
  - Documented that Pages source must be set to **GitHub Actions** in repository settings.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml (key change)
- name: Setup Pages
  id: pages
  uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

- name: Build
  env:
    GITHUB_PAGES_BASE_PATH: ${{ steps.pages.outputs.base_path }}
  run: npm run build

- name: Upload Pages artifact
  uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
  with:
    path: dist/client
```

author: keishis
body:
## 目的

Closes #226

番号で示す引用スタイルで、番号を参考文献項目の表示文字列の先頭へ入れていました。表示は正しく
動作しますが、番号が文献の識別情報ではなく、書誌情報の記述の一部になっていました。

これは #220 の実装時点で、AdocWeaveが`[[[id,表示テキスト]]]`に対応していなかったための回避策
です。AdocWeave 0.27.0（#223）が
[adocweave#383](https://github.com/KeishiS/adocweave/issues/383)へ対応したため、番号をanchorの
表示テキストとして渡せるようになりました。

## 主な差分

生成する参考文献項目が変わります。

```asciidoc
変更前: * [[[smith2024]]] [1] Smith, A. (2024). An Example Article.
変更後: * [[[smith2024,1]]] Smith, A. (2024). An Example Article.
```

- `NoteBibliographyEntry`へ`label`を加えました。番号で示すスタイルでは初出順の番号が入り、
  著者・年のスタイルでは`None`です。
- `CitationStyle::entry_text`から番号の埋め込みを外し、`entry_label`を新たに設けました。
  書誌情報の記述と項目の見出しを別々に組み立てます。
- `crates/marginalis-asciidoc/src/rendering.rs`が`[[[citation key,番号]]]`を生成します。

IDはカンマの手前までなので`smith2024`のままであり、`cite:`との相互linkは保たれます。

## 実行した検証

`cargo make pre-push`が通過しました。カバレッジ測定とNixOS VM E2Eテスト4件を含みます。

追加した試験は`a_numbered_entry_puts_the_number_in_the_anchor_label`です。生成したHTMLに対して
次を確かめています。

- 項目のIDが`smith2024`であり、`smith2024,1`にならないこと
- 番号が書誌情報の記述に現れないこと
- 本文の引用から項目への移動が1件、項目から本文への戻りが1件あること

既存の`the_numeric_style_numbers_citations_by_first_appearance`は、番号が`text`ではなく`label`へ
入ることを確かめる形へ直しました。

## 利用者への影響

**表示は変わりません。** 番号が書誌情報の記述から外れ、AsciiDocから見て文献のラベルとして
扱われるようになります。公開契約の版は変えていません。

## 補足

本文中の引用表示（丸括弧、複数key、locator）はxreftextでは表現できないため、引き続きMarginalisが
組み立てます。この変更は参考文献項目側だけを対象としています。

判断の内容は`docs/adocweave-v0.27-migration.md`に記録済みです。

body:
## 문제

봇 커맨드 5개(`/signal`, `/us_signal`, `/theme`, `/us_theme`, `/ask`)의 Spark 폴백이
`generate_firecrawl_search_response()`를 **검색 옵션 없이** 호출하고 있었다.
`tbs`/`sources`/`location`/`include_domains`가 전부 기본값 `None`으로 들어가면서
최신성 필터도, 1차 매체 allowlist도 적용되지 않았다.

주간 인텔리전스 리포트는 이미 올바른 인자를 넘기고 있었으므로, 같은 저장소 안에
정답 호출과 누락 호출이 공존하는 상태였다.

## 실측 (`tools/bench/probe_firecrawl_tbs.py`, 2026-08-01, "코스피 증시 마감 시황")

```
bare  (현행)  8건 | 날짜보유 0건 (0%)  | 전부 네이버/KB/다음 시세 조회 페이지
tuned (수정)  8건 | 날짜보유 4건 (50%) | 마감시황 기사
```

폴백은 뉴스가 아니라 **정적 시세 페이지**를 컨텍스트로 넘기고 있었고, 모델은
시황을 설명할 근거 없이 답을 써야 했다. `tasks/eval/` 리포트들이
"제공된 뉴스 목록 페이지에서는 개별 뉴스 제목이 노출되지 않아"를 반복한 원인.

## 변경

- **`cores/search_presets.py` 신규** — KR/US 1차 매체 목록 + `search_preset()` + `widen_tbs()`.
  주간 리포트가 중복 정의하던 도메인 목록을 여기로 통일해 두 경로가 갈라지지 않게 함.
- **`telegram_ai_bot.py`** — `_run_firecrawl_command` / `_run_search_and_claude`에
  `search_opts` 추가, 커맨드별 프리셋 배선.
  `signal`=`qdr:w`, `theme`=`qdr:m`, `ask`=`qdr:m` + allowlist off
  (`/ask`는 주제를 예측할 수 없어 매체 allowlist가 정상 출처를 죽인다).
- **`report_generator.py`** — 좁은 기간 필터가 0건이면 `qdr:d→w→m→y` 한 단계씩 넓혀 재시도.
  변경은 `generate_firecrawl_search_response` 함수 내부 단일 hunk로 한정.
- **`tools/bench/`** — 실측 프로브 + 배선 검증 스위트.

## 검증

- `tools/bench/verify_search_presets.py --live` — 프리셋 형태 / 래더 종료 / 함수 시그니처 /
  5개 호출부 AST 배선 / 라이브 대조 **ALL PASS** (로컬 + app-server + db-server)
- 관련 기존 테스트 37 passed
- **app-server 내부 테스트**: 5개 커맨드 프리셋 전부 bare 0/5 → tuned 2/5 이상,
  `/ask`는 2시간 전 기사 확보. 엔드투엔드 생성 정상.
- **db-server 내부 테스트**: `weekly_firecrawl_intelligence.py --dry-run` KR/US 정상 생성, 에러 0.

## 알려진 제약 (후속 과제)

1. **app-server의 firecrawl-py가 4.22.1이라 `include_domains`를 드롭한다**
   (`_search_dropping_unsupported`가 graceful 처리). db-server는 4.30.1이라 정상.
   → app-server 업그레이드 필요.
2. **`tbs`는 백엔드 힌트이지 보장이 아니다.** `qdr:m`에서 `May 28, 2026` 기사가 통과했다.
   창 밖 항목을 폐기하는 Temporal Gate가 별도로 필요하다
   (`tasks/evidence-engine-design.md` 참조).
3. 확장 재시도 경로는 단위 검증만 됐고 라이브에서 트리거된 적 없다.

author: wolf-achtung
body:
Ein Fix in `record_anthropic_call` (`backend/app/services/cost_log.py`), sonst nichts.

## Problem

`input_usd` rechnete nur mit `input_tokens`. Sobald Prompt-Caching aktiv ist, zählt `input_tokens` laut Anthropic-Doku aber nur noch die Token **nach** dem letzten Cache-Breakpoint — der gecachte Anteil steckt in `cache_creation_input_tokens` (Write) und `cache_read_input_tokens` (Read) und fiel komplett aus der Rechnung.

Folge: systematische Unterschätzung, und `ANTHROPIC_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD` greift zu spät. Der Effekt ist genau dann am größten, wenn Caching am meisten bringt — bei einem 13k-Token-Prefix wie `insight_engine.SYSTEM_PROMPT` wäre nach dem ersten Call fast der gesamte Input unsichtbar gewesen.

## Fix

Input-Kosten aus allen drei Töpfen, Multiplikatoren auf die vorhandene `in_rate` (keine neuen settings-Keys):

```
billable = input_tokens
         + cache_creation_5m         * 1.25   # 5m-Write
         + cache_creation_1h         * 2.00   # 1h-Write
         + cache_read_input_tokens   * 0.10   # Read
```

Den 5m/1h-Split liest die Funktion aus `usage.cache_creation` (`ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`) im vorhandenen Duck-Typing-Stil, also SDK-Objekt **wie** dict.

**Konservativer Fallback auf 2.00× für den gesamten Write-Anteil** in drei Fällen: Split fehlt, Split ist nicht als Zahl lesbar, oder seine Summe passt nicht zu `cache_creation_input_tokens`. Der dritte Fall ist über deine Vorgabe hinaus — ein Split, der nicht aufgeht, ist kein vertrauenswürdiger Split, und die Richtung „lieber zu früh cappen" ist dieselbe.

`full_meta` trägt zusätzlich `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_5m`, `cache_creation_1h`, `prompt_tokens_total`.

Die `[CACHE-USAGE]`-Logzeile ist unverändert — sie taucht im Diff nicht auf.

## Eine bewusste Entscheidung, die du kennen solltest

Unter dem Fallback stehen in `full_meta` dann `cache_creation_5m=0` und `cache_creation_1h=<gesamter Write>`. Das ist dann **Preis-Basis, nicht eine von der API gemeldete TTL.**

Ich habe es so gewählt, damit sich `cost_usd_millicents` aus dem Meta rekonstruieren lässt — bei 0/0 wäre die Kostenzahl nicht mehr auditierbar. Steht als Kommentar an der Stelle. Wenn du die beiden Felder lieber als reine Rohdaten hättest, braucht es ein sechstes Flag-Feld, das den Fallback sichtbar macht; sag Bescheid.

## Verifikation

Volle Suite: **1262 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed** (vorher 1258 + 4 neue Tests).

Die Arithmetik zusätzlich unabhängig gegengerechnet, mit der echten SDK-Objektform statt nur dicts:

| Fall | erwartet | gemessen |
|---|---:|---:|
| SDK-Objekt, 4k Write als 5m + 20k Read | 25 500 mc | 25 500 |
| SDK-Objekt, 1k×5m + 2k×1h gemischt | 7 875 mc | 7 875 |
| `cache_creation=None` → Fallback 1h | 3 000 mc | 3 000 |
| `usage=None` | 0 | 0 |
| nur Read, 50k | 7 500 mc | 7 500 |

Neue Tests:

- **`..._bills_cache_tokens`** — Cache-Verkehr erhöht die Kosten: 40 500 statt 30 000 Millicents bei identischem `input_tokens`.
- **`..._cache_write_without_split_bills_1h`** — fehlender Split → 2.00×.
- **`..._ignores_inconsistent_cache_split`** — Split, dessen Summe nicht aufgeht → 2.00×.
- **`..._without_cache_fields_unchanged`** — Regression: `usage` ohne Cache-Felder liefert weiterhin exakt 30 000 Millicents, also identisch zu heute.

---

author: kateinoigakukun
body:
`fd_readdir` called `readEntries` on `any WASIDir`, whose result was an
associated type, so the call could not be specialized for Embedded.

This only surfaced when compiling `WasmKitWASI`. Specialization happens at the
use site, so `WASI` on its own compiled cleanly and hid it. Worth remembering
when checking embedded support: compiling the library proves less than compiling
its consumer.

Erase the iterator behind a concrete `WASIReaddirEntries`, keeping
`WASIReaddirIterator` as the shape implementers conform to.

With the associated type gone, the `ReadEntriesResult` types were named after a
requirement that no longer exists, so they are renamed for what they are:
`HostDirectoryIterator` and `MemoryDirectoryIterator`.

With this the whole stack compiles for `riscv32-none-none-eabi`: `WasmTypes`,
`WasmParser`, `WasmKit`, `WASI`, `WasmKitWASI`.

## Stack

Reviewable in order; each PR targets the one above it. Merge bottom-up.

1. #404 Decouple WASIFile from GuestMemory
1. #406 Make the WASI host module table generic over guest memory
1. #407 Allow linking a subset of the WASI preview1 surface
1. #408 Decouple WASIDir from its associated iterator type **← this PR**
1. #409 Cover WASI in the embedded check and strip unused code
1. #410 Run a WASI guest on emulated hardware in the ESP32 example

#401, #402 and #403 were the first three layers and are merged.

One more branch continues this locally: running the GDB stub on emulated
hardware and driving it with a real lldb. It will be opened once these land.

Unrelated but worth landing first: #405 fixes a debugger crash that makes
`CLICommandsTests` fail intermittently on Linux. It is the cause of the red
runs these PRs will otherwise keep hitting.

GitHub's native stacked PRs are not yet available for this repository, so the
chain is expressed through base branches instead.

## Neden [Google'ın yapay zekâ optimizasyon kılavuzu](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide?hl=tr) en başa şunu koyuyor: mevcut bilginin özeti olan içerik değil, özgün bakış ve birinci elden deneyim. Keşif sayfalarımız şu an ağırlıkla deponun README'sinden üretilmiş Türkçe özet. 366 sayfa, sayfa başına medyan ~275 kelime (menü ve altbilgi dahil). Ayırt edici katma değer ince, bu da ölçekli içerik tarafında zayıf nokta. ## Değişiklik catalog kaydına opsiyonel `trescout_notu` alanı. Doluysa sayfada meta listesinin hemen altında, mevcut `.disc-note` stiliyle basılır: ```html

author: ronitrade123
body:
## What

A new `grok` quota source: subscription tier (e.g. `SuperGrok`), weekly-window reset countdown, and on-demand credits as an `overage` meter. Detail line renders as `SuperGrok · resets 6d 6h`.

## How (no scraping, no cookies)

The Grok CLI ("Grok Build", `~/.grok/bin/grok`) speaks the Agent Client Protocol. The fetcher spawns a one-shot `grok agent stdio`, sends `initialize` followed by the extension method `_x.ai/billing`, and reads the JSON result — reusing the CLI's own OAuth session in `~/.grok/auth.json`. Same spirit as the existing codex-app-server adapter. Round-trip is ~1.2 s, polled at 300 s with the usual cache_util TTL/stale handling.

Example payload xAI returns:

```json
{
  "config": {
    "currentPeriod": {"type": "USAGE_PERIOD_TYPE_WEEKLY", "start": "…", "end": "…"},
    "onDemandCap": {"val": 0}, "onDemandUsed": {"val": 0},
    "prepaidBalance": {"val": 0}, "isUnifiedBillingUser": true
  },
  "subscription_tier": "SuperGrok"
}
```

xAI does **not** expose a percent-used figure for the subscription window itself, so the only meter is on-demand credits (`kind=overage`, `ring=False`, pct only when a cap is configured). If xAI ever ships a used-percent, it slots into the same fetcher.

## Why not HTTP directly

`auth.x.ai` is Cloudflare-gated for non-CLI clients (403), and grok.com cookie scraping is fragile by design (anti-bot headers; the known third-party trackers for it died that way). The ACP route avoids both.

## Changes

- new `host/grok_usage.py` — stdlib only, `signed_in()` + `fetch_quota(force=)`, cache_util/quota_util patterns
- `host/sources_config.py` — `_GROK_POOLS`, `_detail_grok`, one `Source("grok", …, poll_s=300, accent="#8E8E93")` row after zed
- `host/detect_sources.py` — `grok` probe (binary on PATH candidates + `auth.json` holds a key)

## Testing

- `host/test_contract.py`: 21/22 pass — the one failure (`test_rollup_order_follows_the_pinned_provider_order`, expects `focus[0] == "cursor"`) also fails on unmodified `main` on this machine (no Cursor installed), so it looks environment-dependent rather than related to this change. Happy to dig into it separately if useful.
- Live on macOS 15 / v1.4.2 host: `/health` shows `grok: ok · SuperGrok · resets 6d 6h`; `/usage` `providers[]` carries the row with accent/pools; menu bar + iPhone app render it from the feed.

author: infektyd
body:
## What

Grok-powered siblings of the Claude Code workflow pair from #214, running xAI's **Grok Build CLI headless** on GitHub-hosted runners and burning the operator's **Grok subscription** (not Claude usage, not metered xAI API credits):

- **`grok.yml`** — `@grok` in an issue/PR comment (or a new issue body) runs Grok against a checkout plus the issue/PR context and posts the reply as a comment.
- **`grok-review.yml`** — one auto-review per PR at `opened`/`ready_for_review` (deliberately not `synchronize`, to bound subscription burn), posted as a PR comment.

## Auth

`grok login --device-auth` (first-party headless flow) run in an **isolated home** so day-to-day local grok use never rotates the CI token stale; the resulting `auth.json` is stored base64'd as the `GROK_CI_AUTH_JSON` repo secret (already set). Rotation recipe lives in `grok.yml`'s header comment. Token smoke-tested headless before the secret was cut.

## Guards

- `@grok` jobs gate on `author_association` ∈ OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR — drive-by mentions no-op.
- The secret never coexists with fork-controlled code: PR-comment jobs check out the PR head only for same-repo PRs; the review workflow's if-gate skips fork PRs outright (GitHub also withholds secrets there by design).
- `--permission-mode dontAsk --no-subagents --max-turns 30`, 20-minute job timeouts, per-PR concurrency groups.

## Notes

- Research background: xAI ships no first-party equivalent of `claude-code-action`, and the installed "Grok (by xAI)" GitHub App is the OAuth backend for grok.com-side Connectors (chat-triggered), not a GitHub-event bot — hence hand-rolled workflows.
- The device-auth-token-in-CI pattern is supported CLI tooling but not xAI's documented CI recommendation (they steer to API keys); if the token gets invalidated server-side, the fallback is re-minting per the header recipe or switching the auth step to `XAI_API_KEY` metered billing.

author: kateinoigakukun
body:
Compile `WASI` and `WasmKitWASI` in `build-embedded.sh` so embedded support stays
working. `WasmKitWASI` matters on its own: generic specialization happens at the
use site, so `WASI` can compile cleanly in isolation while still failing where it
is actually used.

Build with `-Xfrontend -function-sections` here and in the ESP32 example.
`swiftc` otherwise emits one `.text` section per module, and `--gc-sections`
strips whole sections, so the selective linking added earlier in this stack would
not have removed anything from the image. Objects grow by roughly a quarter
before linking, which the linker then reclaims.

Flag forms that do not work, for the record: `-Xllvm -function-sections` is
accepted but has no effect, and `-Xfrontend -data-sections` is not a valid
argument, so `.rodata` stays coarse.

## Stack

Reviewable in order; each PR targets the one above it. Merge bottom-up.

1. #404 Decouple WASIFile from GuestMemory
1. #406 Make the WASI host module table generic over guest memory
1. #407 Allow linking a subset of the WASI preview1 surface
1. #408 Decouple WASIDir from its associated iterator type
1. #409 Cover WASI in the embedded check and strip unused code **← this PR**
1. #410 Run a WASI guest on emulated hardware in the ESP32 example

#401, #402 and #403 were the first three layers and are merged.

One more branch continues this locally: running the GDB stub on emulated
hardware and driving it with a real lldb. It will be opened once these land.

Unrelated but worth landing first: #405 fixes a debugger crash that makes
`CLICommandsTests` fail intermittently on Linux. It is the cause of the red
runs these PRs will otherwise keep hitting.

GitHub's native stacked PRs are not yet available for this repository, so the
chain is expressed through base branches instead.

author: hongquan-prog
body:
Commit 0b2a2850ff59 ("arch: arm64: fix arch_buffer_validate() wrap bypass") added an addr+size overflow guard that branches to the shared abv_fail epilogue before x3 is loaded with the current DAIF value. On that path abv_fail executes "msr DAIF, x3" with an uninitialized register, so a wrapping buffer validation returns -1 with arbitrary DAIF bits (IRQ/FIQ/SError/Debug masks) set or cleared from whatever the caller happened to leave in x3.

Save DAIF into x3 before the overflow check so that every exit from abv_fail restores the value the function was entered with.

Fixes #115141

author: nobletsylvain
body:
Nouveau core loop : **finca → labo → ruta → punto d'export → liquide → lessive → propre**.
C'est le pendant **macro** de La Loupe — là où La Loupe tient un bloc à la main, El Patrón pilote un pays.

Jouable : `el-patron/` · design complet : **`el-patron/SCOPE.md`** · journal : `NOTES.md`.

## Ce qu'on corrige de Cartel Tycoon

Dix reproches sourcés (tests presse + fils Steam), tableau complet dans `SCOPE.md` §3. Les cinq qui structurent le proto :

| Reproche | Ce que fait El Patrón |
|---|---|
| Les lieutenants ne prennent qu'un ordre à la fois : on redonne l'ordre de convoi à la main, indéfiniment. | Une ruta est un **ordre permanent**. Le joueur édite une *politique*, jamais un trajet. |
| Loyauté : trahisons **aléatoires** et rétroactives sur des biens payés. | **Rien n'est tiré au sort** (R4). Une jauge de *suspicion* monte à chaque passage et déclenche le barrage à 100, avec le compte à rebours affiché en jours. |
| Le blanchiment se remplit contre des plafonds invisibles. | Chaque front est un **tuyau imprimé** : débit, commission, plafond de crédibilité, soupçon. Aucune heuristique cachée. |
| Un bâtiment privé d'entretien s'éteint et **ne se rallume pas tout seul**. | La réserve d'exploitation est prélevée **en premier**, autonomie affichée en jours ; un labo à sec redémarre de lui-même. |
| « Le premier dollar demande autant d'attention que le dernier. » | Plafonds d'entités : on grandit **en montant en gamme**. Grandir n'ajoute aucune tâche. |

## La trouvaille : la prime de chaleur

Dans la première version de ce proto, **tout tirait vers le bas** — produire chauffe, stocker chauffe, grossir chauffe — donc la posture optimale devenait « en faire le moins possible ». C'est le contraire d'un jeu de cartel.

Un corridor surveillé est un corridor où la marchandise **se raréfie**, donc elle se paie plus cher : ×1.10 / ×1.22 / ×1.38 selon le palier, puis ×0.70 à l'extradition. **Le meilleur tarif du jeu est juste avant la falaise.** Sur 220 jours simulés, la partie de référence passe de 30,5 M€ à **48 M€** propres, et la chaleur se stabilise en « Opération » au lieu de fuir vers le bas.

## Ce que la simulation a appris avant qu'un pixel soit dessiné

La sim a tourné en `node` sur 220 jours **avant** l'UI. Quatre défauts de conception en sont sortis, qu'aucune relecture n'aurait attrapés (détail dans `NOTES.md`) :

1. **Spirale de la mort** — les fronts blanchissaient jusqu'au dernier billet ; or les précurseurs se paient en *sale*. À zéro liquide l'usine s'arrête, donc plus d'export, donc plus de liquide : verrou définitif au jour ~12. D'où la **réserve d'exploitation**, devenue un levier de jeu (la mettre à zéro est un vrai mauvais choix).
2. **La chaleur ne pouvait pas être additive** — de 4 kg/j à 1 000 kg/j il y a deux ordres de grandeur. Remplacée par une **cible saturante** vers laquelle la chaleur tend ; bonus, la cible *est* la projection, donc le marqueur fantôme sur la jauge est gratuit.
3. **Le registre se noyait dans son propre bruit** — une ligne par tick. Séparé en `tx()` (ponctuel) et `flux()` (continu, agrégé en une ligne par jour et par cause).
4. **La suspicion se comptait en kilos** — plus le véhicule était gros, plus il était suicidaire, l'inverse de ce qu'on veut d'un investissement. Elle se compte maintenant en **passages**.

## Architecture

- `el-patron/sim.mjs` — **sim pure** : aucun DOM, aucun `Math.random`, aucune `Date`, toutes les constantes d'équilibrage nommées en tête.
- `el-patron/index.html` — coque et rendu. Ne calcule jamais d'économie : lit `rythmes()` / `diagnostics()` et affiche.
- `tools/invariants-patron.mjs` — **31 invariants** sans navigateur.
- `tools/shots-patron.mjs` — sert le dépôt en HTTP (les imports de module ES sont interdits en `file://`, donc `screenshots.mjs` ne pouvait pas servir ce proto), joue la page, résout les événements, échoue sur la moindre erreur console.

## Vérifications

```
node check.mjs el-patron        →  2 fichiers, 0 échec
node lexique.mjs                →  1/1 règle OK
node invariants-patron.mjs      →  31/31 invariants OK
node shots-patron.mjs           →  aucune erreur console, invariants tenus
```

Layout vérifié à **375×667** (petit iPhone) et **412×892** : la carte est bornée en largeur pour garder son ratio — la borner en hauteur letterboxait le SVG et décalait toutes les zones tactiles.

## [DÉCISION REQUISE] — ce que je n'ai pas tranché

1. **R3 « le tactile EST le plaisir » n'est pas honoré, volontairement.** La fantaisie macro est de *piloter*, pas de *faire* (cohérent avec R6/R7). C'est un écart assumé à une règle du dépôt : soit l'échelle cartel le justifie, soit il faut un geste signature — le meilleur candidat étant la **mordida en maintien** (on maintient, le montant monte, la suspicion redescend, on relâche pour payer).
2. **Progression hors-ligne** — l'absence est aujourd'hui *sûre* mais *stérile*. Rattrapage à taux réduit + rapport d'absence ? Ça change la nature du jeu (idle vs session).
3. **Choix de l'acheteur à l'export** — en plus du punto ? Densifie la décision, au risque d'un pop-up de plus.
4. **Tout l'équilibrage est en placeholder** — nommé et groupé, les courbes tiennent sur 220 jours simulés, mais les valeurs attendent le tuning humain (`CHALEUR_K`, `MORDIDA_PART`, prix des fronts).

author: kateinoigakukun
body:
Compiling WASI for the target says nothing about linking or running it. Two
failures were invisible to the compile-only check:

`SystemRandomNumberGenerator`'s conformance calls `swift_stdlib_random`, which
does not exist on bare metal, and it is the default argument for every
`WASIBridgeToHost` initialiser. Linking WASI into firmware failed with an
undefined reference even though no guest called `random_get`. It now traps on
Embedded instead. `next()` bottoms out in the same symbol, so there is no
fallback, and handing a guest predictable bytes it believes are random would be
worse than refusing. Callers inject a generator backed by the SoC's hardware RNG.

The 32-bit page-limit bug at the base of this stack only failed at
instantiation.

Add `WASI` and `WasmKitWASI` as ESP-IDF components and run a guest that writes
through `fd_write` to a console-backed `WASIFile`, asserted in the QEMU smoke
test.

Measured on esp32c6 with `-Osize`, linking `[.stdio, .process]` against the whole
surface:

| Firmware | `.bin` size |
| --- | --- |
| `[.stdio, .process]` | 672,528 B |
| `WASICapability.all` | 699,648 B |

The `WASIImplementation.path_open` symbol is absent from the subset image
entirely; only the `PATH_OPEN` rights constant remains.

Host integration tests cover selective linking, including the case where omitting
a needed capability must change behaviour. Without that one, a subset that
silently behaved like a full link would pass every other test.

## Stack

Reviewable in order; each PR targets the one above it. Merge bottom-up.

1. #404 Decouple WASIFile from GuestMemory
1. #406 Make the WASI host module table generic over guest memory
1. #407 Allow linking a subset of the WASI preview1 surface
1. #408 Decouple WASIDir from its associated iterator type
1. #409 Cover WASI in the embedded check and strip unused code
1. #410 Run a WASI guest on emulated hardware in the ESP32 example **← this PR**

#401, #402 and #403 were the first three layers and are merged.

One more branch continues this locally: running the GDB stub on emulated
hardware and driving it with a real lldb. It will be opened once these land.

Unrelated but worth landing first: #405 fixes a debugger crash that makes
`CLICommandsTests` fail intermittently on Linux. It is the cause of the red
runs these PRs will otherwise keep hitting.

GitHub's native stacked PRs are not yet available for this repository, so the
chain is expressed through base branches instead.

author: copilot
body:
Die aktuelle Audio-/Plugin-Initialisierung war inkonsistent: Worklets konnten je nach Pfadkonfiguration nicht zuverlässig laden, und Manifest/Fallback-Handling ließ inkorrekte Modulmengen zu.  
Diese Änderung stabilisiert den Startup-Pfad, erzwingt die erwartete 16-Modul-Struktur und macht die API-/Manifest-Auflösung robuster.

- **Plugin-Registry: 16-Module-Contract abgesichert**
  - Manifest-Plugins werden nur übernommen, wenn die auflösbaren UI-Plugins vollständig sind (`16` erwartete Module).
  - Bei Abweichungen erfolgt ein deterministischer Fallback auf eine vollständige interne Registry (statt Minimal-Subset).
  - Modulmetadaten (Name/Short/Icon) wurden zentralisiert, um Inkonsistenzen zwischen Manifest und Runtime zu reduzieren.

- **Audio-Workflow: Initialisierungsreihenfolge korrigiert**
  - App-Startup initialisiert jetzt zuerst den Audio-Kontext/Worklets und startet erst danach die Engine-Wiedergabe.
  - Sequencer-Step-Updates werden explizit mit UI-State synchronisiert.
  - Locking beim Wechsel in `PRO` respektiert den Lock-Grant (kein Zustandswechsel ohne erfolgreiches Lock).

- **Worklet-/API-Konfiguration: Pfadauflösung resilient gemacht**
  - Worklet-URLs werden normalisiert (kompatibel für `/public/...` und `/<asset>...`), mit geordnetem Kandidaten-Fallback.
  - `plugin-manifest.json` wurde auf runtime-konsistente Worklet-Pfade umgestellt (`/worklets/...`).

```ts
// Registry-Übernahme nur bei vollständigem Manifest
if (discoveredPlugins.length === EXPECTED_PLUGIN_COUNT) {
  PLUGIN_REGISTRY = discoveredPlugins;
  return PLUGIN_REGISTRY;
}
PLUGIN_REGISTRY = createFallbackRegistry();
```

author: lumiere-bot[bot]
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [jdx/mise-action](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action) | action | minor | `v4.2.3` → `v4.3.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jdx/mise-action (jdx/mise-action)</summary>

### [`v4.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/releases/tag/v4.3.0): : Install age-filtered mise releases

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v4.2.5...v4.3.0)

A small release that adds an opt-in way to hold back from installing brand-new mise releases.

##### Added

##### `minimum_release_age` input ([#​604](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/pull/604) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))

When `version` is omitted, you can now set `minimum_release_age` to install the newest **stable, non-draft** mise release that is older than a given cutoff — a simple way to avoid picking up a mise release the moment it ships (closes [#​603](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/issues/603)).

```yaml
- uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
  with:
    minimum_release_age: 7d
```

It accepts relative durations (`24h`, `7d`, `6mo`, `1y`) as well as absolute ISO dates and timestamps. Age-filtered versions are resolved from the GitHub Releases API (the CDN only serves the latest binary) and downloaded by their exact version. If mise is already present on disk, an age-filtered run updates it to the resolved version rather than keeping the existing binary. An explicit `version` always takes precedence over `minimum_release_age`, and invalid dates fail fast.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v4.2.5...v4.3.0>

### [`v4.2.5`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/releases/tag/v4.2.5): : Resilient mise downloads with automatic retries

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v4.2.4...v4.2.5)

A small patch release that makes setup more resilient to transient network failures when downloading mise.

##### Fixed

##### Retry mise downloads after transient failures ([#​597](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/pull/597) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))

The download helpers previously made a single `curl` or `wget` attempt, so a transient GitHub release-asset HTTP or TLS failure would abort setup before mise or any user command could run (see [#​596](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/issues/596)).

Downloads now run through a retry wrapper that makes up to five attempts with a 2s pause between failures, logging a warning on each retry. This applies consistently to binary, checksum, signature, and version fetches. Checksum and minisign verification still run only after a successful download — never inside the retry loop — so integrity guarantees are unchanged.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v4.2.4...v4.2.5>

### [`v4.2.4`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/releases/tag/v4.2.4): : Reliable locking detection under forced color

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v4.2.3...v4.2.4)

A small patch release that fixes locking-support detection when workflows force colored output.

##### Fixed

##### Detect `mise install --locked` reliably under forced color ([#​580](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/pull/580) by [@​scop](https://redirect.github.com/scop))

When colored output was forced globally (for example via `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1`), ANSI escape codes in `mise install --help` prevented the action from matching `--locked` in the help text, so locking support was reported as unavailable even on versions of mise that supported it.

The help probe now runs with `NO_COLOR=1` in its environment, which overrides `CLICOLOR_FORCE` and guarantees plain-text output for the feature detection — regardless of the surrounding workflow's color settings.

author: wi-fa
body:
### Related Ticket

No existing issue found for this — happy to open one if preferred.

### Summary

After a move drag ends, the browser fires a compatibility `click` on `viewport-controls` (pointer-down and pointer-up land on the same element, and left-clicks are not prevented). `on-click` (`viewport/actions.cljs`) only guards against the rubber-band flow (`(nil? selrect)`), so it reaches `(dw/select-shape (:id @hover))` — and `@hover` at that moment can point at the WRONG shape:

- hover keeps updating during a drag (`hooks.cljs` freezes only `hover-ids`, `@hover` stays live for the ALT-drag distance measure), and
- hover hit-tests resolve against **committed, pre-reflow geometry** (the worker index only sees committed changes, never live modifiers).

So when a flex-layout child is drag-reordered, the release point sits over a **sibling's old bounds** — the trailing click then moves the selection from the dragged shape to that sibling.

The area-select flow already guards this exact hazard: `data/workspace/selection.cljs` clears `selrect` **asynchronously** specifically so the trailing `on-click` doesn't misfire. This PR brings the move flow in line, using the same pattern as the existing `disable-paste-ref`:

- `on-pointer-up` sets a `just-finished-move-ref` when it terminates a `:move` transform (with a scheduled reset for releases that produce no click),
- `on-click` skips the hover reselect for that single trailing click and clears the flag.

Applied to both the classic and wasm viewports. `clj-kondo` passes with no new findings.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a board with a flex layout and four children `[A, B, C, D]`.
2. Press on **A** and drag it rightwards past **B** and **C** (the live reorder swaps it along), release while inside the layout.
3. The reorder commits correctly, but the selection/bounding box lands on **C** (the sibling immediately before A's new slot) instead of staying on the dragged **A**.

The same mechanism can steal selection on any move drag that releases over another shape's pre-drag bounds (not layout-specific).

### Checklist

- [x] Choose the correct target branch; use `develop` by default.
- [x] Provide a brief summary of the changes introduced.
- [x] Add a detailed explanation of how to reproduce the issue and/or verify the fix, if applicable.

author: valarlip
body:
A bug that killed the offline entrypoint's output thread reached `main` and was
caught a day later by the nightly Docker smoke test — as a 60-minute step
timeout. This fixes the bug, the reason the PR gate could not see it, and the
reason the unit suite could not see it either.

## The bug

`DisaggCoreManager` spawns its engines differently and so cannot run
`CoreManager.__init__`. It hand-copied the field block instead, and the copy
drifted: `_flush_stream_batch_fn` was added to the copy (`engine_core_mgr.py`)
and to the API server that assigns it (`api_server.py`), but never to the base
class.

Nothing failed loudly. The server path assigns the hook before the first
request and the disagg path had it from the copy, so only the **offline**
entrypoint was left with neither:

```
Exception in thread EngineCoreOutputThread-DP0:
  File "atom/model_engine/engine_core_mgr.py", line 317, in process_outputs_socket
    if self._flush_stream_batch_fn is not None:
AttributeError: 'CoreManager' object has no attribute '_flush_stream_batch_fn'
```

The thread died on the first streamed token. The engine kept producing tokens
nobody collected, `simple_inference` blocked forever, and the job hit
`The action 'Test Docker image' has timed out after 60 minutes`.

`_init_shared_state()` is now the one initialiser both constructors call. Only
`pp_*` (read solely by this class's spawn loop, and `DisaggCoreManager`
overrides the one method that touches it) and the post-spawn tail stay
per-class — verified by diffing the two field sets.

The tests pin the invariant rather than the single field: whatever
`process_outputs_socket` reads off `self` — **discovered from the source**, so
a newly added read is covered the day it lands — both managers must provide.
All five fail against `main`'s code.

## Why the PR gate missed it

Both the simple-inference step and its golden comparison were `if: false`, so
the offline entrypoint ran only in the nightly Docker release. The accuracy
test is not a substitute: it drives the server over HTTP, and the two do not
share the path that hands tokens back to the caller.

The inference step now runs for every model in the matrix. Completing is the
assertion — the output is printed but not diffed, which suits the failure mode
(the bug hung; it did not produce wrong text) and removes the need for a
per-model golden file. Only one such file was ever checked in, which is why the
comparison was disabled wholesale when the matrix moved to
`models_accuracy.json`; it is deleted rather than left dead a second time.

`extraArgs` also had to stop being interpolated into a double-quoted
`bash -lc "…"`: the host shell stripped the inner quotes, so
`--hf-overrides '{"use_index_cache": true}'` arrived as
`'{use_index_cache: true}'` and argparse rejected it. It now goes through an
env var and over stdin, as the accuracy step already does.

## Why the unit suite missed it

`tests/conftest.py` replaced `atom` and `atom.config` in `sys.modules` with
hand-built module objects, so unit tests ran against a parallel API nobody
updated. It rotted: the stand-in lost `CompilationLevel`, and because the
modules importing it are guarded by a broad `try/except` that skips the whole
file, four test modules stopped running **on every machine, including GPU
hosts** — while blaming a circular import that does not exist.

The stand-ins existed because `import atom.config` was expensive: Python
imports a package before its submodule, and `atom/__init__.py` eagerly imported
`LLMEngine`, so reading a dataclass pulled in zmq, the model runner and AITER.
That is now resolved on attribute access (PEP 562); `import atom.config` loads
no engine module at all, and `from atom import LLMEngine` is unchanged.

That left AITER. `atom.quant_spec` now resolves `QuantType` and `d_dtypes` on
first use — the handles return the genuine AITER objects, so values compare and
behave exactly as before; only the lookup moves. Deferring the import is not
enough by itself: three places evaluated those names while the module body ran,
and each had to move with it (the `LayerQuantConfig.quant_type` default →
`default_factory`; `_QSCHEME_TO_QUANT_TYPE` → a cached function;
`GenericParser._QTYPE_PATTERNS`, a **class body**, likewise). `config.py` then
needs AITER for neither of its two uses: the runtime one has an exact
equivalent in `LayerQuantConfig.no_quant()`, and the annotation moves under
`TYPE_CHECKING`.

**`tests/conftest.py` now fakes nothing at all.** The zmq and xxhash stubs went
too — both are declared dependencies in `pyproject.toml`, so their
`find_spec(...) is None` guard could never fire.

## Test plan

Simulating the CPU gate by blocking `aiter` at the meta path (the unit job runs
on `ubuntu-latest`, where it is genuinely absent):

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| CPU gate (no aiter) | 839 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed | **846 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed** |
| GPU host, full suite | 895 passed, 6 skipped | **902 passed, 2 skipped** |

Coverage rises and skips fall in both. The 2 remaining failures
(`test_mxfp4_moe_has_bias`) are pre-existing on `main` and untouched here.

- [x] 5 new tests for the shared-state invariant; all 5 fail against `main`.
- [x] `test_dspark_swa_fp8_2buff` (2 tests) runs again — it was one of the four
      modules the stand-in silently disabled.
- [x] Host-shell simulation confirming JSON in `extraArgs` now reaches the
      container intact.

## Reviewer notes

- **Commit 2 of 5 (`test: import the real atom modules…`) is red in isolation.**
  Removing the stubs un-skipped tests that need real AITER before the lazy
  import landed in commit 4. The branch head is green; squash-merge, or say the
  word and I will squash 2 and 4 together.
- The CPU-gate numbers come from a meta-path simulation, not a real
  `ubuntu-latest` run. Whether `pip install -e .` there pulls AITER by some
  other route is something only CI can answer.
- `test_profiler_regression.py::test_hipgraph_replay_occupancy` aborts
  intermittently on a GPU host (~4/10 on `main`, similar here). Pre-existing and
  unrelated; it skips on the CPU gate, which is why nobody has hit it.

author: nortaq-playnexus
body:
## Summary

Adds HTTP/HTTPS proxy support to the library and CLI, as requested in #44.

Every request the library makes — search page fetches and image downloads — can now be routed through a configured HTTP/HTTPS proxy. With no proxy configured, behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged (requests still go through the module-level `urllib.request.urlopen`, honouring `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` env vars), so this is a purely additive, backwards-compatible feature.

## What changed

### Public API (backwards-compatible, new params with defaults)

- `Downloader(proxy=...)` — sets the proxy for the whole session (matches the cookie-jar/opener model). Threaded to each engine via `search()`.
- `downloader(proxy=...)` — the module-level legacy wrapper now accepts `proxy` and forwards it to `Downloader`.
- `bbid --proxy <url>` — new CLI flag.

### Internals

- `ImageEngine.__init__` accepts `proxy`; the engine builds a proxied `opener` via a new `_build_opener()` that layers `urllib.request.ProxyHandler({"http": ..., "https": ...})` when a proxy is set.
- `base._http_get` and `Bing._fetch_page` use the proxied opener only when `proxy` is set; otherwise they keep calling module-level `urlopen` exactly as before (this preserves the existing test mock boundary at `better_bing_image_downloader.base.urllib.request.urlopen`).
- `DuckDuckGo` keeps its cookie-jar opener but layers the same `ProxyHandler` on top via a shared `_build_opener(cookie_jar, proxy)` helper, used for both the vqd token fetch and the `i.js` XHR pages.

### Tests & docs

- New `tests/test_v3_8_0_proxy.py` — 11 tests covering: engine `_build_opener` with/without proxy, `_http_get` routing, Bing `_fetch_page`, DDG token + XHR page routing, `Downloader` opener construction, engine-kwarg threading through `search()`, CLI `--proxy` parsing/forwarding, and that the no-proxy path still calls module-level `urlopen` (mock boundary preserved).
- `CHANGELOG.md` — "Added" entry under `[Unreleased]`.
- `README.md` — "Routing through a proxy" section, CLI example, and `--proxy` row in the options table.
- `Downloader` docstring documents the new `proxy` parameter.

## Verification

- `pytest`: **173 passed, 4 skipped, 2 failed** — the 2 failures are pre-existing on Windows only (`test_v3_5_0_manifest.py` `repr` backslash-path assertions, tracked as #51); they fail identically on `main` without this change.
- `ruff check`: clean.
- `mypy`: clean (8 source files).
- `black --check`: clean.
- CLI smoke test: `bbid --help` shows `--proxy`.

## Notes

- Only HTTP/HTTPS proxies are supported (no SOCKS5) in this first cut, per the feature request.
- The proxy is fixed for the lifetime of a `Downloader` instance; to rotate proxies, construct a new `Downloader`.

Closes #44

author: mnikks01
body:
Closes S2-10 — FR-ACAD-030, 031. This is the last item in the Sprint 2 backlog apart from role dashboards.

A teacher records progress per topic; every verified member of the class sees how far each subject has got.

## The write rule is the same object, not a copy

Recording uses `assertTeacherAllocatedToSubject` — the very policy that governs publishing homework. Not a similar rule, the same one, so the two cannot drift: *this* teacher, *this* subject. Reading follows the class, which is what makes coverage answerable by a parent (FR-ACAD-031) without letting them touch it.

## Why `GET /classes/:id/syllabus` exists

The obvious design is one request per subject, and the page started that way. It has a hole: **a class with no subjects never reaches a policy at all**, so a stranger could tell an empty class from one that does not exist. A browser test caught it — the rival-school case rendered "This class has no subjects yet" instead of a 404.

The class-scoped endpoint authorizes once, before any subject is looked at, and returns every subject including the untouched ones at 0%. A test covers exactly that case, and it also removes an N+1 (one query for the class's topics rather than one per subject).

## Design notes

- The overall figure is an **unweighted mean, and says so**. The schema has no notion of how long a chapter takes; inventing weights would put a number on screen that nothing can justify.
- Topics sort by name, because a syllabus is read as a list of chapters, not by when each was last touched.
- Re-recording a topic **updates** it — that is the `@@unique([subject_id, topic])` constraint doing the work, and it is why the endpoint answers 200 rather than 201.
- The coverage bar states its percentage in text beside it and in its `aria-label` ("Chapter 1: Integers: 40% covered"), so colour is a second channel rather than the only one.

## Tests

- **474 API tests** (+31): 25 in a new `syllabus.test.ts` — every role on every endpoint, the upsert, the mean, ordering, subject isolation, fractional and out-of-range percentages, and the empty-class leak.
- **43 E2E** (+3): a teacher records and a student sees it read-only; re-recording updates in place; a rival school gets a 404.
- **Sabotage-checked**: removing either policy fails 5 tests. Restored.
- *Update syllabus coverage* moves from the matrix suite's `UNIMPLEMENTED` inventory into the enforced table. What remains listed is only leave, complaints, billing, and social — none of them built yet.

## One thing I did not solve

The roster permission test (`GET /schools/:id/members` refusing an individual) has failed intermittently in full-suite runs — roughly **one run in eight**, never in isolation, and never the same role twice. I could not reproduce it deliberately: eight consecutive targeted runs and three full runs all passed. Rather than guess, I added the response body to the assertion message, so the next occurrence reports which layer refused instead of only that a status differed. Flagging it here because it will show up in CI eventually and it is not something this PR introduced.

## Still open (unchanged)

Branch protection does not *require* CI checks, and release PRs are being squashed where the git flow calls for a merge commit.

author: dereuromark
body:
Fixes #525.

## What was wrong

Tiptap's image extension declares `group: 'block'`, so an image inserted by any editor with an
image button sits at document level, as a sibling of paragraphs. That is the normal,
unavoidable shape for a real editor.

`ProseMirrorToCarve` mapped it to `Node\Inline\Image` and appended it straight onto the Carve
`Document`, leaving an inline node as a direct child of a block container - a tree Carve's own
parser can never produce, because `![Plan](/x.png)` alone on a line parses into a paragraph
containing the image.

`HtmlRenderer` rendered it anyway. `CarveRenderer` writes block children, has no form for an
inline in block position, and wrote nothing at all:

```
in    doc > image
carve ""
```

The document came back empty, and neither `droppedTypes()` nor `degradedTypes()` said so.

## What changed

An inline node in block position is now wrapped in a paragraph before it is appended, so the
AST is one the parser could also have produced.

```
in    doc > image
carve ![Plan](/x.png "T")
```

The guard is general rather than image-specific - a bare `text` node or any mark-bearing
inline fails identically - and it applies everywhere a block child is built: the document
root, a hoisted `carveSection`, and any block container such as a block quote or list item.

Each adjacent run of block-position inlines shares one paragraph rather than getting one
each, so an image followed by its caption text stays a single block instead of becoming two.

An image already inside a paragraph is untouched, and no existing test changed: the whole
spec corpus uses parser-produced shapes where this never occurs.

## Why the corpus sweep did not catch it

Carve source cannot express a block-position image, so the shape does not exist anywhere in
the spec corpus and a source-first round trip cannot construct it. Same blind spot as #519 and
#524, reached from the ProseMirror side.

Found by sweeping a production Laravel app's own ProseMirror corpus through the bridge; that
app's report editor inserts images at block level, so every figure in a stored document
vanished on the way to Carve source.

---

Touches the same region of `ProseMirrorToCarve` as #532, so whichever lands second needs a
trivial rebase.

author: lylo
body:
Image descriptions were parsed out of markdown and then thrown away, so every image published from Obsidian arrived at Pagecord with no description. Readers using a screen reader got `alt="Uploaded image"`.

## What changed

A markdown image carries two descriptions, and both are now sent:

```
![A boat at sunset](photo.jpg "Sunset on the Mekong")
```

- `alt="A boat at sunset"` describes the image and is not shown on the page
- `caption="Sunset on the Mekong"` appears underneath it

Wikilink images (`![[photo.jpg]]`) have no alt in their syntax, so they are unchanged.

## Also fixes a broken publish

A quoted title used to break publishing entirely. The path group swallowed the title, giving `photo.jpg "Sunset on the Mekong"`, which failed the anchored extension check. The image was skipped, never uploaded, and published as raw markdown pointing at a local vault path.

## Depends on

Pagecord PR 1141, which adds alt text support. Until that ships, the `alt` attribute is accepted but ignored, and captions behave as they do today.

## Note

`npx tsc --noEmit` reports an unrelated pre-existing error in `src/main.ts` about `activeDocument`, present on main and untouched here.

## Özet

`Factory - BakimX` panosunda kapalı issue'ların kartları `In Progress` sütununda asılı kalıyordu.

**Kök neden:** Projede iki yerleşik otomasyon çakışıyordu —
- `Item closed` → issue kapanınca Status=**Done**
- `Pull request linked to issue` → PR bağlanınca Status=**In Progress**

Issue **kapandıktan sonra** PR Development panelinden bağlanınca (`connected` olayı) ikinci otomasyon Done'ı eziyor, `Item closed` bir daha tetiklenmediği için kart orada kalıyordu. 2026-08-01'de 14 kart bu şekilde takıldı (`#203–#218` + `#194`, `#201`).

Kanıt (issue #213 zaman çizelgesi):
```
12:00:24  connected                       (aokcuoglu)
12:00:25  project_v2_item_status_changed  (github-project-automation[bot])
```

## Değişiklikler

- `scripts/project-board-sync.sh` (+ `bun run project:sync`): kapalı issue'nun kartını Done'a çeker; Done'da duran **açık** issue'ları yalnızca uyarı olarak raporlar (otomatik değiştirmez). Idempotent, `--dry-run` destekli, sadece Status alanına yazar.

Repo dışında ayrıca **`Pull request linked to issue` otomasyonu kapatıldı** (GraphQL'de `updateProjectV2Workflow` yok, UI'dan yapıldı). Bu PR o adımın kalıcı kaydı + güvenlik ağı.

## Risk

Düşük. Uygulama kodu, şema, CI ve deploy yolu değişmiyor; script yalnız GitHub Projects Status alanına yazıyor ve elle çalıştırılıyor.

author: zackees
body:
Makes `windows_long_path_publication_survives_fresh_worktree_reuse` explain its own failure. Advances #2186 — this is diagnosis, not the fix.

## The problem with the old failure

```
no archived session stats under ...\shared-cache\cache\zccache\history
```

That message is produced identically by three very different situations: nothing was archived, something was archived under a *different* cache root, or a partial directory was written. It says only that an assertion was reached. Chasing it on #2186, I built and killed four hypotheses — cache-dir relocation, daemon keying, fixture deps/path length, inherited `RUSTC_WRAPPER` — and none of them was it.

## What this reports instead

Everything under the redirected root that bears on the assertion — the `zccache` dir, its `logs` dir, the `history` dir, and the **contents of each session inside it** — plus soldr's own output, which names the paths it actually used. `soldr_cargo_check` now returns that output instead of dropping it, and the warm-build assertion reuses the same description.

## It found the cause in three runs

```
  ...\shared-cache\cache\zccache        -> daemon-state, history, logs
  ...\shared-cache\cache\zccache\logs   -> <empty>
  ...\cache\zccache\history             -> 13644877282573658812
  ...\history\13644877282573658812      -> .complete-v2
```

The session directory exists and contains **only `.complete-v2`**. `cache/zccache/logs` is empty, so `last-session-stats.json` was never written. Reading the archive path (`cargo_front_door/mod.rs:371-395`), `copy_session_artifact` returns `Option` and silently no-ops when the source is absent, while `mark_history_complete` runs regardless.

So **an empty archive is published as a complete one.** That is a robustness bug in its own right, separate from whatever kept the daemon from writing the stats: any consumer walking history sees a session that claims completeness and carries no data. Both halves are written up on #2186.

## Scope

Deliberately not fixing either half here. The completeness-marker fix belongs in `cargo_front_door/mod.rs`, which is 3,600+ lines and already over the ratchet ceiling, so additions there want their own PR — and the daemon-side question is unresolved. Landing the diagnosis first means the next person starts from evidence rather than from four dead hypotheses.

**The test still fails**, exactly as it did before this change and at the previous vendored zccache pin (verified with a clean control worktree). This PR changes what the failure tells you, not whether it happens.

## Also

`soldr_cargo_check` now clears `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, matching `stop_daemon`, which already did. This repo dogfoods, so `soldr cargo test` runs under a wrapper pointing at the *outer* soldr; inheriting it into a fixture build mixes two soldr installations in one compile. Not the cause here — I tested that explicitly — but it should not be inherited.

## Validation

- `loc_ratchet.py` — clean (file is 468 lines)
- `soldr cargo fmt -p soldr-cli -- --check` — clean
- `soldr cargo clippy -p soldr-cli --tests` — clean
- test run confirms the new output above
- `git status` — clean, single file changed
