author: helmerznl
body:
**342 of the 359 records on the production feed were rejected** — the entire catalog. This is the actual cause of the failing MovieVault v2 sync.

The diagnostics added in #462 named it on the first run against the live feed:

```
movievault_v2: release record rejected - missing keys ['aspectRatios', 'audioTracks',
  'discRegions', 'hdrFormats', 'packaging', 'subtitles', 'videoCodecs', 'videoResolution'],
  unexpected keys none
movievault_v2: rejected record (recordType=release operation=upsert revision=633
  releaseId=002245d7-d3ff-5571-b39b-ea3205b1dd4a) on contract distribution-4
```

## What is happening

`_release_record()` made all eight distribution-4 technical fields **required**. The live feed serves release records that carry `poster` but none of them.

The reason is chronological: `poster` landed in distribution-4 first, and the audio/subtitle/packaging/video work came in later rounds. Records published in between were never re-projected, so the `/v4` index is a mix — a minority with the full v4 shape, the bulk with poster-but-no-technical-fields.

MovieVault's own v4 schema marks all eight `required`, so the feed contradicts its own contract. That is worth fixing on the MovieVault side too. But a consumer that discards its entire catalog over it is the more expensive half of the bug, and the half this repo owns.

## The change

The eight fields become optional. A release is identified by its ids, title and barcodes; technical specs are enrichment, and their absence is not a reason to lose the film.

An absent key decodes to exactly the value a record with nothing to report already carried — `[]` or `None`, the same defaults the pre-v4 branch produced. "Not published" and "nothing known" are stored identically, so downstream sees one shape and no caller needs to learn a third state.

Scope deliberately kept tight:

- **`poster` stays required.** It is present on every record the feed serves, so its absence would be a genuine contract break rather than history.
- **Tolerating absence is not tolerating a wrong type.** A malformed value (`videoCodecs: "hevc"` instead of a list) still rejects the record.
- **Records that do carry the fields still decode all of them** — no silent loss for the newer half of the feed.

## Correcting the record on #462

My language-code hypothesis in #462 was **wrong**. `pt-BR`/`en-US` would have broken records, and that leniency is still correct on its own merits, but it was not what your sync was hitting. The diagnostics I added alongside it are what found this — which is the argument for having added them.

## Verification

- Reproduced the production record shape (poster present, eight fields absent) against the new code: accepted, identity and poster intact, technical fields empty. The same record is rejected by the code currently on beta.
- A fully populated v4 record still decodes 2 audio tracks, 3 subtitles and resolution `2160p`.
- Full backend suite: **1379 passed**, 23 skipped.
- MovieVault v2 PostgreSQL suite: **28 passed** against a real PostgreSQL 16 database with migrations applied.

## Tests

Two tests asserting the old strictness are **inverted deliberately** — they encoded the intent this PR changes. New coverage: a record stripped of all eight fields parses with empty defaults and keeps its identity and poster; each video key is individually optional; a missing poster still rejects; a malformed value still rejects.

## Follow-up worth considering

The feed serving records that violate its own published schema is a MovieVault-side issue. Re-projecting the historical records would let every consumer see one consistent shape. Worth raising there — this PR makes DiscVault resilient either way, it does not make the inconsistency go away.

author: seolizer
body:
`PrintLn(StrFromInt(42))` gab den **Zeiger** aus statt der Zeichenkette: `x = 133882772930580`. Über eine Zwischenvariable war dieselbe Rechnung korrekt — der Hinweis darauf, dass nicht die Funktion falsch ist, sondern die Typbestimmung der **Ausdrucksform**.

## Ursache

`cg_inferPrintType` kannte Literale und Bezeichner (lokale Variablen, Globals, Konstanten), aber **keine Aufrufknoten**. Ein `CGN_CALL` fiel auf den Rückgabewert 0 und wurde als Ganzzahl ausgegeben.

Dieselbe Familie wie der f64-Klassifizierer, der `CGN_CAST` nicht kannte: der Typ-Klassifizierer im Codegen erfasst nicht alle Ausdrucksformen, die den fraglichen Typ liefern.

## Umsetzung — die Reihenfolge ist der Kern

1. Der **deklarierte** Rückgabetyp aus der vorhandenen Registry (`fnRetList`, bisher nur über `cg_funcRetClassIdx` genutzt) — `pchar`, `f64`, `bool`.
2. **Nur wenn die Funktion dort nicht steht**, also ein Builtin ist: die Liste der acht Zeichenketten-Builtins (`StrFromInt`, `IntToStr`, `FloatToStr`, `StrConcat`, `StrCopy`, `StrSub`, `StrNew`, `StrTrim`).

Eine reine Namensliste würde eine gleichnamige Benutzerfunktion mit `int64`-Rückgabe falsch behandeln. Umgekehrt tragen die Builtins keinen Registry-Eintrag, weil der Codegen sie unmittelbar emittiert — deshalb beides, in dieser Reihenfolge.

## Test

`tests/print_call_result_test.sh` (6 Prüfungen, in `make test`) prüft den ausgegebenen **Wert**, dazu zwei Gegenproben:

- eine Funktion mit `int64`-Rückgabe muss Zahl bleiben — ohne das wäre eine zu breite Regel („jeder Aufruf liefert eine Zeichenkette") unbemerkt geblieben
- beide Wege, direkt und über eine Zwischenvariable, müssen dasselbe ergeben

Gegen den Vorgängerstand: **1 PASS / 5 FAIL**.

`tests/feature_checks/generics/test_generics.lyx` — der Auslöser aus #1009 — gibt jetzt korrekte Werte aus (`max(10, 20) = 20` statt einer Zeigeradresse).

## Nachweis

- Fixpunkt gen3 == gen4: `9ebb0a80`
- `make test`: 20 PASS / 0 FAIL
- `make test-lyx`: 137 grün / 7 bekannt rot / 0 unerwartet rot
- Beispiele 205/206, Unit-Sweep 379/380 — beide Fehlschläge bestehen auch vorher

Closes #1058 (Issue wird nach dem Merge von Hand geschlossen)

author: vchelaru
body:
## Problem
`BatchDrawCallCounter.BeginBlendMode(Blend)` took a fast path straight to raylib's canned `BlendMode.Alpha`/`Additive` whenever it could, regardless of `_renderTargetBlendActive` — so `Blend.Normal` (the default) and `Blend.Additive` never got the premultiply-consistent alpha accumulation the render-target bake pass exists to provide. Their canned modes square the source alpha instead of accumulating it as coverage, so a render target containing ordinary translucent content ends up under-opaque, corrupting any further composite of that bake.

## Fix
Skip the canned-mode fast path while `_renderTargetBlendActive` is true, and give `Normal`/`Additive` a premultiply-consistent alpha source factor (`One` instead of `SrcAlpha`) alongside their existing (already-correct) color factors.

## Tests
Added two pixel-readback tests to `BlendModeRenderTests` following the existing Replace/ReplaceAlpha/SubtractAlpha/MinAlpha pattern — both reproduced the exact squared-alpha values predicted by hand (191/255 for Normal, 64/255 for Additive) before the fix, and pass after it. Full `RaylibGum.Tests` suite (571 tests) is green.

Closes #4204

body:
## Description

The docs asserted the **opposite** of what [hydradb-application#643](https://github.com/usecortex/hydradb-application/pull/643) (PRO-1215) ships.

`essentials/v2/metadata.mdx` said:

> | Lists | Exact set equality for supported list-shaped comparisons, **not OR/IN**. For example, `tags: ["alpha", "beta"]` matches a stored `"alpha,beta"` set, but `tags: ["alpha"]` does not. |
> | OR | Run multiple queries and union client-side. |

and `query.mdx` said *"Range, contains, fuzzy, and OR operators are not supported"*. PRO-1215 gives list values OR/ANY semantics, so all of that is now wrong.

This PR is docs-only. It states the real contract everywhere a reader can land:

- **A list matches a source holding ANY one of its values.** Separate keys still AND, so `{"department": ["legal","finance"], "status": "published"}` reads as *(legal OR finance) AND published*.
- **There is no ALL/AND operator within a single key.** Called out explicitly — with the three workarounds (model the combination as its own field, split across keys, intersect client-side) — rather than left as an omission. This was the specific review ask on #643.
- **Lists are `VARCHAR`-only.** A list on a declared `INT8`/`INT16`/`INT32`/`INT64`/`FLOAT`/`DOUBLE`/`BOOL` field returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Undeclared fields and everything under `additional_metadata` default to `VARCHAR`, so lists work there.

### Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `essentials/v2/metadata.mdx` | Corrected the filter-semantics table; new "Filtering on several values at once (ANY)" section with examples; "Matching several values on one field" spelling out that ALL is unsupported; "Lists are VARCHAR-only" with the real 400 body; 2 new troubleshooting rows |
| `api-reference/v2/endpoint/query.mdx` | Replaced "OR operators are not supported" with the ANY contract, a worked example, and a case table |
| `api-reference/v2/endpoint/query-overview.mdx` | Replaced "ANDed exact-match constraints"; added the OR/ANY example |
| `essentials/metadata.mdx` (v1) | v1 is still a published version hitting the same backend and never mentioned lists at all — added the ANY section + ALL warning |
| `AGENTS.mdx` | New "Metadata filter semantics" block — agents read this as the quick reference |
| `api-reference/v2/openapi.json` | `metadata_filters` description said arrays were *"set-equality/list-style filters"* |

### Note on `openapi.json`

That file is generated. The description is authored in `scripts/openapi/postprocess.go` in `hydradb-application`, and every prior change here arrived as a `chore(docs): update OpenAPI spec from hydradb-application @ <sha>` sync commit. Editing only this copy would be reverted by the next regeneration, so **the source constant is fixed in hydradb-application#643** (commit `6a512a7b`) and this is the matching sync. The same schema feeds Fern, so the wrong sentence was in the SDK reference too.

Only the one description line changes here — PR #250's additions to this file are untouched.

## Related Issue

PRO-1215. Docs counterpart to https://github.com/usecortex/hydradb-application/pull/643

- [ ] New content (guide, tutorial, API docs)

Behavior confirmed against a local stack (two sources, `department: finance` and `department: legal`, both `priority: 7`):

|---|---|
| *(none)* | `['doc-finance', 'doc-legal']` |
| `{"department":"finance"}` | `['doc-finance']` |

author: bertpl
body:
**TL;DR**: Two counting defects with opposite signs fixed, and the cost-model convention that decides both is now written down.

- `x ** 0` and `1.0 ** x` returned counted results, over-counting downstream work; they now fold to a plain `1.0`.
- `round(x, n)` returned a plain float, silently stopping all downstream counting; it now re-wraps.

## Description

### Problem addressed

- **`x ** 0` kept its result counted** even though `pow(x, 0)` is `1.0` for *every* x (nan and inf included) — so downstream expressions charged work a compiled port never does: `math.sqrt(x ** 0)` counted a full SQRT, `10.0 / (x ** 0)` a DIV, where the port ships a precomputed constant.
- **`1.0 ** x` had no fold at all** and charged a full POW, despite `pow(1, y)` being `1.0` unconditionally.
- **`round(x, n)` dropped countedness**: it counted its RND (and MUL + DIV for nonzero n) but returned the result as a plain float, contradicting the FLOP-types table's own "stays `CountedFloat`" row and silently ending all downstream counting.

### Implementation

- The cost model gains a **third anchoring convention**: zero cost and countedness are independent axes. A float-valued result that *depends on* a counted operand stays a `CountedFloat`; a result whose **bits the operation's semantics fix for every possible counted operand** is a compile-time constant of the port and comes back plain, so downstream folds mirror the port's constant propagation. The constant cases are enumerated (`x ** 0`, `1.0 ** x`, `float.imag`), with bit-level near-misses (`x * 0.0`, `x + nan`) staying counted.
- `__pow__` / `__rpow__` / the `math.pow` patch return the plain constant for a **plain** exponent 0 or base 1; a `CountedFloat` in either slot remains the runtime opt-in (POW, counted result).
- `__round__`'s float-returning overloads re-wrap via the same `float.__new__` idiom as every neighboring dunder.

## Attention points

- **Return types change** for `x ** 0`, `1.0 ** x` (now exactly `float`) and `round(x, n)` (now `CountedFloat`) — deliberate and user-visible, hence the two changelog lines.
- **The opt-in is type-based, not value-based**: `x ** CountedFloat(0.0)` still counts POW and stays counted — the fold applies only to plain (compile-time-constant) operands.

## Tests / Spikes

- **TEST:** end-to-end probe — `x ** 0` and `1.0 ** x` plain at 0 flops, `math.sqrt(x ** 0)` counts nothing, `round(x, 1)` returns a `CountedFloat` with MUL + RND + DIV, `x ** CountedFloat(0.0)` counts POW.
- 4 new test functions (absorbing folds across nan/inf receivers, `math.pow` mirror, counted-operand opt-ins); the constant-exponent parametrization and the round/pow contract tests updated to pin the new return types.

## Changelog entry

Fixed:

```
- `round(x, n)` on a counted value no longer returns a plain float, which silently stopped all downstream counting
- `x ** 0` and `1.0 ** x` now fold to a plain-float constant the way a compiled port would, instead of producing a counted result that over-counted downstream work
```

author: claude-aye
body:
GET /geocode proxies the public OpenStreetMap instance, whose usage policy
allows one request per second per deployment and enforces it unilaterally by
IP — a block would take the whole platform's geocoding down at once.

The Redis cache (#54) is the primary lever; this is the floor under it, for
when the cache cannot absorb: new addresses, a burst of distinct users, or
Redis down — in which case there is no cache at all and 100% of the traffic
goes out. That last case is why the counter is in memory and depends on
nothing: a Redis-backed limiter would go blind exactly when it matters most.

RateLimitedGeocodingService is a decorator over IGeocodingService, wired
between the cache and the adapter (Cache -> RateLimit -> Adapter), so a cache
hit consumes no slot and only calls that really leave are metered. A caller
waits at most 3s for its slot, then is refused with the adapter's exact 502 —
saturation and an outage are the same event seen from the client.

Slots come from a reservation cursor rather than a refilling bucket: the
read-modify-write is one synchronous block, so two callers can never claim the
same slot; reservations are strictly increasing, so service is first-come,
first-served; and capacity is exactly one, so an idle period cannot be spent
as a burst. A refusal reserves nothing, and is raised up front rather than
after sleeping a budget whose outcome is already decided.

The per-process counter assumes a single API instance — true today, and
restated in a boot-time log because replication would multiply the real rate
silently.

author: anupamme
nolte
body:
## Summary

The corpus said nothing about GitHub merge queues. That left the portfolio's merge path — `strict: true` plus a manual serial rebase plus the `automerge` label — looking like the only option anyone had considered, when in fact GitHub ships a feature that automates exactly those mechanics. Nothing recorded whether that feature had been evaluated, so its absence was an omission rather than a decision.

This change makes it a decision, split across the two specs that own the respective halves.

**The load-bearing finding: merge queues require an organization-owned repository.** GitHub offers them "in any public repository owned by an organization, or in private repositories owned by organizations using GitHub Enterprise Cloud." Every `nolte/*` repository is **user-owned** (`owner.type: User`), so no plan tier makes the feature reachable today. The second finding: with a queue enabled, the direct merge API call behind `pascalgn/automerge-action` fails with `Changes must be made through the merge queue` — the queue and the current label path are mutually exclusive, not complementary.

## Changes

**`spec/project/pull-request-workflow/` — new §"Merge queue"** (owns *whether*):
- Availability gate as a **MUST NOT** plan-on-it-before-confirming rule, with the portfolio's user-owned status stated as the current blocker.
- **MUST NOT** run a queue and the `automerge` label path together.
- **SHOULD** adopt only when merge contention is the real bottleneck; independent practitioner sources put break-even near 5–10 merges/day and ~8–10 actively merging engineers.
- **MUST NOT** adopt while required checks are flaky — a queue amplifies flakiness, since a failing entry is removed and the entries behind it rebuild.
- A repository that adopts one **MUST** record which manual mechanisms it supersedes (§Branch freshness `strict: true`, §"Sequential merge" serial rebase).
- The portfolio decision recorded explicitly, revisitable only against availability and contention.
- Cross-references added in §Branch freshness and §Automerge trigger protocol; one new AC; §Sources extended with four triangulated claim entries.

**`spec/project/github-actions-best-practices/` — new §K "Merge-queue event wiring"** (owns *how*):
- **MUST** add `merge_group` (`checks_requested`) to every workflow backing a required check — otherwise the queue waits forever for a status nobody reports.
- **MUST NOT** keep a pull-request-context-only required check registered for a queued branch. In a merge group there's no PR to inspect, and **a workflow that doesn't start reports no status at all** — not a skip that counts green. This repo's `pr-lint` (required per `pull-request-workflow` §"PR lint workflow") is exactly that shape, so any future adoption has to restructure or de-require it.
- **MUST** point third-party CI at the `gh-readonly-queue/{base_branch}` prefix (different SHA from the PR head).
- **MUST NOT** protect a queued branch with a wildcard branch-protection pattern — a queue can't be enabled on one.
- **MUST** derive the merge-group concurrency key from something populated in that context, or a newly queued entry cancels the run the queue is waiting on.
- **SHOULD** account for doubled execution (per PR *and* per merge group) before enabling.
- §J gains a routing line handing the adoption decision to `pull-request-workflow`; one new AC; two new references.

**Structural note:** section letters are cited across the corpus (`cicd-pipeline-design` cites `github-actions-best-practices` §A, §E, §G), so they're stable API. K is appended after J rather than inserted, the same rule that put T8 at the end of the falsifiability taxonomy in #534. Delimitation losing the last-position slot is the lesser cost; no spec rule mandates that ordering.

`spec/project/continuous-integration/` is deliberately untouched: a merge-group run is the same pipeline under a different trigger, and the trigger obligation belongs to the Actions binding.

## Linked issues

None — this came out of the question "does anything in the specs cover `merge_group`?", which nothing did.

## Testing

- `python3 scripts/validate_skills.py` — 124 artifacts, **0C / 9W / 0S / 24I** (warnings pre-existing)
- `vale` (3.15.2, the CI pin) on both canonical `en.md` — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 suggestions
- `SKIP=vale-prose pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only)` — all hooks Passed
- `python3 scripts/check_links.py --offline` — 152 critical, unchanged from the branch point (known pre-docs-build baseline)
- EN/DE parity: `pull-request-workflow` 162 lines / 22 headings / 101 bullets / 20 AC in both; `github-actions-best-practices` 177 / 19 / 107 / 19 in both

### Source list (per `spec/claude/research-triangulate/` §Author-time assertions)

Retrieval date 2026-08-01. Availability is the highest-blast-radius claim and carries three independent sources.

**Availability requires organization ownership** — GitHub Docs gated-feature reusable (Primary, verbatim via the API): `https://github.com/github/docs/blob/main/data/reusables/gated-features/merge-queue.md` · GitHub Blog GA announcement (Primary): `https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-merge-queue-is-generally-available/` · community discussion #51483 (Secondary): `https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/51483`

**Mechanics — same guarantee as `strict`, grouping, removal-and-rebuild, `gh-readonly-queue/` prefix, wildcard limitation** — GitHub Docs "Managing a merge queue" (Primary): `https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue` · merge-queue overview reusable (Primary): `https://github.com/github/docs/blob/main/data/reusables/pull_requests/merge-queue-overview.md`

**`merge_group` trigger obligation** — GitHub Docs, events that trigger workflows (Primary): `https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows`

**Mutual exclusivity with the automerge action** — upstream issue #235 incl. maintainer reply (Primary): `https://github.com/pascalgn/automerge-action/issues/235`

**Adoption thresholds** — Mergify (Secondary): `https://mergify.com/learn/merge-queue` · Tenki (Secondary): `https://tenki.cloud/blog/github-merge-queue-setup`

No source conflicted with another, so `spec/claude/research-triangulate/` §"Conflict resolution" wasn't triggered.

## Risk / rollout notes

Low: spec text only, no repository configuration touched. Nothing in the change enables a merge queue anywhere — the portfolio can't, and the specs now say why.

The one thing to be aware of: §K's PR-context rule means that if `nolte/*` ever moves to an organization and a repository wants a queue, `pr-lint` has to be restructured or dropped from the required set first. That is now written down rather than waiting to be discovered by a queue that hangs.

## What changed

- detect Kelivo's background conversation-title requests before normal turn handling
- generate a short local title without waking the resident Claude process
- keep title requests from resetting heartbeat timing, triggering recovery, or entering private chat context
- document the isolation and add focused regression tests

## Root cause

Kelivo falls back to the active assistant provider when no separate title model is configured. The shim previously treated every Anthropic `/v1/messages` request as a real user turn, so the title prompt and its embedded conversation transcript were queued into the resident Claude process.

## User impact

Automatic title generation remains available, but it no longer duplicates hidden conversation transcripts inside Claude's live context and no longer spends a model turn.

author: vuhnger
body:
`EventArranger.role` blir aldri lest for autorisasjon. `EventRolesGuard` sjekker bare *at* du er arrangør:

```ts
if (event.eventArrangers.find((e) => e.arrangerId === user.arrangerId)) {
  return true;
}
```

Rollen leses ett eneste sted i hele kodebasen, og det er ikke autorisasjon — `events.service.ts:597`, som plukker primærarrangøren for visning.

Konsekvensen er at en `COLLABORATOR` har nøyaktig samme makt som eventets egen arrangør. Org A eier eventet og inviterer org B som co-arrangør; en ADMIN i org B kan da slette eventet, fjerne alle andre co-arrangører, bannlyse deltakere og maile alle påmeldte.

Samme hull i org-grenen av guarden (linje 63-79): den løser opp *hvilken som helst* `eventArrangers`-rad, også en COLLABORATOR-rad.

#53 er ortogonal — den får en organisasjon til å *samtykke* til å bli co-arrangør, men sier ingenting om hva en samtykkende co-arrangør får gjøre, og rører ikke `eventRoles.guard.ts`.

## Avgrensning

Etter avklaring: **redigere, ikke eie.** En co-arrangør er invitert inn for å hjelpe til med å kjøre eventet, ikke for å kunne ta det fra den som lagde det.

| Rute | COLLABORATOR |
|---|---|
| `PATCH /events/:id` (innhold) | ja |
| `POST /events/:id/update` | ja |
| `GET /events/:id/registrations` | ja |
| `PATCH/DELETE .../registrations/:userId` | ja |
| `POST/GET /events/:id/invitations` | ja |
| `PATCH /events/:id` med `coOrganizerOrganizationIds` | **nei** |
| `DELETE /events/:id` | **nei** |

## Fiksen

Ny `@EventArrangerRoles(...)`-dekoratør, samme mønster som `@OrganizationRoles`. Fravær betyr begge roller, som er tilfellet for de fleste rutene — bare de to eierrutene merkes.

Guarden leser den for både direktearrangør-grenen og org-grenen. To detaljer:

- **Faller gjennom i stedet for å returnere.** Er direkteraden ikke god nok, kan samme person likevel være admin i en organisasjon som eier eventet med høyere rolle. Den høyeste tildelingen må vinne, ikke den første som finnes.
- **Feiler lukket.** Mangler `role`, slipper ingen gjennom. `role` er `not null` i skjemaet, så dette er dybdeforsvar — men det avslørte at de eksisterende testfixturene ikke satte feltet, og de er nå rettet.

Co-arrangørlista kan ikke uttrykkes som en helrute-regel, siden det er samme `PATCH` som redigerer innholdet. Guarden legger derfor den matchede rollen på `request.eventArrangerRole`, og handleren avviser feltet for en COLLABORATOR. `syncCoOrganizers` gjør `deleteMany` på alle co-arrangører som ikke er listet, så en tom liste er nettopp måten en co-arrangør ville fjernet alle de andre — inkludert arrangøren som inviterte den inn.

## Verifisert live

Knut er ADMIN i MAPS, som er COLLABORATOR på Digitus' event:

```
1) PATCH tittel                           HTTP 200
2) POST /update (varsle deltakere)        HTTP 201
3) GET deltakerliste                      HTTP 200
4) PATCH co-arrangørlista                 HTTP 403
5) DELETE eventet                         HTTP 403

Kjell, ADMIN i Digitus som eier eventet:
6) PATCH co-arrangørlista                 HTTP 200
```

Underveis demonstrerte testen hullet utilsiktet: et av de første kallene, før fiksen var kompilert inn, fjernet faktisk MAPS som co-arrangør med `{"coOrganizerOrganizationIds": []}` — og etterlot Knut uten tilgang til eventet han nettopp hadde hatt full kontroll over.

Dev-databasen er tilbakestilt (Digitus alene som ADMIN-arrangør, tittel og testoppdateringer fjernet).

## Tester

7 nye i `eventRoles.guard.arranger-role.spec.ts`. Mot **ufikset** guard: `Tests: 3 failed, 4 passed, 7 total` — de tre som feiler er nettopp avvisningene og eksponeringen av rollen på requesten.

`eventRoles.guard.spec.ts` har fått `role` på fixturene sine. Uten det feilet fire eksisterende tester, fordi guarden nå med rette feiler lukket på en rad uten rolle.

Full suite: `Tests: 329 passed, 329 total`.

author: carlelieser
body:
Ran the deslop checklist over all nine files in `docs/`.

## What was found

The corpus is unusually clean: **zero** chatbot leakage, placeholders, model-specific markup, tracking parameters, "Despite its challenges" conclusions, emoji decoration, skipped heading levels, or rule-of-three padding. AI vocabulary density is near zero. Tables all carry real per-row data.

Three genuine patterns, fixed:

**Self-assurance about the text itself (6 instances)** — "Stated because a stack page that lists only benefits is a sales document", "Stated so that the absences are decisions rather than oversights", "Honest about what cannot be written yet", and three more. Each preceded a section whose heading already said the same thing. Deleted; no fact was underneath them.

**Formulaic repeated phrasings (6 instances)** — "a signal attached rather than a plan to think harder later" appeared in three documents; "a regression suite rather than an anecdote" in three. Replaced with direct statements that keep the fact (ADR-0006's ~50 minimum) and drop the frame.

**One sentence-initial "Additionally"** in qa.md §8.

## What was deliberately left alone

`rather than` appears 129 times across ~25k words. I cut 23 where the contrast was decoration and kept 106 where the "rather than" names an alternative that was genuinely considered and rejected — stdio vs. a local HTTP port, Node sidecar vs. Rust, binary extension vs. npm package. That construction is the documents' actual argument; stripping it mechanically would have removed the reasoning.

Also untouched per the checklist's "do not flag" sections: em dashes (consistent house style, not comma-replacement), confident superlatives, plain is/has phrasing, formal register, and the "X, not Y" constructions carrying real design contrasts.

## Flagged, not fixed

- **SQLite-Vector's licence** (`stack.md` §8, `runtime.md` §4.3) is recorded as unconfirmed — GitHub reports no recognised SPDX identifier. Already tracked as open in the docs; worth resolving before it ships in an installer.

No factual claims, numbers, or cross-references were altered.

author: dldnsgkr
body:
`main` 병합 시 EC2에 자동 배포되는 워크플로와, PR 단계 검증 CI를 추가합니다.
백엔드(`Dvely_springboot`)의 `deploy-ec2.yml` / `ci.yml` 패턴을 프론트 특성에 맞게 옮겼습니다.

## 배포 방식

`dist` 심볼릭 링크를 `releases/<sha>` 로 갈아끼웁니다. 정적 파일이라 프로세스 재시작이 없고,
`mv -T`(rename)라 교체 중 404가 나는 구간이 없습니다. 이전 릴리스는 5개까지 남겨 롤백에 씁니다.
빌드는 러너에서 하고 서버로는 `dist` tar만 보냅니다 — 서버 메모리 3.8GB에 MySQL·백엔드·Docker가 이미 올라가 있습니다.

교체·롤백·릴리스 정리 로직은 실제 EC2의 `/tmp`에 같은 구조를 만들어 8회 연속 배포로 검증했습니다.

## ⚠️ 자동 배포는 아직 꺼져 있습니다

`deploy-ec2.yml` 은 **수동 트리거(`workflow_dispatch`)만** 열어 두었습니다.

서비스 중인 빌드가 `6ecb826`(2026-05-28)이라 `main`과 78커밋 차이가 있고, 그 사이 백엔드 API가
V12→V30으로 바뀌어 호환성 확인 없이 한 번에 올리기 어렵습니다. `push` 트리거를 켜 두면
이 PR을 병합하는 순간 78커밋이 그대로 프로덕션에 나갑니다.

수동 배포로 정상 동작을 확인한 뒤 `deploy-ec2.yml` 상단 `push` 블록의 주석을 풀면 됩니다.

## 함께 고친 것

**1. 리눅스에서 빌드가 깨지는 import (실제 버그)**

`src/components/ui/Filter.tsx` 를 소문자 `@/components/ui/filter` 로 import 하던 곳이 2군데 있었습니다.
macOS는 대소문자를 구분하지 않아 로컬에서는 통과하지만, 리눅스 러너와 EC2에서는 모듈 해석에 실패합니다.
`tsc` 도 `TS1261` 로 잡고 있었습니다.

**2. `.env.example` 추가 — 현재 프로덕션 프론트의 API 호출이 전부 깨져 있습니다**

`src/utils/httpClients.ts` 는 `VITE_API_URL` 로 axios `baseURL` 을 잡는데,
서버에 배포된 번들을 뜯어보니 `baseUrl=void 0` 입니다. 빌드 시 값이 없었다는 뜻입니다.

그래서 `/auth/github/url` 같은 호출이 `https://qeploy.com/auth/github/url` 로 나가고,
nginx는 `/api/` 만 백엔드로 넘기므로 SPA fallback에 걸려 `index.html`(HTML)이 돌아옵니다.

워크플로는 빌드 전에 값이 비었는지 확인하고, 빌드 후 그 문자열이 번들에 실제로 들어갔는지까지
대조한 뒤에야 업로드합니다.

## 패키지 매니저는 bun

`package-lock.json` 은 2026-05-25 이후 갱신이 끊겨 `package.json` 과 어긋나 있고 `npm ci` 가 거부합니다
(`i18next`, `react-i18next`, `@tanstack/react-query-devtools` 누락).
실제로 유지되는 락파일은 `bun.lock` 입니다 — `package.json` 을 마지막으로 바꾼 커밋(`2c61c23` "i18n 라이브러리 추가")에서 함께 갱신됐습니다.

두 락파일이 공존하는 상태는 따로 정리가 필요합니다.

## 등록한 설정값

Secrets: `EC2_HOST`, `EC2_USER`, `EC2_SSH_KEY` (CLI로 등록 — 웹 UI 붙여넣기는 줄바꿈이 깨집니다)
Variables: `VITE_API_URL` = `https://qeploy.com/api/v1`

## 남은 일

- [ ] `main` 보호 규칙에 CI의 `Typecheck and build` 를 required status check로 등록 (워크플로 파일만으로는 병합이 막히지 않습니다)
- [ ] lint 에러 17건 정리 후 `ci.yml` 의 `continue-on-error: true` 제거 (대부분 `react-refresh/only-export-components`)

Aus der Lighthouse-Runde, an der Quelle geheilt (Sage-Protokol PR #777).

## Was drin ist — Modul 23 UI

Der „🔑 Schlüssel holen"-Link wurde ohne Adresse erzeugt und bekam eine erst beim Sichtbarwerden. Solange er verborgen war, stand ein zielloser Link im Dokument (Lighthouse `crawlable-anchors`). Die **Sichtbarkeit** hängt unverändert an der echten Anbieter-Kenntnis — fail-soft wie zuvor.

Byte-1:1, Kanon `00a6920535d3`. Die Datei war vorher byte-gleich zum alten Kanon.

## Was BEWUSST fehlt — Modul 17

Der zweite Befund (Widget-Beschriftung über heller Seite nur 3,09:1 / 1,97:1 statt 4,5:1) ist hier **nicht** ausgerollt, und das mit Absicht.

`sbkim/17_floating_widget.js` trägt hier eine **repo-eigene Pflege, die der Sage-Kanon nicht hat** — Klaus' Fix vom 2026-06-28:

```js
// Pro-App-Namensraum: die Schlüssel tragen den App-Pfad, damit
// Geschwister-Apps auf demselben Origin sich NICHT denselben
// Widget-Zustand teilen. Vorher führte ein Schließen in EINER App
// zum Verschwinden in ALLEN.
var LS_KEY_VISIBLE = "sbkim_widget_visible__" + WIDGET_SCOPE;
```

Byte-1:1-Überschreiben würde diesen Fix **zurückdrehen** — auf einer geteilten `github.io`-Adresse genau das Problem, das er behebt. Gleichzeitig fehlt der Fassung hier der Stufen-Render von 2026-05-26 aus dem Kanon. Sie ist also weder Vorgänger noch Nachfolger, sondern eine **Gabelung**.

Das gehört an der Quelle zusammengeführt (Klaus' Namensraum-Fix in den Sage-Kanon holen, dann sind alle wieder byte-1:1), nicht hier weggebügelt. Ist als eigener Schritt notiert.

**Gleiche Lage:** Muttis-Rezeptbuch (identische sha), Mein-Mixarium, BookLedgerPro (dort ein anderer Eigen-Fix: Proxy-ID-Guard gegen Kollision mit dem statischen Siegel-Badge).

author: dseelinger
body:
Closes [#55](https://github.com/retiring-studios/directive-47/issues/55). Part of [#17](https://github.com/retiring-studios/directive-47/issues/17).

Satisfies `Help_ForAnUnresolvedUtterance_OffersTheNearestCanonicalName` — the last criterion on the feature.

## What it does

```
Recover("fewl")   →  I don't recognize "fewl".
                     Did you mean fuel?

Recover("xyzzy")  →  I don't recognize "xyzzy".
                     Here's what I can help with:
                     Your ship
                     Where you are
```

## Done when

- [x] An utterance resolving to no capability produces the nearest canonical name rather than a refusal
- [x] A resolution with no near match says so plainly

## The package question, which the issue notes flagged

Priced before a line was written. Both candidates are clean on the licence allowlist, both zero-dependency, neither ships native binaries:

| | Licence | Deps | Newest TFM | Downloads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Fastenshtein` 1.0.12 | MIT | none | `net10.0` | 11.2M |
| `FuzzySharp` 2.0.2 | MIT | none | `netstandard2.1` | 14.9M |

Hand-rolled won: ~35 lines of textbook Levenshtein doesn't earn a redistributed dependency inside a single-file exe. The real pull toward a package is [#22](https://github.com/retiring-studios/directive-47/issues/22), which needs the same thing over a much larger and more hostile vocabulary — so that's where it gets decided, with two real call sites to compare instead of one to generalize from.

That's also why `NearestName` is internal to `D47.Help` and named for its one job rather than for the general one it resembles. Nothing can start conforming to it in the meantime.

## Other calls, all recorded in decisions.md

- **Pool is capability ids + group names.** Not example utterances — matching those against STT output is the silent-failure mode decisions.md rules out. No spoken-name field either; ids are already short nouns, and a second required string loses to the same argument that kept `Detail` off the descriptor last story.
- **Tolerance is two edits flat, proportional above that.** So `fewl` reaches `fuel` without a fourteen-character group name being held to a four-letter standard.
- **Ties go to the earlier registration**, since that's already the order a spoken answer reads in. An arbitrary tie-break would answer the same utterance differently between runs.

## On the tests

Tests and code went in together on this one, so I never saw red. I paid it afterwards rather than claiming it: tightening the tolerance to `Length / 3` fails five tests including the criterion test, then it goes back green. The mutation isn't in the diff — it was run and reverted.

34 tests, green, no warnings. Tier 0 throughout.

## Manual pass

Nothing to see in a running build — no surface consumes help yet. Review starts at `tests/D47.Help.Tests/HelpRecoveryTests.cs`.

author: evanl1
body:
Delivers A0: an edge-reported Home Assistant topology and observation history that a user can actually see, with the honesty claim enforced at three independent layers.

## What ships

- **CloudLink ingress becomes a deployable process.** `apps/cloudlink` was a library with no composition root; it now has one, its own Railway service, a Broker TLS trust surface, and a shutdown that races `close()` against a deadline.
- **Two public read-only routes** — projection catalog and detail — with tenant scoping taken from the authenticated subject, never from the request.
- **A console view** rendering `receivedAt` as elapsed time rather than a bare timestamp, because a bare timestamp reads as current device state.
- **`authority: edge-reported-copy` / `liveStateAuthoritative: false`** are pinned as application-layer type constants, as API schema constants, and again in the console decoder. If anything renders, the claim holds.
- **Consumes the published AetherContracts 0.1.0-alpha.4** through 101 digest-verified artifacts, replacing the unpublished candidate copy. `tests/aether-contracts-consumer.test.mjs` runs AetherContracts' own verifier against this lock.

## Pre-existing defects fixed along the way

- `aethercloud_cloudlink_health_worker` had `UPDATE` without `SELECT` on `cloudlink_session_heads`, so `complete()`'s close path was broken in production. A new invariant test asserts every table granted `UPDATE` is also granted `SELECT`.
- `apps/api` registered signal handlers with `process.once`, so a second delivery hit the default disposition and killed the process mid-shutdown. The API drained nothing on every deploy stop, and printed nothing either because the app is composed with `logger: false`.
- `apps/api`'s `close()` was unbounded: a stalled database query left the process alive indefinitely after SIGTERM.

## Limitations recorded, not softened

- Authentication in the trusted-connector mode depends **entirely** on Broker-side per-Gateway ACLs. Credential verification is tautological by construction, and this composition consumes none of the per-publish attestation ADR-0014 decision 5 expects.
- The Runtime Manifest is memory-only, so a restart strands a Gateway whose session outlived its manifest.
- A stable MQTT client id means exactly one ingress instance.

## Verification

`pnpm check` — 113 test files, 953 tests. `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` — 38. `pnpm test:mqtt-integration` against a real Mosquitto. `pnpm test:home-assistant-e2e` was **not** run; it needs AetherEdge, and the docs say so.

## O que muda

- corrige a decisão de acesso das assinaturas manuais no `ProtectedRoute`;
- remove o fallback que podia liberar conteúdo privado sem `has_access=true`;
- diferencia falha técnica da RPC, falta de assinatura, e-mail não verificado, aprovação pendente, reprovação e expiração;
- adiciona testes unitários e de componente para o fluxo de acesso;
- reconcilia README, PRODUCT, ARCHITECTURE, TASKS e HANDOFF com o código e o estado real do projeto.

## Causa raiz

A auditoria confirmou que `compute_subscription_access` concede corretamente acesso Pro ao candidato manual válido em `live` e `sandbox`. O problema estava no frontend: exceções da RPC eram engolidas e apresentadas como ausência de cartão/assinatura, enquanto um fallback paralelo podia autorizar conteúdo privado mesmo com `has_access=false`.

## Impacto

O gate agora é fail-closed: somente administrador ou resposta explícita `has_access=true` abre as rotas privadas. Falhas técnicas mostram uma tela própria com tentativa novamente e não são confundidas com checkout.

author: mikelward
body:
Closes rough edge **17**. Rebased onto `307df4a`.

## The bug

```mesh
func f(_a) { puts "got=[$_a]" }
w = "--sleep=0"
f($w)          # mesh: f: unknown flag `--sleep`
```

`scan_call_value` tested the **runtime** `Value::String` for a `--` prefix. So data that merely *looked* like a flag could not be passed to a plain `func` at all — and what a call meant depended on what a variable happened to hold, the opposite of the decidability rule `DESIGN.md` keeps everywhere else ("readable from the line, never data-dependent"). `f("--sleep=0")` failed for the same reason, even though quoting makes a value in every other position.

## The rule

An option is a `--name` **written at the call site**, and the boundary is the `=`:

> Everything up to and including the `=` **names** the option and must be literal text the reader wrote. Everything after it is that option's **value** and may be quoted, expanded or globbed.

```rust
let name = text.split_once('=').map_or(text.as_str(), |(name, _)| name);
let word_globs = expand::segments_glob(word.value.pieces.iter().map(|piece| match piece {
    parser::WordPiece::Text { text, quote: parser::QuoteMode::Bare, .. } => (text.as_str(), true),
    parser::WordPiece::Text { text, .. } => (text.as_str(), false),
    parser::WordPiece::Variable { .. } | parser::WordPiece::Value { .. } => ("", false),
}));
text.starts_with("--")
    && !(word_globs && expand::text_globs(name))
    && (text.contains('=') || word.value.pieces.len() == 1)
```

Three things compose a name, and all are refused:

| composition | example | why it must not bind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| another word piece | `--$name`, `--"force"` | the runtime value picks the option |
| a **postfix chain** | `--FORCE:lower`, `--TAG=V9:lower` | a chain applies to the *whole* word, so the `=` is no barrier — it rewrites the name |
| a name that **globs** | `--*`, `--?orce` | resolves against the filesystem, so `ls` picks the option |

A chained expression is an `Expr::Modifier`, so requiring a bare `Expr::Scalar` refuses it. `--tag=$m.key` and `--tag=$xs[0]` are *not* chains despite appearing so — a member or index inside a word is an ordinary variable piece — and both bind normally.

### The glob test has two halves, and both are load-bearing

The **whole word** must glob for the filesystem to be consulted at all; the **name** must glob for what comes back to differ in the part that picks the option. Either alone admits a word the other catches:

- name only → `--fo*=bad[` is refused, though the unmatched `[` makes the complete word unglobbable, so it is exactly the text written and can no more choose an option than `--bad[` can. Refusing it swallowed the `unknown flag --fo*` command position reports.
- word only → `--tag=*.txt` would be refused, though its name cannot vary.

"Whole word" means every **piece**, not the first: `--fo*=x$v[` closes nothing until its third. Interpolated pieces stand in as placeholders exactly as `expand::word_globs` does it, since a value is literal to expansion and cannot close a class the bare text left open. `expand::segments_glob` is the predicate the expander already uses, so the scan cannot answer differently.

This predicate is deliberately **separate** from `is_bare_literal_word`, which answers a different question: how the bound value *types*, so `--n=2` is an integer and `--n="2"` a string. That one is unchanged, and keeping the two apart is load-bearing — conflating them was the first attempt and it broke every composed attached value.

### Spread stays scanned, deliberately

`f(prod, ...$args)` still reads a `--force` element as the option. Writing `...` is the explicit *"these are arguments, flags included"* gesture, and it is the channel a wrapper needs to forward flags it was handed. `f($w)` says "this is one value".

## Verification

| form | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `w = "--sleep=0"`, `f($w)` | `unknown flag --sleep` | **data** |
| `f("--sleep=0")` | `unknown flag --sleep` | **data** |
| `name = force`, `f(--$name)` | binds the switch | **data**, switch off |
| `f(--"force")` / `f(--"")` | binds / terminator | **data** |
| `f(--FORCE:lower)` / `f(--$name:lower)` | binds the switch | **data** |
| `f(--TAG=V9:lower)` | binds `--tag` | **data** |
| `f(--*)` with `./--force` on disk | binds the switch | **data** |
| `f(--?orce)` / `f(--bad[a-z])` | binds / reports | **data** |
| `f(--bad[)` | `unknown flag --bad[` | unchanged — never globbable, so literal |
| `f(--fo*=bad[)` / `f(--fo*=x$v[)` | `unknown flag --fo*` | unchanged — same reason |
| `f(prod, --force)` | binds | unchanged |
| `f(--tag="v2")` / `f(--tag=$w)` / `f(--tag="$w")` | binds | unchanged |
| `f(prod, --tag=$m.key)` / `f(prod, --tag=$xs[0])` / `f(--tag=x$v[)` | binds | unchanged |
| `f(--sleep=0)` / `f(--nosuch)` undeclared | `unknown flag` | unchanged |
| `f(--n=2)` / `f(--n="2")` | integer / string | unchanged |
| `args = [--force]`, `f(prod, ...$args)` | binds | unchanged |
| `f(--, --force)` | terminator, then data | unchanged |
| `f(prod, force: true)` | binds | unchanged |

`cargo test` 1240 passing, `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

## What the rebase changed

The branch was opened against `585d9b5`. `bf79900`, *"Make a glob a list however many paths it matched"*, landed on `main` in between and removed the single-match collapse — so a pattern is a `Value::List` whatever it matched. Two rows here were measured before that and no longer hold, so they are **re-measured rather than carried over**:

- `f(prod, --tag=*.txt)` with exactly one match used to bind, and now reaches the positionals like any other glob. `scan_call_value` inspects only `Value::String`, so a list falls through.
- `f(--*)` and `f(--?orce)` were asserted through a list-interpolation diagnostic, which is noise rather than the claim. Both glob tests now read the switch through a rest parameter — `force=false n=1` for data against `force=true n=0` for a binding — so "the glob did not choose the option" is asserted directly.

The first is the already-recorded *"a glob after `=` stops being an option"* follow-up, which `bf79900` widened from **multi-match** to **every glob**. That is strictly less surprising than it was — the answer no longer varies with what happens to be in the directory — but it is now a plain divergence from the command spelling, which still binds. `TODO.md` says so, and `a_glob_after_the_option_separator_does_not_yet_bind_in_a_value_call` pins both spellings side by side so the entry cannot go stale silently; it flips to `tag=a.txt n=0` when the follow-up is fixed.

One conflict, in `expand.rs`: `main` had grown `segments_glob` as the single place the glob question is decided, while this branch added `text_globs` for the option scan. Resolved by defining the second in terms of the first rather than keeping two spellings of one rule — which is what both doc comments asked for.

## Tests

Six: `a_value_call_reads_options_from_the_call_site_not_from_the_data`, `an_attached_option_value_may_be_quoted_or_expanded`, `a_composed_option_name_is_data_not_an_option`, `a_glob_cannot_choose_which_option_binds` (scratch directory with a `--force` file beside the script), `glob_syntax_the_expander_refuses_is_still_a_literal_option_name`, and the pinning `a_glob_after_the_option_separator_does_not_yet_bind_in_a_value_call`.

One existing row **moved rather than broke**: `a_modifier_reference_rejects_what_it_cannot_apply` asserted `$m("--x")` reports `unknown flag`. That is what this PR changes on purpose. The bare spelling `$m(--x)` still reports it — verified — so the row is rewritten bare and the quoted form asserted as data beside it.

## Eleven review rounds, and where they landed

The rule above never changed. What changed eleven times was my account of which shapes reach the predicate, so recording them is more useful than hiding them:

1. **Too wide** — reused the typing predicate; broke `--tag="v2"` and `--tag=$w`. A regression I

author: metalmmagic
body:
fix(spaces): crash recovery could race a live rename and call it incomplete

`pendingSpaceOp` is a crash marker written BEFORE the collection work, so a process that dies mid-way
is rolled forward on the next boot. `reconcilePendingSpaceOp` also runs on the config-RELOAD path,
which means the marker a live rename had just written was what the reconciler acted on, in the same
process, while the original was still running. Both call `moveSpaceData`, which renames every
collection `listCollections()` found, so the loser of each collection gets

    MongoServerError: Source collection ... does not exist

and the caller reports "rename incomplete (3 errors)" on a rename that had in fact succeeded.

Recovery now stands aside while an operation is running in THIS process: a live operation does not
need crash recovery, it needs to be left alone. If it dies its marker survives and the next boot
recovers it, which is the marker's whole purpose. Depth-counted, released in a finally, floored at
zero so an unbalanced release cannot wedge recovery off permanently.

Observed once in CI on space-rename and not reproducible on demand — proved from the code instead:
"source collection does not exist" requires a second concurrent mover, and the only other caller of
moveSpaceData is the reconciler.

author: mcboyle
body:
Cut 4 of 4.

## The defect

Both verdicts in the cut-35 gate rest on a list being **empty** — `not offenders` and `not graded_bug`. Emptiness cannot distinguish *"nothing is wrong"* from *"the scan never looked"*. Two mutations proved it, each leaving every other arm of the file passing:

- inverting the reachability polarity → no `tools/` source was ever scanned
- narrowing the finding pattern to crit-only → a `bug` grade was invisible

## Before/after, measured on this branch

| mutation | pristine | with guard |
|---|---|---|
| polarity inversion | **ESCAPED** (exit 0, 2 passed) | **CAUGHT** (exit 1) |
| regex → crit-only | **ESCAPED** (exit 0, 2 passed) | **CAUGHT** (exit 1) |

Not inherited from the preparing agent — re-run here under the full protocol, sha `09af7644bb7c74b2` restored after each.

One detail worth stating: **M2's pristine anchor is the inline regex, not the new named constant.** `_DEFECT_GRADE_RE` doesn't exist before this cut, so mutating it on the pristine file gave `anchor count 0`. I found the inline form (`re.search(r"\[(bug|crit)\s*\]", ln)`) and mutated that instead — otherwise the before-half would have been a claim about a line that didn't exist yet.

## The fix

Each verdict now runs through a named helper — `_scan_for_retired_probes` and `_graded_defect_lines` — and each helper has a **positive control** handing it an input whose correct answer is non-empty by construction.

The control must drive the **same** helper the verdict does. With the controls in place but the assertions still using their own inline copies, both mutations were re-measured and **both still escaped**. Certifying a copy rather than the gate is this file's own subject, one level in.

## Not a meta-gate

The filed objection — *"no test can be its own meta-test, and a tower of meta-gates trades a known gap for an unknown one"* — is answered rather than waved away. These controls assert nothing about this file's text and add no layer over the verdict. They're the ordinary two-sided form the gate **already uses** at the `tools/` reach check and the root-load `[ok` check, applied to the two arms that lacked it.

author: taddom-ceo
body:
## 1. E-Mail: Zeichen vor dem `@` erforderlich

Bisher wurden `@b` und `@anbieter.de` angenommen. Jetzt muss vor **und** hinter dem `@` etwas stehen.

| Eingabe | vorher | jetzt |
|---|---|---|
| `@b`, `@muster.de` | frei | gesperrt |
| `max@`, `max@@` | gesperrt | gesperrt |
| `m@b`, `max@muster.de` | frei | frei |

## 2. Straßenprüfung gegen ein echtes Verzeichnis

Neues Straßenverzeichnis mit **1.165.126 Straßen zu 8.159 Postleitzahlen** aus OpenStreetMap (`openpotato/openplzapi.data`, ODbL). Kein kostenpflichtiger Dienst und kein API-Schlüssel nötig.

Das Straßenfeld schlägt die Straßen der eingegebenen Postleitzahl zur Auswahl vor und weist unbekannte ab.

### Zwei Eigenheiten der Daten, die abgefangen werden mussten

**Abkürzungen.** Die Quelle kürzt „straße" grundsätzlich zu „str.", während Antragsteller sie ausschreiben. Ohne Angleichung wäre ausgerechnet die natürliche Schreibweise `Invalidenstraße` gegen den Bestand `Invalidenstr.` als unbekannt gewertet worden. `normalizeStreet` gleicht Schreibweise, Punkte, Bindestriche und Groß-/Kleinschreibung an.

**Lücken im Bestand.** Für **1.691 der 9.839 Postleitzahlen (17 %)** enthält das Verzeichnis gar keine Straßen. Dort wird nicht blockiert, sondern nur die Form geprüft — sonst käme in diesen Postleitzahlen niemand durch das Formular. Die Statuszeile meldet in diesem Fall „Für diese Postleitzahl liegt uns kein Straßenverzeichnis vor" statt fälschlich „Adresse bestätigt".

### Datenhaltung

671 statische Bündel unter `public/streets`, gruppiert nach den ersten drei Ziffern der Postleitzahl. Pro Eingabe werden 7–31 KB geladen statt 17 MB, und das Serverless-Bundle bleibt unberührt.

## Tests

Gegen den Produktions-Build im Browser durchgespielt:

| Fall | Ergebnis |
|---|---|
| PLZ 10115 | 53 Straßen in der Vorschlagsliste |
| `Invalidenstr.` / `Invalidenstraße` / `invalidenstrasse` | alle erkannt, „Weiter" frei |
| `Ackerstr.` | erkannt |
| `Fantasiestraße` in 10115 | abgewiesen mit Hinweis |
| `Musterweg` in 10115 und 01067 | abgewiesen |
| erfundene Straße in 01054 / 01056 (keine Daten) | „Weiter" frei, Hinweis auf fehlendes Verzeichnis |
| Bündel `/streets/101.json`, `/streets/803.json`, `/streets/999.json` | HTTP 200, 7–31 KB |

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — fehlerfrei
- `npm run build` — erfolgreich

## Hinweise

- Das Repository wächst um rund 19 MB (672 neue Dateien).
- Die Quelle dokumentiert selbst, dass die OSM-Daten nicht fehlerfrei sind. Bei sehr neuen oder ungewöhnlich erfassten Straßen sind vereinzelte Fehlalarme möglich. Falls das Risiko zu hoch ist, lässt sich das Blockieren auf reines Vorschlagen umstellen, ohne die Daten anzufassen.

author: damir434566
body:
Follow-up to #738 (merged). Rebuilds the "Where to buy" row to match a supplied design reference, and reworks the gallery on `/product/[id]`.

All changes are in `src/components/product/ProductClient.tsx`.

## Retailer row

- Logo becomes a 56px circle on white, up from a 40px rounded square.
- Store name goes to 15px medium; the `BEST` badge inverts to a solid `--foreground` pill; `Official Store` sits beneath it.
- A vertical divider separates the store block from the buy block.
- Availability moves up as an uppercase label paired with a status dot — green for in stock, amber for low stock, grey and struck through for sold out — above a `text-2xl` bold price.
- The bare chevron becomes a solid `View on Store` pill with an outbound arrow, so the row reads as a button. It fills with `--foreground` and takes `--background` for its text, so it inverts correctly in both themes.
- Rows stack vertically below `sm` so the CTA stays reachable on mobile.

Ratings are kept but move under the store name: the reference has no rating to place, and the buy block is now a fixed three-part layout with no room for stars.

## Gallery

- Thumbnails move from a row beneath the photo to a column beside it, top-aligned on the left, growing to 80px at `lg`.
- The photo grows from 438×584 to 528×703 via a wider left grid column, and `sizes` is updated to match.

The photo is deliberately **not** stretched to the info panel's full height. At this column width that produces a 468×1072 box, and since product shots are portrait and rendered with `object-contain`, roughly two thirds of it would be empty white. The 3:4 ratio is kept and the increase comes from column width instead.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run build` succeeds on the rebased base.
- `eslint` on the changed file reports only the two pre-existing warnings in the retailer-logo `onError` handlers, which this change doesn't touch.
- Rendered in Chromium at 1440px in both themes and at 390px. Measured: photo box 528×703 (was 438×584), thumbnail rail 80×80 top-aligned at the same `y` as the photo box, rows stacking correctly at mobile width.

`tsc` caught a real defect during this work: the availability check was written against `"out of stock"`, but the union is `"in stock" | "low stock" | "sold out"`, so the sold-out branch could never fire. Fixed to `"sold out"` before commit.

body:
## Stack position

This is **PR1 of four implementation PRs**, preceded by compatibility PR0 #707. Its base is `test/function-system-contracts` at `5d6518bd61a7557f8b8605438e79cba57930306d`.

> **Do not merge this PR.** It must remain a draft until the maintainer reviews and merges it. The agent must not merge, mark ready, retarget, or enable auto-merge.

## Roadmap

The rewrite is five stacked PRs total: PR0 followed by four implementation PRs.

1. **PR0 — Compatibility baseline** — #707 (open draft)
2. **PR1 — Engine + catalog vertical slice** — #710 (this PR, open draft)
3. **PR2 — Complete function-system migration** — planned
4. **PR3 — Static composition and feature separation** — planned
5. **PR4 — `.mecb`-driven native builds** — planned

A later PR5 may clean up the specialization macro source, but it is not required to complete the architecture.

### PR0 — Freeze compatibility contracts

Freeze source operations, exports, specialization choices, runtime IDs, bytecode fixtures, and native/WASM behavior without changing production architecture.

### PR1 — Establish the replacement architecture

Replace `mech-program` with `mech-engine`; introduce immutable `FunctionCatalog`, per-program mutable `FunctionEnvironment`, and an explicit legacy boundary; propagate one `FunctionSystem` through programs, interpreters, and `RuntimeBuilder`; and migrate `math/add` as the first complete source/bytecode vertical slice.

### PR2 — Migrate the complete function system

Proposed title: `refactor(functions): replace legacy dispatch with explicit catalogs`

Migrate math, comparison, logic, range, matrix, set, string, statistics, combinatorics, tables, assignment, access, and conversion; route syntax operators through canonical `OperationId`s; move exact prelude/module visibility into export metadata; migrate runtime factories, closures, and user-function visibility; remove direct machine construction, legacy descriptors and tables, name heuristics, module scanning, inventory-based composition, the temporary fallback, and the remaining interpreter package boundary. **At the end of PR2 there is no legacy fallback.**

### PR3 — Separate standard composition and build profiles

Proposed title: `refactor(stdlib): make machine composition explicit`

Create `mech-stdlib` as the standard composition crate; remove standard machine dependencies from `mech-engine`; separate runtime kernels, source specializers, and bytecode lowerers; forward features only to selected machines; and define minimal runtime, source, compiler, native, and browser profiles.

### PR4 — Build minimal native applications from `.mecb`

Proposed title: `refactor(build): generate native applications from mecb requirements`

Record deterministic runtime requirements in `.mecb`, derive exact packages/features, generate a minimal Cargo project, link only required implementations, support source and `.mecb` inputs, produce a compiler-free executor, add native output to the maintained build path, and delete legacy `mechc`.

## What changed

- replaced the obsolete `mech-program` package with `mech-engine`, preserving the public `MechProgram` concept while removing dead run-loop, persistence, and filesystem remnants
- added immutable `FunctionCatalog` construction and mutable per-program `FunctionEnvironment` visibility/binding state
- paired the catalog with an explicit immutable, collision-safe `LegacyFunctionBoundary` in one `FunctionSystem`
- ensured custom systems—including empty ones—never inherit hidden ownership from the default system
- propagated the exact same function-system identities through interpreters, child interpreters, checkpoints, programs, retained programs, runtime-created programs, and `RuntimeBuilder`
- added inventory-independent `math/add` source and runtime installation for every enabled scalar/shape family
- made `math/add` prelude-visible only; it is not falsely exported as a named module item
- routed named source calls through canonical name/ID validation, with collision-safe diagnostics and no hard-coded `math/add` literal in generic dispatch
- routed bytecode reconstruction through the catalog first; a catalog-owned missing factory now returns `RuntimeFunctionUnavailable` instead of silently falling through
- kept `GuardFunctionSafety::Unsupported` because mixed-kind and mutable-reference specialization reads live values and cannot truthfully claim static purity
- made the compiler-free fixture remove the migrated add factories from the legacy inventory before execution, proving add reconstruction uses the catalog while cosine/range/string operations still use the explicit temporary boundary

## Temporary fallback boundary

PR1 intentionally retains a named fallback only for operations not yet migrated. It is migration scaffolding, not the destination architecture.

PR2 migrates every remaining standard operation and factory, then deletes the boundary and fallback completely. User-defined functions remain supported through the new function model; they are not a legacy fallback.

## Compatibility facts

- bytecode remains version 1
- all frozen PR0 JSON and `.mecb` artifacts are byte-for-byte unchanged
- native default factory count: 196
- required minimal profile: 14
- browser/WASM profile: 56
- all 14 scalar kinds with all enabled shapes: 1,148
- frozen `math/add` operation ID: `00cc529041cb60c3`
- frozen representative runtime IDs remain unchanged, including `AddSS<f64>`, `AddSMD<f64>`, `AddMDS<f64>`, `AddMDMD<f64>`, and `AddV2S<f64>`

## Validation cost correction

The original GitHub run took **27m13s** because a 26m32s step serialized the bytecode boundary, all PR0 contracts, the PR1 catalog gate, and ordinary example/feature checks. An intermediate run still took **20m59s**, entirely because its monolithic Windows job ran for 17m51s after a 3m08s runner queue.

PR1 now runs these independent groups concurrently:

- ordinary Cargo feature/example checks
- three PR0 compatibility slices
- the PR1 engine-catalog vertical slice
- the existing language, runtime, native, browser, Windows, macOS, and dynamic-module jobs

A final required check named `cargo` fails unless the ordinary Cargo job, every PR0 slice, and the PR1 catalog job all succeed. The PR1 gate also runs the nine unique `math/add` tests once in one tailored standalone profile; it no longer compiles a default math suite and then repeats most of it in a second profile.

Windows now runs 67 platform-relevant assertions instead of 981 mostly generic duplicates. All resolver/workspace portability contracts, isolated directory/path tests, Windows serve behavior, formatter behavior, and one real linked CLI remain covered. The runtime portability compile runs in parallel with the CLI/platform shard, and the stable required check remains named `Windows CLI`. The browser job also reuses its first WASM package build instead of rebuilding it for the static-bundle smoke.

Authoritative final GitHub timings:

- complete workflow: **13m26s**, including about **3m20s** of hosted-runner queue while PR0 and PR1 ran together
- longest actual job: **10m28s** (ordinary feature/example coverage)
- Windows CLI/platform shard: **7m36s**, down from **17m51s**
- Windows runtime portability shard: **2m55s**, concurrent with the CLI shard
- browser: **8m15s**, down from roughly 12 minutes
- focused engine-catalog slice: **5m45s**
- PR0 surface: **3m02s**; machines: **4m15s**; compiler-free consumer: **40s**

## Validation

- focused catalog gate passed: 17 core catalog tests, 9 unique add tests, 6 interpreter ownership/propagation tests, 2 exact engine propagation tests, and 1 runtime propagation test
- all three PR0 compatibility slices passed on the restacked production tree
- native source corpus: 2/2 passed
- `mech-core`: 180 tests in the complete suite
- `mech-interpreter`: 163 unit tests plus integration suites
- `mech-engine`: 99 unit tests plus integration suites
- `mech-bytecode`: 9/9 passed
- compiler-free frozen bytecode

body:
## Phase 6 — API hardening + compatibility promise (final phase)

Documents how Keel's public API evolves and adds a runtime version accessor.

### Deliverables
- **`docs/compatibility.md`** — the authoritative contract:
  - **source + static-relink** compatibility within a major version — *not* binary/ABI (Keel is a static lib consumers embed; callers allocate many structs by value, so a version bump is a recompile, never a `.so` swap). This keeps the core dependency-light and W^X/static-linking friendly.
  - SemVer meaning of `KL_VERSION`; what's **stable** (function signatures, existing struct field order/meaning, enum values, vtable pointer order) vs what may **evolve on a minor** (appending trailing struct fields — recompile, not source edit; new functions; appended enum values), with `KlAsyncOp._terminal` / `kl_async_cancel` (Phase 4) as worked precedents.
  - the **`struct_size`/`api_version` convention for *future* extensible vtables** — a convention going forward, not a retrofit (adding a leading field to an existing struct would shift every offset = a MAJOR break).
  - how the `integrations/` adapters track existing core vtables; and the standing policy that no dynamic loading / plugin registry / executable memory / global backend registration is ever introduced.
- **`keel.h`** — `KL_VERSION_NUMBER` packed macro (`major*10000+minor*100+patch`, e.g. `20900`) for `#if` gating + **`kl_version()` / `kl_version_number()`** runtime accessors that report the **linked library** (macros describe headers; these describe the built lib → a static-relink of a newer Keel is verifiable at runtime).
- **`src/version.c`** (added to `CORE_SRC`) implements them; **`tests/test_version.c`** asserts runtime == macros.

### Validation
- `make test` = **58 suites, 0 failures**.
- clang + gcc-14 + MinGW cross-compile clean.

---

This completes the core-completion + integrations roadmap (Phases 0–6). Summary in the PR discussion.

author: hendripermana
body:
## PER-212 — Person-to-person debt (Utang-Piutang), Slice 1 of PER-211

Makes informal person-to-person lending/borrowing first-class by **reusing the
existing ledger**, not inventing a debt sub-ledger. Design was locked by grill;
implemented exactly.

### Locked design

A person-debt is **not** a new ledger concept — it's an ordinary
`RECEIVABLE`(ASSET) / `LOAN`(LIABILITY) account **flagged** by a link to a
"person" contact. Lend/borrow/repay are **ordinary transfers** through the
existing `createTransactionForFamily`, so double-entry, signed amounts, atomic
`{increment/decrement}` balance updates, idempotency, tenant-reference
validation, RLS scoping, and append-only audit all hold **for free**.

| Flow             | Transfer          | Derived kind     | Effect                  |
| ---------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------- |
| Lend             | cash → RECEIVABLE | `funds_movement` | their debt to you grows |
| Borrow           | LOAN → cash       | `liability_draw` | your debt to them grows |
| Repay receivable | RECEIVABLE → cash | `funds_movement` | they pay you back       |
| Repay loan       | cash → LOAN       | `loan_payment`   | you pay them back       |

The `kind` is derived by the ledger core from the two account types — never
passed in.

### Schema (migration `20260801130000_person_debt_counterparty`)

- `Merchant.kind` — `"business"` | `"person"` (default `"business"`,
  CHECK-constrained). A person = a Merchant with `kind="person"` (the PER-189
  extension point: one counterparty concept unifies payee + debt-party).
- `Account.counterpartyMerchantId` — nullable **tenant-safe composite FK** to
  `Merchant(id, familyId)` (Pattern A / ADR-0010, `MATCH SIMPLE`), indexed. Its
  presence is the only discriminator of a person-debt account.
- Additive only: no backfill, no data movement.

### Reuse-the-ledger approach (backend)

- `src/server/debts.ts`: `createPerson`, `recordLend`/`recordBorrow`/
  `recordRepayment`, `getPersonDebts` (Utang-Piutang net positions),
  `getPersons`. Each mutation ensures the right person-debt account exists
  (create-if-absent, **idempotent by lookup**) then posts a transfer via
  `createTransactionForFamily`. No new balance authority.
- `getAccountsForFamily` gains `includeCounterparty` (default **true**, so
  net-worth math and every existing caller keep seeing debt accounts); the main
  Accounts page passes the full set to the net-worth card and hides
  counterparty-linked accounts from the list.

### Net-worth TOTAL invariant

Person-debt accounts stay RECEIVABLE(ASSET)/LOAN(LIABILITY), so they are already
in the total by construction (`normalizeNetWorthAt`, ADR-0038). **The total does
not change.** The only change is presentation: one grouped **"Personal debts
(net)"** line on the net-worth card. Proven by a real-Postgres test asserting
the total is identical whether or not the debt accounts are counterparty-linked.

### Frontend

- New `/debts` (Utang-Piutang) route — `ssr:false` + loader awaiting
  `collection.preload()`; per-person net position + settled ("Lunas") state; a
  record-debt flow (create person inline + lend/borrow/repay, ad-hoc); refetch
  after every mutation.
- Net-worth card renders the grouped "Personal debts (net)" line; sidebar entry.

### Scope

Ad-hoc amounts only. Installment schedules, reminders, and interest are later
PER-211 slices (documented in the ADR).

### ADR

`docs/adr/0049-counterparty-personal-debt.md`.

### Test evidence

- `vp check` — clean (formatting + lint + types, 238 files).
- Integration (real Postgres) — new `tests/integration/person-debt.integration.ts`
  (6 tests): lend grows RECEIVABLE + drops cash; borrow creates LOAN
  (`liability_draw`) + grows cash; net-position aggregation across a person's
  accounts; repay-to-zero ⇒ settled; **net-worth total identical linked vs.
  unlinked**; tenant isolation; idempotency replay is a no-op. Shared-surface
  subset (person-debt + accounts-manual-ux + account-delete +
  merchant-category-quick-create + tenant-reference-validation + cross-tenant-fk
  + db-constraints) = **7 files, 83 tests passed**. Full suite run attached in
  the final report.
- e2e — new `tests/e2e/person-debt.e2e.ts`: onboard → lend to a new person →
  assert Utang-Piutang net position + net-worth aggregate line (not the
  Accounts list) → repay → settled. **1 passed.**

author: gumclaw
body:
## What

Puts the payment-method list token (shipped in #6755) behind a new per-seller Flipper flag `checkout_payment_method_list_token`, so the token path can be ramped rather than being on for 100% of checkouts.

- `Checkout::StripePaymentPresenter` mints the token only when the flag is active for **every** seller in the cart (`sellers.present? && sellers.all? { _1.present? && Feature.active?(...) }`) — the same seller-complete keying the wallet and Apple Pay merchant-token gates already use, with the empty-cart case excluded so an absent seller cannot read as unanimous consent.
- `Order::PreparePaymentIntentService` verification stays **deliberately ungated**. A page loaded while the flag was on can prepare up to six hours later (the token's `TTL`); dropping its token because the flag flipped off in between would re-resolve in exactly the way gumroad-private#1528 fails. With no token minted, prepare falls back to the resolver — byte-for-byte the pre-#6755 behaviour.

## Why

#6755 shipped the token on every checkout, so there was no way to ramp it or to compare it against the re-resolve path on live traffic. This adds the ramp control without changing behaviour for any seller until the flag is turned on.

Related: gumroad-private#1528 (the confirm failure the token exists to fix).

## Test Results

CI green at `3340adc`: **77 successful check-runs, 1 skipped, 0 pending, 0 failed.** The only
commit since is the evidence image below, so that run still covers all the code on this branch.

Both affected spec files run locally at `3340adc` — **220 examples, 0 failures**:

![Spec run for the token ramp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/antiwork/gumroad/0e285e4c4320bbd6191cf099dc22d0ddf1689788/qa-media/pr-6792-test-results.png)

New specs:
- `spec/presenters/checkout/stripe_payment_presenter_spec.rb` — no token issued for an unflagged seller; a token issued for a flagged seller that round-trips through `PaymentMethodListToken.verify`; no token when only one of two cart sellers is flagged.
- `spec/services/order/prepare_payment_intent_service_spec.rb` — a verified issued list is still honoured after the seller is ramped **down** (the central design claim of this branch); the no-token lane re-resolves.

## Fable-5 adversarial review — **READY-TO-MERGE**

Run against branch head `3340adc` before this PR was opened. No P1, no P2. Three P3 nits accepted in place rather than churn a green head.

| Sev | Location | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| P3 | `spec/services/order/prepare_payment_intent_service_spec.rb:712` | The `ensure Feature.deactivate_user(...)` is dead cleanup — `spec_helper.rb:338` flushes Redis before every example, so Flipper state cannot leak. | Accepted; harmless. |
| P3 | `spec/services/order/prepare_payment_intent_service_spec.rb:667` | "re-resolves when the token flag is off and no issued list is submitted" is vacuous w.r.t. this branch (no service code reads the flag) and duplicates the pre-existing example at `:542`. | Accepted; keeps the ramp-down/ramp-off pair readable side by side. |
| P3 | `app/presenters/checkout/stripe_payment_presenter.rb:282` | `payment_method_list_token_enabled?` is a single-caller wrapper. | Accepted — it is deliberately parallel to `payment_element_wallets?` / `request_apple_pay_merchant_tokens?` one method above. |

### What the review CONFIRMED safe

1. **No code since #6755 assumes the token exists.** `git log 4593d3c22..origin/main` over `app/services/order/`, `app/services/checkout/`, `orders_controller.rb` and the checkout JS is empty — #6755 is the newest commit touching any consumer. Every consumer is nil-safe by construction: `orders_controller.rb:60` (`.presence`), `prepare_payment_intent_service.rb:720` (`.presence`), `payment_method_list_token.rb:48` (`return nil if token.blank?`), and `issued_payment_method_types` ends `issued&.select { … }.presence`. Frontend: the prop was `string | null` from day one (`payment.ts:86`), and `purchase.ts:327` only sends the param when non-null.
2. **The resolver fallback is not dead code.** The resolver runs on *every* prepare regardless of the token — `block_ineligible_for_client_confirm` and `confirmation_token_request_options` consume it first — and the no-token lane has been continuously spec-exercised since #6755. Unflagged sellers land on live, tested code, not a rotted path.
3. **Element/intent consistency at nil token is the pre-#6755 baseline, by design.** Residual drift is caught by the previewed-method append, which runs on every lane; Stripe rejects only when the *confirmed* method is missing from the list. The presenter's Link comment stays true: `stripe_link_enabled` derives from the same local the Element mounts, token or no token.
4. **The ungated verify opens nothing.** A token can only exist if the flag was on for every cart seller at page load; it is seller-bound, 6-hour-limited, and every echoed type still passes `payment_method_offerable?`, so a ramped-down seller's token can honour a list for at most the TTL but can never widen past a rollout gate. Multi-seller carts never reach client-confirm (`payment_method_resolver.rb:172` rejects `unless sellers.one?`) and a crafted multi-seller prepare dies at `block_multiple_sellers` before the token is read. A seller-mismatched token verifies to nil → warn → re-resolve, identical to main.
5. **No new warn/Sentry noise for the unflagged population.** The warn is gated `if submitted.present? && issued.nil?`; unflagged checkouts submit nothing, so "not issued" is silent and is never read as tampering.
6. **Gate keying matches its siblings** (`:267`, `:273`, `:283` are the same shape), `sellers` is `.uniq`'d, and a nil seller is caught both by `_1.present?` and upstream by `fallback_reason_for`'s `unknown_seller`.
7. **Specs are not vacuous where it counts.** The unflagged example fails if the guard is deleted; the flag-on example pins *per-seller* rather than global keying; the multi-seller example really builds two sellers and fails under an `any?` gate; and the ramp-down example pins the ungated-verify decision by setting `ip_country: "Greece"` — gate the verify side and it re-resolves to `%w[card link]`, failing the `%w[card link cashapp]` assertion.

### Only verifiable live

- Stripe's actual ConfirmationToken rejection semantics (rejects only when the *confirmed* method is missing). Code-consistent here, but only live traffic settles it.
- Whether real traffic still carries pre-flag tokens beyond the 6-hour window at ramp-down.
- Per-render cost of the added per-seller Flipper read on client-confirm props.

## QA steps for the reviewer

This touches checkout, so **not self-merging** — @rmarescu, the merge call is yours.

1. With `checkout_payment_method_list_token` **off** for a seller, load their checkout and confirm `elements_options.payment_method_list_token` is absent from the props and the purchase completes on card (this is the pre-#6755 path).
2. Turn the flag **on** for that seller, reload, confirm the token is present, and complete a purchase.
3. The one that matters: load the checkout **with the flag on**, turn the flag **off**, then complete the purchase from the already-loaded page. It must still succeed using the issued list — this is the ungated-verify decision, and it is why verification is not behind the flag.
4. Multi-seller cart: confirm no token is issued when only one seller is flagged, and that the cart falls back to the non-client-confirm lane as it does today.

Written by gumclaw (Claude Opus 4.5 via Hermes Agent). Adversarial pre-merge review by a separate headless Claude instance; verdict reproduced above in full.
