author: mnikks01
body:
Sprint 2 is done — the committed backlog **and** all three stretch items — so this closes it out and proposes Sprint 3.

## Sprint 2 review notes

| Item | PR |
|---|---|
| S2-0a object storage | #19 |
| S2-0b cursor pagination | #20 |
| S2-1..S2-4, S2-6 academic content + notifications | #21 |
| S2-7 class feed · S2-8 notification bell | #22 |
| S2-5 notices and events | #23 |
| S2-9 class timetables | #24 |
| S2-10 syllabus coverage | #25 |
| S2-11 role dashboards | #26 |

Tests grew from **268 → 479 API + 57 UI + 47 E2E**. The permission-matrix suite's `UNIMPLEMENTED` inventory halved, from sixteen rows to eight: everything academic is now enforced test-for-test.

The notes record what the sprint *found*, not only what it built:

- **The defect that mattered most.** Publishing was gated on the token's role claim, but registration creates every individual as `USER` and approval writes a membership rather than promoting the profile — so no teacher who registered through the product could ever publish. 341 API tests missed it because they hand-sign tokens carrying a role the real flow never issues.
- **Two more gaps of the same shape**: a student could not find their own class, a teacher could not find the classes they teach. Both invisible until someone built the screen that needed them.
- **An authorization hole a browser test found**: syllabus coverage fetched per subject, so a class with no subjects never reached a policy — a stranger could tell an empty class from a missing one.
- **The intermittent suite failure, finally diagnosed**: not a wrong status code but a twenty-second hang in `beforeEach`. A connection left idle in a transaction blocks `TRUNCATE`, and a late reset wipes the fixture the next test just created. Now loud instead of silent — **but the cause is still unknown**, and it is carried into Sprint 3 as a named risk.
- **Documentation drift found by diffing, not reading**: comparing registered routes against the endpoint table exposed three gaps, one of them an edit that had silently matched nothing because Prettier re-pads table columns.

Sprint 2 is marked `Status: Done`. The retro section is left for the team, as Sprint 1's was.

## Sprint 3 — Workflows

Leave and complaints (`FR-WF-001..012`). Two properties make it a good next sprint:

- It is the first sprint with **no platform prerequisites**. `leave_application` and `feedback` are already in the schema, `assertClassTeacherOf` and `assertPrincipalOfSchool` are already written, notifications already fan out. Purely product work.
- It is the first place where **who may decide depends on an allocation rather than a role** — the class teacher of *that* class, the principal of *that* school.

Named risks include: both policies have never been exercised by an endpoint (expect the first integration test of each to find something, as S2-1 did); a class with no class teacher cannot approve leave at all; and `start_date`/`end_date` are `@db.Date`, so a timezone applied on the way in moves a leave day for a school in `Asia/Kolkata` — worth deciding in `API/01-conventions.md` before either endpoint is written.

## Still open for you, third sprint running

- Branch protection does not **require** the CI checks — they run, but nothing blocks a merge on failure.
- The `development → main` release PR is still being squashed where [the git flow](.docs/CI-CD/00-git-flow.md) specifies a merge commit. `development` is now 11 commits ahead of `main`; a release is due, and doing it as a merge commit this time would stop `main`'s history from re-listing work already shipped.

author: oudaykhaled
body:
## Which chip — established from the run's own frames

The report named the wrong widget and the wrong word, so this was checked first-hand
before anything was changed.

The stale chip is **`order_summary_status` in `OrderChatPinnedSummary`** — the customer
order-chat header ("Your Jeeber"). **Not** live tracking: the same run shows the tracking
stepper *correct* at In transit (`g5/12-customer-code.png`) and at At Door
(`dev-e2e/a33/G4-10-track-order.png`). Not the orders list either — that chip was never
caught stale in any captured frame.

| time | frame | state |
|---|---|---|
| 21:43:43 | `g5/02-picked.png` | jeeber marks **Picked** |
| 21:44:16 | `g5/03-advanced.png` | jeeber marks **InTransit** |
| 21:44 | `g5/04-customer-tracking.png` | customer chat header `( Matched )` — **stale** |
| 21:46 | `g5/06-tracking-expanded.png` | still `( Matched )`, header **expanded** — **stale** |

The stale value was **"Matched"** (`_statusLabel`'s `default` arm), not "Pending". The word
"Pending" in the report is the **adjacent tier chip** in that same expanded header — a
different defect, fixed in #208.

## Is it on the push-only path? Yes.

Triggers today: screen open, `didPopNext`, `onAppResumed`, and a `RefreshTopic.order` push.
The 60 s safety net was deliberately deleted (`chat_detail_screen.dart:53-60`) and must stay
deleted. The first three are attention-**return** events — none of them fires for a customer
who never leaves the thread — so while they sit there the push is the only live trigger. On
that hardware it did not land: the same run's gateway journal reads
`fcmAccepted=3/24 deviceRows fcmRejected=21`.

## Change

A timer is not the answer (owner mandate; `armed-poll-inventory.py` would gain a site).
What the screen was missing is not a clock — it is the ability for the customer to **ask**.

Expanding the strip is the one user-caused event on this screen that names this data, and
the captured frame is precisely that interaction returning a stale chip. It now asks the
host for one catch-up read, through the existing single-flight latch, so
expand/collapse/expand cannot storm. Collapsing asks for nothing. Customer-only, matching
`_armSummaryRefresh`'s `!isJeeber` gate, so the Jeeber's strip gains no read path.

## Test plan

`dart analyze lib` clean. `flutter test` shows zero new failures against a `-3` baseline.

- **negative** — with the callback unwired (the pre-fix state, exercised in-test) expanding
  changes nothing and the chip stays "Matched" while the delivery is really at Picked.
  Also *ran* as a source revert: deleting just the `_toggle` call turns the suite red
  (`+1 -3`), and the negative-control test correctly stays green.
- **positive** — expanding asks exactly once and the chip advances "Matched" → "Picked up"
  through the real widget and the real ARBs.
- **bounded** — collapsing asks nothing; expand/collapse/expand asks twice.
- **wiring** — `ChatScreen` is asserted to forward the callback down to the strip, so the
  three-layer plumbing cannot silently break.

## What this does NOT fix

A customer who sits on the thread and touches nothing still learns nothing until a push
lands. Closing that needs a reliable push/subscribe transport for the status axis — the
same owner/architecture decision `live_tracking_cubit.dart` already records for the
position axis. This change makes the stale state **recoverable by the user**; it does not
make the transport reliable.

## Rollback

Revert the commit; the callback is nullable everywhere, so the plumbing simply goes unused.

author: openaimag-dao
body:
## Summary

After PR #49 (v5.5 Market Scanner) deployed to production, the dashboard's Market Scanner page showed no data. Railway logs (`gptagent2` service) showed `compute_market_scan_job` failing on every single 15-minute cycle:

```
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'float' and 'decimal.Decimal'
  File "app/services/common/scoring.py", line 54, in weighted_average
    weighted_sum = sum(weights[name] * value for name, value in available.items())
```

Root cause: `WatchdogSnapshot.committee_confidence_pct` is a `Numeric(6,2)` column. asyncpg returns `decimal.Decimal` for `Numeric` columns in production Postgres, but every test fixture in the scanner's test suite used a plain `float` (`SimpleNamespace(committee_confidence_pct=75.0, ...)`), so the unit tests never exercised this path. `MarketScannerEngine._ai_context()` passed `snapshot.committee_confidence_pct` straight into `committee_alignment_score()` → `score_alert_quality()` → `weighted_average()`, where `Decimal * float` raises. This exception was caught by `compute_market_scan_job`'s top-level `except Exception`, so the app never crashed but also never persisted a single `ScannerSnapshot`/detection since deploy -- exactly matching the "no data" symptom.

## Fix

Cast `committee_confidence_pct` to `float` at the DB-row boundary in `MarketScannerEngine._ai_context()` (`app/services/scanner/engine.py`), the same pattern already used everywhere else in this codebase when a Decimal-typed DB column crosses into pure-function code (e.g. `universe.py`'s `float(data["price"])`).

## Test plan

- [x] Added `test_ai_filter_handles_decimal_committee_confidence_pct_from_postgres` in `tests/test_scanner_engine.py`, using a real `decimal.Decimal` fixture -- reproduces the crash without the fix, passes with it.
- [x] `python -m pytest -q` -- 814 passed
- [x] `ruff check app tests` -- clean
- [x] `node --check app/static/dashboard/app.js` -- clean
- [ ] Deploy and confirm `compute_market_scan_job` runs cleanly in production, `GET /api/scanner` returns real data

author: chemaclass
body:
Closes two confirmed drift findings from the 2026-08-01 target audit. Both are "does the wrong thing" rather than "does nothing", so they get more review care than an additive change: grouped in one PR, no merge by this pass.

## #536 — Cursor: description-only rules forced to `globs: "**/*"`

**Vendor evidence** (https://cursor.com/docs/rules, fetched today):

> | `alwaysApply` | `description` | `globs`  | Behavior                                                         |
> | :------------ | :------------ | :------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------- |
> | `true`        | —             | —        | Always included. Globs and description are ignored.              |
> | `false`       | —             | provided | Auto-attached when a matching file is in context.                |
> | `false`       | provided      | omitted  | Agent reads the description and pulls the rule in when relevant. |
> | `false`       | omitted       | omitted  | Included only when you `@`-mention the rule in chat.             |

**Contradicted:** `internal/adapters/cursor/cursor.go:363-368` (pre-fix) fell through to `globs = "**/*"` unconditionally whenever `alwaysApply` was `false` and no native `globs`/`paths` were set, whether or not a `description` was present. That collapses both the "Apply Intelligently" row and the "Apply Manually" row into the "Auto-attached" row: the rule's full body reaches every file on every turn, functionally `alwaysApply: true`.

**Fix:** `mdc()` now leaves `globs` empty in both of those rows instead of defaulting to `**/*`, so Cursor applies its own matrix instead of agnostic-ai flattening it.

**Explicit decision on the "neither description nor globs" case**, since the issue asked for one rather than a default "docs are ambiguous, keep current behavior": the docs are not ambiguous. The table states plainly that `alwaysApply:false` + no description + no globs is "Apply Manually" (`@`-mention only), not "every file". So this fix omits `globs` for that case too, not only the description-only case the issue title names. Same function, same two lines, same root cause: a broad `**/*` fallback where the vendor defines something narrower.

`#443` (already merged) special-cased the `alwaysApply: true` row at `cursor.go:357-362`; that code path is untouched by this change.

**Verified beyond green tests:** ran the built binary through a full `sync` → `import cursor` → `sync` cycle over a description-only rule, a manual-only rule, and an always-apply control rule. Output came back byte-identical across the cycle; no `globs: null` or stray `**/*` leaked back into the source. `import_cursor.go`'s `normalizeCursorRuleMeta` already dropped a catch-all `globs` value independent of this fix (it also guards a hand-authored catch-all glob, not just the emitter's old default), so its behavior needed no change, only a comment correction: it described the emitter's old always-fill-`**/*` behavior as still current, which is no longer true.

Closes #536

## #537 — Gemini: hook-event validator knows 4 of 11 documented events

**Vendor evidence** (https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/configuration, fetched today):

> - **`hooks.BeforeTool`**: Hooks that execute before tool execution.
> - **`hooks.AfterTool`**: Hooks that execute after tool execution.
> - **`hooks.BeforeAgent`**: Hooks that execute before agent loop starts.
> - **`hooks.AfterAgent`**: Hooks that execute after agent loop completes.
> - **`hooks.Notification`**: Hooks that execute on notification events (errors, warnings, info).
> - **`hooks.SessionStart`**: Hooks that execute when a session starts.
> - **`hooks.SessionEnd`**: Hooks that execute when a session ends.
> - **`hooks.PreCompress`**: Hooks that execute before chat history compression.
> - **`hooks.BeforeModel`**: Hooks that execute before LLM requests.
> - **`hooks.AfterModel`**: Hooks that execute after LLM responses.
> - **`hooks.BeforeToolSelection`**: Hooks that execute before tool selection.

**Contradicted:** `internal/cli/native_capabilities.go:35-38` (pre-fix) mapped `gemini` to only `BeforeTool`, `AfterTool`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`. A hook spec with `event: BeforeAgent` (or any of the other 5 missing events) emitted correctly, but `agnostic-ai validate` reported it as an unrecognized event: a false positive nudging users to "fix" a spec that was never broken.

**Fix:** added the 7 missing events (`BeforeAgent`, `AfterAgent`, `Notification`, `PreCompress`, `BeforeModel`, `AfterModel`, `BeforeToolSelection`) to `hookEventsByTarget["gemini"]`.

**Confirmed the "generic passthrough, no emission change needed" claim rather than relying on it as given:**

author: bender0oo0
body:
Closes #1718

#1718 describes SSE fanout across API replicas/workers as unimplemented, quoting the `ponytail:` comment in `sse-broker.ts` that names Redis pub/sub as the missing upgrade. That comment was accurate on 2026-07-26 when it was written, but is stale: cross-replica fanout for both plain pushes and access-invalidation already exists, added two days later.

**Why the issue's premise no longer holds:**
- `createSseBroadcastEventConsumer` and `createAccessInvalidationEventConsumer` (`pipeline/system-hooks.ts`) both run with `delivery: "per-instance"` — every API replica polls the shared event log with its own `(name, instanceId)` cursor and calls `pushToChannel` / `publishAccessInvalidation` on its own local broker. A write on replica A reaches replica B's clients without `sse-broker.ts` needing to know about other processes.
- Both consumers are wired **by default**: `server.ts` defaults `sseConsumerEnabled` and `accessInvalidationEnabled` to `true` whenever a DB connection + sseBroker exist (#1524 "global-by-default").
- The underlying per-instance delivery mechanism is already pinned by `event-dispatcher-multi-instance.integration.test.ts` — no test gap to fill.
- Landed via #1563 (dispatch-stream subscribe) and #1575 (access-invalidation consumer), both 2026-07-28, after the comment was written.

The worker-process bullet in the issue isn't a fanout gap either — a worker has no SSE clients of its own; it reaches browsers only by appending an event, which the per-instance consumer then delivers on every API replica.

**Change:** replace the stale `ponytail:` comment (which asserted a false security property — "security control is single-node") with a short pointer at the actual mechanism, so a future reader isn't misled into re-implementing Redis pub/sub for something already solved.

No behavior change — comment-only, no changeset needed.

body:
## What problem does this solve?

The signed channel panel surface currently has no transport adapter, so a channel with signed Buzz job activity still shows only the empty placeholder. It also did not subscribe to the signed job kinds for live updates, making new activity invisible until a later history refresh.

## What this implements

This stacked follow-up composes a bounded, read-only panel projection from the existing signed job lifecycle events (kinds 43001–43006):

- loading while the current channel timeline resolves;
- empty when no signed job activity is available;
- ready with the latest lifecycle status, event count, latest note, timestamp, and source-event provenance;
- bounded to 64 source events and plain-text note content;
- explicit status mapping for requested, active, complete, blocked/cancelled, and failed job states;
- source links routed back through Buzz’s existing timeline/thread navigation; and
- live channel subscriptions now include all six signed job lifecycle kinds.

The projection is scoped to the current channel’s h tag, accepts canonical channel UUIDs across UUID versions, excludes pending/unsigned or malformed event ids, and preserves each signed source event id and kind.

## Existing paths reused

The adapter consumes ChannelScreen’s existing authenticated `resolvedMessages` timeline events, uses the existing `getChannelIdFromTags` channel boundary, renders in the existing auxiliary-panel shell, and reuses the existing source-event-to-thread navigation path. No new event kind, HTTP endpoint, or remote UI runtime was added.

This PR is intentionally stacked on #4102 (renderer) and #3882 (contract); the review delta is commits 246bd5ac, 16963084, and 0bef5967.

## Tests and validation

Added focused regression coverage for:

- latest-event/status selection and source provenance;
- cancellation/failure mapping;
- unsigned, pending, malformed, cross-channel, and non-v4-channel filtering;
- bounded plain-text notes;
- inclusion of every signed job kind in the live channel filter; and
- the empty panel plus ready panel with signed source provenance in Playwright.

Commands run:

```

pnpm check

git diff --check
```

The focused unit, typecheck, repository checks, E2E build, file-size check, and ready-state Playwright test passed. Command-palette/autocomplete work remains separate. Canvas revision history, workflow run history, structured handoff cards, and any broader panel transport decision remain separate follow-ups.

No OEXL-specific code, matching, acceptance, payment, accounting, settlement, or marketplace semantics were added.

author: infektyd
body:
Claude Code was loading Minni's hooks, skills and commands from a tree nothing owned, while `minni wire` managed a verified payload right next to it and wired only the MCP server from it. This puts the plugin surface on the wire pipeline too.

## What was actually wrong

- `installed_plugins.json` pinned `minni@minni` to `~/.claude/plugins/cache/minni/minni/0.3.0` — installed by a marketplace flow in July, then overwritten in place by `propagate.py`'s `rsync -a --delete`. It is content-stale against HEAD: older `dist/server.js`, no `threads` command, no `readme-audit` skill, older skill bodies.
- `known_marketplaces.json` pointed the `minni` marketplace at an unrelated stale worktree whose `hooks.json` carries `timeout: 10/20/30`. A `/plugin update` would have refreshed the cache from that, silently reverting the payload's `timeout: 60`.
- Meanwhile `wired.json` had all four platforms on `~/.minni/plugin/<version>`, hash-manifested and verified.

## Design decisions

Full reasoning, rejected alternatives and the cutover runbook: `docs/design/DESIGN-wire-claude-plugin-adoption.md`.

**1. Registration points at the versioned install root, not a `current` symlink.**

The brief called `update_current_symlink`'s early-return for PEP440-local versions a defect to fix. It is not — it is deliberate, and pinned three ways in `tests/test_wire_hardening.py` under a docstring naming the "release-only `current` symlink gate". A dev build must not move the pointer a released install depends on. Rather than break that invariant, this takes the explicit alternative the brief allowed: register the versioned path, so no `current` is needed. Two further reasons — GC matches literal version-dir strings and skips symlinks, so a registration behind `current` would be invisible to it; and Claude Code's `installPath` symlink handling is undocumented with open upstream issues. Versioned paths are free here because Claude Code reads plugin manifests **once per session**, so churn between wires is never observed mid-session.

**2. Registration is a normal step of `minni wire claude-code`; no marketplace.**

Claude Code loads from `installPath` alone — the `@marketplace` suffix is namespacing, and the live machine already proves it (the plugin loads from a cache path while its marketplace points somewhere unrelated). Registering a marketplace would buy nothing and re-arm the `/plugin update` foot-gun.

Idempotence is exact: when `installPath`, `version` and `gitCommitSha` all match, `lastUpdated` is not touched and the file stays byte-identical. Other plugins, other scopes, and `installedAt` are preserved; a corrupt registry raises rather than being overwritten, because it holds other plugins' entries.

**3. Cutover is `minni wire-adopt claude-code`, dry-run by default.**

`--apply` registers, repoints Claude Desktop, retires the stale marketplace entry, and removes the legacy cache. Every step reports `changed` and is individually idempotent. **Not executed against any live machine in this PR** — verified below.

## Absorbed audit findings

From the parallel deployment audit, only the ones load-bearing for this design:

- **GC blind spot (D4)** — taken. `default_config_scan_paths()` gains `installed_plugins.json`. `wired.json` alone is insufficient: `flow.py` stamps configs before `run_verify` and returns on failure without `upsert_wire`, so the registry can be a tree's only reference. Relatedly, the registration deliberately does **not** repeat that pattern — it runs after verification passes, alongside `upsert_wire`.
- **check_deployments blind spot (D2/C3)** — taken, narrowly. `~/.minni/plugin/*/dist` added, so the deployment this PR makes load-bearing is no longer the one the staleness check cannot see. The `hooks/`/`skills/` subtree drift coverage is **not** addressed.
- **update_claude_config rewrite (C4/D10)** — taken structurally. propagate's `claude-code` spec is gone and the `claude-json` dispatch branch removed, so the workspace-id-dropping rewrite is unreachable rather than merely unused. No writer added here swallows an exception.
- **marketplace.json / check_versions (D1/C5)** — **not taken.** This retires the *machine-side* `known_marketplaces.json` entry, which is a different artifact from the repo's published `marketplace.json`. Whether to keep publishing that is its own call.
- **all-expansion disagreement (D7)** — documented, not reconciled. Removing `claude-code` from propagate's list narrows the gap with wire's `ALL_EXPANSION_V03` by one; the lists still disagree both ways.

## propagate.py

`claude-code` now raises with a pointer to wire instead of writing to a dead directory. It is dropped from `--platform all` (with a loud notice) so the other platforms keep working rather than every run aborting.

Codex keeps working but resolves from **its own** cache tree, taking the PEP440 maximum over directories that actually exist — never a pip-metadata version that need not exist, and never the literal `current` segment, which is not a directory the codex cache ever has.

Claude Desktop's only route in was the `claude-code` platform. Rather than orphan a live surface, `wire-adopt` repoints it — necessary, not optional, since the cutover deletes the cache dir Desktop currently launches from.

## Contradictions with the brief, found while verifying

1. **`update_current_symlink` is not a defect** — it is intentional, tested behavior (see decision 1). Resolved via the allowed explicit alternative.
2. **`plugin_version_segment` does not resolve from pip metadata primarily** — it prefers the `current` symlink and only *falls back* to pip metadata. The stated symptom is real, but its cause is the missing `current` on dev machines, which couples it to (1).
3. **`sorted()[0]` does not appear in propagate.py.** PEP440-max is implemented correctly regardless, with a test pinning that a two-digit minor outranks a one-digit one.
4. **The 0.3.0 cache's `hooks.json` already carries `timeout: 60`** — the `timeout: 30` foot-gun is in the *marketplace worktree*, which `/plugin update` would copy *from*. The cache is stale in content, not in hook timeouts.
5. **Double MCP registration exists today and is not fixed here.** The payload's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` declares its own `mcpServers`, so a loaded plugin registers a second Minni server beside the wire-stamped one. Both are live now; this moves which tree the plugin half loads from without deduplicating. Documented with the recommended follow-up.

## Verification

```
engine  pytest -q                     1306 passed, 7 skipped
plugin  npm test                      833 pass, 0 fail
pre-push make check                   833 plugin + 33 scoped engine, OK
        ruff check                    All checks passed
        scripts/check_versions.py     all versions agree at 0.4.1
```

New tests: 20 (`tests/test_wire_claude_plugin.py`) + 14 (`test_propagate_wire_adoption.py`), including a GC test asserting a registered tree survives pruning **with no `wired.json` record at all**.

End-to-end cutover smoke ran against a throwaway `HOME`: dry run wrote nothing, `--apply` performed every step, re-apply left the registry byte-identical.

Live machine state confirmed untouched after all work — `installed_plugins.json` still pins 0.3.0, the `minni` marketplace entry is still present, the 0.3.0 cache is still there, and `~/.minni/plugin` is unchanged. Cutover remains a separate operator step.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Thinking Path

The deterministic failure occurs before the refund assertion. The fixture labels an unpersisted synthetic run as `provider_quota`; once the source assignee is removed, that classification intentionally routes recovery into the provider-quota monitor, which persists `retry_of_run_id` and correctly enforces a foreign key to the source heartbeat run. Production always persists `latestRun` before that path, so weakening the FK or service behavior would hide a test-only invalid state.

The refund test is intended to exercise the ordinary budgeted owner-wake path. Its fixture was wrong in two ways: it selected the provider-quota path, and it assumed unchanged issue activity even though the first escalation system comment correctly advances `lastActivityAt`.

- Changed the synthetic run classification from `provider_quota` to an ordinary `adapter_failed` failure so the test remains on the owner-wake/refund path it names.

body:
## 概要

user-IPC 認可 (`assertPathAllowed` / `assertWritePathAllowed` / `isPathAllowed` / `isPathWithinAnyAllowedRoot` / `canonicalize`) が持っていた realpath 結果の LRU cache (上限 256・invalidation 無し) を撤去し、**毎回 fresh に realpath する**ようにした。#453 の「判断が要る点」に対する結論は **cache を捨てる**。

判断の根拠 (いずれも本セッションで確定させた事実):

- **cache key は「realpath に成功した path 自身」**だった。実在 file では full path 1 本が載るだけで、鮮度を保存するのは「同じ path の 2 回目以降」に限られる。初回アクセスは元から fresh なので、symlink retarget への追随が「その path を過去に触ったか」という観測不能な条件で変わっていた
- **invalidation は持てない**。retarget の通知経路が無い (chokidar は `followSymlinks: false` で retarget を change event として emit する保証がない)。これは L3 index 取り込みゲート `resolveInsideRoot` が元から cache を通していない理由 (#406 Finding 1) と同根で、user-IPC 認可だけ別扱いにする根拠が無かった
- **削減できていたコストが小さい**。認可 1 回につき realpath 1 回で、`node` probe の実測は深さ 8 の path で **21.9 µs** (macOS warm dcache、symlink を 1 段挟んで 31.3 µs)。fs:read の open + stat + read に埋没する。call site はすべて「IPC 1 回 / 画像 1 枚 / workspace open 1 回」につき定数回で、ループ経路は無いことを確認済み
- **境界が緩む方向の変化は無い**。祖先 retarget が外を指せば fresh 解決は拒否 (現状より厳しい)、内を指せば新しい解決先で許可 (ユーザーの見え方と一致)

副産物として、cache の存在を前提にしていた機構が消える: `invalidateRealpathCacheEntry` と fs.ts の `withStaleCacheRetry` (ELOOP を「cache stale」/「認可後 swap」に切り分けて 1 度だけ再認可する helper)。cache が無ければ認可時点で canonical の末端が symlink であり得るのは realpath が解決できないとき (dangling / 循環) だけなので、ELOOP はそのまま fail-closed で伝播させる。

## 関連 Issue

closes #453

- [x] Stage 6: 仕上げ・配布・切り替え

## 変更内容

- `path-guard.ts`: `realpathCache` / `REALPATH_CACHE_MAX` / `cachedRealpath` / `invalidateRealpathCacheEntry` を削除。`realpathBestEffort` は `realpath` 直呼びに戻し、`clearWorkspaceRoots` から cache clear を落とす。撤去の根拠を doc として残す
- `fs.ts`: `withStaleCacheRetry` を削除し、`readFileImpl` / `readFileBase64Impl` / `writeFileImpl` を「認可 → O_NOFOLLOW I/O」の直列に戻す。ELOOP の意味論を doc に書き直す
- `fs.test.ts`: cache hit を swap 窓の fixture に使っていた 6 本を、**「前回の認可を持ち越さない」性質の pin** として意味を書き直す (fixture と assert は据え置き)

author: kilowatto
body:
The five kindergarten formats now exist as real, tappable elements at
`/{locale}/reto-demo/`, and running the auditors over them found a critical
accessibility violation that had been on the site since S0.

**All five are tap. Dragging does not exist.** At 4-6 dragging is measurably
slower and more error-prone than tapping, and that difference disappears around
7-10 (plan §9). **Targets are 88 px** — a four-year-old needs ~23.7 mm to hit
90% of the time against an adult's ~9 mm, so WCAG's 24 px and Apple's 44 px both
fall short here.

**No child writes anything.** Red line #3: the five formats are tap, choose or
count. There is not one `<input type="text">`.

**`flash_ms` is stimulus exposure, not a clock.** It hides the dots once and does
not return: no countdown, nothing displayed, nothing scored (D-024). There is
deliberately no animation rule that could draw a shrinking bar.

Three real accessibility violations, found by running axe rather than by reading:

- **`button-name` [critical]** — the ten-frame cells were empty `<button>`s. For
  anyone using a screen reader, ten unnamed buttons are ten identical buttons.
- **`aria-prohibited-attr` [serious]** — `aria-label` on a bare `<div>`; a
  generic div accepts no name. It is `role="img"` now: dots described by a count.
- **`listitem` [serious]** — `role="group"` on a `<ul>` overrides list semantics
  and orphans every `<li>`. A `<ul>` is already a group; it just needed the label.

**And one that was already live: `meta-refresh` [critical], WCAG 2.2.1.** The root
`/` was serving `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="2;url=/en/">` with no `lang`
attribute — so it also failed 3.1.1. A delayed refresh under 20 hours pulls the
page out from under anyone reading slowly or with a screen reader.

It came from Astro's own `redirectToDefaultLocale: true` stub, which was
**overriding** the hand-written `src/pages/index.astro` that had been there all
along. Turning it off lets our page serve the root: it picks the browser's locale
with `location.replace` and leaves a visible link for anyone without JavaScript.
A fixed `_redirects` rule was considered and rejected — it would send everyone to
English and throw away the locale detection.

`axe-a11y` now passes: **379 pages, 0 WCAG 2.2 AA violations, 64,171 nodes.**
It is the first time it has run.

Two auditor findings on my own work, fixed rather than suppressed:

- `brand-image` caught three invented colours (`#FFF4EC`, `#F6F6F6`) that are not
  in the Ignia palette. They are palette tokens now.
- `ipad-usabilidad` had a **real bug**. Its check looked *backwards* for an
  `@media …min-width` to know whether a `min-width` was bounded, which fails on
  exactly the correct case: when the `min-width` **is** the media query condition,
  the preceding text does not contain it yet. It flagged
  `@media (orientation: landscape) and (min-inline-size: 900px)`, which is the
  right way to bound it. It now skips `@media` preludes, and still catches a bare
  `min-width: 900px` — seen failing.

**`contrast` ran for the first time and found three failing pairs that are not
mine.** Recorded in `docs/dudas.md` §14 rather than fixed, because changing the
brand palette is the owner's call. The one that matters:

    --color-accent (#F36B1C) sobre --color-surface (#F7F7F8) — 2.83:1, exige 3:1

CLAUDE.md documents 3.03:1 **on white** and concludes the orange is fine for
graphics and controls. The real surface is not white, it is `#F7F7F8`, and
against it the same orange gives 2.83:1 — below the 3:1 a graphic or control
needs. The brand colour does not clear the bar we thought it cleared.

Evidence:

  $ node audits/axe-a11y.mjs       → 379 páginas, 0 violaciones
  $ node audits/touch-targets.mjs  → 22 blancos, 88px kinder
  $ node audits/bundle-budget.mjs  → 379 páginas, JS 2.6 KB gz
  $ bash .githooks/pre-commit      → verde

What this change does NOT do:

- **Criterion #39 stays open.** The formats respond to touch, but nothing is
  wired to a session or an item: the demo page scores nothing and records
  nothing. `touch-targets` also reports itself INACTIVE until F2, since no file
  declares a band yet and everything is judged as PUBLICO at 24 px.
- `contrast` is still not blocking. Activating it would block every commit on a
  palette decision that is not mine to make.
- The labels on the demo page are hardcoded Spanish, not message keys. It is a
  demo surface, and that is exactly the kind of shortcut that becomes permanent —
  it must not survive into the real challenge screen.
- **Nobody has looked at it.** 379 pages verified by auditors, zero seen.

author: yogthos
body:
Calva asks for a classpath with `jolt -A:test:dev -Spath`, which failed twice over: an undeclared `:dev` threw out of `resolve-project`, and `-Spath` was an unknown command. This brings up the whole `clj` option surface.

**Fixes**
- An undeclared alias warns and is skipped, like tools.deps (`WARNING: Specified aliases are undeclared and are not being used`). Verified against `clojure -A:test:dev -Spath` — it warns on stderr and exits 0.
- `-A` no longer resolves the project itself. Everything it re-dispatches to resolves for itself, so each `-A` was walking the dep tree twice and printing its warnings twice.

**Report options** — answer something about the project and run nothing. Each takes the aliases on either side of it, so `-A:x -Spath` and `-Spath -M:x` both report on the resolution that run would use:
- `-Spath` — the resolved source roots.
- `-Stree` — the dependency tree in the tools.deps format (`.` for a dep that made the resolution, `X <reason>` for one that lost: `:use-top`, `:older-version`, `:excluded`, `:superseded`, …). The expansion already made those decisions, it just wasn't recording them.
- `-Strace` — the same log written to `trace.edn`, `{:log [...] :vmap {...}}`, long-hand keys, one decision per line.
- `-Sdescribe` — version, deps.edn chain and cache locations as edn, resolving nothing, so an editor can ask cheaply and offline.
- `-P` — fetch every dependency, then stop.

**Other options**
- `-Scp CP` runs against the given roots and expands nothing: `jolt -Scp "$(jolt -Spath)" -M:test` runs offline. The deps.edn is still read (aliases, `:main-opts`, `:tasks`); tools.deps' `--skip-cp` skips `calc-basis` in exactly the same way. A *dependency's* `:jolt/native` libs go with the expansion; the project's own still load.
- `-Srepro` ignores `~/.clojure/deps.edn` per run; `-Sverbose` reports which files are read and which caches are fetched into — on stderr, not clj's stdout, so `-Sverbose -Spath` still pipes.
- `-Sforce`, `-Sthreads N`, `-Jopt` accepted and ignored (nothing to force, serial fetches, no JVM). Any other `-S` option names itself as unsupported instead of being reported as an unknown deps.edn task.

**Unrelated fix, found while verifying:** the `cts` gate was flaky — `clojure.core-test.realized-qmark` asserts a `(future (sleep 1))` is not yet realized and races `future-cancel`, which it loses under the parallel workers. A namespace whose counts don't match the baseline is now re-run once on its own before it counts. A deterministic mismatch still fails the gate (verified with a planted baseline entry).

Tests: 24 new checks in `host/chez/deps-alias-smoke.sh` (88/88). `make test` green end to end.

```
$ jolt -A:test:dev -Spath
[jolt.deps] Specified aliases are undeclared and are not being used: [:dev]   (stderr)
/proj/test:/proj/src:…                                                        (stdout, rc=0)

$ jolt -A:test -Stree
jolt-lang/db f368b12
weavejester/integrant bcad6bc
  X weavejester/dependency 0.2.1 :use-top
jolt-lang/nrepl v0.1.0
  . cider/orchard 0.44.0
```

author: pbwise
body:
Five commits. Closes #29, #30, #31.

The three issues turn out to be one story: the static catalog was quietly understating what a codebase authors, in three different ways.

---

## 1 · `fix:` a spread of members no longer vanishes (#29)

```tsx
useAgentComponent({ type: "repro.spread", ...buildMembers() });
```

Appeared in **neither** list — not the catalog, not the `UNREAD CALL SITES` entries that exist to say the catalog is incomplete. `capabilitiesFromGroup` returns early when `observations`/`actions` are absent as literal keys, and `hasSpread()` only downgraded *surviving* capabilities to `partial`; both calls no-op'd.

The extractor now resolves what a spread *can* contribute — `...(props.instance ? { instanceId } : {})` has a written-out key set and stays quiet, `...buildMembers()` is reported. It reports **even when a literal group resolved alongside**, which the issue didn't catch: a literal `observations` says nothing about the `actions` the spread may add. Note the ordering in the fixture — literal-then-spread trips `TS2783` and TypeScript warns you; spread-then-literal compiles silently, so that's the one pinned.

`AS-COVER-002` restated: the guarantee is about *a registration the extractor cannot fully enumerate*, not only *a call site it cannot read*.

## 2 · `feat:` wrapper hooks resolve one hop up (#31)

```tsx
export function usePanel(type: string) {
  useAgentComponent({ type, observations: { … } });
}
usePanel("devices.table");      // ← the id lives here
```

Reported unread, one such wrapper hid **91% of a real application's surface**. The ids are still determined by source text, just one frame up — so the extractor follows the call sites and emits one capability set per literal. Same one-hop budget already spent going *sideways* to a same-module `const`, pointed the other way. Positional and destructured spellings both read.

**Safety is the design.** A call site resolves only when it provably calls *that* wrapper: same file, or an import whose specifier resolves to the wrapper's file. Anything else stays unread — attributing the wrong call would put ids in the catalog that no component authors, and a **fabricated** entry is worse than a missing one. Every other gap in this tool understates; that one would overstate. The fixture pins an impostor — a same-named local function in another file — and asserts it is never attributed.

Resolution is per call site: 15 literals and 2 variables give 15 capabilities plus one unread line naming the two.

Two things it needed on the way — `propertyOf` didn't read shorthand, so `{ type }` (what a forwarding wrapper actually writes) looked like a config with no `type` at all; and the enclosing function is tracked walking *down* rather than via `node.parent`, which `ts.createProgram` leaves unset until something forces the binder. Forcing it means building a type checker. Measured cost of the join as written: **nil** (2.44s vs 2.5s baseline).

## 3 · `feat:` per-entry acceptance for unread call sites (#30)

`--allow-unresolved` was all-or-nothing. A repo with one permanent unread site had to choose between failing forever and accepting every *future* one silently — and picks the second, turning the check off. `.agent-surface/unresolved-allow.json` now mirrors `coverage-allow.json`.

**The key was the real question**, and it's `file#reason`:

- **not the line** — churns on every edit above the call site; a ratchet that fails because someone added an import gets deleted
- **not the note** — prose for humans, and it got reworded *in this very PR*

So `reason` is a new stable discriminator (`dynamic-type`, `spread-members`, `granular-hook`, …); renaming one is a breaking change. `inspect` prints the key under every unread entry, because nobody guesses `file#reason`. Coarser than a line by design, bounded to one file and one construct. Composes with the blanket flag; a stale entry in either list fails through both.

## 4 · `chore:` restore version lockstep

The 0.11.0 changeset named only `core` and `cli`, so the other four took dependent patch bumps to 0.10.1. Bump levels are relative, so a grouped changeset alone would *preserve* the gap — realign the four manifests to 0.11.0 first, then one changeset listing all six carries them to 0.11.1. Those four skip 0.11.0 on npm; nothing was published there for them.

## 5 · `docs:` describe the CLI, not its history

`20-cli.md` narrated how it got to its current shape. It opened by rebutting an `--entry ./router.ts` nobody proposed, then two more sections of backstory before the commands appeared. 14 instances of version archaeology removed; four headings renamed from rebuttals to descriptions.

---

## Verification

**432 tests** · conformance **115/115** (`AS-COVER-008`, `AS-COVER-009` added; `AS-COVER-002` restated) · build · typecheck · frozen install · docs build. Example app's catalog and committed baselines both unchanged.

## Adopter impact

Two changes make `check` stricter, in the same direction and for the same reason — the count was previously claiming a completeness it didn't have:

- a spread the extractor can't read is now reported, so repos using that shape will see new unread entries
- capabilities behind a wrapper hook now **appear**, which means they can now be `unreached` too

`unresolved-allow.json` and `coverage-allow.json` are the ratchets for both, and `--allow-unresolved` is still the blanket dial.

author: lvolland
body:
the ten boxes on #17: godot, webassembly, mongodb, powershell, vim, cobol, ruby, php, c++, c#.

one commit per language, each touching only its own files plus the three shared lines, so you
can drop any of them without unpicking the rest.

![the ten new languages rendered with the github-dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvolland/core/assets/langs-demo.png)

| | class | detection |
|---|---|---|
| cobol | `shj-lang-cobol` | ✅ |
| c++ | `shj-lang-cpp` | ✅ |
| c# | `shj-lang-cs` | ✅ |
| gdscript | `shj-lang-gd` | ❌ |
| mongodb | `shj-lang-mongodb` | ❌ |
| php | `shj-lang-php` | ✅ |
| powershell | `shj-lang-ps1` | ❌ |
| ruby | `shj-lang-rb` | ✅ |
| vimscript | `shj-lang-vim` | ✅ |
| webassembly | `shj-lang-wat` | ❌ |

### verified

```
10/10   new languages: rules well formed, every match carries /g, tokenize
        reconstructs the source exactly, under budget, coverage 59-83 %
33/34   existing languages unchanged (plain colours nothing by design)
37/37   existing fixtures detect exactly as they did before
```

that last line is the one that mattered. a detection regex is the only way a new language can
break an existing one, so every entry was tested against the whole fixture set, and **four
languages ship with no detection at all** because the candidate regex had real false positives:

- `wat` — `\b(local|global)\.(get|set|tee)\b` also matches ordinary java, js and python
- `gd` — `@export`-style prefixes collide with jsdoc tags and python decorators
- `mongodb` — matches pymongo
- `ps1` — `Verb-Noun` is also how title case works in prose

`cpp` is registered at weight 500 rather than 100: `std::cout` cannot occur in valid c, and at
100 the six `#include` lines in the fixture made `c` win on volume.

### what the review pass caught

each grammar was written, then attacked by a second pass whose job was to break it. eight of the
ten came back with real defects, fixed before this branch existed. the ones worth naming:

- **cobol** — `\b[\w-]+[ \t]+(DIVISION|SECTION)\b` was quadratic
- **php** — `#[Attribute]` was swallowed whole by the `#` comment branch, and a `?>` inside a `//`
  comment never handed control back to html
- **ruby** — the heredoc rule accepted any `\w+` after `<<`, so `a << b` opened a string
- **gdscript** — a multi-line `"""` string leaked, and `7%2` was read as a `%variable`
- **vimscript** — vim does not escape backslashes in single quotes, and the `@"` register opened a
  string that ate the rest of the line

### known limits, stated rather than hidden

- nested `(; … ;)` in wat stops at the first `;)` — the same compromise `c.js` already makes for `/* */`
- a lone apostrophe outside a literal in cobol opens a string to end of line
- c# raw strings (`"""`) have no rule yet
- the `func` rule idiom (`/[a-z_]\w*(?=\s*\()/`) is quadratic on a very long identifier with no
  paren — measured at 480-500 ms on 20 000 chars. that is not new: `c`, `py`, `rs` and `java` all
  score within 40 ms of each other on the same input, so i kept the shared idiom rather than make
  these ten diverge. flagging it because it is the repo's slowest path, not because of this pr

### notes

- names follow the existing convention — file extension for the class (`rb`, `cpp`, `cs`, `ps1`,
  `gd`, `wat`), full name in the readme table. `mongodb` and `cobol` have no natural short form,
  so they are spelled out. all of that is yours to overrule
- the last commit only widens the readme table's name column by one character, because
  `webassembly` is 11 wide and the column was 10. it is whitespace only and safe to drop
- `dist/` untouched

body:
Two features, one per component.

## drivecast — adding a drive no longer rescans everything

Adding a drive in Settings re-walked **every** selected drive. Scoped per-drive refresh already existed (`POST /api/refresh` takes `{"drives": [...]}`, and a section change one line below already used it) — the drive-add branch just never passed a scope.

- `POST /api/settings` now walks `added_drives ∪ section_changed`. The union matters: the Settings UI sends an add *and* its tab assignment in one request, and the old `if/elif` silently dropped the add.
- Removal needs the opposite — a rebuild with no walk — so `start_refresh`/`Scanner.scan` gain an explicit-empty-scope **cache-only rebuild**: re-derive `library.json` from `data/scan_cache.json` so a deselected drive's titles leave without touching Drive.
- A pure **reorder** takes the same path, because drive order decides which drive wins a cross-drive season merge (**D-013**).
- A *non-empty* scope that filters to nothing starts nothing — except on the mid-scan drain, where "nothing left selected" is exactly the removal the queued rebuild exists to apply.
- A cache-only rebuild reports `total=0`; the web UI and menu bar now say "updating library…" rather than `(0/0)`.

## drivecast-app — sort & group on the home grid

The grid was fixed at `added_at` desc, then title.

- **Sort** pill: Recently added / A–Z / Year; re-picking the current key flips direction. Nulls sort last in both directions.
- **Group** pill (Entertainment): labelled category groups, then *Other*, with the sort applied within each group. Suppressed while a category chip is filtering, and the pill reports the effective state rather than the raw pref.
- Both persist in DataStore and seed synchronously on re-entry, so back-nav renders the right order on frame one.
- Logic is pure functions over `List<Title>` in `SortAndGroup.kt`, covered by 20 JVM tests. Group headers are full-span and non-focusable.

## Tests

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `drivecast` pytest | **465 pass** (+21) |
| `drivecast-app` unit | **28 pass** (+20) |
| `assembleDebug` / `assembleRelease` | both clean |

The union test uses genuinely disjoint added/section-changed sets, verified by mutation to fail in **both** directions — the first version passed with the union broken.

## Not verified here

No on-device (Fire TV) pass — the focus/scroll behavior around the new controls row is argued from Compose semantics and JVM tests, not an instrumented run. `docs/DECISIONS.md` **D-014** records the two focus traps this routed around.

body:
Line coverage only proves a line ran, not that a test fails when it is
wrong. Every package here is already at 90%+ coverage, so mutation
testing is the next thing that can still find something: pkg/phpcs sits
at 100% line coverage and only 73% MSI.

- pin quality-gates/mutago v2.7.7 via the go.mod tool directive, the
  same way deadcode is pinned, so Dependabot keeps it current
- mutago.yaml holds file selection only; thresholds stay on the command
  line because the PR gate and the full run need different ones
- make mutate runs the whole module locally
- go.yml gains a blocking `mutation` job scoped to the lines the PR
  changes (--git-diff-lines against the merge base, 70% MSI). Scoring
  the full module per PR would be slow and would fail on survivors
  nobody touched; PRs with no mutable changes generate no mutants and
  pass
- mutation.yml scores the full module weekly, never blocking, and
  uploads mutago-agentic.json as the worklist of existing survivors

Also corrects the docs' stale claim that mocks are named mock_*.go --
mockery v3's testify template emits one mocks_test.go per package, which
is why generated code needs no mutation exclusion.

body:
## 概要

ロール一覧を開くたびに全ロールの権限集合と権限目録（/platform/permissions）まで読み込んでいたのを、一覧は group by 集計の権限個数だけを返す要約に置き換え、権限コードの列挙は編集モーダルを開いた時点の詳細取得へ分離した。

## 変更内容

- バックエンド: `GET /platform/roles` を要約応答（`permission_count`）へ変更。`RoleSummary` projection（JPQL group by）で集約を経由せず件数を集計し、EAGER の権限集合ロードを排除
- バックエンド: `GET /platform/roles/{id}` を新設。編集フォーム向けに権限コードの列挙と楽観ロック用 `version` を返す
- フロント: ロール編集モーダルを開くまで mount しない構造にし、権限目録とロール詳細の取得を編集時点まで遅延。409 競合時は詳細を取り直して version 固着を防ぐ
- フロント: スタッフ管理のロール選択（RolePicker / Staff*Modal）は要約型（id/name のみ使用）へ型を差し替え

## 検証

- [x] `task lint` exit 0
- [x] `task test-unit` 相当（backend `./gradlew test` exit 0 / frontend Jest 79 suites 521 tests 全緑）
- [ ] `task build`（CI の Lint and Test ジョブで実行される）
- [ ] `task e2e`（ローカルで複数セッションの docker が並行しており実行不能。roles.feature は本変更で断言対象の画面要素が変わらないことを確認済み）
- [ ] ローカルで code-review 実施済み

統合テスト: `task test-integration` を 2 回実行し、本変更が触る `PlatformStaffManagementIT` は 19/19 緑（一覧の permission_count / permissions 非列挙 / GET /{id} の新断言を含む）。`PlatformStoreApiIT.updateInvalidatesDomainLookupCache`（店舗ドメイン照会キャッシュ失効）だけが全量実行時に落ちるが、単独実行では緑で、本変更とは無関係（ローカルで複数セッションの compose が同一プロジェクト名を共有して干渉している疑い）。CI での確認を根拠とする。

## 決定ログ

- 一覧応答から `version` も落とした。楽観ロックの往復は詳細（GET /{id}）が担うため、一覧に残すと陳腐な version を掴む経路が復活する
- 件数集計は domain 層の interface projection（`RoleSummary`）+ JPQL `group by`。`OrderView` の既存読み側 projection パターンに合わせた。left join にしたのは、権限ゼロのロール（不変条件上は存在しない）が行ごと消えるのを防ぐ保険
- モーダルは常駐 mount + open prop から「開いたときだけ mount」へ変更。これにより権限目録（/platform/permissions）の取得もページ表示時から編集時へ自然に遅延する
- 409 時のフォーム最新化は「一覧から編集対象を導出して refetch で入れ替える」旧方式から「モーダル自身が詳細を取り直す」方式へ。一覧が要約になったため旧方式は成立しない

## 備考 / レビュー観点

- 応答形状の変更（一覧から `permissions` が消え `permission_count` が入る）はワイヤ契約変更。フロントの消費箇所は全て追随済み（RolesPage / RolePicker / Staff*Modal）
- `PlatformStoreApiIT` の flaky はこの PR とは別件。再現条件（全量実行時のみ）が安定しているため、必要なら別 issue に切り出す

author: kelvinmwega
body:
## Symptom

Clicking a valid magic link landed on `https://asset-mgt-ten.vercel.app/signin?callbackUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fasset-mgt-ten.vercel.app%2F` — the sign-in form — instead of the app.

**Sign-in was never broken.** The session was established correctly every time; the user was simply shown the sign-in page while authenticated.

## Evidence (production logs)

```
14:28:29  GET /                          307  [edge-middleware]   ← bounce to /signin?callbackUrl=…
14:28:46  POST /signin                   200                      ← link requested
14:29:33  GET /api/auth/callback/resend  302                      ← token verified, cookie set
14:29:34  GET /signin                    200                      ← ⚠ no `GET / 307` in between
14:31:14  GET /                          200                      ← same session: 200, not 307
```

The absence of a `GET / 307` at 14:29:34 proves the callback's 302 targeted `/signin` directly rather than being bounced there; the 200 at 14:31:14 proves the session was valid throughout.

## Root cause

Two compounding defects:

1. **`src/app/signin/actions.ts`** called `signIn("resend", { email, redirect: false })` with no `redirectTo`. Auth.js falls back to the `Referer` header — `const callbackUrl = redirectTo?.toString() ?? headers.get("Referer") ?? "/"` (`next-auth/lib/actions.js`). The Referer of that server action is the page the form sits on, which for anyone the middleware bounced is `/signin?callbackUrl=…`. That URL got baked into the emailed link.
2. **`src/app/signin/page.tsx`** had no session guard. `/signin` is deliberately outside the middleware matcher (it must stay public), so nothing upstream bounces an authenticated visitor off it.

## Fix

- `redirectTo: "/"` on the `signIn` call. A **constant**, never caller-supplied — this is the app's only unauthenticated mutation and must not become a redirect gadget. `/` routes on by role.
- A self-guard on `/signin` that redirects an authenticated visitor to `/`.

### The guard is not a bare session check — deliberately

`src/app/page.tsx:21-23` redirects a **deactivated** user holding a still-valid JWT to `/signin`. A naive `if (session) redirect("/")` would bounce them straight back into an infinite loop, locking out precisely the leavers the kill-switch exists to stop. The guard therefore DB-reads `deactivatedAt`, mirroring `requireRole`, and only when a session cookie is present — the anonymous path (the one exposed to unauthenticated traffic) touches no database.

`src/app/signin/page.integration.test.tsx` pins all three cases, including the loop guard.

## Verification

- `pnpm test` — 222 passed (22 files), including real-DB integration
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm build` with zero env populated — passes; `/signin` still `ƒ` (dynamic)
- Prettier clean on all changed files (4 pre-existing `docs/*` warnings are untouched and predate this branch)

## Review note

Security-touching (auth), so **Tier 3 — advisor review required before merge** per CLAUDE.md.

## Out of scope — surfaced by the same log dig

- `MissingSecret` error group on `/middleware`, 18 occurrences, last 2026-07-30. `src/middleware.ts` does `NextAuth(authConfig)` and `authConfig` carries no `secret`, relying on `process.env.AUTH_SECRET` reaching the edge runtime. Sessions decode fine now, but the middleware is one env change away from silently failing open to "no session".
- `AUTH_EMAIL_FROM` threw Resend 422 `Invalid \`from\` field` at 14:24 today; appears resolved by 14:28.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

`sim/startup/`'s 45-point matrix stopped completing once the DUT gained
`Xilimit` (#11 / PR #39) and `Xsoftstart` (#38 / PR #44): ngspice's default
trapezoidal integrator rings across the near-short branch's fast
current-limit clamping event and collapses the whole deck's global timestep
(all three load branches share one `tran` analysis). Adding
`.options method=gear` (Gear/BDF integration, the standard SPICE fix for
exactly this failure mode) restores the deck to ~12s CPU per corner and the
matrix is runnable again.

## Changes

- `sim/startup/testbench/tb_startup.spice`: add `.options method=gear`, with
  a header comment documenting the measured CPU cost (before/after) and a
  same-corner sanity check of the affected vs. unaffected branches.
- `sim/startup/testbench/tb.json`: disclose the integrator change in the
  Claim (per the `sim/soft-start/` precedent for disclosing integration
  changes), and correct the stale "issue #11 is open ..." text in the Claim
  and `operating_conditions` — #11 is closed and the DUT instantiates
  `Xilimit`, so the near-short branch is now inrush into a *protected*
  near-short. No pass/fail checks are added for it (a near-short is outside
  the ratified 0-50 mA load range and `README.md`'s target table has no
  short-circuit-current row).
- `sim/startup/records/20260801-142159-38317d9.md` (+ matching
  `netlist-snapshots/` and `corners/` evidence): new 45/45-point record,
  `--supersedes 20260801-003159-b64d60e`.

## Investigation (before/after CPU, measured at `tt_27c_3.30v`)

| configuration | result |
|---|---|
| full 3-branch deck, default (trapezoidal) integration | >120s CPU, did not finish the 6ms window (matches the issue's own ~2min-CPU-for-1.49ms-of-6ms finding) |
| near-short branch alone, default integration | did not finish within 900s wall (re-measured from scratch this session) |
| full 3-branch deck, `.options method=gear` | **11.7s CPU, completes cleanly** |
| `_full`/`_min` branches alone (unaffected either way) vs. gear-integrated combined deck | tsettle/overshoot agree to <1.2%, confirming gear doesn't distort the measurements |

This directly addresses the issue's root-cause hypothesis about the near-short
branch's stiffness (current-limit clamping under trapezoidal integration),
without needing to split branches into separate experiments or loosen
tolerances (`reltol`/`abstol`/`vntol`/`chgtol` stay at ngspice defaults).

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Verification |
|-----------|--------|--------------|
| 45-point matrix completes in a reasonable wall/CPU budget against the current DUT, without relaxing any ratified spec/check threshold | ✅ | `python3 sim/run_corners.py startup -j 6 --timeout 600 --supersedes 20260801-003159-b64d60e` completed 45/45 points in 995.7s wall (under heavy host contention: load average ~80 on 28 cores from concurrent sims in other repos); no check thresholds touched |
| New record written with `--supersedes 20260801-003159-b64d60e`, append-only | ✅ | `sim/startup/records/20260801-142159-38317d9.md`, `Supersedes: 20260801-003159-b64d60e`; superseded record untouched |
| `tb.json`'s `claim` and `tb_startup.spice`'s header no longer say "no current-limit/foldback circuitry exists yet (issue #11 is open ...)" | ✅ | Both updated; #11 is closed, DUT instantiates `Xilimit`, near-short branch reframed as a protected near-short. No `ipeak_short_ma` check added (still evidence-only) |
| Chosen direction documented with measured before/after CPU cost | ✅ | Documented in `tb_startup.spice`'s header comment and `tb.json`'s Claim, and in this PR body's Investigation table |

## Test Plan

- `python3 sim/run_corners.py startup -j 6 --timeout 600 --supersedes 20260801-003159-b64d60e` — 45/45 points completed (previously 0/45, every point timing out at 300s)
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s sim/tests` — 90/90 tests pass (no harness code changed, testbench-only fix)
- Manual single-corner sanity run through the harness (`--no-write`) before committing to the full matrix, to confirm the fix end-to-end

Note: the new record's overall verdict is **FAIL** — `tsettle_full_ms`/`tsettle_min_ms` now exceed the 3ms target at every corner because `Xsoftstart`'s ramp itself takes 2.3-5.8ms to settle. This is a genuine design finding (likely related to #42's open compensation-marginality issue), not a harness artifact, and is recorded honestly rather than masked.

Closes #48

author: suleymanozkeskin
body:
## Change

- `_ensure_states_exist` (the tick-loop self-heal for missing schedule-state rows) no longer runs its existence read every tick. It runs on a ~60 s wall-clock cadence — `_EXISTENCE_CHECK_INTERVAL_S`, tick count derived once at init as `max(1, round(60 / check_interval_seconds))` — while healthy, and every tick while unhealthy. A **failed re-init** is what re-arms per-tick checking until a fully healthy pass; a missing row whose re-init succeeds in the same pass counts as healthy and the cadence resumes immediately. `_ensure_states_exist` now returns that health as `bool`.

## Semantics

- The check guards rare conditions: startup init failure and external row deletion. Conditions → result from a production deployment: 108 schedules at a ~1 s tick issued the existence read 84k times/day, reading 9.1M rows/day (6.5% of total DB time) and returning all names every time — an answer that changes only on those rare events.
- Liveness preserved with a tick-independent bound: worst-case dormancy for an externally deleted row is ~one check interval (~60 s) regardless of `check_interval_seconds` — seconds denomination chosen per review (60 ticks at a 10 s tick would have been a 10-minute bound). The pre-guard behavior was dormancy until restart.
- A DB error on the existence read raises to the tick seam as before, and leaves the countdown at zero so the retried tick re-checks instead of skipping.
- The due-states read is untouched and still runs every tick.

## Verification

- Five cadence tests: skip-within-interval, re-run-after-interval, every-tick-while-unhealthy then cadence resumes, re-check on the tick retried after a DB error, and tick-count derivation across `check_interval_seconds` 1/10/60 → 60/6/1. Revert-verified: with the cadence gate removed in place, exactly the three cadence-skip tests fail; with the fix, all 96 pass.
- The five pre-existing self-heal tests pass unchanged (first tick always checks, so single-tick expectations hold).
- Pyright delta vs main on changed files: all `reportPrivateUsage` occurrences of the test file's existing `scheduler._check_and_run_schedules` idiom.

author: rarhs
body:
Slice 2 of the multi-routines plan (spec: `apps/vault/docs/multi-routines-spec.md`). Replaces slice 1's nil-only bridge with the real collection semantics across merge, ops, and the queue.

## Merge (`sync/merge.ts`)
Union by id with per-id last-write-wins. Tombstones participate like any edit: a newer local deletion wins **and is pushed**; a newer remote edit revives a deleted routine; ties go to remote. Touched local-only routines are pushed; an untouched local seed is discarded once the remote contributes anything (no ghost "Starter Push" on second devices); remote-only routines are adopted. If a merge leaves nothing live, `withLiveRoutine` (shared with `loadPersisted`) appends a fresh seed so the app never ends up routine-less.

## Ops, plan, queue
- `PushPlan.routines: Routine[]` (documents to write) replaces the boolean; `RemoteState.routines: Routine[]` includes tombstones.
- `opsForTransition` diffs routines by id — new, edited, and tombstoned documents each become a `put-routine`; switching the active routine still emits nothing.
- `SyncQueue` coalesces `put-routine` per routine id, so writes to distinct routines no longer clobber each other in the offline buffer.

## Interim shim, now confined to the adapter
`SupabaseBackend.putRoutine` drops non-nil and tombstoned documents — the singleton schema can't represent them, and without this guard a newly created routine would overwrite the one server row. `fetchState` wraps the row as a one-element array. This guard is exactly what slice 3 (schema migration) deletes. Covered by a new contract test.

TDD red→green; suite 149 passing, all 7 live contract tests green against the local Supabase stack, `npm run check` clean.

author: copilot
body:
Each drink category previously computed its own independent amount and all were summed, causing massive overestimation — e.g. ~3 L total for 1 guest × 4 hours at 0% buffer (9 categories × individual rates).

## New approach

**`drinkRates.js`** — Add a single total-budget constant:
```js
const BASE_RATE_PER_PERSON_PER_HOUR = 0.5; // 1 person × 4 h = 2.0 L
```

**`calculateEventDrinks.js`** — Replace the single-pass per-category loop with a two-pass calculation:

1. **Compute total budget**: `(adults + children) × BASE_RATE × hours × seasonFactor × durFactor`
2. **Distribute proportionally**: existing per-category rates (`erwachsene × anteilTrinker × typeFactor`) become relative weights; each selected category receives `totalBeverage × (weight_i / Σ weights)`.

```
// 1 adult, 4h, uebergang, all 9 default categories
// Before: 0.8 + 0.6 + 0.4 + 0.5 + 0.12 + ... ≈ 3.0 L  (additive)
// After:  2.0 L total, split proportionally          (fixed budget)
```

Erfahrungswerte (calibrated rates), event-type factors, and guest preference multipliers all continue to influence the distribution — they shift the proportional weights rather than scaling absolute amounts. Legacy rate-based custom drinks remain unchanged.

**`calculateEventDrinks.preferences.test.js`** — Updated one hardcoded absolute-value assertion to match the proportional model; added two new realism tests verifying the 2 L total and linear guest scaling.

author: metalmmagic
body:
feat(client): the Overview says whether the space is answering, not just what it holds

The UI half of the per-space usefulness work. #608 records demand and payoff; this shows them where the
owner asked for them.

A Usage panel over the last 7 DAYS, not 24 hours: usefulness is a question about a habit, and a space
queried every Monday reads as dead in a one-day window.

- Tiles for calls, recalls, answered, writes and mean duration; the answer rate as a bar with the mean
  best-hit score beside it; slow calls (over a second, with the true maximum) only when there are any.
- The bar's thresholds are INVERTED against the storage bar directly above it. There, full is bad. Here
  a low rate is the warning — questions arriving and going unanswered is the content gap this panel
  exists to make visible, and reusing the storage colours would have said the opposite.
- "Answers nothing" and "was never asked" render differently, because they call for opposite responses
  from an operator: fill the space, versus find out why nothing queries it. Zero recalls shows as an
  em dash, never as 0%, which would read as a judgement about answer quality. Mutation-verified —
  returning 0 there fails the spec.
- A window with no traffic still renders the panel, saying so. Hiding it would look like a failed load,
  and "nothing was asked of this space" is an answer.
- For a proxy space the shell sums its members and recombines the means from their weights, rather than
  averaging per-space averages — otherwise a member with one call gets the same say as one with a
  thousand.

Two icons the panel wanted (chart-line, pulse) are not in the registry, so it uses registered ones: an
unregistered Phosphor icon renders an EMPTY svg with no error at all.

Gates: overview-tab (+6 — the rate, the never-asked distinction, the empty-window render, the
hidden-until-loaded case, and slow calls only when present), brain.component mock extended so the shell
fetch is exercised rather than stubbed away.

body:
## Summary
Adds three `KubeletConfiguration` fields to the global kubelet patch (`talos/patches/global/machine-kubelet.yaml`). All are version-independent of the pending Talos 1.14 upgrade and supported on our current k8s v1.36.2.

- `maxParallelImagePulls: 3` — bound concurrent image pulls per node. `serializeImagePulls` is already `false`, so pulls were previously unbounded.
- `imageMaximumGCAge: 168h` — GC images unused for a week, independent of disk-pressure thresholds. Keeps superseded Renovate tags from piling up until the 85% high-threshold purge. (Kubelet resets last-used tracking on restart, so the window restarts after node reboots.)
- `crashLoopBackOff.maxContainerRestartPeriod: 60s` — cap CrashLoopBackOff at 60s instead of the 300s default, so pods that crashed while a dependency (NFS on TrueNAS, a database, a broker) was down recover within a minute of it returning. Beta/default since k8s v1.35 (KEP-5593); per-node scope.

## Test plan
- [x] `talhelper genconfig` renders all three fields into `extraConfig`
- [x] `talosctl validate -m metal` passes for miirym, palarandusk, aurinax
- [ ] `task talos:apply-node IP=...` per node (no reboot; kubelet restarts to pick up config) — roll node-by-node

author: mokenuf
body:
## Summary

- Sube `@nuxt/devtools` de 3.2.4 a 3.3.1 (junto con `-kit` y `-wizard`), que parchea **GHSA-279x** (Critical): el canal RPC de DevTools no tiene autenticación — cualquier cliente que alcance el endpoint de HMR de Vite puede invocar métodos RPC y ejecutar comandos arbitrarios, sin token, handshake ni chequeo de origin.
- El impacto está limitado a desarrollo (los builds de producción no corren DevTools), pero el vector incluye a una web maliciosa abriendo un WebSocket cross-origin mientras corre el dev server. Ambas apps tienen `devtools: { enabled: true }`.
- Cambio de **lockfile únicamente**: `@nuxt/devtools` es dependencia transitiva de `nuxt` y el rango declarado ya acepta 3.3.1, así que ningún `package.json` se toca, `nuxt` se mantiene en 4.4.8 y `vite` en 7.3.6.
- No se sube Nuxt a 4.5.1 (donde este parche también entra) a propósito — ver Motivación.

## Changes

| File | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `@nuxt/devtools`, `@nuxt/devtools-kit` y `@nuxt/devtools-wizard` de 3.2.4 a 3.3.1. Sin cambios en ningún `package.json`. |

## Motivación

El 2026-07-27 se publicaron cinco advisories de Nuxt, todas parcheadas en 4.5.1. La respuesta obvia sería subir Nuxt, pero **4.5 rompe el SSR de producción en ambas apps**: `pnpm build` sale verde y todo request devuelve 500 (`Cannot destructure property '__extends' of '__toESM(...).default'`), por un problema de interop CJS→ESM de tslib —que entra vía `@supabase/*`— en el bundle de servidor de Nitro. Es un error de evaluación de módulo en runtime, así que `check`, `test` y `build` pasan los tres sin chistar. Se confirmó por bisección: 4.4.8 responde 302, 4.5.0 responde 500, con la misma codebase y rebuild limpio.

Como `@nuxt/devtools` es un paquete aparte con su propia línea de versiones, se puede parchear sin arrastrar Nuxt. Eso deja el repo cubierto sin comerse el bug.

Las otras cuatro advisories no aplican a este proyecto: todas requieren features que no usamos (verificado por grep — cero archivos `.server.vue`, cero referencias a `NuxtIsland`, cero `routeRules` y sin `vue.runtimeCompiler`).

## Advisories del 2026-07-27 y exposición

| Advisory | Sev. | Requiere | ¿Aplica? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GHSA-279x (DevTools RPC) | Critical | `@nuxt/devtools` < 3.3.1, solo dev | **Sí — es lo que arregla esta PR** |
| GHSA-9473 (RCE server islands) | High | `vue.runtimeCompiler: true` + server islands | No |
| GHSA-wm8w (fuga de payload entre usuarios) | High | `routeRules` con `cache`/`swr`/`isr` | No |
| GHSA-hxvh (bypass de route rules) | High | `routeRules` | No |
| GHSA-9pgf / GHSA-hxcr (DoS de islands) | High | endpoint de islands | No |

## Test plan

- `pnpm dev:trainer` y `pnpm dev:client`: ambas levantan y el panel de DevTools abre sin errores en consola.
- Confirmar en el lockfile que `nuxt` sigue en 4.4.8 y `vite` en 7.3.6, y que ningún `package.json` quedó modificado (`git diff development...HEAD --stat` debe listar solo `pnpm-lock.yaml`).
- Verificar que el bundle de producción no se vio afectado: `pnpm build` y después, por cada app, `node apps/<app>/.output/server/index.mjs` + un request a `/`. Ambas deben responder 302 (redirect a login) sin errores en el log.
- `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build` — pasan limpio.

author: abelalejandroperezreynoso
body:
## Problema

El mes en curso se dibujaba sólido y sin aviso aunque su contenido fuera casi todo predicción (`m.esFuturo = m.ym > ymActual` sólo marca los meses posteriores). El día 1 del mes, la barra se leía como dinero ya registrado.

## Cambios (`dashboard.html`)

- `construirMesesDesglosados()` acumula, en espejo de cada segmento, la parte proyectada: `ingresosProyectados`, `destacadosProyectados` y el ya existente `gastoRecurrenteProyectado`. Tras el recorte al total del mes calcula `corrienteIngresoProyectado` y `gastoRecurrentePorOcurrir`, ambos acotados a su segmento.
- Cada concepto se dibuja ahora en **dos datasets apilados**: el tramo real con color sólido y el proyectado justo encima con `ALPHA_PROYECTADO = 0.3`. El gasto variable no lleva gemelo porque la proyección nunca lo genera.
- Nueva constante `ALPHA_PROYECTADO` y helper `segmento()` que arma cada dataset.
- Los meses 100% futuros caen enteros en el tramo proyectado por construcción, así que desaparecen los arreglos de color por mes (`meses.map(m => m.esFuturo ? ... : ...)`).
- El título añade `(incluye proyección)` cuando el mes mezcla real y proyectado, y el balance al cierre se atenúa igual que en los meses futuros.
- El panel de detalle abre con una línea `⏳ Aún no ocurre: +$X de ingresos y -$Y de gastos`, calculada sobre lo que está visible (respeta los filtros de tipo).

## Verificación

- Sintaxis de los bloques `<script>` validada.
- 17 aserciones en Node ejecutando la función real `construirMesesDesglosados` sobre un escenario "1 de agosto" (julio real, agosto con un gasto real y el resto proyectado, septiembre íntegro proyectado): reparto correcto por mes, gasto variable real intacto, y el invariante `proyectado <= segmento` en todos los meses y segmentos. Las 17 pasan.
- Render de la gráfica real con Chart.js en Chromium headless: julio sólido, agosto en tono fantasma con el gasto real dibujado sólido encima del proyectado, septiembre fantasma completo.

author: ys-ll
body:
## Summary

Add terminal character encoding support to Telnet sessions, mirroring the existing SSH implementation. Connections to non-UTF-8 devices (e.g. GBK, GB2312, Big5, Shift-JIS) will now render Chinese / Japanese text instead of tofu blocks.

### Changes

- **`backend/session/telnet_session.go`**: port `SetEncoding` / `decodeOutput` / `encodeInput` from `ssh_session.go`. `encodeInput` is applied in `Write`; `decodeOutput` is applied after `filterIAC` in `handleRead` (avoids feeding IAC bytes into the codec). Thread safety via `baseSession.mu` matches the SSH implementation. Reuses the package-private `encodingByName` helper.
- **`app.go`**: apply `SetEncoding` on `*TelnetSession` alongside the existing SSH branch in the session setup path.
- **`frontend/src/components/ConnectionForm.vue`**: show the existing encoding dropdown for both `ssh` and `telnet` connection types. No new i18n keys needed (`conn.encoding` already exists in all locales).
- **`frontend/wailsjs/go/models.ts`**: regenerated by `wails dev`.

### Notes

- `sendAutoLogin` (username / password) is still written as UTF-8 raw bytes; SSH behaves the same. Configured credentials are typically ASCII, so this is consistent with the existing SSH behavior and out of scope for this fix.
- Proper RFC 2066 CHARSET negotiation was not implemented — the post-hoc codec approach matches what SSH does and is sufficient for the issue's symptom.

Fixes #455

### Test plan

- `go build ./...`
- `go test ./backend/session/...`
- `npm --prefix frontend run build`
- Manual: create a Telnet connection, set encoding to `GBK` / `GB2312` / `Big5` / `Shift-JIS`, connect to a server that emits those encodings, and verify the terminal renders Chinese / Japanese characters correctly instead of tofu blocks.
- Manual: verify the default `Unicode (UTF-8)` Telnet behavior is unchanged.

---

## 概要

给 Telnet 加上和 SSH 一样的终端字符编码支持。连接到非 UTF-8 设备（如 GBK、GB2312、Big5、Shift-JIS）时，终端将正常渲染中文 / 日文字符，而不是显示方块。

### 改动

- **`backend/session/telnet_session.go`**：从 `ssh_session.go` 移植 `SetEncoding` / `decodeOutput` / `encodeInput`。`encodeInput` 在 `Write` 里套用；`decodeOutput` 在 `handleRead` 里 `filterIAC` 之后套用（避免 IAC 字节混进 codec）。通过 `baseSession.mu` 保证并发安全，与 SSH 实现一致。复用包内私有 `encodingByName` 函数。
- **`app.go`**：在 session 创建路径的 SSH 分支后，增加对 `*TelnetSession` 调用 `SetEncoding`。
- **`frontend/src/components/ConnectionForm.vue`**：现有 encoding 下拉框现在在 `ssh` 和 `telnet` 两种连接类型下都显示。不需要新增 i18n key（`conn.encoding` 在各语言里都已有）。
- **`frontend/wailsjs/go/models.ts`**：由 `wails dev` 重新生成。

### 说明

- `sendAutoLogin`（用户名 / 密码）仍以 UTF-8 裸字节写入，与 SSH 行为一致；典型配置凭据是 ASCII，此处与 SSH 保持一致，不在本次修复范围内。
- 未实现 RFC 2066 CHARSET 协商；采用 SSH 同款的后置 codec 方案，对应 issue 描述的症状已经够用。

修复 #455

author: lucapinello
body:
Adds `chorus/analysis/background_sampling.py` and its equivalence tests. **Touches no builder** — that's the extract-then-migrate shape, so a later per-oracle migration PR that changes a number is a regression rather than an ambiguity.

## An AST-level audit found much less divergence than the issue implies

#125 describes 8 `ReservoirSampler` copies, "one divergent". Hashing every method's AST across all eight suggested *worse* — 7 distinct class hashes, `to_cdf_matrix` in 4 apparent versions. So I read the bodies instead of trusting the hashes:

- **`to_cdf_matrix` is numerically identical** in all four "versions". The hashes differ by `np` vs `numpy`, one docstring, and `indices` vs `idx`.
- **`add()` is numerically identical** in all three — a docstring and type annotations.

Across ~30 duplicated definitions there are exactly **four** genuine behavioural divergences. Each is preserved as a **parameter** rather than unified away, because each may be deliberate:

| divergence | preserved as |
|---|---|
| AlphaGenome capacity **20,000** | `ReservoirSampler(capacity=…)`, default 50,000 |
| LegNet N-threshold **0.3** | `get_sequence(max_n_fraction=…)`, default 0.5 |
| log2fc / logfc / diff | `compute_effect(formula=…)` |
| EPInformer-seq **`(4, L)`** | `one_hot_encode(channels_first=…)` |

Unifying any of them silently would change a shipped background. Whether LegNet's stricter 0.3 is intentional for a 200 bp window is a question for its owner, not something to settle by taking the majority value. Each has a test asserting it stays a parameter.

## Verified against the live copies, not a snapshot

`tests/test_background_sampling.py` extracts each builder's `ReservoirSampler` **by AST and execs it** in an isolated namespace — following the `tests/test_cherimoya.py:581` idiom, since several builders do work at module scope and can't be imported. Comparing against pasted-in code would pass forever while the real copies drifted.

**All 8 builders' samplers are byte-identical** to the shared one on a 500-value stream across 3 tracks at capacity 50 — so the *replacement* branch of algorithm R is exercised, not just the fill branch.

## It settles an open question in #125

**AlphaGenome's hand-vectorised 37-line `add_batch` is proved equivalent** to the 3-line loop (400 values in 37-value chunks at capacity 40). It's a safe optimisation, not a divergence. The shared module keeps the loop anyway — the speed only matters for AlphaGenome's larger fan-out, and 3 lines are easier to trust.

## Behaviour the copies relied on and none documented

- `compute_effect`'s log2fc branch matches `cherimoya_source/scoring.py` **bit-for-bit** across 6 edge cases including `(0,0)` and `(1e-6, 3.3)`. That module is the one place builder/oracle sharing is already enforced, so it's the reference.
- **A short reservoir interpolates onto the full grid rather than padding**, so every stored entry is a real quantile estimate — which is precisely why the percentile denominator must be the grid width, not the sample count (#119). A padded tail would have justified the old behaviour.
- Non-ACGT becomes an all-zero column. `get_sequence` tolerates up to `max_n_fraction` N, so that path is live.
- An empty track stays all-zero, which is how `_has_samples` detects it.

The `get_sequence` docstring records the offset arithmetic every builder's ref substitution depends on (1-based centre lands at index `length//2 - 1`) and notes that only EPInformer-seq actually validates it.

`649 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed` (622 + 27 new)

Next: one PR per oracle, each proving byte-identical sample counts before and after the switch.
