body:
No schema do ZimaOS, `x-casaos.tips.custom` é uma **string**. O mapa de idiomas (`en_us`/`pt_br`) só é aceito em `tips.before_install`.

Com o mapa em `custom`, o `zimaos-app-management` falha ao decodificar e descarta o compose inteiro:

```
failed to load compose app definition
'Tips.Custom' expected type 'string', got unconvertible type 'map[string]interface {}'
app: zimaapp://v2app/immich2youtube
```

O efeito é enganoso: o container sobe saudável, com as labels de projeto certas e respondendo na porta, mas **o app não aparece na home do ZimaOS** — e a interface não mostra erro nenhum. O erro só existe no journal:

```bash
journalctl -u zimaos-app-management --since "-15 min" --no-pager | grep "failed to load compose"
```

Diagnosticado numa instalação real (ZimaOS, Docker 28.3.2, Compose 2.38.2). Depois da troca para `before_install`, o `installed/list` passa a carregar o app sem erro de parse.

author: ratzori
body:
projectRings()/projectLines()/projectPoint() picked their radial-distance formula through a ProjectFn template parameter, defaulted to equidistant. That default made a mismatch against a corresponding inverse call an easy, silent bug, and every real caller (the Qt bridge's useOrthographic toggle) already selects the formula at runtime anyway -- the template parameter never reflected how the choice is actually made, and forced the bridge to write each call out twice in a ternary. Replaced with a ProjectionType enum argument, with no default: it names directly what the choice selects (equidistant vs. orthographic), matching how these are already described in cartography generally. The per-point hot loop stays exactly as templated and inlined as before (detail::projectRings() etc.); the runtime choice costs one branch per call, not per point.

projectEquidistant() (equidistant.h) is named to match its projectOrthographic() sibling (orthographic.h), rather than being the one radial-distance formula identifiable only by the absence of a suffix.

Deploys the Product Catalog API container to GKE Autopilot with standard enterprise hardening: unprivileged execution user, read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities, and matching resource requests/limits. Wires configuration via ConfigMap and sensitive database password via Secret.

author: badsonstudios
body:
Closes #134

Fourth item of epic **E18** (`docs/plans/05-transport-migration.md`).

## What this does — plain English

Until now there was no way to test the new way of talking to Claude without
actually using your subscription — every test would have burned real tokens and
needed you logged in, which means it could never run automatically.

This builds a stand-in: a small program that pretends to be Claude and speaks
the new protocol convincingly, including the part that matters most — stopping
mid-task to ask permission and waiting for an answer. Tests can now drive the
whole conversation, including the exact `.claude/` permission case that started
this whole piece of work, with no login and no network.

The existing stand-in (the one every current test uses) is completely untouched.
There are simply two now, one per way of talking.

Nothing about the app changes for you yet.

## What to test

**Nothing to click — this is internal; the gate is the test suite.**

If you want one command that shows the point of the epic working end to end:

```
npm run build && npm run check:fake-stream
```

It spawns the compiled fake over real pipes and walks the whole exchange —
including a permission request for `.claude/scripts/coverage.sh`, answered
"allow", **with the file actually written**. That's S-10 probe B reproduced as a
repeatable check instead of a one-off spike script. 14/14 pass.

## Structure, and why

**Split into protocol + plumbing** for a constraint worth remembering: **the CI
unit job does not run a build.** Anything asserting on a compiled entry point
could only ever *skip* there — and a test that silently doesn't run is worse than
none (#107's lesson).

So all behaviour lives in `fake-stream-protocol.ts` (20 synchronous tests, no
spawn), and the compiled program is proven over real pipes by a new
`npm run check:fake-stream`, following the four existing `check:*` entries.

**Two fakes, selected by distinct VALUES of one variable** —
`SWITCHBOARD_FAKE_PROVIDER=1` is the original PTY fake, `=stream` is the new one
— rather than two variables, so both modes can't be on at once and race to
register the same `claude-code` id.

## The check earned its place immediately

It caught a bug the unit tests **structurally could not**. `fake-stream-cli.ts`
is a rollup *entry* so it lands in `out/main/`, but `fake-stream.ts` is imported
by bootstrap and rollup placed it in `out/main/chunks/` — so
`join(__dirname, 'fake-stream-cli.js')` resolved one directory too deep.

Worse, it failed as a **15-second spawn timeout**, because a child that can't
resolve its script dies on stderr while we wait on stdout. It now tries both
candidates and **throws a named error** if neither exists: a wrong path must fail
as a wrong path.

## The fake reproduces the surprising behaviour, not the intuitive one

`system:init` is emitted **once per turn**, because that's what S-11 measured the
real CLI doing. A fake kinder than the real thing hides the bug it exists to
catch — #135 and #139 each need to pin that. Every message shape is copied from
S-10's captured payloads, including `decision_reason_type: "safetyCheck"` and
`permission_suggestions`, which is exactly what #137 renders.

## A done-when I corrected rather than quietly redefined

The issue claimed *"an e2e drives a full turn in stream mode against the fake."*
**That is unmeetable by this item** — a full turn needs session wiring (#135) and
a way to *create* a stream session from the UI (#138). This item only builds the
fake.

**It was my planning error in `/pm`, not a shortfall in the work.** The criterion
has moved to #138; both issues carry a comment and the plan file records it in
both places.

## Gate

lint ✓ · typecheck ✓ · **728 unit (+20)** · **98 e2e, untouched** ·
`check:fake-stream` **14/14 PASS** · `references/testing.md` updated (the two
fakes, and why the `check:*` layer exists for build-dependent proofs) ·
no user-facing change, so no `docs/manual/` page.

Sweep now closes the record of every running session whose instance it destroyed or found already gone, and `jamstream status` corroborates a running record against its provider (the same `list_tagged` call `end` uses) before repeating it: a gone instance prints `stale` with a pointer at `jamstream end`, and the JSON gains `"corroborated"` on rows recorded running, so the uninstallers' pre-flight match on `"status": "running"` stops seeing a bare running for a session that died weeks ago. Status stays read-only.

Only `end.rs` ever wrote `SessionStatus::Ended`, so a session that died via sweep, the idle self-exit, the max-duration kill, or a crash kept its record at running forever, and a stale record blocked the uninstaller. Absence of evidence closes nothing: a provider that could not be searched or asked (no credentials in the shell, network down) leaves its records alone with a note, so an unverifiable session still blocks an uninstall while a confirmed-dead one no longer does. The close goes through one `SessionState::mark_ended` helper so every death leaves the shape `end` leaves, issuer key dropped included.

The app's Recent list needs no change here: stale is a live judgment against the provider, never stored, and the state file shape is unchanged. Wiring the app's launch sweep to the new `sweep::reconcile` is the next wave.

Test plan: new `crates/cli/tests/reconcile.rs` runs both layers against the mock provider, covering destroyed, already-gone, unsearched-provider, unlistable-provider, and dry-run cases for sweep, plus live, gone, unresolvable, unlistable, and ended records for status, and asserts the uninstall regex contract on the pretty JSON. `cargo fmt`, clippy, and the cli and client suites pass.

Closes #321

## Corrections

- **Test count** said 341; the suite collects **342**.
- **The feedline is identified.** CLAUDE.md said it was unconfirmed whether the 5.7 dB cable was the 10 ft feedline. The delay measurement settles it: **14.7 ns at VF ≈ 0.70 is 3.09 m = 10.1 ft**, and the 8.9–10.5 ft spread across plausible velocity factors brackets 10 ft. The loss figure does apply to the directivity work. The note now separates the measured 13.75 ns from the 0.97 ns the operator declared for the calibration reference plane.
- **Radio state reconciliation** added to both maturity tables.

## The finding: the active frequency profile does not survive a restart

`SafetyLimits()` is constructed with its defaults in `Runtime.__init__` and nothing persists `active_profile`. Every start silently returns to **`bench_cabled` (70 MHz – 6 GHz)** — the closed-circuit profile.

This surfaced from trying to *write down* that the bench was on `ism_conservative` and checking first. It wasn't. The profile had been narrowed deliberately on 2026-07-31 because antennas had gone on the bench, and a later service restart widened it back with no notice.

That's a safety gate reverting silently, so it's now a gotcha in its own right and has been folded into **engineering-queue item 2**, ahead of the calibration state that item used to be about. A correction that is lost is a degraded measurement; a gate that is lost is a gate.

**Not fixed here** — it's a code change and belongs in its own PR.

Live bench has been set back to `ism_conservative` manually.

author: chrysa
body:
Ports the anchored coverage parser into this repo's vendored `scripts/quality_gate.py`.

## The defect
`_parse_coverage` scanned every line containing `total`/`coverage`/`covered` and returned the first `N%` it found. With `-v` in `addopts` — the fleet default — pytest prints one line per test with a progress marker:

```
tests/test_thing.py::test_value_is_covered PASSED   [ 13%]
```

so the gate reported **13.0** for a suite sitting at 94%. Observed for real on pre-commit-tools: 13.0 against a 58.0 baseline.

## The fix
Anchored patterns (`^TOTAL … %`, `Total coverage: X%`, istanbul `All files |`, nyc `Statements :`), then a fallback to the `line-rate` of a written `coverage.xml` for the `--cov-report=xml`-only case.

Identical to the canonical implementation in chrysa/shared-standards (#259) and to chrysa/chrysa-lib#218.

## Why this arrives as one PR of many
The same defect has now had to be fixed by hand in **16 repos**, because `quality_gate.py` is vendored rather than distributed — chrysa/shared-standards#274. Behaviour verified on the patched file: `[ 13%]` progress marker → 94.0, `Total coverage: 87.5%` → 87.5, XML fallback → 94.12.

body:
## Summary
Two bugs in the biometric second factor path of SendCrypto:

**Bug 1 — Cancel consumed an attempt slot (fail-honest violation)**
`USER_CANCELLED`, `KEY_PERMANENTLY_INVALIDATED`, and `biometryNotEnrolled` all collapsed into `TWO_FACTOR.WRONG`, burning one of the 5 attempt slots. Five taps on the OS "Cancel" button locked the session captioned "Incorrect."

**Bug 2 — Silent dead-end on verifier rejection**
`submitReauth` had `try/finally` with no `catch` — a rejecting verifier escaped as an unhandled rejection with no error shown and no send proceeding.

**Fix**:
- Adds `src/lib/stepUpFactorOutcome.js`: pure classifier with `STEP_UP_FACTOR` codes (`CANCELLED`, `KEY_INVALIDATED`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `MISMATCH`) and `countsAsAttempt`/`recoveryRequired` shape
- Biometric leg in `SendCrypto` uses new `evaluateBiometricSecondFactor` — separates non-credential failures from wrong-credential failures
- `submitReauth` gains a `catch` surfacing `send.reauth.errors.unavailable` without counting an attempt or reaching `sendTx.mutate()`
- `TwoFactorGate` gains `verdict?.neutral` so cancelled/invalidated outcomes skip the attempt counter; the `oom` path is unchanged

Every failure path still refuses the send. The only relaxation is attempt accounting, and in biometric mode there is no knowledge factor being guessed while the OS rate-limits the sheet itself.

Aplica o pacote de alterações do relatório de 01/08/2026, na ordem de prioridade definida por ele.

## 1. Validade pericial das fotos (pasta 4 — alta)
- **Armazenamento pericial** (`app/helpers/upload_pericial.php`): o arquivo recebido é guardado intocado, nomeado pelo próprio SHA-256, gravado como somente leitura, com o hash conferido depois da gravação. As cópias de exibição são derivadas do original, nunca no lugar dele.
- **Tabela `midia_custodia`** (`marco_urbano2_midia_custodia.sql`): hash, EXIF, autor, IP e momento do recebimento.
- **12 regras de bloqueio** (`app/helpers/validacao_midia.php`): WhatsApp, sem EXIF, sem GPS, sem data, cópia reduzida, fora da obra, foto antiga, data futura, duplicada em outro trecho, tipo inválido. Sem liberação excepcional. Lançamento tudo-ou-nada: um reprovado e nada é gravado, nem as medidas do trecho.
- **Conferência no navegador** (`assets/js/validacao-midia.js`), para não esperar o upload de 12 MB até a recusa.

## 2. Relatório oficial em PDF (pasta 1 — alta)
- Identidade Marco Urbano, com cabeçalho e rodapé repetindo em todas as páginas via `thead`/`tfoot`.
- Quadro de identificação, resumo consolidado e assinatura do responsável técnico.
- **Totais separados por tipo de pavimento** — itens distintos da planilha contratual, com preços unitários próprios.
- Campos que dependem do contrato (período, responsável técnico, ART) saem como "a confirmar" até serem preenchidos em `app/config/relatorio.php`.

## 3. Peso das imagens (pasta 3 — média)
- `planejador/thumb.php`: miniaturas com cache em disco, ETag e 304.

## 4. Correções de tela (pasta 2 — baixa)
- Contenção de imagem, galeria em grade e responsivo — apenas as regras de tela, já que o `@media print` do pacote 1 vence conforme a precedência.

## Decisões de integração que se afastam do pacote
- **Whitelist do `thumb.php`** estendida para aceitar o nome SHA-256 em subpasta (precedência nº 2 do relatório), mantendo as barreiras contra travessia de diretório. Acrescentado o ramo `IMAGETYPE_WEBP` (precedência nº 3).
- **Imagens do relatório carregam como `eager`.** O `lazy` dependia do evento `beforeprint`, que não dispara na geração headless de PDF — verifiquei e as fotos saíam em branco no documento oficial. Como as miniaturas já resolvem o peso, correção do documento ganha da economia.
- **`mu_url_midia` / `mu_path_midia`** resolvem tanto o acervo anterior (`uploads/fotos/nome.jpg`) quanto o formato novo, para não quebrar o que já foi lançado.
- **Mensagem da regra `FOTO_ANTIGA`** corrigida: mandava "pedir liberação ao responsável técnico", mas não existe liberação — mandaria o pessoal de campo atrás de algo inexistente.
- **Mídia da obra fora do git** (`uploads/.gitignore` + `.htaccess`): é dado de produção e prova pericial.

- [x] `php -l` em todos os arquivos alterados e novos
- [x] **12 regras exercitadas contra fixtures gerados** (foto válida 12 MP, fora da obra, 272 dias atrás, sem GPS, cópia reduzida 3,4 MP, arquivo de WhatsApp, data futura, PNG, sem aparelho) — cada uma disparou o código correto, com a foto válida passando

The live application (router, guards, pages under `src/`) was already in place from prior merged PRs; this PR removes the dead Next.js scaffolding that remained alongside it and would break a clean `tsc`/install.

**Dependency fix (`react-helmet-async` is incompatible with React 19)**

**Removed orphaned Next.js files** (replaced by the Vite/React-Router SPA):

author: corablack
body:
## Summary
- Remove `Object::create<T>()` and move object creation into `UniqueObject`
- Add `UniqueObject::create<T>(args...)` and `UniqueObject::create_with_classname(class_name)`
- Make `ClassDB::create(class_name)` return `std::optional<UniqueObject>` instead of `std::unique_ptr<Object>`
- `ObjectPool::create<T>` now accepts and forwards constructor arguments
- Temporarily disable tests that relied on `Object::create<T>` (`test_unit`, `test_unit_iterator`, `test_value`)
## Motivation
`Object::create<T>()` constructed objects directly with `make_unique`, bypassing the `ObjectPool`. Since `UniqueObject` resolves objects by id through the pool, such objects could not be managed by `UniqueObject`. Moving construction into the pool keeps every created object tracked and addressable by id, and paves the way for the reflection `ClassDB::create` to produce pool-backed objects.
## Changes
- `include/gkit/core/object.hpp` — remove `Object::create<T>()`; friend `ObjectPool`
- `include/gkit/core/unique_object.hpp` / `src/core/unique_object.cpp` — new `create<T>` / `create_with_classname` static factories; private default ctor
- `src/core/object_pool.hpp` — `create<T>(args...)` forwards ctor args via `new T(std::forward<Args>(args)...)`
- `include/gkit/core/reflect/registry.hpp` / `src/core/reflect/registry.cpp` — `ClassDB::create` returns `std::optional<UniqueObject>`; `Factory` now yields `UniqueObject`
## Testing
- `test_reflect.cpp` updated for the new optional/`UniqueObject` API (create by class name; non-existent class returns `nullopt`)
- Tests depending on `Object::create<T>` are disabled pending migration

author: youknowone
body:
Two independent changes.

## 1. Decline to fold float-result pure calls in the walker

`try_fold_pure_call_via_executor` routed every constant-funcbox `CallPure*`
through `executor::execute_pure_call`, whose `Float` arm calls
`call_int_function` and reinterprets the **integer** return register via
`f64::from_bits`.

That convention is a caller contract, not a property of the descr. Two emitters
bake operand 0 of a residual call, with opposite float conventions:

| emitter | funcbox | float return |
|---|---|---|
| `majit-translate` codewriter (LLBC path) | the callee's **own address** | real `f64` register |
| runtime `*_canonical_via_target` (`jitcode/assembler.rs:3343`) | `JitCallTarget::concrete_ptr` | `i64` with `f64::to_bits` pre-packed |

Both land in the same walker handlers and dispatch on `descr.result_type()`
alone. `CallDescr` records the signature, not which emitter produced the
pointer, so no descr-based dispatch can be right for both — feeding a
codewriter funcbox to the `i64`-bits arm reads whatever was left in the integer
return register.

The fix returns early on `result_type() == Type::Float` and leaves the recorded
`CallPure*` for the backend, which calls the same pointer with the descr's real
signature (`majit-backend-wasm/src/codegen.rs:909 residual_call_float_sig`
builds an `f64`-returning `call_indirect` from it). `execute_pure_call`'s
`Float` arm keeps the `i64`-bits convention, now documented as a caller
contract.

Adding a `bh_call_f` instead would only *flip* which channel is broken. The
discriminator does exist in the data — `JitCode::call_descr_to_call_target`
(`jitcode/mod.rs:367`) maps a descr slot back to its `JitCallTarget` — but
nothing in `pyre/` reads it today, so folding these is left to a future change.

**Evidence.** New regression test `walker_declines_to_fold_a_float_result_pure_call`
drives a real `WalkContext` over an `f64`-returning callee plus an `Int`
control. Without the decline the float box folds to `Float(3.5e-323)` =
`f64::from_bits(7)` — the argument still sitting in the integer register —
while the `CallPureI` sibling in the same fixture folds to `42`, so the fixture
is not the problem. A standalone probe against `jit_bigint_to_f64_or_inf`
mismatches 7/7 (`std::hint::black_box` is required, or LLVM sees through the
transmute and re-emits a correctly-ABI'd direct call, which is why the
pre-existing `float_result_routes_through_call_int_function_with_bits_packing`
test passed).

**Latent, not live.** Instrumenting the fold for `result_type() == Float` and
sweeping all ~1400 files of `pyre/bench` + `pyre/bench/synth` (check.py's
corpus) found zero occurrences.

## 2. Allow three deny-by-default clippy lints in `majit-ir`

`cargo clippy -p majit-ir` failed to compile on three deny-by-default lints, so
the crate could not be linted at all. Each is a false positive against
deliberate structure and gets a scoped `#[allow]` plus a comment stating why:

- `ineffective_bit_mask` on the eval-breaker flag-width static assertion — every
  operand is a constant, so there is no runtime value to compare.
- `absurd_extreme_comparisons` on `OpCode::is_final` — `FINAL_FIRST` is
  `OpCode::Jump as u16` == 0 today; the bound is kept symbolic to match the
  sibling classifiers and to stay correct if the category stops leading the enum.
- `mut_from_ref` on `SharedConstPool::as_mut_vec_for_gc` — the pool is
  `UnsafeCell`-backed so the GC root walker can mutate through a shared
  reference, and the existing `# Safety` clause carries the contract.

No behavior change; the crate now reports 0 errors and 41 warnings.

## Verification

- `python3 pyre/check.py --backend dynasm,cranelift`: 14 failed / 351 passed per
  backend, **byte-identical failure set to the clean-HEAD control** and to a
  repeat run. All 14 are pre-existing (6 missing jit-stats baselines from #934,
  8 jit-stats regressions incl. the `exception_reraise_tb_depth_jitstress`
  family).
- `cargo test -p pyre-jit-trace -p majit-metainterp --features dynasm`: green.
- `cargo test -p majit-ir`: 307 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p majit-ir --no-deps`: 0 errors.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.



## 3. Record the six missing synthetic jit-stats baselines

`hot_loop_exit_then_class_stmt` (#890) and five fixtures from #934/#948 were
added without a committed `.jitstats`, so check.py failed them on both backends
with "no committed jit-stats baseline". Recorded one fixture at a time with
`--snapshot --synthetic-pattern <name>.py`, so no existing baseline is
rewritten; 350 synth scripts now have 350 dynasm and 350 cranelift baselines.

Two record a weak floor worth revisiting: `pypy_dict_primitives_nonbinding`
compiles no loop at all (`loops_compiled=0`), and `raise_reg_unbound_jitstress`
enters at `loops_aborted=10`.

## CI status — the remaining 8 failures are pre-existing on `main`

`main` at `f3bddb31f28` fails `pyre/check.py` on all three platforms with
**exactly the same 14 fixtures and the same numbers** as this branch did before
commit 3 (compare run 30707884899 against 30713388334). This PR introduces no
check.py regression; the 6 baseline recordings above take it from 14 to **8
failed / 357 passed** per backend.

The 8 that remain are jit-stats floor regressions that entered `main` between
#947 (which recorded the baselines) and the current tip. Measured root split —
one build with an env-gated early `return true` in
`optimizeopt/heap.rs quasiimmut_field_still_valid`, all 8 fixtures re-run both
ways:

| fixture | with #956's backstop | backstop disabled |
|---|---|---|
| `exception_reraise_tb_depth_jitstress` | aborted 0→1198, compiled 805→305 | **passes** |
| the other 7 | as reported | unchanged |

So exactly one is #956's quasi-immutable revalidation. Reverting #956 is not
the fix: PyPy aborts 2100× on this same script (`abort: force quasi-immut`), so
firing here is faithful — what pyre lacks is upstream's *primary* mechanism,
`opimpl_jit_force_quasi_immut` (`pyjitpl.py:1104-1118`), which aborts early at
the write instead of letting every event fall through to the optimizer
backstop. `ABORT_FORCE_QUASIIMMUT` is a dead counter in pyre today
(`pyjitpl.rs:15634`, no site raises it). That port is a separate slice.

The other 7 (`closure_freevar_branch_resume`, `exception_args_virtual`,
`exception_multi_handler_warmup`, `list_length_hint_validate`,
`sre_pattern_methods`, `sre_wasm_min`, `sre_wasm_min1`) have a different,
still-unbisected root in the same window.

— *authored by Claude*

author: mafarrag
body:
# Description

`Bands._set_color_table` attaches a palette to a band but left the band's **colour interpretation** unset — the
`SetColorInterpretation` call was commented out. As a result a raster written through `Dataset.color_table` was
tagged differently from one written through the COG path, which already sets `GCI_PaletteIndex`
(`dataset/engines/cog.py`). GDAL and downstream readers use the interpretation to know the pixel values are
palette indices rather than raw data, so the two write paths produced inconsistently-tagged paletted rasters.

This sets `band.SetColorInterpretation(gdal.GCI_PaletteIndex)` after the palette is attached, matching the COG
writer. `gdal` is already imported at the top of the module; no new dependency.

This is the "bonus" cleanup identified in #782. The other item flagged there — removing a stale `TODO` — is a
no-op on `main`: that `TODO` only exists on the unmerged `docs/improve-netcdf-docs` branch, and `main`'s
`bands.py` already has no such comment. The genuinely open parts of #782 (reconciling `color_table` with the
raster attribute table, and adding a colour-ramp → colour-table path) are out of scope here and stay tracked in
the issue.

# Issues

- Refs #782 — implements the palette-interpretation consistency fix (the "bonus" item); does not close it.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

The change adds a tag that was intended but disabled; it does not alter the palette itself or any public
signature.

# How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] New `test_set_color_table_tags_palette_interpretation` — asserts a band's interpretation flips from
      `Undefined` to `Palette` when a colour table is assigned.
- [x] `pytest tests/dataset/plot/test_plot_color.py tests/dataset/unit/test_unit_properties.py
      tests/dataset/cog/test_unified_write_policy.py tests/dataset/create/test_dataset_create.py` against the
      branch → **194 passed**. Includes the existing `test_dataset_create.py` assertion that a freshly-created
      band stays `Undefined` (unaffected — only colour-table assignment now tags the band).

# Checklist:

- [ ] updated version number in pyproject.toml.
- [ ] added changes to History.rst.
- [ ] updated the latest version in README file.
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes.
- [ ] documentation are updated.

author: hallovorld
body:
# PREREG (FREEZE CANDIDATE) — standalone residual-momentum: one run, one verdict

**Frozen on merge of this PR. No IC, no score, no label statistic may be computed for
this study before that merge.** The design was reviewed to approval as model#161; the
inference method's construction protocol as model#162. This document resolves every
constant both left open, and nothing else — where it and #161 disagree, THIS document
governs.

## 0. Known-trap checklist (each names a measured failure this design must not repeat)

| trap | guard here |
|---|---|
| overlapping-label naive t (killed model#124/#128/#135) | worst-case calibrated bar, §4; no N/h anywhere |
| permutation null's wrong width (model#153: real ρ₁ 0.82–0.975, permuted ≈0) | permutation is centring-only, never width |
| Bartlett L=h−1 oversized (probe + independent audit: size 0.117 @ nominal .05) | L = 59 AND empirically calibrated bar, §4 |
| "both bars published" as pseudo-control (codex on #162) | precommitted worst-case rule, §4.3 |
| running before freezing (Stage-0's own reverted violation) | §7 execution gate |
| same-name-different-object labels | §2 pins the label constructor quote and file digests at run time |

## 1. Candidate (all constants FROZEN here)

Residual momentum, exactly as approved in #161 §2: rolling OLS of daily dividend-adjusted
TR returns on SPY-TR over `t−273…t−21` (window **252**, skip **21**, min obs **200**);
score = `Σε/(σ_ε·√N)`; per-date cross-sectional z. Feature family F1–F5 as approved
(§2b), composite `S` = equal-weight z-mean over available features, **≥3 of 5** required,
ETFs carry no F3.

**The 43 no-dividend-column names (frozen verbatim in §2) are VERIFIED non-payers
`[本次实测 2026-08-01]`:** the vendor's dividend endpoint returns **zero dividend events
since 2016-01-01 for 43/43, 0 query failures**. Same-vendor caveat, stated: this is the
same vendor (yfinance) whose per-file `dividend` column the OHLCV store carries — no
independent vendor exists locally (the TR study measured `adj close` 100% NaN for every
watchlist name carrying it), so a vendor-wide omission would evade this check.
The verification is persisted as a versioned audit artifact —
`doc/research/data/2026-08-01-goal7-nonpayer-verification/vendor_dividend_check.json`
(query date 2026-08-01, range 2016-01-01..query date, per-ticker event counts and
failure statuses), sha256 `268f21f1bee9b27335de63ca7ca7f458c492573b2907dd58bdf759e89b61ad87` — so the 43/43 claim is
reproducible data, not prose. **Precommitted handling, closed:** any evidence of payment
for any of these names surfacing before execution → the run is **UNRESOLVED-DATA**.
There is no amendment path and no exclusion path: the study population cannot change
after this freeze. No directional-bias argument is made (in a cross-sectional rank
statistic the direction of such an error is not identifiable, per review). The sector map is
`data/ticker_sectors.json`, snapshot `as_of 2026-05-18`; its sha256 is recorded by the
runner at execution and the snapshot-PIT limitation is inherited as stated in #161.

## 2. Data — pinned by digest NOW `[本次实测 2026-08-01]`

| input | sha256 |
|---|---|
| `data/alpha158_291_fundamental_dataset.parquet` (2,599 dates, 292 names) | `55811f6387e67411fe11a20eb1d5d929086c5a9dc2675496f3d8592fed2c0dba` |
| `data/ticker_sectors.json` (as_of 2026-05-18) | `ec26bb1efcf8463519366478ae72c933f93c9d110d65f8af1634e2fcbb578d3b` |
| OHLCV combined (sha256 over sorted `ticker:file-sha` lines, **292/292** present) | `4d4638a9f0d69f940fb36a73c28e92883d51b686ab032aebedf559c174c2c1d0` |

Labels are per-date z-scored price-return excess vs SPY (constructor quoted in #161's
AC4 comment; Spearman invariant to the z-scoring; the in-label dividend omission is a
recorded limitation biasing against payers). Eligible dates: formation-feasible only
(measured ≈2,150); names/date floor **50**; the runner records every exclusion count.

**The 43 no-dividend-column names, frozen verbatim:** ABNB, ADBE, AFRM, AMD, AMZN, ANET,
APP, BSX, CMG, COHR, COIN, CRWD, DDOG, DOCU, ESTC, EW, FTNT, GLD, HUBS, ISRG, LITE, MDB,
NET, NFLX, NOW, OKTA, ON, PANW, PCTY, PLTR, RBLX, SHOP, SMCI, SNOW, SOFI, SPOT, TEAM,
TSLA, VEEV, VRTX, WDAY, ZM, ZS.

**UNRESOLVED-DATA rule:** at execution the runner recomputes all three digests and the
43-name list. ANY mismatch → the run completes nothing and reports **UNRESOLVED-DATA**
with the differing digests; proceeding on changed inputs is not an option this document
grants.

## 3. Estimands

* **E1 (decision):** mean per-date Spearman IC of `S` vs `fwd_20d_excess`, all eligible
  dates. h=20 declared from theory in #161; h=60 descriptive only.
* **E2 (parsimony):** paired per-date `ΔIC = IC(S) − IC(F1)`.
* Per-feature ICs: Bonferroni α/5 diagnostics, never decision inputs.

## 4. Inference — the #162 protocol, instantiated and closed

1. **Statistic pipeline `T`:** HAC-t (Bartlett, **L = 59**) on the per-date series, via
   `renquant_common.metrics.hac_se.hac_t_stat(lag=59)` (measured equal to the frozen
   SE_HAC formula; model#159), **pinned to the implementation that will execute**: the
   PINNED runtime copy `.subrepo_runtime/repos/renquant-common/src/renquant_common/metrics/hac_se.py`,
   sha256 `c568ed51428b642c936eda865779b57e0282814f170bb1528e86be2ba9f9b8bc`. The runner
   verifies this digest BEFORE computing anything; mismatch → **UNRESOLVED-DATA** — a
   shared-library change after this merge cannot silently alter the frozen statistic.
2. **Admissible generator family (the frozen DGP argument):** the momentum IC series'
   dependence has two named sources — label overlap (MA(19) **by construction** of a
   20-day forward label) and signal persistence (a 252-day formation window advancing
   one day at a time, an AR-type component). The family is therefore
   `{overlap-MA(19) variance-matched, AR(p) fitted per #162 §2 with p ≤ 20}` — both
   sources represented, neither assumed away. This argument is the one #162 requires a
   consumer to freeze; it is hereby frozen.
3. **Bar (precommitted worst-case, closing the stress path):**
   `t* = max(t*_MA, t*_AR)` at **α = 0.025 two-sided per test** (the §6 Bonferroni split
   of a 0.05 family across the two decision tests), each `t*` the seeded **97.5th
   percentile** of |T| under its generator (**5,000 reps exactly**, seed **20260801**,
   n = the realized eligible-date count). AR adequacy envelope: max abs ACF deviation over lags
   1…40 ≤ 2 plug-in SEs. **If the AR fit fails adequacy, the outcome is
   UNRESOLVED-METHOD** — per #162's governing rule, a family whose persistence member
   cannot be justified does not get to proceed on the overlap member alone; dropping a
   named dependence source is not a fallback, it is an unjustified null.
4. **Validation gates (all must pass before any verdict is read), with frozen
   arithmetic:** each gate runs **5,000 reps** at seed **20260801**; Monte-Carlo
   SE = √(0.025·0.975/5000) ≈ 0.0022; the frozen tolerance is **±3·SE = ±0.0066**.
   * positive control: the committed pure-noise series' rejection rate under the full
     protocol must lie within **[0.0184, 0.0316]**;
   * machinery self-check (#162 §4): series simulated from each admissible generator,
     pushed through the identical pipeline, must reject within the same band;
   * both `t*` values and the realized ACF are published regardless of outcome.
5. **Decision:**
   * `H1`: mean IC(S) ≥ **+0.04** AND `|T|` ≥ t\* AND placebo mean |IC| < **0.01**
     (5 within-date permutation draws, centring only) → RETAIN-to-shadow; else KILL.
   * `H2` (only if H1 passes): if `ΔIC`'s HAC-t < t\* (family adds nothing) AND F1
     independently satisfies the full H1 criterion → deploy F1; else deploy S.
   * `UNRESOLVED-METHOD` if any validation gate fails; `UNRESOLVED-POWER` if the
     realized `MDE = t*·SE_HAC` exceeds **0.06** (a bar that cannot be met by a
     plausible effect must be said, not run through).
6. KILL and UNRESOLVED are reportable outcomes with the s

author: claudianus
body: ## Related Issue N/A — follow-up freeze class after prior scroll harden PRs. ## Problem Fast transcript wheel scroll still froze the TUI when cold history cards entered the viewport: geometry measure and pure-scroll paint ran full highlight/pretty-print, and large tool/shell bodies formatted synchronously on the main thread. ## What changed - Geometry measure and pure-scroll **cheap-paint** skip cold highlight/pretty-print without poisoning full-quality paint caches. - **Dual-slot cheap/full caches** on Markdown and width/children render caches so pure-scroll amortizes after the first cold frame. - Large tool/shell bodies: plain content first, budgeted deferred format queue, bounded Write/Edit highlight and diff LCS. - Tests for measure isolation, deferred format, multi-k Markdown amortize, and related freeze classes. ## Checklist - [x] I have reviewed the repository contribution notes. - [x] I have linked a related issue, or explained the problem above. - [x] I have added tests that prove my feature works. - [x] Ran `gen-changesets` skill, or this PR needs no changeset. - [x] Ran `gen-docs` skill, or this PR needs no doc update. --- ## Summary by cubic Stops TUI freezes on fast transcript scroll by skipping cold highlight/pretty-print during geometry and pure-scroll, and deferring large tool/shell formatting off the main thread. Scrolling is smooth; expanded content still formats and highlights shortly after. - **Bug Fixes** - Added pure-scroll cheap-paint mode to skip expensive formatting on cache miss without polluting paint caches. - Introduced dual-slot caches (cheap vs full) for Markdown and render caches to amortize multi‑k bodies after the first cold frame. - Deferred formatting for large tool outputs and shell runs via a budgeted queue; plain text paints immediately with a small “formatting” hint. - Soft‑capped diff LCS input and windowed code highlighting to keep large Edit/Write previews responsive. - Viewport caches now bust on content revision so plain→pretty transitions re-render correctly. - Added tests for measure isolation, cheap-paint behavior, deferred queue, truncated output defer, and cache separation. Written for commit 1ad9af27aef6d9963eddfe3f913a9ea05db86cd5. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance** * Improved transcript responsiveness during fast scrolling and layout measurement. * Large tool and shell outputs now appear immediately in plain text while enhanced formatting loads in the background. * Added safeguards to keep large diffs, code highlights, and Write/Edit previews within practical limits. * **Bug Fixes** * Prevented stale deferred formatting from overwriting newer or disposed views. * Ensured completed background formatting refreshes the transcript correctly. * Added a patch release for `@superliora/liora`.

author: alkiswani-web
body:
جميع المتاجر في «رصيد روزميري ← المتاجر» كانت تعرض **مسحوب = 0** رغم وجود مسحوبات مسجّلة. السبب سببان مستقلان، وكلاهما مُصلَح هنا لأن أياً منهما وحده كافٍ لإخفاء المسحوبات.

## 1) الجلب مقيّد بـ `sessionId` وحده

`_opWithdrawals` كانت تُجلب هكذا:

```js
db.collection('operator_withdrawals').where('sessionId','==',_opCurrentSession.id)
```

بينما كل البيانات الأخرى في نفس الدالة (`operator_sales`، `operator_expenses`) تُجلب **بالمدى الزمني للجلسة** ثم تُفلتر بتسامح:

```js
.filter(s=>!s.sessionId||s.sessionId===_opCurrentSession.id)
```

النتيجة: أي مسحوب سُجّل ضمن جلسة سابقة يختفي كلياً بينما تبقى المبيعات ظاهرة — أي «قابل للسحب» بقيمته و«مسحوب» صفر.

**الحل:** دالة `_loadOpWithdrawals()` واحدة تُرجع اتحاد:
- سجلات الجلسة الحالية (`sessionId == sid`)، و
- سجلات المدى الزمني للجلسة مع التسامح مع ما لا يحمل `sessionId`.

وتُستدعى من مواضع الجلب الأربعة بدل تكرار الاستعلام في كل مرة (`_loadOpSessionData` وبعد حفظ مسحوب/دفعة متجر/دفعة مجموعة).

## 2) المطابقة بالاسم الحرفي

```js
_opWithdrawals.filter(w=>w.storeName===store.name)
```

اسم كرت المتجر مصدره **الطلب** (`o.pageName||o.storeName||o.source`)، بينما `storeName` في المسحوب مصدره **سجل المتجر** من القائمة المنسدلة. اختلاف مسافة مزدوجة أو مسافة طرفية أو حالة أحرف يكسر المطابقة.

**الحل:** `_wdForStore(w, storeName, storeId)` تطابق بالمعرّف إن توفّر في الطرفين، وإلا بالاسم بعد التطبيع (توحيد المسافات + قصّ الأطراف + حالة أحرف موحّدة). طُبِّقت على كرت المتجر وكرت المجموعة.

## ما لم يُمَس عمداً
استعلام **حذف** المسحوبات عند تصفير الجلسة بقي مقيّداً بـ `sessionId` وحده — توسيعه للمدى الزمني كان سيحذف سجلات خارج نطاق التصفير.

## التحقق
- `node --check app.js` ✅
- اختبار وحدة لـ `_wdForStore` على 6 حالات (تطابق معرّف، اسم بمسافات زائدة، معرّف يطابق واسم مختلف، اسم يطابق ومعرّف مختلف، لا تطابق، اختلاف حالة أحرف) — كلها نجحت.
- تحميل التطبيق في Chromium والتأكد من عدم وجود انحدار في عرض قسم الطلبات.
- رفع النسخة إلى `v179`.

> ملاحظة: هذه الثغرة سابقة لإعادة تصميم قسم الطلبات (#280/#281) ولا علاقة لها بها — مصدرها منطق الجلسات في لوحة الحسابات.

author: jbailes
body:
Retires the last of the `aimee-llm` container, gives `aimee-kb` a 2x2 image
matrix, and makes the embedder and synthesis settings one surface instead of two.

## What changes

**One name per setting.** The embedder and synthesis settings had two parallel
surfaces — config keys and environment variables — because only 4 rows in
`config_fields[]` declared an env var and the embedder/synthesis rows declared
none. They were read by ad-hoc `getenv()` and hand-plumbed through compose. They
are now ordinary table-declared fields: `EMBEDDER_URL` / `EMBEDDER_DIMS` /
`EMBEDDER_MODEL` / `EMBEDDER_API_KEY` and `SYNTHESIS_ENDPOINT` /
`SYNTHESIS_MODEL` / `SYNTHESIS_API_KEY` / `SYNTHESIS_THINKING`. The config *file*
uses these names too — it was still writing `embedding_*` while the fields behind
them had moved, so the file and the key could diverge.

**One synthesis role.** Tier-A/Tier-B is gone. Every curator stage resolves the
same provider. The split also made the reasoning stages *refuse* the env
endpoint, so a bundled-model deployment ran extraction and left synthesis idle.
Thinking becomes a global, user-settable `synthesis_thinking` (default on)
instead of a rule implied by the stage.

**Four aimee-kb images**, one Dockerfile, selected by build-args:

|                  | no llama.cpp     | llama.cpp bundled    |
| ---------------- | ---------------- | -------------------- |
| bekko-a25m (384) | `aimee-kb`       | `aimee-kb-llm`       |
| nomic-v2 (768)   | `aimee-kb-nomic` | `aimee-kb-nomic-llm` |

**Bundled synthesis runs beside the kb**, with the weights baked into the `*-llm`
images at UD-Q6_K_XL (7.46 GB E4B, 4.71 GB E2B) and built once via a separate
`aimee-model-*` image rather than once per variant per arch. The container
downloads nothing at runtime: a first-start fetch fails on a rate limit, a proxy,
a flaky link or an air-gapped host, and every one of those reaches the operator as
"synthesis never started" long after the deploy looked fine. `--no-mmproj` plus
`LLAMA_ARG_MMPROJ_AUTO=false`: every benchmark passed `--no-mmproj` and the
shipped service never did, so production loaded a ~0.5 GB vision projector for a
text-only task.

**The wizard** asks the two questions that remain, and states the embedder
one-way door at the point of choice.

## CI

`publish-images.yml` now runs on `pull_request` — **build only, push nothing**.
Publishing stays a merge-time act, enforced in four places because any one left
alone would still push or fail: `push=` on the build output, the ghcr login, the
digest export/upload, and the merge job that tags the manifest. A merge rebuilds
from cache and pushes then.

## Bugs found on the way

Each of these was silent — no error, just a setting that stopped working:

- `deploy_apply.c` compared env prefixes with hand-counted lengths (`21`, `24`).
  `21` was right for `AIMEE_LLM_AUTH_TOKEN=` and wrong for `SYNTHESIS_API_KEY=`
  (18), so the managed-credential filter leaked a second copy of the key into the
  child environment. Now `sizeof-1`.
- `readiness.ts` computed "is an embedder configured" from a deleted field, so
  the wizard's embedder step could never complete.
- `RESTART_KEYS` listed nine retired keys, so the restart notice could never fire.
- `KB_SETTINGS` named renamed keys, and `console_settings()` *skips* rows it
  can't resolve — those settings would have vanished from the KB console.
- `config_save.c` wrote YAML keys that `config.c` no longer parsed.
- `EMBEDDER_API_KEY` was emitted by the deploy layer and received by no container.

## Not verified

**All six images now build in CI** on amd64 and arm64, which resolves the earlier
"no image has been built" caveat and confirms the `unsloth/gemma-4-E{2,4}B-it-GGUF`
repo names against the Hub — the build fetches from them.

**No container has been run.** Building is not booting: nothing in
`.github/workflows/` invokes `scripts/aimee-kb-docker-smoke.sh`, so the
llama-server invocation, the loopback handover and `start_synthesis`'s branch
logic are still unexercised by CI. The smoke script does cover them
(`scripts/aimee-kb-docker-smoke.sh:234-270`) and is being run by hand against
`aimee-kb-llm-e4b` on the disposable test box before this reaches any real
deployment. Wiring it into CI is follow-up work, not part of this PR.

`LLAMACPP_SHA256` is present but empty, so the build warns rather than verifying
the release asset.

Both are written down in `docs/SYNTHESIS_MODELS.md` rather than left implicit.

## Upgrade impact

**Hard cut, no aliases**, per an explicit decision. A deployment that upgrades
without editing its environment and `aimee.yaml` keeps running, falls back to the
builtin lexical embedder and idles synthesis, without erroring.
`docs/UPGRADING.md` has the full old→new table and what to check afterwards.

## Verification

`make lint` (40 checks) · `make all` · 28 C tests touching this surface ·
`tsc -b` + 155 frontend tests · docs-gen-check, check-kb-container-packaging,
check-sidecar-clients, check-deploy-env-consumed, check-curator-story,
check-config-encapsulation, check-proposal-links.

author: jasongross
body:
Adds 13 `extra-dev` recipes for packages whose newest archive release is capped below Rocq 9.0 but whose upstream metadata already claims Rocq 9.x, `dev`, or no upper bound. Companion to #3811, which covers packages whose upstream has not been ported.

| package | newest release | archive cap | upstream's own constraint | last upstream commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| coq-stalmarck | 8.20.0 | `< 8.21` | `coq {= "dev"}` | 2026-05-22 |
| coq-stalmarck-tactic | 8.20.0 | `< 8.21` | `coq {= "dev"}` | 2026-05-22 |
| coq-waterproof \* | 2.0.1+8.17 | `< 8.18` | `rocq-core {>= 9.1 & < 9.2 \| = dev}` | 2026-06-15 |
| coq-mathcomp-abel | 1.2.1 | `< 8.17~` | `rocq-core {>= "9.0"}` | 2026-07-21 |
| coq-hanoi | 1.0.0 | `< 8.16~` | `coq {>= "9.1"}` | 2026-01-29 |
| coq-cds4ltl | 1.0.0 | `< 8.17~` | `rocq-core {>= 9.1 & < 9.2~}` | 2026-05-04 |
| coq-mmaps | 1.1 | `< 8.21` | `coq {>= "8.16"}`, unbounded | 2026-06-22 |
| coq-mathcomp-apery | 1.0.2 | `< 8.19~` | `coq {>= "8.20"}`, unbounded | 2026-04-25 |
| coq-bits | 1.1.0 | `< 8.17~` | `coq {>= "8.16"}`, unbounded | 2026-03-03 |
| coq-coqtail | 8.20 | `< 8.21` | `coq {>= "8.17"}`, unbounded | 2026-04-13 |
| coq-comp-dec-modal | 1.2 | `< 8.21` | `coq {>= "8.16"}`, unbounded | 2024-08-11 |
| coq-sum-of-two-square | 8.10.0 | `< 8.11~` | `coq`, unbounded | 2026-01-30 |
| coq-exact-real-arithmetic | 8.10.0 | `< 8.11~` | (no opam file upstream) | 2026-02-05 |

\* `coq-waterproof` follows upstream's `coq-master` dev-tracking branch; every other row follows its repository's default branch.

## Recipes

Each recipe uses upstream's in-tree `.opam` file, drops `version:`, replaces the source with `url { src: "git+<repo>#<branch>" }`, and removes Coq/Rocq upper bounds because opam orders `dev` above every numeric version.

There are three other departures:

- `coq-waterproof` keeps only `coq {= "dev"}` of the three prover packages named upstream. `coq.dev` already brings `coq-core {= version}`, `rocq-runtime {= version}`, `coq-stdlib`, and `rocq-stdlib {= version}` at `dev`.
- `coq-sum-of-two-square` corrects `homepage`, `dev-repo`, and `bug-reports`, which point to a nonexistent `thery/SumOfTwoSquare` repository upstream.
- `coq-exact-real-arithmetic` has no upstream opam file, so its recipe starts from the newest release and swaps the tarball for git. It drops the obsolete `remove:` field and `light-uninstall` flag.

On waterproof's former `main` branch, this was necessary rather than cosmetic: `rocq-prover.9.3.dev` pins `rocq-core` to `9.3.dev`, which cannot coexist with the `rocq-runtime.dev` selected by `coq.dev`. The branch declares `version: "3.1.1+9.0-dev"`; `coq-master` declares `version: "3.1.1+dev"` and avoids `rocq-prover`. Tracking a dedicated prover branch is established practice: 71 of 304 `extra-dev/packages` `url { src: }` fragments use something other than `master` or `main`.

All rows now constrain the prover to `{= "dev"}`. The initial loose lower bounds let `opam-build:4.09.0`, which constrains `ocaml-base-compiler < 4.11.0`, resolve ported sources against old provers because `rocq-runtime` has required `ocaml >= 4.14.0` since 9.1+rc1. Pipeline 1455718, job 7695087 showed the result:

| resolved prover | rows | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `coq.8.16.dev` | coq-comp-dec-modal, coq-mmaps | installed — **green, and meaningless** |
| `coq.8.20.dev` | coq-coqtail | installed — **green** |
| `coq.9.0.dev` (via `rocq-core.9.0.dev`) | coq-waterproof | installed — **green** |
| `coq.8.16.dev` | coq-bits, coq-exact-real-arithmetic, coq-sum-of-two-square | failed — **red, and equally meaningless** |
| — | the remaining 6 | `Package conflict!`, correctly skipped |

The failures were also old-prover artifacts. `coq-exact-real-arithmetic` and `coq-sum-of-two-square` use `From Stdlib Require`, producing `Cannot find a physical path bound to logical path ZArith with prefix Stdlib` on 8.x. `coq-bits` mixed `coq.8.16.dev` and `coq-mathcomp-algebra.2.2.0` with `coq-mathcomp-zify.dev`, then failed with `make: rocq: No such file or directory`.

The recipes therefore pin all 11 rows that did not already do so to the dev prover. They also pin the otherwise-unconstrained mathcomp dependencies of `coq-mathcomp-abel`, `coq-mathcomp-apery`, and `coq-bits` to `dev`. `coq-cds4ltl` (`rocq-core {>= "9.1"}`) and `coq-hanoi` (`coq {>= "9.1"}`) were already skipped on OCaml 4.09 because Rocq 9.1 requires OCaml 4.14; tightening those two is hygiene, while tightening the other nine fixes the bad resolutions.

## CI

Pipeline 1458297 tested PR head `0d8d6f9dc` merged with master. All three legs terminated. `opam-build:4.09.0` skips all 13 rows as not installable; zero are built, and its `succeeded`, `failed`, and `can never be installed` ledgers are empty. This is the intended resolution result, but it exercises none of the new recipes.

The 4.14.2 and 5.3.0 legs agreed: 13 attempted, 0 skipped, 8 installed, and 5 failed, with the same first error on both legs. Every installed row compiled files, ranging from 25 for `coq-cds4ltl` to 112 for `coq-mathcomp-apery`. The three pinned mathcomp rows had the same plans before and after tightening, so the change affects only 4.09.0.

| row | verdict | first error |
|---|---|---|
| coq-bits | installed | |
| coq-cds4ltl | installed | |
| coq-exact-real-arithmetic | installed | |
| coq-mathcomp-abel | installed | |
| coq-mathcomp-apery | installed | |
| coq-mmaps | installed | |
| coq-stalmarck | installed | |
| coq-sum-of-two-square | installed | |
| coq-stalmarck-tactic | failed | `dune-project:2 Error: Extension coq was deleted in the 3.24 version of the dune language` — `(using coq 0.3)` |
| coq-waterproof | failed | same error, `(using coq 0.8)` |
| coq-comp-dec-modal | failed | `edone.v:10 Unable to locate library mathcomp.ssreflect.ssreflect` |
| coq-coqtail | failed | `Complex/Canalysis_def.v:46 Error: The '%' scope delimiter in 'Arguments' commands is deprecated, use '%_' instead` |
| coq-hanoi | failed | `extra.v:225 Error: The LHS of subn_eq0 (_ - _ == 0) does not match any subterm of the goal` |

#3819 capped `dune < 3.24` for the 16 released elpi versions using the deleted extension and fixed the earlier `rocq-elpi.3.4.0` failure `Extension coq was deleted in the 3.24 version of the dune language`; both dev legs now resolve every elpi row to `dev`. The two remaining dune failures occur in `coq-stalmarck-tactic` and `coq-waterproof`, the only rows here that depend on dune. Their trees specify `(lang dune 2.8)` / `(using coq 0.3)` and `(lang dune 3.8)` / `(using coq 0.8)`, respectively, so their recipes add the same ceiling used by #3819:

```
-  "dune" {>= "2.8"}
+  "dune" {>= "2.8" & < "3.24"}
```

The waterproof constraint is likewise `{>= "3.8" & < "3.24"}`. This remains compatible with `rocq-runtime.dev` and `rocq-core.dev`, which require `dune {>= "3.21"}`. Both files pass `opam lint --warn=-21`. The ceiling is a stopgap until the projects move to `(using rocq …)`.

`coq-waterproof` also moves from `#main`, upstream's released line, to its development-prover branch:

```
-  src: "git+https://github.com/impermeable/coq-waterproof.git#main"
+  src: "git+https://github.com/impermeable/coq-waterproof.git#coq-master"
```

`coq-master` contains the adaptations for `rocq-prover/rocq#21987` and `rocq-prover/rocq#22114`; `main` trails it by 90 commits across 117 files, including 12 under `src/`. The 10 commits present only on `main` are a `3.1.1+...-dev` version bump, two coq-lsp documentation updates, and a notation tweak.

### Dune cap and waterproof branch results

The dune-cap-only commit 072925e2d ran in pipeline 1459862. `opam-build:4.14.2` (job 7723631) and `opam-build:5.3.0` (job 7723632) produced byte-identical ledgers: `coq-stalmarck-tactic.dev` installed, while `coq-waterproof.dev` failed. The capped packages' own solves selected:

```
- install dune 3.23.1 [required by coq-stalmarck-tactic]
- install dune 3.23.1 [required by coq-waterproof]
```

Those attributions occur at log lines 364

author: fania17hernan
body:
…ield capped at 6)

Sign-in was completely broken: the code email carries 8 digits on this project, but the input had maxLength 6 and the submit gate required exactly 6, so the real code was truncated and every attempt returned 'wrong or expired'.

OTP length is a Supabase PROJECT SETTING, not something the client controls, and it can change without a deploy. So instead of hard-coding 8, accept a range (OTP_MIN_LEN 6 .. OTP_MAX_LEN 10) and let the server be the authority. Copy no longer promises '6-digit'.

Verified: esbuild parse clean; OTP unit tests 7/7 incl. the 8-digit regression.

author: barefootbetters
body:
Implements **WP-483 / EC-518** — the cards half [WP-474](docs/ai/work-packets/WP-474-per-scheme-approved-loadout-consumers.md) split off, **completing the per-scheme gauntlet variety arc**. Consumes **D-24283** (no new decision).

## Why the split existed
WP-474 shipped legends-board only because WP-471's `getGauntletConfig` was **Node-only** (`readFileSync` at module load, reachable only via the registry root barrel) and broke `apps/registry-viewer`'s Vite browser build.

## What
**Browser-safe export:**
- `scripts/generate-gauntlet-configs.mjs` (new) bakes `data/gauntlet-configs.json` into `packages/registry/src/gauntletConfigs.generated.ts`; root `gauntlet:configs` / `gauntlet:configs:check` scripts (mirroring `gauntlet:loadouts`).
- `gauntletConfigs.ts` imports the literal and validates it at load — **drops `node:fs` / `node:path` / `node:url`**. `getGauntletConfig` / `getActiveYear` / `validateGauntletConfigs` signatures + `undefined`→menu-fallback preserved verbatim.
- new `@legendary-arena/registry/gauntletConfigs` subpath (transitive imports: `zod` + `./playerCountSetup` + the literal — no Node built-ins). Server barrel import unchanged.

**Cards consumers:**
- `gauntletQualificationCheck`: load-bearing `schemeId` + injected `approvedComposition`; per-scheme branch → `qualifies` with `variantIndex: 0`, else the menu path.
- `loadoutGauntletPackImport`: `resolveGauntletLegLoadout` prefills the leg's own adversaries from the injected composition (menu fallback for an absent leg).
- `LoadoutBuilder.vue`: `resolveLegConfig` resolves the leg config via the browser-safe `getGauntletConfig` and injects it into the badge + prefill call sites.

## Verification
- registry **202/0** (+1 in-test freshness deep-equal — the enforcing CI drift gate); registry-viewer **203/0** (+6 per-scheme); `vue-tsc` typecheck clean; `pnpm -r build` green (the browser bundle builds with the new subpath — AC#1); `gauntlet:configs:check` verified (exit 1 on a hand-edit, 0 restored — AC#2).

`User-Visible Surface = cards.legendary-arena.com` — **D-24026 live-verify operator-pending** (a Dr. Doom "Secret Invasion…" pack prefills Skrulls and the badge qualifies against the leg; a non-swapped scheme → Brotherhood).

**Arc complete:** WP-471 → WP-472 → WP-473 → WP-474 → WP-475 → WP-483.

author: technickai
body:
Fork PR — runs the bots before we take this upstream to `diegosouzapw/OmniRoute`.

## The bug

`STREAM_EARLY_EOF` means the upstream returned **HTTP 200**, opened the SSE stream, then closed it without emitting a single non-ping event. The combo path lumped it in with `STREAM_READINESS_TIMEOUT` via `isStreamReadinessFailureErrorBody()`, and the readiness exemption in `shouldRecordProviderBreakerFailure` meant the whole-provider circuit breaker never counted it.

During the Anthropic outage on 2026-07-29 (19:45–21:26 UTC, published as "Elevated errors across all models") that made the breaker blind:

- 311 early-EOF events over 7 days, **302 on `claude-opus-5`**
- **265 of that day's 502s fell inside the published outage window**
- provider breaker `claude`: **CLOSED, failure_count=0 the entire time**
- 189 failures in the burst hour; requests kept being dispatched to the failing provider instead of shedding to the free codex rung
- downstream cost: Hermes clients gave up on the router entirely and fell through to their own metered fallback

## Why the two codes are different

The readiness probe is a **pre-flight** liveness check on a connection we have not committed to yet — failing it means "this connection looks stale", not "this provider is down". An early EOF is the opposite: the provider **took the request and then failed to serve it**.

The single-model path already agrees: `shouldTripProviderBreakerForResult` (chatPredicates.ts) has no readiness exemption at all, so a 502 early EOF trips the breaker there. This makes the combo path consistent with it.

## Approach

`isStreamReadinessFailureErrorBody` **keeps matching both codes** — the transient-retry path and the round-robin semaphore-cooldown path genuinely do want identical treatment for both. Only the breaker needs to tell them apart.

So the distinction is added as a narrow predicate (`isStreamEarlyEofErrorBody`) plus an optional arg, rather than by editing the shared classifier. **Omitting the new arg reproduces previous behaviour exactly.** This follows the additive-override pattern already established by `isProxyUnreachable`.

Deliberately unchanged: client-abort and plain-429 exclusions, and the `sameProviderNext` deferral.

## Verification

- Bug demonstrated against **unmodified** `release/v3.8.50` before writing the fix
- 11 new tests, all passing — including a regression test asserting the old call shape still yields the old result, and 5 tests proving the override is additive (client abort, `skipProviderBreaker`, `requestScopedFailure`, `sameProviderNext`, and 429 each still veto the trip)
- 34/34 existing breaker tests still green (`8376-econnrefused`, `7907` abort trip, `combo-breaker-429`, `2743` consumer, client-abort)
- `npm run typecheck:core` clean, prettier clean, eslint clean

## Next

Deploy to our production router, verify for 24h against live traffic, then open upstream.

body:
## Quoi

Quatre chantiers du module « Deux solitudes », approuvés un à un en preview par Adrien (2026-08-01) :

1. **Module resserré en desktop** (closes #372, closes #374, closes #266 : l'axe fleur/érable compacté règle l'optimisation d'espace demandée, jugée concluante par Adrien) : radar 760px max (au lieu de 1000), score 88px, titre 44px (retour d'Adrien après essai à 38), axe fleur/érable compacté (106→84px, marges 22/20→12/8px). Hauteur du module : ~1450px → **1120px** à 1440px de large. Le bloc ≤768px fige ses propres valeurs : mobile inchangé (vérifié à 375px).
2. **Légende améliorée au survol** (closes #308) : survoler la zone bleue ou rouge du radar fait suivre au curseur le symbole de sa région (fleur de lys = Québec, feuille d'érable = Canada). La légende s'explique là où le regard se pose. Sans effet au tactile ; le glyphe s'efface au profit de l'infobulle des points.
3. **Score relatif en hero** (vers #258 — on ne la ferme PAS : proposition à faire approuver par Yannick, c'est le prototype demandé) : le grand chiffre devient l'écart entre la convergence du moment et l'habituel (médiane annuelle de la calibration glissante, repli 31), libellé « plus convergent/divergent que d'habitude ». L'intensité (« un peu » / « nettement », bandes p20–p80, repli 16/42) vit dans la bulle ⓘ avec les niveaux réels. Le score absolu recule d'un rang : bulle stylée au survol du marqueur de la jauge. Les flèches de l'axe redeviennent directionnelles et animées (vers le centre = plus convergent que d'habitude, vers l'extérieur = plus divergent, immobiles à écart nul et sous `prefers-reduced-motion`).

4. **Note méthodo sur le chevauchement visuel** (closes #363) : ajout à « Limites et honnêteté » (le recouvrement des formes dépend de la position des sujets autour du cadran, pas du score) et correction de la phrase d'« Affichage » qui affirmait le contraire.

4 tests `relScore` ajoutés (212 au total, tous verts).

## Note de journal

Le module Deux solitudes se fait plus compact et plus parlant : son grand chiffre indique désormais si l'actualité québécoise et canadienne se rejoint plus ou moins que d'habitude, et survoler les zones du radar affiche le symbole de la région concernée.

author: agent-farnsworth[bot]
body:
## Summary

A repo-creating test harness rewrote a live agent worktree, producing a tree-deleting commit titled `initial` on branch `fix/2631-multi-channel` and authoring it as `agent-farnsworth`. This adds a sandbox-root guard to every repo-creating harness in the CLI test assembly and the receipt test harness, strips the ambient git variables that caused the retarget, and moves both harnesses onto a non-conflicting sentinel identity.

Refs #2632

## Root cause

The issue body's stated mechanism — a harness resolving its working directory to the caller's worktree — **does not reproduce**. Both harnesses already root their sandbox at `Path.GetTempPath()`.

The real mechanism is ambient environment inheritance. When these suites run under `scripts/repo/githooks/pre-commit`, git exports `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` pointing at the **caller's live worktree**. `UpdateNoOpRebuildSkipTests.RunGit` located its repository *only* via `ProcessStartInfo.WorkingDirectory` and passed no `-C`. Git prefers the environment over the working directory, so every `add -A` / `commit` in that harness was silently redirected at the developer's branch — while the harness itself believed it was operating on its temp sandbox.

That also explains the identity theft the issue flagged as its sharper half: the same hook environment exports `GIT_AUTHOR_*` / `GIT_COMMITTER_*`, so the fixture commit was authored under the real bot identity rather than any placeholder.

## Changes

- **`GitSandboxGuard`** (new) — one definition of the invariant, shared by both harnesses. `AssertSandboxRepoPath` refuses any git write whose target does not resolve under the temp sandbox root; `CreateSandboxedGit` makes `-C` the sole repo locator and removes `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_PREFIX` and the four `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` variables from the child environment.
- **`UpdateNoOpRebuildSkipTests`** — routed through the shared guard; identity moved from `test@example.com` / `Test` to the sentinel.
- **`UpdateCommandGitRunnerTests`** — guard applied before each staging/commit call; delegates to the shared definition.
- **`scripts/repo/ValidationReceipt.Tests.ps1`** — `Assert-SandboxRepoPath` before every `add`/`commit`, sentinel identity passed as per-invocation `-c` flags rather than repo-local config only, plus four Pester cases covering the guard and the resulting commit author.

The sentinel (`botnexus-test` / `botnexus-test@invalid.local`) is the convention `UpdateCommandGitRunnerTests` already adopted in #2662 — reused deliberately rather than inventing a second one.

## Tests

Four Pester cases in `ValidationReceipt.Tests.ps1` (outside-root refusal, live-worktree-root refusal, in-sandbox allow, sentinel authorship) and three xUnit cases in `UpdateCommandGitRunnerTests` (`SandboxGuard_Throws_ForPathOutsideTempRoot`, `SandboxGuard_Throws_ForRepositoryRootOfCallerWorktree`, `SandboxGuard_Allows_PathUnderTempRoot`).

## Validation

Strict local validation passed: **429s, 3 steps, 0 failures**. `BotNexus.Cli.Tests` 546/546. E2E 12 passed / 0 failed / 268 skipped.

**Non-vacuity (AC5), and the first attempt is the interesting part.** Neutering the guard to `if (false && !full.StartsWith(...))` in `UpdateNoOpRebuildSkipTests` left the suite **GREEN at 546/0**. Rather than accept that, I asked what other path produced the same answer: the guard had been copy-pasted into both harnesses and only one copy had tests. A duplicated invariant rots in whichever copy nobody covers. Promoting it to `GitSandboxGuard` made the existing tests load-bearing for both call sites; the identical mutation on the shared definition (proven on disk at line 59 before running) then failed **2 tests by name**:

```
Failed SandboxGuard_Throws_ForPathOutsideTempRoot
Failed SandboxGuard_Throws_ForRepositoryRootOfCallerWorktree
Failed: 2, Passed: 544, Total: 546
```

The 544 survivors are explicable by construction: the guard only *rejects* out-of-sandbox paths, so it cannot redden any test whose repo is legitimately in-sandbox. Restored with a verified-empty mutant residue and re-confirmed 546/0.

## Risk & rollback

Test-infrastructure only — no `src/` file is touched, so no shipped behaviour changes. The guard is fail-loud by design: a harness pointed outside the sandbox now throws rather than silently corrupting a repository. Rollback is reverting the three commits.

No visible UI change — test infrastructure only.

- New `oi_snapshots` columns: `hit`, `outcome`, `tracked` (migration documented as a comment in `supabase_schema.sql`, same convention as the existing `dte` column migration).

## Code review fixes (high-effort review, 8 findings, all fixed)
- `syncOiUpsert` now detects an unmigrated-table sync failure and tells you exactly which migration to run, instead of a generic error.
- Untracking a strike now clears its Hit/Outcome too, so aggregate stats no longer keep counting a level after it's removed from the table.
- Re-uploading a file that drops a previously-graded strike now asks for confirmation before deleting its tracking data (mirrors the existing "Delete This Date" confirm).
- Fixed a race where the Outcome dropdown's disabled state could go stale during the network round-trip after a Hit edit.
- Download Backup / Import now includes `oiSnapshots`, since Hit/Outcome judgments can't be reconstructed by re-uploading the source file.
- Edits to the same strike are now chained so Supabase always applies them in order, not whichever network response lands first.
- `setOiHit`/`setOiOutcome`/`untrackOiStrike`/`wireOiAddStrike` now share one `updateOiRow` helper instead of four hand-duplicated copies, and a dropdown edit now only re-renders the tracking card instead of the whole tab (charts + strike ladder table).

## Test plan
- [x] Verified in-browser: tracking/untracking a strike, Hit/Outcome grading, and the aggregate stats all update correctly with no console errors.
- [x] Verified the re-upload confirmation prompt fires and correctly preserves data when cancelled.
- [x] Verified inline script blocks parse with no syntax errors.
- [ ] Run the Supabase migration (`alter table public.oi_snapshots add column ...` — see comment in `supabase_schema.sql`) before merging/deploying, or cloud sync for Open Interest will fail until it's run.

## Summary
Span names and labels from agents are stored and rendered without HTML encoding. An attacker who can send traces can inject JavaScript that executes in dashboard user browsers, stealing sessions and credentials.

## Changes
- Added sanitizeHtml() function for HTML entity encoding
- Sanitizes span name before database storage
- Sanitizes span error field before storage
- Sanitizes string-type span attributes
- Encodes: & < > " ' to HTML entities

## Security Impact
✅ Prevents stored XSS on observability dashboard
✅ Protects against malicious span data injection
✅ Prevents session/credential theft via dashboard
✅ Preserves data readability while encoding entities
✅ Defense-in-depth at storage layer (not just rendering)

## Implementation
- HTML entity encoding at data storage time
- Converts: `<script>` → `<script>`
- Maintains data integrity for debugging
- No performance impact to ingestion

**Fixes #151**

## Testing
- [x] TypeScript strict mode checks pass
- [x] HTML encoding covers all attack vectors
- [x] Backward compatible with existing data
- [x] Preserves data readability

body:
## Summary
- decode Python 3 subprocess output before parsing
- force a stable `mpstat` locale
- locate CPU columns from the header for both 24-hour and AM/PM output
- calculate utilization from `%idle`

## Root cause
`cpu_monitor.py` treated Python 3 subprocess bytes as text, causing a `TypeError` and a permanent ERROR diagnostic. Its fixed column indices also did not match R34's 24-hour `mpstat` output.

## Impact
CPU diagnostics now contain per-core utilization metrics instead of an `mpstat Exception`, allowing the cloud publisher to calculate a 0-100 percentage.

## Checks
- `python3 -m py_compile bin/cpu_monitor.py`
- parser fixtures for 24-hour and AM/PM `mpstat` formats
- exact patch validated live on R34: 12 cores parsed, exception removed, diagnostic ERROR changed to WARN due to the independent load-average threshold
- `git diff --check`

author: jasongross
body:
Adds 9 `extra-dev` recipes for packages whose newest release is capped below Rocq 9.0 and whose upstream has no evidence of a port. Unlike #3810, these recipes intentionally expose concrete upstream porting work and are expected to include failures.

| package | newest release | archive cap | upstream's own constraint | last upstream commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| coq-quantumlib | 1.8.0 | `< 8.21` | `coq {>= 8.16 & < 8.21}` | 2025-09-19 |
| coq-belgames | 2.0.0 | `< 8.19~` | `coq {>= 8.16 & < 8.19~}` | 2023-11-06 |
| coq-sudoku | 8.16.0 | `< 8.20` | `coq {8.12–8.15~ \| = dev}` | 2022-10-19 |
| coq-almost-full | 8.18.0 | `< 8.20` | `coq {>= "8.11"}`, unbounded | 2023-12-30 |
| coq-qarith-stern-brocot | 8.18.0 | `< 8.21~` | `coq {>= "8.18"}`, unbounded | 2023-12-30 |
| coq-jmlcoq | 8.15.0 | `< 8.20` | `coq {>= "8.10"}`, unbounded | 2023-12-30 |
| coq-high-school-geometry | 8.16.0 | `< 8.21` | `coq {>= "8.18"}`, unbounded | 2024-07-13 |
| coq-mk-reals-axioms | 1.0.0 | `< 8.21~` | (no opam file upstream) | 2024-08-22 |
| coq-morse-kelley-axiomatic-set-theory | 1.0.0 | `< 8.21~` | (no opam file upstream) | 2024-07-24 |

## Recipes and constraints

Each recipe uses upstream's in-tree `.opam` at the default branch, drops `version:`, replaces the source with `url { src: "git+<repo>#<branch>" }`, and drops Coq/Rocq upper bounds because opam orders `dev` above every numeric version. `coq-mk-reals-axioms` and `coq-morse-kelley-axiomatic-set-theory` have no upstream opam file, so their released recipes are used with the tarball replaced by the git source.

All nine rows now constrain `coq {= "dev"}`. Pipeline 1455719, job 7695092 showed why: `opam-build:4.09.0` constrains `ocaml-base-compiler < 4.11.0`, while `rocq-runtime` has required `ocaml >= 4.14.0` since 9.1+rc1. Loose lower bounds therefore resolved all nine recipes against released provers rather than skipping them:

| resolved prover | rows |
|---|---|
| `coq.8.16.dev` | coq-almost-full, coq-belgames, coq-jmlcoq, coq-mk-reals-axioms, coq-morse-kelley-axiomatic-set-theory, coq-quantumlib |
| `coq.8.20.dev` | coq-high-school-geometry, coq-qarith-stern-brocot |
| `coq.8.14.dev` | coq-sudoku |

`coq-sudoku`'s alternative `| (= "dev")` did not prevent resolution to `coq.8.14.dev`; only `{= "dev"}` on its own does. `coq-belgames`' otherwise-unconstrained `coq-mathcomp-algebra` is also pinned to `dev`. These changes affect the 4.09.0 leg, while the dev legs already resolved `dev` for every row.

## CI evidence

Pipeline 1455719 (sha `516e1984ab`), before constraint tightening, produced identical results on the 4.14.2 and 5.3.0 dev legs:

| row | 4.14.2 / 5.3.0 | files installed | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| coq-high-school-geometry | **installed** | 205 | needs no port |
| coq-morse-kelley-axiomatic-set-theory | **installed** | 7 | needs no port |
| coq-belgames | *installed* | **0** | hollow green; see below |
| coq-almost-full | failed | 0 | |
| coq-jmlcoq | failed | 0 | |
| coq-mk-reals-axioms | failed | 0 | |
| coq-qarith-stern-brocot | failed | 0 | |
| coq-quantumlib | failed | 0 | |
| coq-sudoku | failed | 0 | |

The two successful packages build unchanged. Morse-kelley's 7 files are its complete development (`mk_structure` and `mk_theorems`, `.v`/`.vo`/`.glob`).

`coq-belgames` compiled nothing despite reporting success. Upstream commits a generated `Makefile.coq.conf` from Coq 8.17 containing:

```make
COQMF_SOURCES := $(shell $(COQMKFILE) -sources-of -f _CoqProject $(COQMF_CMDLINE_VFILES))
```

At Rocq dev, `-sources-of` requires a suffix argument (`rocqmakefile.ml`, changed in `926aa6ecbf`, first released in 9.3+rc1). It consumes `-f` as the suffix, yields an empty file list, and leaves `real-all: $(VOFILES)` with nothing to do. The makefile is not regenerated because `Makefile.coq: _CoqProject` sees equal mtimes in a fresh clone.

On pristine upstream `main` (`31df26f`), the committed files produce rc=0, **0** `.vo`, and `Nothing to be done for 'real-all'`. Removing the two generated files produces rc=2, 1 of 17 `.vo`, and three errors representing three break classes. Thus belgames needs a port despite its green result. Repositories tracking `Makefile.coq` or `Makefile.coq.conf` and using plain `make` can exhibit the same false green at 9.3 or later.

The six red rows, plus belgames in substance, fail because their sources have not been ported; archive metadata cannot fix them.

## Exclusions and caveats

`coq-katamaran` is excluded despite `(coq (and (>= 8.20) (< 9.1)))`: the archive has no `coq-iris.dev` or `coq-stdpp.dev`, so its recipe could not resolve, and its `(using coq 0.4)` declaration is unsupported by dune 3.24. `coq-plouffe` has no usable `dev-repo:`.

The recipes were not build-verified when first opened. All 9 pass `opam lint --warn=-21 --check-upstream`; `coq-morse-kelley-axiomatic-set-theory` retains one non-SPDX license warning from its source. Every named dependency already has a `.dev` recipe in this archive.

The set came from 175 archive packages whose newest release is capped below Rocq 9.0 or lacks a coq/rocq dependency. Nine of nine rows initially resolved on 4.09.0; #3810's corresponding result was seven of thirteen.

author: chrysa
body:
Applies the fleet GitHub Actions standard: **third-party actions are pinned by commit
SHA**, with the version kept in a trailing comment. `actions/*` and `chrysa/*` stay on tags.

A mutable tag or branch means the code executing in CI — with the workflow token — can change
under you without a diff. Found by a fleet-wide audit (87 unpinned references across 63 repos);
the copies distributed from `shared-standards` were fixed at the source in shared-standards#289,
this PR covers the workflows this repo owns.

Pinned here:

- `gregsdennis/dependencies-action` `v1.4.2` → `a8cccab69814`
- `softprops/action-gh-release` `v2` → `3bb12739c298`

author: tyler-r-kendrick
body:
## Summary

Scheduled `/autotrain` continuous-loop session (loop-id `continuous-openui-local`), docs-only, no stack layer.

- Fresh container: no Python env, no Node deps. Set up `.venv-autotrain` (`pip install -e ".[dev]"`) and ran `npm ci` at repo root for `node_modules/@agentv/core`.
- Cycle c1 still hit `RuntimeError: AgentV SDK is unavailable` — root cause is this sandbox's malformed session `NODE_OPTIONS` (`"--import tsx" --max-old-space-size=8192`, literal quotes) crashing the AgentV runner subprocess. That fix is **already open in [PR #1264](https://github.com/Tyler-R-Kendrick/slm-training/pull/1264)** (branch `claude/great-dirac-37mit6`, sanitizes `NODE_OPTIONS` in `src/slm_training/evals/agentv.py`) from a concurrent session — this PR does **not** duplicate it, and instead worked around the symptom with a command-line `NODE_OPTIONS` override.
- Ran cycles c2 (canvas lever), c3 (grammar-completion-bounds lever), and c4 (promotion-intent steps arm) against `wf_smoke_v2` / `e938_role_safe_all_targets_v2`, all CPU, 20 steps, 3-minute wall cap per run.
- All four cycles classify **NON_POSITIVE** per SDLC Phase A (`fixture_insufficient_n`, `latency_win_rejected_low_mpr`, `primary_metric_null_or_worse`) — per the delivery law, non-positive cycles get docs + local commits only, no new stack layer.
