author: oliviermadre
body:
Closes #369.

## Why

`get-statistics.ts` was 671 lines, 556 of them inside a single `execute()` that
computed ~15 aggregates inline over 10 stores. Three problems compounded:

- **`toDTO()` ran per entity, per bucket.** A year of daily buckets meant ~730k
  DTO conversions for a response that needs a few thousand.
- **Cumulative flow rescanned every ticket's move list at every boundary** —
  O(buckets × tickets × moves), ~7.3M iterations on a realistic dataset.
- **I/O was spread over four sequential `await` points** even though none of the
  reads depended on each other, which is why the summary and time series emitted
  placeholder zeros and patched them back in later.

## What

The pipeline is now **load → materialise → slice → compute → assemble**. The use
case is the only thing touching stores or the clock; each aggregate lives in
`application/utils/statistics/` as a pure function over plain rows.

- One `Promise.all` of 12 store calls; placeholder/backfill machinery deleted.
- Each entity converted exactly once, at a single `buildDataset()` boundary.
- Cumulative flow merges all transitions into one chronological stream and
  sweeps it once. Throughput gets the same treatment — buckets tile the range
  contiguously, so a sorted forward cursor replaces the per-bucket filter.
- Three `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>` casts removed. They hid a
  `dto.status === 'active'` branch that `SessionStatus` cannot produce.
- Magic `1000` / `50_000` / `60_000` named.

## Performance

365 buckets, 5 000 tickets, 20 000 comments, 10 000 executions, ~20 000 move
events. Median of 5 runs, cache defeated between runs:

| | wall time |
|---|---|
| before | 12 443 ms |
| after | **61 ms** |

**~204× faster** (target was 5×).

## Correctness

The refactor is pinned by a full-response inline snapshot **written and committed
against the old implementation before any restructuring**, and never re-recorded.
It still passes byte-identical, as do the five pre-existing tests, unmodified.

- 565 tests pass across 73 files; `npm run lint` clean.
- New: 14 cumulative-flow edge-case tests covering the ordering assumptions the
  sweep newly depends on — a transition landing exactly on a boundary, a ticket
  born and moved at the same instant, two moves sharing an instant, `cancelled`
  dropping out of all five columns, degenerate and clamped ranges.
- New: a `toDTO()` call-budget test asserting the count stays flat as the window
  widens from 1 bucket to 365.

### One intended behaviour change

`activeSessions` now counts only `'running'`. The old code also accepted
`'active'`, which is not a member of `SessionStatus` — dead code reachable only
through the casts that this PR removes. Provably a no-op.

### One deviation from the spec

The spec froze the constructor signature, but also asked for a truncation
warning, and the convention here is injected `LoggerPort`. I appended an
**optional** `logger?` parameter: the single call site passes `container.logger`,
every other construction is unaffected. Flagging it rather than deciding quietly.

## Follow-ups (deliberately not fixed here — behaviour-preserving PR)

- [ ] `firstDoingAt` asymmetry in lead time: a ticket that never passed through
      `doing` is dropped from the series entirely.
- [ ] `prsCreated` and `prsMerged` are bucketed on different date fields, so the
      two lines are not directly comparable.
- [ ] Panel/move fetch limits now warn on truncation, but the limits themselves
      are unchanged and still silently cap the window.

## Test plan

- [x] Golden snapshot unchanged (verified under UTC, America/New_York, Asia/Tokyo)
- [x] 5 pre-existing tests pass unmodified
- [x] Full server suite: 565 passed
- [x] `npm run lint` (palette ratchet + typecheck across all 6 packages)
- [ ] Spot-check the statistics page renders identically against a real dataset

author: suavecito585
body: Fix 2 of THE-688, and the half that would actually have caught the outage. ## Why fix 1 wasn't enough Fix 1 stopped doctor **claiming** readiness it never checked. It could not **prevent** the failure: Ollama was removed while the config still named it, and for two days every semantic query returned `embedding_provider_error` while `doctor` exited 0. `doctor --probe` embeds one short fixed string against the configured provider and reports what it **observed**. `ready` is now a word only the probed path may use. ## Off by default — that's the design A diagnostic that reaches the network as a side effect of being run is a different tool than the one people reach for when something is already broken. Every other check stays offline. It uses the **sync** `createEmbeddingProvider` deliberately: that factory already refuses `provider: "module"` with an actionable error, so doctor's *"diagnosing must not execute operator-supplied code"* rule holds **by construction** rather than through a special case here that could drift. ## Why an embed and not a ping A TCP connect or a HEAD on the base URL would have **passed** for the failure this closes. Ollama's container was gone — but a wrong model name or a missing API key look identical to a reachability test and are just as fatal. The probe also compares the returned dimension against `embeddings.dimensions`: a mismatch indexes garbage at the configured width while every reachability signal stays green. ## Running it against a real gateway changed the design A cold `bge-m3` answered in **89,475 ms**. Capping the probe (~15 s) was the tempting fix and would have been wrong — it reports `UNREACHABLE` for a provider that genuinely works, a false negative worse than the ambiguity being removed. A slow success stays `ok` and earns a **note** instead. "Reachable" and "reachable but unusable" read identically in a boolean. ## The failure is named correctly An unreachable provider is a **warning**, not a fail — the config is valid and the server still boots. Summary and remediation now split on it. Before, the single warning text said *"a retrieval stream is enabled but inert"* and advised setting provider to `bge-m3`, which sends an operator to rewrite a perfectly good config while the endpoint stays down. ## Verified end to end, both directions ``` default → configured (ollama, nomic-embed-text, dim 768) — not probed --probe, dead → ! UNREACHABLE — request failed --probe, live → READY — probed ok in 89475ms (openai, BAAI/bge-m3, dim 1024) ``` ## A vacuous test, fixed Making `run` async broke one test loudly and one **silently**. `doctor-generic-provider`'s `not.toMatch` was stringifying an un-awaited promise to `"{}"` — which satisfies the negation for a reason unrelated to what it claims to check. It would have gone permanently green. Now awaited, with a positive guard so it can't pass on an empty payload again. 86 tests pass across 7 doctor/CLI suites; typecheck, biome, all `check:*` gates, `docgen:facts-check` and `map-check` green. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: jiaweihan88
body:
## The drift

`app/src/shared/panelTheme.ts`'s `LIGHT` map is a hand-copy of the renderer's `theme.css` — the panel preload cannot read the renderer's stylesheet — and it silently drifted past the light redesign, the same way `titleBar.ts`'s `PALETTE` did.

It still held the pre-redesign warm-paper values while `theme.css` moved to the cool wash. **Effect: a docked pack panel (`WebContentsView`) rendered on warm paper inside a cool-blue app, in light mode only.**

Nothing caught it. The existing `panelThemeVars` assertions compared the copy against itself, and `themeTokens.test.ts` names `#faf8f3` / `#f0eee7` / `#1567b3` as dead literals — but only ever scans `theme.css`, so this second copy drifted unguarded.

## What changed

`LIGHT` now mirrors `theme.css`'s `:root[data-theme='light']` block under the mapping `DARK` already followed:

| panel token | theme.css source | old (warm) | new (cool) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bg` | `--bg-1` | `#faf8f3` | `#eef2f9` |
| `surface` | `--bg-2` | `#ffffff` | `#ffffff` (unchanged) |
| `surface-2` | `--bg-hi` | `#f0eee7` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.62)` |
| `text` | `--ink` | `#18181b` | `#101823` |
| `dim` | `--dim` | `rgba(24, 24, 27, 0.7)` | `rgba(28, 42, 64, 0.68)` |
| `faint` | `--faint` | `rgba(24, 24, 27, 0.25)` | `rgba(28, 42, 64, 0.3)` |
| `hair` | `--hair` | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06)` | `rgba(26, 48, 84, 0.09)` |
| `accent` | `--signal` | `#1567b3` | `#1f6fd0` |
| `danger` | `--danger` | `#f27a6b` | `#c93b3b` |

`DARK` was already correct and is unchanged.

`surface-2` takes `--bg-hi` verbatim, translucent and all, rather than a flattened approximation. Panels composite it over `--argus-bg` exactly as the renderer does, and an exact value is what lets the guard below be a strict comparison instead of a fuzzy one.

## The guard

Mirrors `titleBar.test.ts`'s `"mirrors theme.css — the copy this module admits it is"`: read the stylesheet from disk and hold the hand-copy to it.

It covers **both** maps across **all nine** tokens via an explicit token → source table, so dark cannot drift either — the previous assertions only spot-checked two tokens per theme. `panelTheme.ts` carries the same mapping as a comment so source and test agree.

I confirmed the guard bites rather than assuming it: reintroducing `bg: '#faf8f3'` and making a one-character dark edit (`#7ec4ff` → `#7ec4fe`) both fail, with the offending token named in the assertion message.

## On the public contract

`panelThemeVars` is documented as a stable **public** contract for third-party panels, so this was worth checking before touching. It holds:

- The spec (`part-3a-2`, §Interfaces) and the in-file comment both scope the decoupling to **names** — *"deliberately decoupled from Core's internal `--void`/`--ink` token names so panels don't break on renames."*
- The sample packs consume the tokens as `var(--argus-bg, #0a0a0b)` — a themed value that follows the app is the entire point.

Token names, `PANEL_TOKENS`, and the `panelThemeVars` signature are untouched. Only values move, which is what a theme change is.

## Verification

Run from `app/`:

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm test` — 5102 passed / 13 skipped

One caveat, disclosed rather than buried: full-suite runs intermittently fail `acp/__tests__/client.test.ts > ... child exit delivers a synthetic {type:"error"} item`. Across four full runs with identical content it passed twice and failed twice, it passes in isolation, and there is no import path from the ACP driver to either changed file. It is the known subprocess-backed-poll flake class, not this change — but it is pre-existing and worth a separate look.

author: etlami
body:
## What

The Gas Calculators cover **analysis** (MOD, best mix, END, gas consumption, rock bottom) but there's no **blending** tool — "how do I fill this mix?". This adds a sixth tab: a partial-pressure blender that outputs the fill order and the intermediate pressures to top up to.

Related community request: discussion is around blending; this is the fill-side companion to the existing analysis calculators.

## Highlights

- **Real gas, not ideal.** Compressibility via Van der Waals virial coefficients (O₂/N₂/He), so intermediate pressures are accurate at real fill pressures rather than drifting like a pure partial-pressure approximation.
- **Nitrox and trimix.** Two-gas O₂ balance for nitrox targets; a three-gas He/N₂/O₂ linear solve for trimix, with up to three configurable fill gases applied in a chosen order (default O₂ → air → helium).
- **Clear failure modes.** Reports *why* a blend is impossible: target not higher than start, invalid mix (O₂+He > 100%), identical fill gases, no helium source for a trimix target, or a negative amount required.
- **Unit-aware.** Pressures use the diver's pressure unit (bar/psi); the mix percentages drive the math in bar internally.
- **Reset-aware.** Wired into the page's existing "reset all".

## Implementation

- `domain/gas_blender.dart` — pure, dependency-free math (`zFactor`, `normalVolume`, `pressureForVolume`, `computeBlend`) returning a structured fill procedure or a typed `BlendError`.
- `presentation/widgets/gas_blender_calculator.dart` — the tab UI (cylinder state, target, three fill gases, step-by-step result).
- 6th tab in `GasCalculatorsPage`; blender state + reset in the shared providers.

The algorithm is ported from the open-source Blei-Log blender.

## Tests

- `gas_blender_test.dart` cross-checks the Dart port against the reference implementation's exact intermediate pressures and volumes (EAN32 nitrox and Tmx 18/45 trimix), plus every error path.
- `gas_blender_calculator_widget_test.dart` covers the default nitrox render, the below-start-pressure error, and a trimix procedure.

Verified locally (Flutter 3.44.8 / Dart 3.12.2): `flutter analyze lib` clean, `dart format` clean, `flutter gen-l10n` run, gas-calculator + arb-parity suites green. New `gasCalculators_blender_*` strings are translated into all ten non-English locales.

author: davidpp09
body:
David pidió que los 5 platillos que rotan resalten sobre los 7 fijos.

## Dos cambios

**1. Negrita.** Los fijos vienen en negrita desde la plantilla y los del día se escribían en redonda: en el papel impreso, lo que hay que mirar se veía más flojo que lo que nunca cambia. `HELVETICA` → `HELVETICA_BOLD`.

**2. Reparto.** La interlínea pasa de **13.5555 a 15.686 pt**. Al quitarse la milanesa quedaron 10.56 pt muertos entre el último platillo del día y el primer fijo; ahora los 5 renglones se reparten por todo el espacio y el hueco desaparece. El paso sale de dividir en 5 la distancia del primer renglón (758.19) al primer fijo (679.76), así que la separación con el bloque de abajo queda igual que la de dentro del bloque.

Que el día respire más que los fijos es a propósito: junto con la negrita, es lo que hace que lo que cambia destaque.

## Lo que NO se pudo hacer, y por qué

David pidió también letra más grande. **No es posible**, y el motivo no es el que parecía: el límite no es vertical sino **horizontal**.

| | |
|---|---|
| `COSTILLA DE CERDO EN SALSA DE MANGO HABANERO $115` a 9 pt | **272 pt** de ancho |
| Ancho disponible (`ANCHO_LINEA`) | **263 pt** |
| Tamaño mayor que le sirve a los 5 a la vez | **8.5 pt** |

Ese platillo ya se está encogiendo hoy. Y ampliar `ANCHO_LINEA` no salva nada: el interior del recuadro mide 274 pt, así que quedan **4 pt de holgura, un 1.5%**, que daría 8.63 pt en vez de 8.5.

Medido sobre el PDF renderizado, no estimado.

## Verificación

- Separaciones tras el cambio: **15.37 / 15.85 / 15.85 / 15.37** dentro del bloque y **15.37** hasta el pozole. Sin huecos.
- El test de coordenadas **falló** al cambiar la interlínea, que es exactamente lo que tenía que hacer, y se actualizó a 15.686.
- Suite en **90**, en verde.

author: raulmoranguerra
body:
The stability gate was set at **12 raw counts of spread** for both pedals. That is unusable on the brake, and the evidence was already sitting in the firmware's own config:

```cpp
BrakeArmRaw = 750;  // on-car cal 2026-06-27: brake-to-arm (R2D);
                    // released ~580 (noise to ~730), arm just above
```

A released brake pedal spans **~150 counts of noise at rest**. A 12-count gate can never be satisfied — so `BRAKE_REST`, the capture the derived arming threshold depends on, could never be taken at all.

Measured it in the running UI to be certain rather than inferring:

| Signal | Spread at rest | Old gate | New gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accelerator | 2 | 12 ✅ | 40 ✅ |
| Brake | **150** | 12 ❌ **blocked** | 200 ✅ |

## Per-signal, because the sensors are nothing alike

- **APPS — 40 counts.** ~5% of the smaller 680-count span. The bench calibration applies ~13 counts of margin at each endpoint, so the channels are quiet.
- **Brake — 200 counts.** Clears the measured 150-count band with margin, still under a tenth of usable travel.

Both remain an order of magnitude below real pedal movement (APPS travel 860 and 680 counts; brake a couple of thousand), which is what the gate is actually there to detect — *"the operator is still moving the pedal"*, not *"the ADC is perfectly quiet"*.

## Corrects a wrong premise

The old comment claimed the ECU rejects an unstable sample and the gate merely saved the operator a refusal. **It does not.** `SampleUnstable` is defined in the protocol but `cal_session.cpp` never emits it — the ECU accepts whatever it is handed.

So this gate is the **only** stability check anywhere in the system. That makes it more important than advertised, not less, and makes setting it to an unreachable value strictly worse than having no gate: the operator simply cannot proceed. The Capture tooltip now states the real situation and shows the actual numbers rather than repeating the false claim.

## Verification

`npm run check`: 124 files, 0 errors. `npm run build`: clean. Spreads above measured by driving the panel with realistic on-car values (brake cycling 580–730, APPS held).

> This is a fix to behaviour shipped in **v2.10.0**. The calibration wizard is currently released with a brake capture that cannot be completed.

body:
Теперь ясно, почему приложение ощущалось сломанным. Это были не абстрактные проблемы, а три конкретных пользовательских дефекта.

## Исправлено

- Web session storage больше не in-memory: токены сохраняются в `localStorage`, поэтому reload не превращает пользователя в другого/анонимного.
- Logout теперь всегда чистит локальную сессию, даже если backend недоступен или текущий refresh/access token уже протух. Это исправляет зависший аккаунт в Expo.
- После успешного sign-in/sign-up экран автоматически переходит в приложение, а не остаётся на форме.
- Route fixes для создания объекта и смены состояния уже находятся в этой ветке из текущего master: frontend использует реальные Nest endpoints.

## Проверенный flow

1. Sign-up: `POST /v1/auth/sign-up`, session сохраняется, переход в `/`, затем `GET /v1/spaces`.
2. Sign-in: `POST /v1/auth/sign-in`, session сохраняется, переход в `/`, затем spaces/surface загружаются.

author: dinho149
body:
## Summary

Standup **Generate** walked the user through five pickers on *every* run — tracker sources, team members, code sources, repositories/projects, documentation sources — before it would accept their update. The answers were already persisted in `standup_config` and the page always targets the same session, so those pickers were only ever re-confirming the previous run's choices; the saved values merely preselected the checkboxes.

Generate now opens with a summary of the saved setup:

```
    Use your saved setup?
    ←/→ move · Enter choose · Esc cancel

      Trackers  Jira, Azure DevOps
      Members   Alice, Bob, Carol +3 more
      Code      2 GitHub repo(s) · 1 Azure project(s)
      Docs      Confluence

      ╭───────────╮  ╭──────────╮  ╭──────────╮
      │ Use saved │  │  Change  │  │   Back   │
      ╰───────────╯  ╰──────────╯  ╰──────────╯
```

**Use saved** goes straight to "Your update for today". **Change** walks the five pickers exactly as before, still preselected. **Back**/Esc cancels with no run. First runs and incomplete setups are unchanged — the gate only appears once there is something to reuse.

Scope is TUI-only: gate predicate, confirm loop, screen builder, two `_BTN_COLORS` entries. No engine, storage, schema, CLI or MCP change — the headless engine already resolves saved config on its own, so scheduled/CLI/MCP runs are untouched and no surface-parity capability is owed.

**Two rules decide whether a saved setup may be reused**, both in `_standup_saved_setup`:

1. A step's `*_configured` flag is required only when its integration actually exists in env. `_standup_code_configure` / `_standup_documentation_configure` return early *without* setting their flag when there is no GitHub/Azure or no Confluence/Notion, so demanding all three flags would have hidden the gate permanently from exactly those users. An empty `documentation_sources` with the flag set is a real answer ("I opted out"), not missing data.
2. Saved selections must still be a subset of what is configured today. Walking the pickers used to self-heal a removed integration — they only ever list what is currently available — so reuse re-asks rather than silently carrying a stale source.

## Review

An independent fresh-context review raised two `should-fix` findings, both addressed here: rule 2 above (saved selections outliving their integration), and making the tmp-DB fixture in the new test file `autouse` so no future test can open the developer's real `~/.yeaboi` store. Its nits were also taken: dropped two parameters that had no production caller, restored the `tui-standards` viewport spacer with the matching `header_h=7`, added `_BTN_COLORS` registration and click-branch tests, moved the render tests in with the other standup screen tests, and the summary now names the roster rather than just counting it.

## Test plan

- `make test` — **7512 passed, 46 skipped** (includes `test_surface_parity.py`, which needed no registry edit)
- `make lint` — clean
- New coverage: the gate's four flow paths (use / change / cancel / no-saved-setup), a truth table for the reusability predicate including every "integration since removed" case, the confirm loop's keyboard and click handling, and screen render tests
- Manual: rendered the gate at several widths and roster sizes

author: dealappseo
body:
## What

The golden-math tripwire asserts HAL's crown-jewel claim (math F1 0.94, zero false positives). It failed locally and read as a quality regression. It was not one — a stale `GROQ_API_KEY` 401'd and gemini 404'd, so HAL answered on **2 families**. That is exactly `MIN_QUORUM_FOR_VETO`, so nothing was marked `degraded` and ordinary verdicts came back.

A tripwire that reports a provider outage as a quality regression costs more than it saves — it sends the reader hunting for a scoring bug. A bare pass is just as misleading the other way: green at 2 families does not re-establish a number measured at 3. Same defect as the HAL F1 spread (0.34 / 0.74 / 0.886 / 0.890) — different rulers reported as one scale.

## Change

Width is asserted **first and separately**, and a pass now records the width it passed at. A dead key fails as a dead key, names the fix, and prints the decisions it did reach. Test-only; no production behaviour changes.

## What the degraded run showed — flagged for Sean, deliberately not fixed here

At 2 families the set produced **2 false positives on TRUE arithmetic** — `3 to the power of 4 is 81` and `the sum of the first 5 prime numbers is 28` were both vetoed.

`MIN_QUORUM_FOR_VETO` is **2**; the zero-false-positive claim was measured at **3**. Under a partial provider outage HAL may therefore veto at a width where its own frozen accuracy claim does not hold — and a veto costs an agent real RepID. Raising the floor is a live scoring change, so it is flagged, not made in a test commit.

author: crysisdeu
body:
## Problem

The dashboard i18n mechanism has never been audited end-to-end, so nobody could
answer two questions with evidence: **is it built correctly**, and **do we
measure whether the translations are any good**. The second question turned out
to be the one that matters — 46,161 target-catalog values ship across nine
locales with no quality metric of any kind.

## Why it matters

Structural gates catch structural defects. They cannot catch a fluent, confident,
wrong translation, and nothing in CI distinguishes one from a correct one. The
absence that compounds is **stale-source invalidation**: `mergeCatalog` is
insert-only, so when an English string changes the translation silently stays. That
is correctness decay, not a coverage gap, and it gets worse on its own.

Separately, localization stops at the dashboard React tree. The window frame around
it, the notifications it sends, the CLI that installed it, and the site it was
downloaded from are all English-only — a coherent scoping decision, but one worth
recording rather than rediscovering.

## Fix (symptom → root cause → change)

**Symptom:** no answer to "is our i18n good". **Root cause:** the gates measure
structure (parity, plural categories, placeholder integrity) and nothing measures
language. **Change:** this RFC records the audit and proposes six changes ordered by
value-per-diff, with source-hash staleness detection first because it is the
smallest diff against the largest compounding risk.

Docs-only. No code, test, or configuration changes.

### What the audit found

Structurally the mechanism is, in places, above industry practice — CLDR plural
categories are exactly correct in all ten locales (45 families re-derived per
locale against 5,014 non-plural keys), key parity is exact, exactly one dynamic key
site exists, and the pseudolocale implements a monotonic adaptation of the IBM/W3C
expansion-by-length curve rather than the flat 40% heuristic.

The gap is measurement: no word-count coverage, no review-status ladder, no
MQM/LQA scoring, no MT-quality metric, no stale-source invalidation, no
missing-key telemetry. The RFC tabulates each against what Weblate, Crowdin,
Lokalise and Transifex actually report.

### One finding is withdrawn as already fixed

The audit found that `qa-allowlist.json` could absorb any violation via a single
`--update`. #1060 had already deleted it and moved the strict gates to diff scope.
That fix is better than the one the audit would have proposed, and the RFC says so
explicitly rather than quietly dropping the finding. `website/AGENTS.md` — not the
commit body, which is empty — carries the team's own measurement of what the
bypass cost in practice.

## Tests

None. Docs-only change; there is nothing executable to lock in. The RFC's own
claims were verified against the tree rather than by test (see below).

## Manual verification

The document is entirely factual claims, so verification *was* the work:

- Audited at `f6ec5834`, then **every number re-measured against `5ec356d5`**
  before publication — two i18n commits (#1046, #1060) had landed in between and
  one of them invalidated a finding.
- Local review gate run per `prepare-pr`: `gpt-5.6-sol` mirroring
  `codex-review.yml` and `claude-opus-5` mirroring `claude-review.yml` +
  `AUTOSDE.yaml` + `AGENTS.md`. **~24 findings, essentially all legitimate**, all
  corrected before push. The substantive ones: the `i18nT` denominator, a
  translated-value count that omitted all 45 plural families, a Tailwind claim
  describing v4 behaviour, an `index.css` clipping example pointing at a
  numeric-only element, a pseudolocale assertion that checks the runtime registry
  rather than bundle bytes, a self-contradicting `localeCompare` proposal, and a
  `#1060` citation aimed at an empty commit body.
- A focused verifier then caught that **two of those corrections were themselves
  wrong** — taken from a reviewer's count without independent checking. Re-measured
  directly; the reviewers had disagreed because they were counting lines, values and
  occurrences respectively.
- Where two reviewers gave conflicting numbers and the repo could not adjudicate
  (the `i18nT` total, Tailwind's emitted RTL selector), the RFC now **defers to the
  repo's own tooling or drops the claim** rather than picking a side. Unmeasured
  magnitudes are labelled unmeasured.

Placement confirmed clean: root `docs/` is outside every packaged surface — the
wheel takes package data under `src/kiro_crew` only, `MANIFEST.in` is an allowlist
that never names root `docs/`, electron-builder ships `files: ["dist/"]`, and
`site/` references no `docs/` path.

author: forge-rubigd
body:
## Keep the scraped prefill + pasted URL on "Fetch details"

Fixes the live bug the operator hit on the demo: on the list-detail page, pasting a
product URL and clicking **Fetch details** scrapes fine ("Fetched — review and add.")
but every field ends up empty — the scraped name/image/price and the pasted URL are
discarded.

### Cause
The add-item form is `superForm(data.addForm)` with the library default `resetForm: true`,
so **every** successful submit — including the `?/preview` action — resets `$form` to its
initial empty state and discards the server-returned draft.

### Fix (intent-preserving)
- **Client**: `superForm(data.addForm, { resetForm: false })` — a preview success keeps
  the returned draft (name/url/image/price), and the pasted URL survives even a "couldn't
  fetch" result.
- **Server** `?/add` success: return a **fresh empty form** so the add form still clears
  for the next item (since the client no longer resets it). Failure paths and the default
  `invalidateAll` (items-list refresh) are unchanged.

Invariants held: (1) preview populates + persists the fields, (2) the pasted URL survives
a failed scrape, (3) a real add still clears the form.

### Verification (required test + real-browser)
- **Committed regression test** (`add-preview.svelte.test.ts`) — fails before this fix,
  passes after. It asserts `?/preview` returns the scraped draft and keeps the pasted URL
  on a failed fetch, and `?/add` returns a fresh empty form on success. Because the route
  server module transitively imports `sveltekit-superforms` (which pulls in a `.svelte`
  file), the test runs under the svelte-transform test project, with small `$app/*` test
  stubs so those imports resolve. All 41 web tests pass; lint / svelte-check / build green.
  - A full-page jsdom mount of `superForm` was impractical (it needs SvelteKit's `$app/*`
    virtual modules), so I tested the server contract that makes the fix work; the
    client behavior is covered by the real-browser check below.
- **Real browser (Blink)** — I ran the built app against a stub backend and drove the
  "Fetch details" flow in headless Chrome. On the **pre-fix** build the fields are wiped
  (bug reproduced); on the **fix** they populate and persist. This is the fails-before /
  passes-after evidence for the actual user-facing behavior. The final live click-test on
  the authed demo is the operator's redeploy step.

### Files
- `.../lists/[id]/+page.svelte` (client `resetForm: false`)
- `.../lists/[id]/+page.server.ts` (`?/add` returns a fresh form)
- `.../lists/[id]/add-preview.svelte.test.ts` (new regression test)
- `vitest.config.ts` (`$lib` + `$app/*` stub aliases on the svelte-transform project) and
  `src/lib/testing/app-stubs/*` (the stubs, never invoked)

Recovers a commit that missed its ride. `af3688684` was written on `feature/billing-checkout-link` at 23:41:50, three minutes *after* PR #3959 merged at 23:38:52, so it never reached `main` and the closed PR will not pick it up. Cherry-picked here onto current `main`, unmodified.

### The defect

`AdminCustomerDetail.vue` renders the Colonel checkout-link button unconditionally. The endpoint behind it is wrapped in a `configuration_guard` that fails **every** request when billing is disabled, so in that configuration the button is present, clickable, and guaranteed to error.

Fix is a `v-if="billing.enabled"` on the button, with a comment naming the guard as the reason.

Four eslint autofix hunks reflowing `<span>` closing brackets on the secrets / receipts / organizations count headings. Cosmetic, carried along rather than split out to keep the cherry-pick byte-identical to the original commit.

## What

- Select a least-privilege CSP by stored MIME type.
- Allow only same-origin media for video and same-origin images for image blobs.
- Apply the policy consistently to full 200 and ranged 206 responses.
- Preserve default-src none for downloadable attachments.

## Why

Direct navigation to a Buzz-hosted MP4 currently creates a browser-native video element, but the response header default-src none falls back to media-src none and blocks the element from loading its own URL. The files and range responses are valid; the response policy is the failure.

author: rhizonymph
body:
## What

Turns focus mode from a single pinned node into a **focus stack**, and gives each frame a **trace direction**.

**Focus stack.** `graphStore.focusStack: FocusFrame[]` replaces `focusNodeId` + `focusDepth` (empty = unfocused, last frame = what's on screen).

```ts
type FocusDirection = "both" | "upstream" | "downstream";
type FocusFrame =
  | { type: "node"; nodeId: string; depth: 1 | 2; direction: FocusDirection }
  | { type: "edge"; source: string; target: string };
```

- Focusing a node from inside a focused view **pushes** a deeper frame, so focus mode is real exploration rather than a one-shot neighborhood.
- Focusing the target of the *current top* frame **replaces** it instead of pushing, so there are never duplicate frames; depth/direction changes ride the same path.
- The breadcrumb is now a trail: root "All" chip + one chip per frame (truncated node name, or `A → B` for an edge frame), with the depth selector and direction toggle on the current frame. Clicking an earlier chip pops back to it, X clears the whole stack.
- **Esc now pops ONE frame** and exits focus only when the stack empties, instead of always exiting. Deliberate change — Esc retraces the drill-down the way the user walked in.
- A new frame inherits the current frame's depth/direction unless specified, so drilling deeper keeps the trace settings you set up.
- All transition logic stays as pure reducers in `graphViewModel.ts` (`reduceEnterFocus` / `reduceExitFocus` / `reducePopFocus` / `reducePopToFrame` / `reduceSetFocusDepth` / `reduceSetFocusDirection` over `FocusViewState { viewMode, focusStack }`). The store only sequences fetch + commit: `applyFocusState` re-fetches the new top frame and commits stack + neighborhood together, so `focusNeighborhood` always belongs to the top frame and a failed fetch leaves state intact.
- `viewMode` interaction unchanged in spirit: entering module view clears the whole stack.

**Directional trace.** `CodeGraph::neighborhood(focus, depth, kinds, direction)` where `FocusDirection` is `Both` (default, the previous bidirectional behavior) / `Upstream` (`reverse_adj` only — callers) / `Downstream` (`forward_adj` only — callees). The direction applies at **every hop**, so an upstream trace never turns around and pulls in a callee of a caller. `Neighborhood` echoes the direction back; the enum is serde `rename_all = "lowercase"` to match the frontend union. The `get_neighborhood` command takes it too — no compat shim, all call sites updated. In the UI it is a `callers | both | callees` toggle on the breadcrumb's current frame; changing it refetches that frame.

## Why

Focus was a dead end: you could drill into one node's neighborhood and the only way onward was back out and in again, losing your place. A stack makes drill-down navigable, and the direction toggle separates the two questions the bidirectional blob could not — "who calls this?" and "what does this reach?".

## Updated test rationale

`packages/app/tests/focusReducer.test.ts` is rewritten rather than extended. Its assertions pinned the single-focus semantics this PR deliberately replaces (`reduceEnterFocus` overwriting `focusNodeId`, `reduceExitFocus` clearing focus in one step, Esc always exiting). The new file covers the stack semantics that supersede them: push / replace-top / pop-one / pop-to-frame / clear, successive-Esc unwind ordering, per-frame depth and direction, view-mode interaction, purity, derived accessors and breadcrumb labelling. No other existing test was touched; the Rust neighborhood tests gained the `FocusDirection::Both` argument and new direction cases alongside them.

## Expected conflicts with sibling branches

- **`feat/edge-drill-in`** (suggested to merge FIRST): overlaps in `graphStore.ts`, `graphViewModel.ts`, `FocusBreadcrumb.tsx`, `PixiRenderer.ts`. This branch already defines the `edge` variant of `FocusFrame` and handles it generically in the stack mechanics, breadcrumb trail (`focusFrameLabel` renders `A → B`) and reducers, but never constructs one — `fetchFrameNeighborhood` in `graphStore.ts` returns `null` for edge frames with a comment marking where `get_edge_detail` plugs in. Resolution should keep this branch's stack/reducer shape and drop the edge fetch into that helper, entering frames via `pushFocusFrame(frame)`.
- **`feat/pinned-selection`**: Esc handling moved out of `FocusBreadcrumb` into a new window-level hook, `packages/app/src/canvas/useEscapeKey.ts` (mounted in `App.tsx`), holding an explicitly ordered precedence chain — step 1 is a labelled slot reserved for "clear a pinned selection", step 2 is the focus-frame pop. Insert the selection check at that marker. If that branch instead consumes Escape in the capture phase, this hook needs no edit at all: it is an ordinary bubble-phase listener and simply never sees a consumed event. Either way the prose about Esc in `docs/OVERVIEW.md` / `docs/features/zoom_views.md` will conflict textually.
- **`feat/details-panel`**: no known overlap beyond `graphStore.ts` imports.

## Store API for siblings

```ts
focusStack: FocusFrame[];               // empty = unfocused; last = on screen
focusNeighborhood: Neighborhood | null; // always the top frame's

enterFocus(nodeId, depth?, direction?): Promise<void>;  // pushes a node frame
pushFocusFrame(frame: FocusFrame): Promise<void>;       // generic push/replace
setFocusDepth(depth: 1 | 2): Promise<void>;             // top frame only
setFocusDirection(direction: FocusDirection): Promise<void>;
popFocus(): Promise<void>;                  // Esc: one frame
popToFrame(index: number): Promise<void>;   // breadcrumb; -1 = root chip
exitFocus(): void;                          // clear the stack
```

Pure helpers exported from `graphViewModel.ts`: `nodeFrame`, `focusFrameKey`, `focusTopFrame`, `focusTopNodeId`, `focusIsActive`, `focusFrameLabel`, `truncateLabel`. Note `focusNodeId` / `focusDepth` no longer exist on the store; `focusTopNodeId(focusStack)` is the replacement (the `F` hotkey resolver still takes a `focusNodeId` field and is fed from it).

author: rukadeakshay01
body:
Our hole-to-hole check modelled every drill as a circle of radius `min(w,h)/2`. Upstream models a hole as a **`SHAPE_SEGMENT`**: a round drill is a zero-length segment whose width is the diameter, and a slot carries the milled axis. One model covers both — and the circle version silently **under-reports along a slot's length**, checking a 2 mm slot as though it were a 0.4 mm hole.

## What else the old check was missing

All upstream behaviour, not embellishment:

- **Co-located holes are their own violation** (`holes_co_located`), reported *instead of* too-close rather than as well as. Upstream's branch is an `else if`.
- **Two blind or buried vias sharing no copper layer are exempt** — they are drilled before the stack is laminated, so they cannot meet.
- **The minimum has the DRC epsilon subtracted**, so a hole placed exactly at the limit is legal rather than marginally illegal.

## Microvia drills

Microvias now report under `microvia_drill_out_of_range` rather than the general code — the whole reason upstream splits them is that the two carry separate severities in Board Setup. Via drills also gained a **maximum**, which only a rule can express.

## Tests

`qa/unittests/pcbnew/drc_holes.test.ts` — 15 tests. Three mechanisms mutation-checked: collapsing the slot back to a circle reddens the slot case, removing the blind-via exemption reddens that one, and making co-location non-exclusive reddens the else-if case. The slot test also checks that the axis **rotates with the pad**, since a slot fixed to horizontal would be wrong on any rotated footprint.

Full suite: 2133 passing, 188 files.

Part of #200 §B — takes it to 26 of ~72.

author: ioradsun
body:
## What & why

Follow-up to #111. Completes the audit's remaining steps (5–6): navigation feels local, and a dropped socket self-heals.

## Changes

- **`use-predictive-prefetch.ts`** (mounted in `Feed`) — warms the immediate neighbors' deck-core into the **same cache the deck reads**: next, next+1, previous — *nothing else*. Runs on `requestIdleCallback` so it never competes with the active navigation render. The likely-next market gets the full trio (market-change + evidence + creator); the others just the deck-core. `prefetchQuery` no-ops when data is fresh, so feed re-ranks don't refetch. `neighborIds` is pure/tested; the effect keys on the neighbor **set** so a poll returning the same neighbors doesn't re-run it.
- **`coordinator.ts`** — reconnect is **reconcile, not reload**. Beyond socket-error recovery, it now re-syncs the visible surfaces once (debounced) on the browser's own reconnect signals: window `online` and a hidden tab becoming visible (mobile suspends the socket in the background). Because the client refetches rather than folds deltas, a refetch **is** the resume — and the live tape resumes from its **own cursor** (its queryFn fetches only events newer than the row it already holds), so a reconnect replays just the missed tail.
- **`use-predictive-prefetch.test.ts`** — covers `neighborIds` (order, ends, dedupe, invalid).

## Verification

- Reducer + selectors: 27/27 assertions; `neighborIds` covered by its own vitest file (CI).
- Typecheck clean on all changed files.

## Status

**All six audit steps are now landed** across #109–#112: one snapshot, one socket (market_state + events + wallet_beliefs), one client reducer, patched cache, event-driven activity + positions, predictive prefetch, and reconcile-on-reconnect.

author: dbaldauf147
body:
## Summary
This PR enhances the cross-device synchronization system to keep devices in step continuously, not just at startup. It introduces tombstone-based deletion tracking to prevent deletes from being undone by stale devices, and implements last-write-wins conflict resolution for collisions.

## Key Changes

- **Continuous device synchronization**: Devices now re-sync whenever they come to the foreground, wake from back/forward cache, reconnect, or have been idle, ensuring they don't show stale history. Failed syncs now retry with backoff instead of staying device-only for the session.

- **Tombstone-based deletion**: Added a new `deleted` collection to track deletion tombstones (`{ kind, key, at }`). Deletes are recorded as tombstones and replayed on other devices, preventing them from being undone by stale syncs.

- **Last-write-wins conflict resolution**: When two devices edit the same item, the most recently edited copy wins, preventing re-labeling on one device from being reverted by another holding the old value.

- **Updated API contract**: Extended the `/api/games` endpoint to support the new `deleted` collection alongside `library`, `stats`, and `active`.

- **Documentation improvements**: 
  - Clarified the four-layer backup strategy
  - Explained profile-based isolation (name + passphrase)
  - Added guidance on troubleshooting different history across devices
  - Noted that profiles are whitespace-trimmed to prevent accidental splits

## Implementation Details

- The merge strategy remains union-based (no device can wipe another's data), but is now refined with tombstone replay and timestamp-based conflict resolution
- Profile codes are displayed in the sync line to help users identify profile mismatches
- The deletion tombstones are stored under their own Redis key, namespaced per profile like other collections

author: imolloy
body:
Fixes #324

initPanelButtons() unconditionally zeroed num_pumps/num_lights and wiped every button's special_mask while rebuilding the fixed button array for the detected panel type/size. This function runs via the bus auto-configure handshake (setPanelInformationFromPanelMsg(SIM_NONE) -> setPanelByName() -> setPanel()) whenever device_id isn't hard-coded (device_id=0xFF), which happens after config parsing has already built aqdata->pumps[]/lights[] from button_XX_pumpID/pumpIndex/pumpType etc.

The underlying pump/light struct data (including each entry's .button pointer back into aqbuttons[]) is untouched by this reset - only the num_pumps/num_lights counters and each button's special_mask flag are lost. processPentairPacket() matches pumps by scanning the fixed-size MAX_PUMPS array directly, independent of num_pumps, so raw bus data keeps updating pumps[0] forever - but everything bounded by num_pumps (matchPump() in iaqtouch.c, and the MQTT publish loop in net_services.c) permanently stops working after this one-time reset, even though the data driving it is fine.

Symptoms this fixes: "Got pump message '...' but can't find pump # N, please update aqualinkd.conf" logged forever despite correct config, and RPM/Watts/GPM/Mode/PPC never publishing to MQTT for a configured VSP even though the raw values are being read correctly off the bus.

Fix: capture num_pumps/num_lights before the reset, let the existing button-rebuild run unchanged, then re-apply the pump/light association (special_mask + special_mask_ptr) from the still-intact pumps[]/ lights[] arrays before returning.

author: wingedsheep
body:
## Why

Cards granting *"You may look at the top card of your library any time"* — Glarb, Calamity's Augur; Glowcap Lantern; Madame Web, Clairvoyant; The Lunar Whale; The Belligerent — already had a working engine half. `ClientStateTransformer` sends details for that card to its controller, and the Deck browser's **Library order** tab renders it face up.

The pile itself still drew a card back, so actually using the ability meant opening an overlay every time you wanted to remember what was on top.

## What

`ZonePiles.tsx` now renders entry **0** of the library zone face up whenever the server sent details for it — amber ring, 👁 badge, and the standard hover preview.

The library zone is always transmitted in full (opaque ids for unknown cards), so position is all the client needs, and the rule is simply *"whatever the server revealed"*. That keeps the client rules-free and picks up three cases at once:

- private peek — `LookAtTopOfLibrary` (the ask)
- public reveal — `PlayFromTopOfLibrary` / `RevealTopOfLibrary` (Future Sight, Goblin Spy), including on an opponent's pile, which is correct for those cards
- a scry/surveil the viewer just performed — the same knowledge the Library-order tab already shows, and cleared on shuffle by `LibraryRevealUtils`

No engine or protocol change: the masking decision stays entirely server-side.

## Screenshots

Deck pile, same scenario (Glarb on the battlefield, Lightning Bolt on top), before → after:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wingedsheep/argentum-engine/top-card-deck-pile-screenshots/crop-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wingedsheep/argentum-engine/top-card-deck-pile-screenshots/crop-after.png) |

## Tests

New `TopOfLibraryClientViewTest` pins the two properties the UI leans on, neither of which was covered before:

- position 0 of a library's `cardIds` is the top card
- `LookAtTopOfLibrary` is **private** — absent from an opponent's view, absent without the ability, and gone again when the source leaves the battlefield

body:
Hält die Entscheidung fest, damit sie nicht in einem halben Jahr neu untersucht wird.

## Anlass

`imapclient` bricht auf Python 3.14 (`imaplib.IMAP4.file` ist read-only geworden, upstream gefixt aber unreleased). `imap-tools` läuft dort, wird aktiver gepflegt und hat Type Hints — auf dem Papier die bessere Wahl.

## Warum trotzdem nicht

Gemessen, was tatsächlich über die Leitung geht:

| | Kommando |
|---|---|
| imapArc heute | `FETCH (ENVELOPE INTERNALDATE)` |
| imap-tools `headers_only=True` | `UID FETCH (BODY.PEEK[HEADER] UID FLAGS RFC822.SIZE)` |

`ENVELOPE` lässt den **Server** parsen und liefert strukturierte Felder in wenigen hundert Bytes. `BODY.PEEK[HEADER]` holt den kompletten rohen Header-Block — bei echter Mail mit Received-Ketten und DKIM 2–10 KB pro Nachricht, clientseitig zu parsen. Der billige Scan über tausende Mails beruht genau auf diesem Unterschied.

Das Verhalten zu erhalten hieße, die High-Level-API durchgängig über `mb.client.uid(...)` zu umgehen und imapclients ENVELOPE-Dekodierung (Adressstrukturen, RFC 2047) nachzubauen. Mehr Code, nicht weniger.

`imap-tools` ist die richtige Bibliothek für Anwendungen, die Mail *konsumieren*. imapArc will rohe Bytes und serverseitig geparste Envelopes, weil es archiviert — die angebotene Abstraktion ist genau die, die hier stört.

## Geprüft wurde außerdem

Alle vier kritischen Fähigkeiten sind in imap-tools erreichbar (`mark_seen=False`, `client.capabilities`/`client.uid` für UID EXPUNGE, Folder-Flags für `\Noselect`, NAMESPACE über `client`). Es scheitert nicht an fehlender Funktionalität, sondern daran, dass der Mehrwert für diesen Anwendungsfall nicht abgerufen wird.

Neu bewerten nur, wenn imapclient wirklich verwaist — nicht wegen Release-Frequenz.

author: trognes
body:
Step 0 of `cribs.md` §12: the two options from §8 that depend on nothing else in
that plan and are worth having on their own.

## `--full-text`

Prints the whole decrypted message under each progress line, wrapped and
indented, instead of the 19-character preview (16 under `-4`).

```
 -4.3335 B241 AAA QEW AB CD EF GH IJ KL                      THEQUICKANALYSISOFL
  THEQUICKANALYSISOFLONGMESSAGESISWHATMAKESTHISWORTHWATCHINGATALLXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
  XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
```

The preview is enough to notice a board turning into German and not enough to
decide a run is finished — which is what matters when the stop criterion is a
person reading the output rather than a score threshold.

Three things that matter in how it is built:

- **It prints below the line, not by widening it.** The columns are budgeted to
  land on exactly 80 and have to keep lining up whether the option is on or off.
- **Decoded on the fly from the current board**, the same reason the preview is:
  `m.plaintext` holds an earlier candidate while a climb is running.
- **Nothing on the hot path.** A progress line is emitted only when a board beats
  everything echoed so far, so this runs once per improvement — tens of times in
  a run — not once per board scored.

## `--no-plug LETTERS`

Marks letters as carrying no cable. It is the counterpart of `-s`: that one says
"these two are plugged to each other", this one says "this one is plugged to
nothing". Until now the only way to express it was to invent a fake pair.

Worth more than it looks, because a cable has two ends: each marked letter
removes 25 of the 325 candidate plugs, not one.

Both end up in the same `plug_fixed[]` mark, so the climb, the SA toggle and the
re-pair skip the letter for free — the difference is only the board they start
from (`-s` pairs its letters, `--no-plug` leaves its letters self-steckered).
Two places needed real work:

- **The `--random` kick.** It draws from self-steckered letters, which is
  exactly what a `--no-plug` letter looks like, so `perturb_steckerbrett()` now
  tests `plug_fixed[]` as well as `steckerbrett[i] == i`. Without this the kick
  would plug the very letters the option says are unplugged.
- **`--exhaust`.** Marked letters are excluded from its forced pairs (both the
  parallel first-pair list and the recursion) and come off its free-letter bound,
  so `--exhaust E` is refused when `E` no longer fits.

Fatal on a letter `-s` also plugs (the two statements contradict each other), a
repeated letter, a non-letter, or a run with no `-c` — the last for the same
reason `--random` needs `-c`: with no climb there is nothing to constrain.

## Testing

13 new checks, all sized to the property rather than to realism (one
fully-specified key for the display checks, 8 restarts for the climb ones):

- the full text round-trips to the plaintext, is absent by default, and stays
  within 80 columns;
- no marked letter appears in **any** converged board across the restarts — with
  a control showing that unmarked letters do get plugged, so the check cannot
  pass vacuously;
- `-T`-independence, the four rejections, and the `--exhaust` accounting
  (16 marked letters ⇒ 45 first pairs, `E`=5 accepted, `E`=6 refused).

`make test`: **322 passed, 0 failed**. Clean under `clang++ -Werror` and under
ASan+UBSan, including a 1024-letter message through `--full-text`. clang-tidy
reports nothing in the new code.

`make bench BASE=dev`: `search` **−0.4%**, `hillclimb` **+1.7%** — both inside
their noise floors (±0.5% and ±4.5%), as expected since neither option touches
the climb move loop or the scorers.

## Docs

`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `--help` document both options. `cribs.md` records
step 0 as done and notes that these two are built while the rest of §8 is still
a proposal.

A backlog entry that silently disappears teaches nothing; the reasoning error is the reusable part, so the entry is marked resolved with the actual explanation kept in place. Also did **not** touch C7, which is unaffected and still open.

## Tier 3 — Compliance flags

## Tier 4 — Verification

- **Unit tests**: `not-applicable` for this diff (markdown), but the underlying claim was verified by running the affected suite — see below.
- **Integration tests**: `not-applicable`
- **Metrics / logs introduced**: `none`

- **Perf numbers**: not applicable.

**Verification actually performed**:

| Claim | How verified |
|---|---|
| The fixture bug is already fixed | Read `ActivityView.test.tsx:150-175` on `main` — the `Math.max(1, …)` clamp is gone, replaced by a day-1 anchor with a collision nudge |
| The fix is #3042 | `git log -- driver-app/__tests__/components/ActivityView.test.tsx` → `0bb951e` "fix(driver-app): make ActivityView test date fixture day-of-month robust (#3042)" |
| It landed at 19:05 UTC | `git log -1 --format='%ci' 0bb951e` → `2026-08-01 13:05:39 -0600` |
| The test now passes on the 1st | `cd driver-app && TZ=UTC npx jest __tests__/components/ActivityView.test.tsx` on `main` at `7a53caa` → **6 passed, 6 total**, run today |
| CI tests the merge ref, not the branch head | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no explicit `ref:` on any `actions/checkout` step, so the `pull_request` default (`refs/pull/N/merge`) applies |
| Timing lines up | Failing runs are all before 19:05 UTC; the passing run (job `91408494120`) started 19:27:50 UTC |

**What was NOT verified**: I did not re-run the full `driver-app` suite, only the affected file — the claim being corrected is scoped to that one test. I also did not verify #3042's fix against a faked clock for other days of the month; that PR's own verification covers its approach, and this PR does not modify it.

**Pre-merge checklist**:

- [x] Ran the changed code against real Supabase dev (not just mocks) — if backend change — *n/a*
- [x] Tested with rider + driver + admin accounts — if multi-surface — *n/a, docs only*
- [x] Verified the rollback command actually works (not just exists) — if `risk:high` — *n/a, risk is low*
- [x] Updated `CLAUDE.md` / `.claude/context/*.md` if a convention changed — *no convention changed*
- [x] No PII added to logs, Sentry payloads, or analytics

---

### What actually happened

`pull_request` workflows check out the **merge ref** — the PR branch merged with its base — not the branch head. #3042 landed on `main` at 19:05 UTC. Every `driver-app-test` run on #3037 before that time tested a merge with a `main` lacking the fix and failed; the 19:29 run tested a merge with a `main` that had it and passed. My local run failed because that working tree was #3037's branch, based on pre-#3042 `main`.

So I compared CI's *merged* tree against a *stale unmerged* one and read the difference as a gate defect. Both results were correct; they were answers to different questions.

| Run | Tested tree | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `1b22c59`, `8f1b863`, `5d84857` (pre-19:05) | merge with `main` **without** #3042 | ❌ |
| `4a5c976` (19:29 UTC) | merge with `main` **with** #3042 | ✅ |
| local | #3037 branch on **pre-#3042** `main` | ❌ |

The original #3041 diagnosis was right and #3042 fixes exactly it. Only my later claim that it remained unfixed was wrong. #3041 is now closed, with the same correction posted there.

body:
## Summary
- Added an explicit lifecycle transition matrix with a guard test so every enumerated transition has named scenario/unit coverage.
- Reworked the review-steering selfcheck to reach Review via the real start + hook + session-summary projection route, then assert append-only transition history including the second in_progress entry.
- Tightened runtime-state-hub PR/projection tests to assert transition history, not only current column placement.
- Deleted the orphaned Playwright selfcheck spec/config and removed the CI Chromium install plus verify-script exemption. Chosen deliberately because the accepted lifecycle coverage is tRPC/server-route coverage; the browser wrapper only wrapped a tRPC steer and did not assert a UI-only behavior.

## Red -> Green
- Forced red by temporarily removing `hook` from `canWakeFromAnyReviewReason`; the rewritten scenario failed with: `Timed out waiting for card selfcheck-steer-review to have entered in_progress 2 time(s)`. Restored the code and the same scenario passed.
- The first rewrite also exposed a harness issue: the browser selfcheck had a fake fixture path and a 20s Playwright timeout. Since it did not assert behavior beyond the tRPC lifecycle route, I removed the Playwright selfcheck path rather than keeping it half-connected.

## Verification
- `git commit --amend` pre-commit hook passed: Biome staged check, `verify:precommit` including 121 fast test files / 1165 passed / 3 skipped and 68 web-ui test files / 524 passed.
- `npx vitest run test/runtime/verify-script.test.ts test/runtime/core/lifecycle-transition-matrix.test.ts test/runtime/server/runtime-state-hub.test.ts` passed: 3 files / 37 tests.
- `node --import tsx -e ...givenReviewCardWhenSteeredThenMovesToInProgress...` passed after restore.
- `node --import tsx -e import("./test/selfcheck/run-selfcheck.ts")` passed: 14 passed, 0 failed.
- `npm run build` passed before the cleanup amend.
- `npm run verify` was attempted multiple times; it failed during the full-parallel `test:fast` phase with unrelated git/worktree fixture timeouts in files such as `test/runtime/git-history.test.ts`, `test/runtime/state/workspace-state.test.ts`, `test/runtime/trpc/workspace-api.test.ts`, and `test/runtime/workspace/archived-worktree-reconciliation.test.ts`. The failed files I reran directly passed. This matches the known a654c flake; I am not claiming full-tier green.

## Retro
- Summary: Shipped test/harness coverage for lifecycle transitions rather than changing production behavior, and removed the dead Playwright selfcheck path instead of paying CI browser-install cost for nothing. The main judgement call is that no UI-level behavior was being tested by the removed wrapper.
- What fought back: `npm run verify` repeatedly timed out in unrelated parallel git/worktree tests; the same files passed directly, and pre-commit passed `verify:precommit`.
- Process: The card identified the synthetic Review setup correctly, but did not mention that `run-selfcheck.ts` routed this one scenario through Playwright while steering via tRPC anyway.
- Design: Transition coverage lived across scenarios and unit tests with no explicit ledger; `test/selfcheck/transition-matrix.ts` now makes that claim reviewable and keeps configurable-columns work honest.

author: dollspace-gay
body:
## What changed

- add the shipped bootable multicore-kernel design and all 16 requirement records
- extend Thermite with `u8`/`u16`, final mutable byte-slice contracts, and closed `platform(domain)` effects
- add the no_std `thermite-kernel` crate with generation-safe capabilities, memory, atomics, SMP, scheduler, synchronization, DMA/IOMMU, device, event/action, and service models
- add the frozen 104-operation `x86_64-pc-uefi-smp-v1` registry and a freestanding UEFI runtime
- implement real INIT/SIPI AP startup, xAPIC/IPIs, TLB shootdown, per-CPU state and timers, ring-3 syscall/fault handling, allocator/OOM behavior, PCI/virtio block DMA, entropy, reboot, and poweroff
- add Forge `kernel-image` publication with exact boundary matching, deterministic artifacts, tamper-evident receipts, validation, and replay
- add QEMU/OVMF nominal 1/2/4/8-CPU, AP-failure, and reboot release scenarios plus CI coverage

## Why

Thermite previously stopped at a verified freestanding rlib. This closes the proof and implementation closure over one frozen platform so the project can publish a real bootable multicore image while honestly reporting assurance as `to_platform_boundary`.

## Impact

The existing `--target kernel` library flow remains intact. The new `kernel-image` target is opt-in and fail-closed: registry drift, boundary drift, proof failure, artifact tampering, nondeterministic rebuilds, or incomplete boot evidence prevent publication.

## Validation

- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` with the repository-pinned EPR solvers
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- UEFI runtime Clippy for `x86_64-unknown-uefi`
- `forge check` at L3 for both kernel conformance programs
- Verus `--no-cheating` transition proofs
- requirement registry/status checks and formatting
- deterministic image build and independent `verify-build --replay --json`
- QEMU/OVMF: nominal 1/2/4/8 CPUs, injected AP-start failure, and reboot

Final local image SHA-256: `dc48e069a0edc6d23128da26e941339a5d6fd055d273b424bbc772f891efcd0c`.

author: aganesy
body:
## Summary

`qfai-implement` gates every TDD item on "the test actually fails for the
expected reason". That is the **entire** admissibility standard qfai shipped —
the phrase appears three times in the assistant tree, always as an obligation,
never as a definition, and `grep -rni "watch it fail|expected reason"
packages/qfai/src/` returns zero hits.

Two things follow.

**The inadmissible form is guaranteed by the skill's own ordering.** Phase Red
writes the test; Phase Green writes the production code. For any row that
introduces a new module or symbol — the normal case at the start of a spec — the
test file cannot import at Red time, so the only failure available is a
collection error. There was no step that created a seam first, and nothing said
the load error was not the RED. The gate was met **vacuously by construction**,
for exactly the rows where discriminating power matters most.

**The evidence contract could not record the difference.** `RED result` blessed
truncated output; there was no failure-mode field, no requirement that the
failure originate inside the row's own `Selector`, and no requirement that the
message name the owned predicate. The four Evidence hard rules bar status-only,
stale and empty entries — none of them bars a failure that would occur
identically if every assertion in the test were deleted.

## The criterion

`references/red-admissibility.md` states it both ways.

**Admissible** when all four hold: the test module loads; the failure is raised
by an assertion (or expected-exception check) executing inside the row's own
`Selector`; the message names the predicate the row owns; and deleting every
assertion would make the run pass.

That last clause is the one the whole gate exists for. It is the property RED is
supposed to establish, and qfai had no vocabulary for it — a case-insensitive
grep of the shipped tree for `mutation`, `vacuous`, `tautolog`, `falsifiab`,
`oracle` and `can fail` returned **zero** hits.

**Not a RED** — a *missing seam*: collection / import / module-resolution,
syntax, missing symbol or export, fixture or harness setup, or any failure
raised outside the row's `Selector`. Each proves the seam was absent. None says
anything about the assertions.

## Making the admissible form reachable

A criterion that the skill's own ordering makes unsatisfiable is not a fix, so
Phase Red gains **step 3a**: create the minimal seam the test imports — module,
export or signature with no behaviour — before running.

It is explicitly not Phase Green's production code: it implements no predicate.
Its only job is to turn a resolution failure into an assertion failure.

## Recording it

- `RED failure mode` — `assertion` | `expected-error` | `falsifiability`.
  **There is no admissible value for a load error**, which is the point: a row
  whose only failure was a load error has not observed RED yet.
- The truncation allowance is narrowed rather than removed: truncate the stack
  tail, never the assertion message and its location. Those are what demonstrate
  admissibility, so blessing their loss defeated the field before it existed.
- Gate item 3 and `constitution/workflow.md` now carry the criterion. Both
  previously restated the obligation and added nothing.

## The one legitimate exception

A correct test can pass on first run when a sibling row already satisfies the
obligation. That case already has its own evidence rules
(`red-not-observable.md`), and it is routed there explicitly —
`RED failure mode: falsifiability` — so it does not become a second, unaudited
way to accept a load error. "Never weaken a correct test in order to manufacture
a RED" is restated in the new file, because that is the pressure a stricter
criterion creates.

## Verification

- `tests/assets/redAdmissibility.test.ts` — 18 tests across both trees: the
  positive criterion, all four excluded forms, the vacuity clause, step 3a, the
  failure-mode field, the narrowed truncation allowance, and both mirrors
- `tests/assets/`, `evidenceContract` — 408 pass
- `SKILL.md` at 497 lines, under the 500 ceiling (the criterion lives in the
  reference; the skill carries the one-line rule and the pointer)
- `prettier`, `sync:ssot` clean

Fixes #361

author: anarkiwi
body:
## Bugs fixed

**1. `Shell.read_file` corrupted every chunk.** It ran `base64.b64decode` on the whole reply payload, but the firmware answers `fs read` with a JSON envelope:

```
{"data":"ewogICJmb3JtYXRfdmVyc2lvbiI6ICIxLjAiLAog...","read":96}
```

so it base64-decoded the envelope text itself. Now decodes `reply.json()["data"]`.

**2. The chunk size was in the wrong units.** `_read_limit()` returned `fs_caps()["read_max_bytes"]` (256 on `1.0.0-rc.37`/`rc.40`) and `read_file` then requested 256 *decoded* bytes, which base64-encodes to 344 characters, overruns the limit and truncates the reply. `read_max_bytes` bounds the base64 payload, so requests are now sized `read_max_bytes // 4 * 3` (192 decoded bytes; 96/request verified working on hardware). Exposed as `shell.decoded_limit`.

Together these meant no file could be read off the device correctly.

## Capabilities moved in from downstream

- **`fs hash`** — `ShellClient.hash_file` / `Videomancer.file_hash`. Advertised as `fs_hash: 1` in `fs caps`; a stable cache key for anything derived from a program binary, without dragging the file over the chunked read path.
- **Program manifest** — new `pyvmancer.programs` (`ProgramManifest`, `ProgramEntry`), read via `ShellClient.program_manifest`. Coverage is partial by design: firmware built-ins are not listed, so `ProgramManifest.missing(names)` reports which device-reported programs it does not describe.
- **Typed program parameters** — `const.ParamRole` + `classify_param`: `0..1` is a boolean resolving on at `BOOL_THRESHOLD`; a small integer range quantises to `max-min+1` positions (`Posterize 0..7` has 8, so sampling it at 32 steps wastes device time); `-` / `Null <n>` is unassigned. `ProgramParameter` gains `role`, `steps`, `assigned`, `crossfader`, `as_bool`, `sample_values`. The enumerable/sweepable boundary is the caller's own resolution, so it is a `sweep_steps` argument, not a constant.
- **`resync()`** — bounces `video timing` away and back to re-initialise the output raster, since no reboot verb short of `reboot bootloader` exists. The alternate standard is **discovered** from the firmware's own `video timing` usage string or supplied by the caller, never hardcoded. The bounce drops the input selection, so it is reasserted; lock flags lag the signal, so the outcome is polled; it leaves `overridden: true`. Verification is by `video status` only — whether frames are actually arriving is the caller's problem, as only the caller has a capture.
- **`video status` lock semantics** — `pyvmancer.video.VideoStatus`: the top-level `locked` flag tracks genlock so it reads false whenever timing is overridden, and the selected input's own sub-status is authoritative in both directions. Documented plainly as advisory: the firmware reports `connected: false` while passing video and a locked input while passing nothing.
- **Additive addressing** — `ShellClient.combined_values` and `Videomancer.park`. `Parameter = Manual + Modulation + MIDI`, so a CC is an offset; parking every manual value at a reference makes CC addressing absolute. Writes are paced (an unpaced burst of 24 messages drops the LSB of 14-bit CC pairs, leaving MSB-only values like 128) and the readback settles before verification (serial and MIDI are asynchronous). `PARK_REFERENCE` leaves P12 open because it is the crossfader and gates the output even when `program info` names it `Null 12`.

Also: `vmancer manifest`, `vmancer hash <path>`, `vmancer resync`; `CHANGELOG.md`; README/protocol/firmware-notes updated.

## Version

0.2.0 — bug fixes plus purely additive API on an 0.x line. Nothing was removed, but `read_file` now returns different (correct) bytes.

## Verification

No hardware was touched. Everything is exercised against the existing in-memory fakes.

```
pytest -n auto -q   496 passed, coverage 99.13% (gate 85%)
black --check       0
pylint pyvmancer tests  10.00/10, exit 0
```

author: zenglingbiao
body:
## Summary

Cancel unread Microsoft Teams Graph response bodies before releasing their guarded fetch resources.

The final branch is intentionally narrow:

- message metadata responses
- hosted-content collection responses
- existing hosted-content `$value` responses

The unrelated shared Gateway test-helper changes were removed.

## What Problem This Solves

`fetchWithSsrFGuard()` returns both a `Response` and a `release()` callback. The callback clears guard state and closes its dispatcher, but it does not consume or cancel an unread response body.

The message and `$value` non-ok paths released the guard with unread bodies. The collection path attempted to cancel first, but awaited that cancellation. Awaiting can deadlock when response capture has cloned and teed the stream because cancellation waits for the other tee branch.

Slow, large, or stalled Graph error bodies can therefore retain the pinned connection and dispatcher after the caller has finished handling the failure. Small finite JSON errors may already be buffered, so this PR does not claim every Graph error leaks a connection.

Microsoft Graph defines JSON error response bodies, and Undici requires callers to consume or cancel response bodies:

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/errors
- https://github.com/nodejs/undici#garbage-collection

## Fix

Add one local `releaseGraphResponse()` owner helper that:

1. starts best-effort cancellation when the response body is unread;
2. does not await cancellation, avoiding cloned-stream deadlock;
3. awaits the guarded fetch `release()` callback.

All three guarded Graph response owners use this helper. The shared SSRF guard remains unchanged because streaming consumers have different response-lifecycle contracts.

## Evidence

Exact reviewed head: `c37c2c9206ee995a7cfce583f4c42424731bdd85`

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox, fresh PR checkout, public network, no Tailscale, no instance profile, no hydration:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/attachments/graph.test.ts`
  - 1 file passed
  - 20/20 tests passed
  - run `run_2c674c8df4cc`
- Added regressions for:
  - failed message response cancellation
  - failed hosted-content `$value` response cancellation
  - cloned failed collection response where cancellation starts before release without blocking the operation
- Trusted-main pinned-dispatcher fixture:
  - stalled unread 500 + `release()` only: release completed after about 101 ms, while the server-side socket and response remained open after 1 second
  - stalled unread 500 + cancellation before `release()`: release completed in about 1 ms and the socket/response closed in about 5 ms
- `git diff --check` clean
- Autoreview clean, patch correctness `0.98`

## Scope

- Production: `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/graph.ts`, +10/-4, net +6
- Tests: `extensions/msteams/src/attachments/graph.test.ts`, +98
- No config, persistence, SDK, protocol, or user-visible behavior changes

author: jonathangu
body:
Two bugs found by playing the merged game in a browser rather than reading the
diff. `pnpm check` passes; verified by replaying a match at Ace and reading the
HUD back.

## The opponent was named after its seat

`buildMatchConfig` used `['Rookie', 'Rally', 'Pro', 'Ace'][index]`, indexed by
**seat**. In a duel the opponent is always seat 1 — so it was always called
"Rally", whatever difficulty you picked. Choose Ace, play someone labelled Rally.
`apps/room-worker/src/index.ts` had the same list and the same defect.

## "Rally" meant two things at once

That name collided head-on with the rally counter the fun pass just added. The
HUD showed `RALLY 2` — a player's score — directly beside `RALLY 0`, a rally
length, and left the player to work out which was which.

## Fix

Opponents are named from a new `AI_DIFFICULTY_LABEL`, keyed by the difficulty
they actually play at. The `rally` tier keeps its id — it is in the protocol and
in persisted room config — but displays as **"Steady"**, so "rally" means exactly
one thing on screen. Multi-AI rooms get "Steady 2", "Steady 3" rather than four
bots with unrelated names.

The rally chip also reads label-first (`RALLY 2`) to match the score pills next
to it.

## Why the tests didn't catch it

Neither bug is a logic error — both are about what a word means when it sits
next to another word. `tests/ai.test.ts` verifies the difficulty ladder by
counting goals and is entirely indifferent to what the opponent is called. This
is the class of thing that only shows up on screen, which is the argument for
driving the built app as part of review rather than only running the suite.

author: not-stbenjam
body:
## What changed

Pass `--skip-config-write` when OCP-42982 creates its explicit `p42982-1` project. The project is still created, and the test already supplies `-n p42982-1` to the subsequent command.

## Root cause

`openshift-tests` runs extension tests concurrently with the same injected `KUBECONFIG`. OCP-42982 used `oc new-project p42982-1` without `--skip-config-write`, so `oc` rewrote that shared file to select a context named `p42982-1`. Other test processes could load the kubeconfig during that update and fail before their test body with either:

```text
invalid configuration: context was not found for specified context: p42982-1/...
```

or the same error plus `cluster has no server defined`.

The 5.0 CI stability study found 79 such observations across 72 builds from April 7 through July 24, 2026, spanning AWS, Azure, GCP, and bare metal. Every observed dangling context was named `p42982-1`, while the victim test varied; the long-running OCP-42982 test overlapped the sampled failures.

## Impact

Retained JUnit was streamed for all 72 affected builds. Fifty-seven builds had a passing retry, 15 had at least one unrecovered context failure, and 6 failed Prow jobs had no independent blocking failure. The conservative historical counterfactual is therefore **6 additional green Prow jobs**; no aggregate parent is additionally counted because each affected parent retained an unrelated aggregation failure.

## Validation

```text
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p=2 -run '^$' ./test/e2e
```

### 💡 What:
Introduced a global `_PASSED_TESTS` execution tracker and a base `TrackingTestCase` in the test suite. Optimized `_run_module_suite` inside the `TestRefactoredSuitesStillPass` meta-test class to recursively extract the test cases in the loaded suite, and compare their IDs against `_PASSED_TESTS`. If they have already run and passed during standard discovery, `_run_module_suite` returns a mock successful result immediately, bypassing the redundant child runner execution.

### 🎯 Why:
During full test suite runs (e.g., via `python3 -m unittest discover`), the test runner runs standard discovery, executing all 23 tests in `test_pr_accessibility.py` and 11 tests in `test_readme_ux.py`. However, the meta-test suite `TestRefactoredSuitesStillPass` also loads and programmatically re-executes those identical test suites again. This means 34 tests were run twice, wasting CPU cycles and testing overhead.

### 📊 Impact:
- **Reduces total redundant test executions by 100% (34 bypassed runs).**
- **Saves CPU cycles** and setup overhead during full test suite runs.
- Maintains 100% regression safety, as running only `test_setup_class_optimization.py` still falls back to programmatically executing the target suites.
