author: bithighlander
body:
Gate-3 OLED capture found the address verification screen silently truncating any bech32 address longer than one line.

```
displayed  bc1p5cyxnuxmeuwuvkwfem96lqzszd02n6xdcjrs20
actual     bc1p5cyxnuxmeuwuvkwfem96lqzszd02n6xdcjrs20cac6yqjjwudpxqkedrcr
```

**20 characters dropped, with no indication anything was missing** — and the QR beside it encodes the *full* address, so the two disagreed. Someone "verifying" a receive address on the device was checking two thirds of it.

## This is not a taproot bug

The threshold is ~42 characters at body font, so it already affects **native segwit multisig on shipping firmware**:

| Type | Length | |
|---|---|---|
| p2wpkh `bc1q…` | 42 | fits exactly — which is why this went unnoticed |
| **p2wsh `bc1q…`** | **62** | **truncated today** |
| p2tr `bc1p…` | 62 | truncated |

Confirmed on the emulator for both. P2WSH before the fix:
```
displayed  tb1qr6xa5v60zyt3ry9nmfew2fk5g9y3gerkjeu6xxd
actual     tb1qr6xa5v60zyt3ry9nmfew2fk5g9y3gerkjeu6xxdz7qga5kknz2ssld9z2z
```

Targeted at `develop` on its own rather than folded into the taproot stack, since it fixes a live bug independent of that work.

## Cause

The address draws at `TOP_MARGIN_FOR_ONE_LINE + font_height + ADDRESS_TOP_MARGIN` = y=46, line height 14, on a 64px canvas. A second line starts at y=60, and `draw_char_with_shift()` checks `img->height + p->y <= canvas->height`, returns false, and `draw_string()` stops — **without reporting anything**. Silent truncation, not an error.

## Fix

Smallest lever first:

1. close the inter-line padding for multi-line addresses (14 → 10)
2. only if still short, raise the block by exactly the overflow

Both are needed, and the order matters:

- **Raising alone is wrong.** I tried it first. The QR is drawn *after* the text and overwrote the start of the raised first line — cost the first six characters. Trading one silent corruption for another.
- **Closing the padding alone is not enough.** The font is 10px, so two lines from y=46 need 66.

Together the second line lands at y=54..64, clear of the QR which ends at ~41.

Single-line addresses are untouched — the whole branch is gated on `calc_str_line() > ONE_LINE`.

## Verified

- both 62-char addresses render in full and legibly, QR intact
- p2pkh confirm screen unchanged (normal spacing)
- existing `test_msg_getaddress_segwit` suite still passes — 6/6 green
- both device variants build clean, zero warnings

Before/after captures attached in review.

author: axailotl
body:
## What

The encoding-smuggling scanner only examined base64 runs of 80+ chars, contiguous hex of 120+, and
percent-runs of 24+ groups. Published attack payloads are routinely shorter than all three, so a
smuggled override passed with **zero labels** — and since L1 is the first gate, it continued
downstream labelled clean rather than merely unscreened.

## Approach — option 2 from the bead, not lower thresholds

A run below the unprompted threshold is examined only when a **decoding cue** sits within a bounded
window either side of it, and it is flagged only when the decoded text **also** hits the injection
probe. Long runs keep their existing unprompted behaviour.

Simply lowering the thresholds would have fired on ordinary embedded images, inline hashes, and
identifiers — a screener that flags normal content makes enforce mode unusable, which is the same
failure mode from the opposite direction as `hrmrq.39`.

## Precision evidence

The `data:image` exemption is now **decisive even for a short cue-adjacent payload whose decoded
bytes are text-like**, and it handles parameterized data URLs (`;charset=utf-8;base64,`) that the
previous end-anchor missed. Asserted explicitly:

- a short cue-adjacent blob decoding to non-probe text stays silent
- plain `data:image/svg+xml;base64,…` stays silent
- parameterized `data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8;base64,…` stays silent

## Policy ownership

Candidate bounds, decoding cues, and the decoded-content probe move out of hardcoded constants into
`config/intake-l1-rules.json`, compiled fail-closed with the rule snapshot (`encoding-policy.ts`
validates ranges, rejects unbounded patterns, and refuses empty-matching regexes — no silent
defaults). Ten entries drop off the hardcoded-settings baseline as a result, per `7qeo1.15`/`.18`.

## Evidence

- Three corpus fixtures flip known-gap → enforced: `evasions-base64-01`, `evasions-hex-02`, `techniques-binary_streams-01`
- CogSec suite 690 passing; adversarial harness 40/40; local gate attested `5741e67bff45`
- No change-budget exception required

author: artback
body:
Refreshing everything on one cadence gets both halves wrong at once: the Tate changes its programme faster than a weekly sweep notices, and a village radio museum whose site last changed in 2019 is read fifty times a year to confirm it still says the same thing. With **54,168 distinct museum websites** and one request per host per second, the sweep budget is the scarce resource.

## `museum sweep` — a seventh subcommand, always up

A long-running service like `enrich`, kept out of the API process so an unbounded crawler never shares the request path. `-once` gives the batch form for cron; `-dry-run` shows the scheduler's decisions without reading anything.

Each site carries its own due date, adapted from what the last reads found:

| Signal | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing changed | interval × 1.5, to 60 days |
| Something changed | interval ÷ 2, to 2 days |
| **An exhibition closes on the 14th** | **due on the 15th, whatever the rate says** |
| Read failed | backoff × 2, parked after 6 |
| Never read | ahead of everything with a due date |

The closing-date rule is the one that earns its keep — the only moment staleness is certain rather than inferred. Everything else is left to settle per site, because nobody could configure 54,168 of them and any rate chosen centrally is wrong for most.

## Two gaps that had to close first

**Nothing recorded an attempt that found nothing.** The only evidence a site had been read was an exhibition row, so a museum read and found empty was indistinguishable from one never tried. The coverage report told callers *"nobody has looked here yet"* about areas read that morning, and every dead site was retried at full cost forever at Tate priority.

**Nothing removed an exhibition that vanished.** `SaveExhibitions` was a pure upsert, so a listing whose page was pulled stayed forever — and permanent displays, carrying no closing date, leaked permanently. Retirement is a column rather than a `DELETE`, and runs only after a read that found *something*: a site answering half a page would otherwise erase a museum's whole programme irreversibly.

## One reader, two callers

The scheduled sweep and the API's on-demand area scrape now share one code path. When they didn't, they worked against each other — the sweep reread sites the API had read minutes earlier, none of the API's work fed the interval, listings were retired down only one path, and an area the API had just scraped still reported that nobody had looked. That last one was a regression I introduced by moving coverage onto the attempt record; it has a test now.

## Found by running it, not reading it

- **Three sweepers starting together deadlocked applying the schema** and one died before it started. Always latent — the schema is applied on every start and this stack starts several processes at once — but a service worth running two of made it easy to hit. Schema application now takes an advisory lock.
- **A host that answered nothing at all was recorded as a museum that lists nothing.** The scraper skips failed pages quietly by design, so "unreachable" and "empty" looked identical to the sweeper — the exact distinction it exists to make.
- **The first read of a site was treated as a change**, which would have moved every site off the starting interval at once and in the same direction, on one sample with nothing to compare against.
- **The on-demand path went blind** once sites became rows, returning nothing for museums not yet discovered — the case someone panning a map to a newly crawled city hits first.

## Verified against real sites and a live Postgres

- Continuous run: discovered 4 sites, read them, `3 changed, 1 failed, 16 exhibitions`, clean SIGINT shutdown.
- **Three sweepers over four due sites performed four reads between them, not twelve.** This is the one that matters: getting it wrong means two crawlers pointed at the same museum's server. Claims use `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` with a 30-minute lease, so a sweeper killed mid-batch strands nothing.
- `-rate` caps sites per minute across the whole sweep, separately from per-host politeness, because on a first run every site is due at once.

## Notes for review

- `first_seen_at` and a `source` column are in but unused, so submissions and alerts need no backfill later: an alert is "what appeared since T", and a submission must never be retired because nothing will see it on a museum's site.
- `-due` moves off `refresh` onto the new command, leaving `refresh` area-based only.
- A museum with no coordinates is skipped by the sweep — its exhibitions could not be found by any radius query anyway — and joins by itself once enrichment places it.

`go vet` and the full suite pass, including the database tests against a live Postgres.

author: mirkofr
body:
## Problem

Phase 4 provides fitted probabilistic models and differentiable posteriors, but callers still have to construct random base samples manually. Phase 5 requires reusable posterior samplers for Monte Carlo acquisition functions.

## Solution

Add `motorch.sampling` with a stateful `PosteriorSampler` contract, IID normal sampling, scrambled Sobol QMC normal sampling, cached common-random-number base samples, explicit seeds, and cache reset behavior. Extend the posterior protocol with base-sample metadata required by generic samplers.

## Public API impact

Adds `PosteriorSampler`, `IIDNormalSampler`, and `SobolQMCNormalSampler`. The structural `Posterior` protocol now explicitly includes `base_sample_shape`, `dtype`, and `device`, which existing concrete posteriors already implement.

## Numerical behavior

IID samples use a local seeded `torch.Generator` and do not consume global random state. Sobol samples use PyTorch's scrambled Sobol engine and inverse-normal transform with endpoint clamping. Base samples are reused while shape, dtype, and device remain unchanged.

## Tests

Covers shape semantics, multidimensional sample shapes, batching, cache reuse and invalidation, seed reproducibility, reset behavior, dtype/device preservation, posterior gradients, state-dictionary behavior, invalid inputs, conditional CUDA behavior, IID/QMC standard-normal statistics, and posterior moment recovery.

## Benchmarks

No performance claims. Statistical tests use stable sample counts suitable for CI.

## Documentation

Adds `docs/sampling.md` and updates README, documentation index, and changelog.

## Compatibility

No new dependency. Uses existing PyTorch random generators, Sobol engine, and inverse-normal transform. Supports the existing Python 3.10/3.12/3.13 CI matrix.

## Risks and limitations

Sobol construction flattens posterior batch and event dimensions into the Sobol dimension and is not intended for extremely high-dimensional events. Cached base samples are runtime state and are not persisted in `state_dict`. Dedicated CUDA CI remains unavailable.

author: yhaspel
body:
Phase 5 of `development-plans/phase-05-forms.md`: fill an AcroForm and save the answers into the file, build a form on a document that has none, import/export the data, flatten.

## What ships

**Engine** — `apps/pdf_engine/engine/forms.py`: the read model (`has_form`, `is_xfa`, per-field type/rect/value/default/options/flags/placements), `fill_form`, `edit_fields_batch` (add/update/delete over six field types), `export_form_data` / `parse_form_data` (JSON + CSV, both layouts, BOM-tolerant). Flatten reuses the existing `flatten what=form`.

**API** — `GET …/form/`, `GET …/form/export/?format=json|csv`, and three operations on the job pipeline (`fill_form`, `edit_form_fields_batch`, `import_form_data`). Both isolation sweeps extended to the new endpoints.

**Frontend** — `FormsFacade` plus Forms mode:
- *Fill* hands the page to PDF.js so the user types into the real widgets, mirrored through `[(formData)]`; a field panel gives the same values a keyboard route, with export/import and flatten-behind-a-confirm.
- *Form builder* draws field boxes on the Phase-3 overlay, with a property panel (name, options, required/read-only/multi-line, alignment, size). A whole builder session commits as **one** `edit_form_fields_batch` — one version.
- `/fill-pdf-form` tool page, prerendered and in the sitemap.

## Four PyMuPDF limits, measured not assumed

| Limit | What was done |
|---|---|
| Radio widgets raise "bad xref"/"bad rect" and give every kid the same `Yes` on-state | Group written at the pikepdf level: one parent field, N kids, per-kid appearance-state rename |
| `field_value = ""` + `update()` silently writes nothing | Empty `/V` written through the xref — this is the "clear" step of the import round-trip criterion |
| `/AcroForm` may be an inline dict, so resolving it by hand misses half of all XFA files | Path lookup `xref_get_key(catalog, "AcroForm/XFA")` |
| The phase doc says PyMuPDF cannot create `/Sig` fields — it can | pyHanko used anyway: it is what consumes the field in Phase 8, and `SigFieldSpec` carries seed values the Widget API cannot express |

The radio group's temporary kid names also needed a printable separator: a `\x00` does not survive PyMuPDF's string writer, and the pikepdf pass then found no kids and quietly produced loose checkboxes.

## Two bugs the E2E run found that are not about forms

1. **The PDF viewer had no credential — in view mode too.** `GuestFacade.principal()` is a `computed` over `TokenService.isAuthenticated`, which was a plain localStorage getter. With no signal behind it the computed cached whatever it read first; evaluated once on the login page it stayed `null` for the session, so `authHeaders()` sent the viewer's own fetch (which bypasses the HTTP interceptor by design) with nothing attached. Every document 404'd and no page ever rendered, for accounts and guests alike. No test caught it because none asserted that a page draws. `TokenService` now holds the token in a signal.
2. **A job that failed before its handler stayed `running` for ever.** `registry.get_op` sat outside the worker's try, after `mark_running` — so a worker holding a stale registry left the client polling a job that could never reach a terminal state. Moved inside.

## Acceptance criteria

All five ticked with evidence in `PROGRESS.md`. Deviations are in the Decisions log; the one that touches a normative doc is §10's `import_form_data` row, amended from "file ref" to the inline payload the op actually takes (there is no generic file-upload endpoint — §13's `uploads/…` is images only).

## Gate

Fresh stack `reset.sh --yes && up.sh && test.sh --e2e`:

- backend **517 passed** (was 453) · frontend **104 passed** (was 84) · e2e **21 passed** (was 17)
- coverage `apps` **92%** (gate 85) · `pdf_engine` **93%** (gate 90)
- `spectacular --fail-on-warn` 0 warnings / 0 errors · `ruff` clean · `manage.py check` clean

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Self-review — four lenses, eighteen further defects, all fixed on the branch

**Correctness** (each reproduced before being fixed):

- **A radio option that is not already a bare PDF name could never be selected** — including `Option 1`, the builder's own default text. The option is stored as a PDF *name*, so it is escaped on write (`Option#201`) and handed back raw, and `field_value` re-escapes whatever it is given. Labels are decoded on the way out, and the selection is now written at the PDF level (parent `/V`, kids' `/AS`).
- **Any field placed on two pages was misread as a radio group** — a signature line repeated on every page of a contract is the commonest AcroForm shape there is. It ended up with no options, and the "nothing selected" cleanup then erased its value, so export blanked it and the UI drew a choice list with no choices.
- **Radio kids stayed registered as top-level fields** (the `/AcroForm/Fields` filter ran after `/T` had been deleted) and **a deleted group left a dangling parent**, so update — being delete-then-add — produced two fields with the same name. Invisible to us; visible to Acrobat and to the pyHanko pass Phase 8 will run.
- **An export→import round trip wrote `/V ()` onto every `/Sig` field**, after which pyHanko refuses to sign it.
- **The pyHanko box lost the page origin on a rotated page** — `~transformation_matrix` only carries it at rotation 0.
- **Dragging a field reset its max length, alignment, font size and default**, because an update re-adds from the spec and those were never in it.
- **The radio auto-layout clamped instead of reflowing**, stacking every option past the page bottom into one box.

**Security** — ownership, `Content-Disposition`, PDF-name injection and data-remanence on delete all came back clean, and the guest path was walked end to end anonymously. Three findings: `values` and `data` were the only unbounded params in the schema file and are retained on the Job row and echoed on every poll (measured 11 MB from a single `GET /api/jobs/`); the unknown-name error echoed the entire payload (900 KB); and Export CSV passed spreadsheet formulas straight through (CWE-1236). All three fixed, plus the read model is now capped at 2 000 fields — a 30 000-widget PDF inside the guest caps measured 4.3 s of API CPU and an 11 MB response.

**Regression** — the token fix above had turned each browser tab into a private session: a login, logout or refresh rotation in one tab became invisible to the others, so a tab that still believed it was anonymous would mint a *guest* session and a logged-in user's upload would quietly acquire a 24-hour TTL. Both tokens are now signals seeded from storage and refreshed on the `storage` event.

**Plan conformance** — phase-05's named appearance-stream mitigation ("golden pixel checks on two zoom levels") did not exist and now does; `align` was write-only, so the property panel showed Left for a centred field and wrote that back over it; the PDF-native flip lived outside `geometry.py`, where §8 says conversions live; and "visible in external viewers" is now asserted with pypdf — a second library — as Phase 3 did.

**Gate re-run after the fixes**, fresh stack: backend **534** · frontend **114** · e2e **21** · coverage `apps` 92% / `pdf_engine` 93% · spectacular 0/0 · ruff and `manage.py check` clean.

author: absence0760
body:
Three pieces that make the watch UI — and the simulation of it — look and work like a product, plus the tooling that verified them. ADRs 426–428.

## 1. The sim window renders a device (ADR 426)
`SharpMipDisplay.cs` drew a 230x144 strip: flat gray bezel bars, outlined boxes, 5x7 labels. It now renders the panel at 3x (each LCD pixel a 3x3 cell with a darkened inter-pixel gap, the texture real MIP glass shows) recessed behind glass inside a bezel ring inside a gradient-shaded case, with the five keys as rounded tabs carrying their §350 function words. The static shell composes once into a cached backdrop, so a repaint stays an `Array.Copy` + panel blit. `DumpFrame` — the byte contract every sim assertion reads — is byte-identical before/after, and `HitButton` shares the key painter's geometry arrays so the click map cannot drift. `sim/shell_harness/` (dotnet + stubbed Renode types) is the loop that renders it on a machine with no Renode; `bin/watch-preview.sh` renders every host-composed page to a contact sheet with just cargo + ImageMagick.

## 2. A live clickable watch window that needs no Renode UI (ADR 427)
The macOS arm64 .NET Renode build cannot start its Avalonia UI from a terminal (renode/renode#886) — it falls back to a stdin console that reads the backgrounded launch's closed stdin as `quit`, so `--gui` died 0.1s after boot. `watch-sim.sh` now names that cause, and `bin/watch-view.sh` + `sim/live_view.py` provide the working route: a Tk window attached to the running headless sim's telnet monitor, polling `DumpCanvas` ~5 fps, resolving clicks through the display model's new monitor-callable `HitButtonAt`, and firing the virtual-time button macros (a raw press/release over a socket lands under the firmware's ~10 ms poll). Closing the window detaches; the sim keeps running — verified live. pnpm aliases: `watch:view`, `watch:preview`, `watch:sim:idle`.

## 3. The 8x16 text face becomes Spleen (ADR 428)
Every text row was Source Code Pro thresholded to 1-bit at 8x16 — the pipeline behind the ragged look and a whole failure class ('+'=='-', invisible '|', '!' reading as ':'). Spleen 8x16 (BSD 2-Clause, vendored at tag 2.2.0, digest-pinned) is drawn pixel-by-pixel for this exact cell: uniform strokes, heavier ink, every pixel intentional. Same 8x16 monospace cell, so every layout budget and row-pinning face test holds by construction. `gen_font.py` loses the rasteriser entirely — a pure bit transcription of the BDF, reproducible by construction. The numeral hero faces stay rasterised from Source Code Pro Bold (§292/§339), where the small-size failure mode does not exist. Two test pins rewritten for the properties they actually protected (bar-glyph weight consistency; the medium hero being a native rasterisation rather than a row-doubling, with a control leg).

## Verification
- Host: full watch sweep green (28 suites), sharp_mip/render clippy clean, MCU release build green.
- Sim (renode 1.16.1, macOS arm64): full 23-page BTN4 cycle closed + idle faces + settings menu captured with the new font and shell; `DumpCanvas` returns the 724x548 device window as designed.
- Live viewer: attached to a running sim, rendered, macro presses landed, sim survived window close.

Note on ADR numbering: this branch was cut while upstream ADRs advanced past the numbers the work was authored under; the final commit renumbers the three entries to 426–428 and fixes the internal references. Some intermediate commit messages still carry the old numbers — content is correct throughout.

body:
The headline problem: signups had been silently failing for three weeks. Cold outreach and Supabase Auth shared one Resend quota, the daily outreach run consumed it every morning, and /signup returned 500 for the rest of the day. Nine people created accounts they could never confirm, including a logistics company and five would-be agents. Nobody noticed until a job applicant typed "error sending confirmation email" into the live chat.

Email
- Auth moved to Amazon SES on loadboot.com, with DKIM and a custom MAIL FROM domain. It no longer shares a quota with anything.
- Outreach moved to mail.loadboot.com on Resend. Separate domain, separate reputation; a complaint storm on cold email cannot reach a password reset.
- delivery-worker v12 pins outreach.* to the marketing identity before the dispatch and billing rules run. DISPATCH_RE matches the word "carrier", so outreach.carrier.* had been sending from dispatch@loadboot.com — the address that carries real load mail.
- bl_out_0194 gives outreach a hard daily ceiling above its existing warm-up ramp, configurable in one settings row, with a staff alert when it truncates a run.
- bl_ops_0193 watches the signup funnel hourly and raises an incident when confirmations stop landing. It caught this outage on its first run.
- The call CTA in every email was slimmed to one line above the footer; the card it replaced outweighed the actual call to action and wrapped badly on phones.

Live chat
- bl_lc_0190: a dispatcher with two years' experience asked to apply for a job four times and was never shown careers.html — she got a setup answer, then the dispatch service, then instructions for installing the mobile app. That last one was a matcher bug: the bare pattern 'app' trigram-matches "apply". Narrowed, and a job-application answer added above the dispatch-service row.
- bl_lc_0191 / 0192: the bot now speaks Spanish. A visitor opened with "Hola", explained his background in Spanish and was answered three times in English before leaving. English behaviour is untouched — Spanish routes to its own flow, and only 'es' is ever stored, so a visitor who switches mid-conversation is still picked up. Sixteen Spanish knowledge-base answers cover pricing, loads, verification, payments, jobs and signup trouble.
- bl_lc_0188 / 0189: the bot was still handing out the retired 737 number; it now reads from retell_config and can never go stale again. The setup prompt offered a role the system doesn't have while omitting dispatcher. Greetings used full names. Follow-up promises had no timeframe.

author: mostafaaymansaber
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a complete segmented landing page system for Wise Advances, a merchant cash advance (MCA) broker. The application generates 37+ dynamic landing pages targeting different business segments (industries, geographies, intent-based, and industry-geo combinations) from a shared template and content configuration system.

## Key Changes

- **Content-driven architecture**: Created `SegmentContent` type contract in `src/content/types.ts` that defines the structure for all landing page configurations. Each segment (industry, intent, geo, industry-geo) exports a `content` object matching this schema.

- **Segment registry**: Built `src/content/index.ts` to aggregate all 37+ segment files into categorized exports (`industrySegments`, `intentSegments`, `geoSegments`, `industryGeoSegments`) used for route generation and content lookup.

- **Shared landing page template**: Implemented `LandingPage.tsx` as the master template that renders Hero → How It Works → Why Us → FAQ → CTA sections, with all content driven by the `SegmentContent` object passed to it.

- **Reusable section components**: Built content-driven section components:
  - `HeroSection.tsx` — renders headline, subheadline, CTA, and hero benefits
  - `HowItWorksSection.tsx` — static 4-step process
  - `WhyUsSection.tsx` — renders dynamic "why us" points from content
  - `FaqSection.tsx` — accordion-based FAQ from content
  - `ApplicationSection.tsx` — form with validation, analytics tracking, and GHL webhook submission

- **Application form system**: Created `src/lib/application.ts` with form validation, error handling, and integration with GoHighLevel (GHL) webhook for lead capture. Form tracks analytics events and captures UTM attribution.

- **Analytics & attribution**: Implemented `src/lib/analytics.ts` for GA4 tracking and `src/lib/attribution.ts` to capture UTM parameters and referrer data on first visit.

- **WordPress integration**: Added build scripts for WordPress embedding:
  - `scripts/prerender.mjs` — prerenders all routes to static HTML for SEO/first-paint
  - `scripts/build-wp-embeds.mjs` — extracts main content and creates self-contained HTML fragments with scoped CSS/JS
  - `scripts/wp_push_new_pages.py` — Python script to push generated fragments to WordPress via REST API with Basic Auth

- **Dual build system**: Configured separate Vite builds:
  - Main build (`vite.config.ts`) — full SPA with React Router
  - Embed build (`vite.embed.config.ts`) — IIFE bundle for WordPress embedding with scoped Tailwind CSS

- **Styling**: Set up Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui primitives, custom color variables (HSL-based), and scoped embed variant (`tailwind.embed.config.ts`) to prevent style leakage into WordPress theme.

- **UI components**: Added shadcn/ui primitives (`Button`, `Accordion`) and supporting utilities.

- **Navigation & pages**: Built `NavBar.tsx`, `Footer.tsx`, `MobileStickyBar.tsx` for consistent layout, plus utility pages (`Terms.tsx`, `Privacy.tsx`, `AllPages.tsx` listing all segments).

- **Environment configuration**: Created `.env.example` with GA4 Measurement ID and GHL webhook URL placeholders.

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Content-first design**: All 37+ landing pages are generated from a single template + content files, making it trivial to add new segments or update messaging across all pages.
- **SEO-ready**: Each page has unique `seoTitle`, `seoDescription`, and structured H1/subheadline via `SeoHead.tsx` and `Helmet`.
- **Analytics tracking**: Form start, field changes, and submission are tracked to GA4 with segment context.
- **WordPress-native**: Prerendered static HTML + scoped CSS/JS bundle allows dropping pages directly into WordPress without proxy/rewrite config.
- **Validation**: Form validates business name, email (regex), phone (10+ digits), and required dropdowns; errors display inline.

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: Hardcoded JWT secrets ("secret", "dev-secret-change-me") were used as fallbacks in CLI tools, scripts, and shell launchers.
🎯 Impact: If the `PINAK_JWT_SECRET` environment variable is not set, the system falls back to a known, hardcoded secret, allowing attackers to mint valid JWTs and bypass authentication completely.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Wires three task groups into the generalization harness from #393, adds a provider-neutral model runner so real models (not just scripted policies) can produce eval rows, and ships a checked-in zero-shot transfer matrix over two reference models.

Stacked on `devin/1785616605-generalization-harness` (#393) and merges `devin/synthetic-verifier-fixtures` (#394) for group C, so the diff includes #394's fixture files.

**Groups** (`src/generalization-registry.ts` is the single source of truth for descriptors, frozen hashes, and expected per-split task counts):

| group | source | tasks | splits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `automationbench-simple-api` | `src/automationbench-offline.ts` | 72 | 48/12/12, seed 7 |
| `event-categorizer` | `skills/design-simulated-environment/examples/event-categorizer/` via new `src/event-categorizer-offline.ts` | 12 | 8/2/2, seed 7 |
| `synthetic-workflow-shapes` | `src/synthetic-workflow-offline.ts` (#394) | 9 | 5/2/2, seed 7 |

Group A's frozen holdout hash is asserted against the pinned `a22a8e98…f5a62701` in tests. Group B is a **new TypeScript port** of the existing Python verifiers example's rubric (category 0.7 + priority 0.3, structured-output/nonempty as subscores) so it scores offline with no Python, network, or live tools.

**Model runner** (`src/generalization-model-runner.ts`): one text-only protocol across Anthropic Messages and Fireworks OpenAI-compat, so the two providers are comparable — the model must emit one JSON object per turn (`{"tool":"api_fetch","arguments":{…}}` / `{"tool":"finish"}`), parsed by balanced-brace extraction from prose or fences, with a single corrective repair turn before the episode ends. Provider-native tool schemas are deliberately not used. `temperature: 0`, bounded 429/5xx retries, injectable `Transport` for zero-network tests, per-call receipts (tokens, latency, HTTP status, truncated raw reply) and optional full transcripts. A `BudgetLedger` reserves estimated USD *before* accepting a response and throws rather than overspending:

```ts
reserve(prompt, completion, price): number  // throws if spent + usd > budgetUsd
```

**Hard errors added to `deriveGeneralizationReport`** (all previously silent or absent):
- per-group `frozen_split_sha256` — a holdout row is checked against its own group's hash, falling back to the manifest hash
- `require_content_hashes` — a row missing `provenance.task_content_hashes.{env_sha256,verifier_sha256}` aborts the analysis
- `expected_task_counts` per group × per-arm `eval_splits` — the allowed split set is `arm.eval_splits ?? manifest.eval_splits ?? ["holdout"]`; an undeclared split, a missing declared split, or a per-split count that disagrees with the registry aborts
- `require_all_groups_scored` — a declared non-`planned` group with no scored rows aborts

Scoring is now computed **per arm** (`report.arms[].score`) with an aggregate over arms that are not `exclude_from_score`, so a scripted demo can no longer contaminate the headline number.

**Checked-in run** (`experiments/generalization-transfer-matrix/`: manifest, rows, receipts, transcripts, `report.json`, `report.md`), zero-shot, no training:

| Arm | AutomationBench | Event Categorizer | Synthetic workflows |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| zeroshot-haiku-vs-gptoss | +0.410 (n=24) | +0.258 (n=12) | +0.148 (n=9) |
| mechanism-demo (excluded) | ◆ +1.000 (n=72) | -0.400 (n=12) | -0.074 (n=9) |

Candidate `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` vs baseline `accounts/fireworks/models/gpt-oss-20b`; A on dev+holdout, B and C on all splits; 0/45 transport errors per model. `train_groups: []` for the zero-shot arm, so every cell is a transfer cell and `in_domain_gain`/`generalization_score` are honestly `null` — the diagonal fills in when a tuned checkpoint is dropped in. The `mechanism-demo` arm (oracle on A, deliberately degraded on B/C) exists only to exercise the diagonal, negative transfer, and the forgetting penalty end-to-end; it is flagged `mechanism_demo: true` / `exclude_from_score: true`.

Absolute means behind the deltas: Haiku 0.91 / 0.68 / 0.15 vs gpt-oss 0.50 / 0.42 / 0.00. Both models are weak on the synthetic workflow shapes. Parse-failure rates (share of rows with ≥1 unparseable reply) are 54-58% for gpt-oss-20b and 11-29% for Haiku — a real property of the text protocol under a small reasoning model, reported rather than prompt-tuned away.

Estimated spend $0.33 total ($0.015 Fireworks + $0.315 Anthropic, list-price assumptions, receipts are estimates not bills), against a $60 ceiling.

**Plug point for tuned arms**: a tuned checkpoint arm supplies only a rows file, model id, and optional receipt path; its rows must carry the same task ids and the same content hashes as the baseline, which the parity gates enforce. `understudy benchmarks generalization-run --group … --model … --provider … --budget-usd …` generates those rows for any registered group.

Verified: `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `git diff --check`, and focused offline tests (`tests/generalization.test.mjs`, `tests/generalization-transfer-matrix.test.mjs`, `tests/synthetic-workflow-offline.test.mjs`, 45 tests). body:
Closes #16

## Summary

- `YNAB_DEMO=1` (or `true`) runs the stdio server against a canned, entirely fictional **Demo Budget** — no `YNAB_TOKEN`, no YNAB account.
- Implemented as a fixture-backed `fetch` (`src/demo.ts` + `src/demo-fixtures.ts`) injected into the existing `YnabClient` seam from ADR-0001. Tool handlers, schemas, and client methods have no demo-specific branching — the client can't tell the difference.
- Fixture data: 3 accounts (checking/savings/credit card), 4 category groups / 15 categories with budgeted/activity/balance, ~34 transactions with realistic (fictional) payees across June–August 2026, and 4 scheduled transactions.
- Every response is wrapped and shaped exactly like a real YNAB API response, so it validates through the same Zod schemas in `src/schemas.ts` as live traffic — a malformed fixture fails the test suite.
- Writes (create/update/delete transaction, bulk update, update category budget, create account/payee/scheduled transaction, etc.) mutate the in-memory state for the life of the process. State is per-process and discarded on exit.
- `src/stdio-config.ts` extracts the bootstrap's "should we exit, and why" logic out of `src/index.ts` (mirroring `worker-config.ts`'s existing pattern), making it unit-testable: `YNAB_DEMO` truthy makes `YNAB_TOKEN` optional; otherwise the missing-token exit behavior is unchanged.
- README documents demo mode as a supported, credential-free way to try the server.

## Design notes / deliberately left out

- Categories carry a single budgeted/activity/balance snapshot representing the *current* month; every `/months/:m` endpoint returns that same snapshot rather than tracking a full per-month ledger. Documented in `demo-fixtures.ts`.
- `last_knowledge_of_server` delta filtering is accepted but not honored — full state is always returned (with the current `server_knowledge`).
- Payee locations and money movements return empty (valid, coherent) lists — no GPS/money-movement fixture data.
- Scheduled-transaction recurrence math isn't simulated; `date_next` is just set to the requested `date` on create.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` (tsgo --noEmit, oxlint, oxfmt --check, vitest run) passes — 171 tests, 33 new.
- [x] `test/demo.test.ts`: read path (list_budgets/list_accounts/list_transactions/list_categories/list_scheduled_transactions/get_budget/get_month "current" alias, budget-alias resolution, unknown-budget 404) — all validated through the real client + Zod schemas.
- [x] `test/demo.test.ts`: write path (create/update/delete/bulk-update transaction with balance adjustment, payee auto-creation, update_category_budget, create_scheduled_transaction, create_account) and a `handleTool`-level create-then-list round trip.
- [x] `test/demo.test.ts`: read-only gating still rejects write tools when combined with demo mode.
- [x] `test/stdio-config.test.ts`: `YNAB_DEMO=1`/`true` starts without `YNAB_TOKEN`; unset/falsy `YNAB_DEMO` still requires it; toolsets/read-only/budget-id passthrough.

author: inferenceailab
body:
Closes #205. Fourth story of M9.

## Why

Retirement is refused while instances hold a version (#203), so an operator needed a way to *see* what is holding one. Otherwise the only way to find out is to attempt the removal and read the error.

## What

`/api/workflows` reports `activeInstances` per version, and the placeholder workflow list becomes a real view: id, version, input type, and whether the version can be retired.

## One grouped query, not one per version

A host with fifty versions would otherwise make fifty round trips on a page an operator reloads. The EF Core provider groups **in the database** rather than pulling active records back to count them — which would make the page cost proportional to how busy the engine is, exactly backwards.

## A default interface member, deliberately

Eleven test doubles implement `IWorkflowStore` by delegating to an inner store. Forcing each to hand-write a method it does not care about would add eleven copies of one line and make the next addition worse.

The default is **correct and slow** — it lists and groups in memory — and both shipped providers override it. A contract nobody wants to extend is a worse outcome than a default that is right but unoptimised, and the comment says which it is.

## The screen and the engine agree by construction

Both count non-terminal instances of the exact `(id, version)`. A scenario asserts it directly: the version reporting none retires, the one reporting one does not, and the refusal's count equals what the screen showed. A page disagreeing with what the engine allows would be worse than no page.

Versions nothing is running are **absent** from the store's answer rather than reported as zero — the store knows what ran, only the registry knows what is registered. The API turns that absence into a zero so a client never has to.

## The zero-as-string scenario is not hypothetical

`activeInstances` generates as `number | string` because the served document declares int32 as either, and `'0'` is **truthy**. A template testing it loosely would report every idle version as busy — the exact inversion an operator would act on.

## Verification

- `dotnet test` — 658 passing (80 API, 358 core, 220 specs), 0 failed
- `npm test` — 189 passing · `npm run lint` / `build` — clean
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` — clean
- OpenAPI snapshot and generated client regenerated — the contract test doing its job

author: paddione
body:
## Summary

**Root cause:** `scripts/arbitration/detect.sh` and `apply.sh` called `"$GH_AXI" pr list --json ...` with the default `GH_AXI=gh-axi`. But gh-axi (v0.1.22) **never emits JSON** — `pr list` prints a human-readable table and `api` prints `key: value` lines. Every run therefore hit `jq: parse error: Invalid numeric literal at line 1` → `Found 0 cluster(s)` → Merge Arbitration **never judged**, independent of the runner being up.

**Second latent defect:** even with a JSON-capable CLI, the scripts parsed a **GraphQL shape** (`labels.nodes`, `statusCheckRollup.state`) that real `gh pr list --json` does not produce (it emits REST arrays: `labels:[{name}]`, `statusCheckRollup:[{status,conclusion,__typename}]`). The test stubs encoded that fictional shape, so tests passed while production was dead.

**Fix:**
- Default `GH_AXI` to `gh` (the real CLI, same convention as `scripts/factory/babysit-prs.sh:72`); env override kept for tests.
- `detect.sh`: parse `labels` as array (`map(.name)`); derive ci_state from `statusCheckRollup` array (FAILURE on red conclusion, "" empty, SUCCESS only when all completed green — pending stays eligible, matching the fail-open design).
- `apply.sh`: `check_idempotent` reads `.labels // []` instead of `.labels.nodes`.
- Test stubs in `tests/spec/merge-arbitration/*` updated to emit the real `gh` REST shapes.
- Design doc updated (`gh-axi` → `gh`).

Runner-side root cause (host reboot left the GitHub Actions runner service stopped; unit re-enabled 2026-08-01 23:05) was already fixed operationally — this PR closes the code-side blocker.

## Test Plan
- `bash tests/unit/lib/bats-core/bin/bats tests/spec/merge-arbitration/` → 6/6 ok
- `task test:changed` → 52 pass
- `task freshness:check` → clean, no generated drift
- Live `bash scripts/arbitration/detect.sh` with real `gh` → clean `[]`, no jq parse errors (previously `jq: parse error` + `[: : integer expression expected`)

body:
Bumpt `psgscoring[ml]` 0.13.0 → 0.13.1. **Geen scoringswijziging** — elk profiel is byte-identiek, bevestigd door de golden-harness.

**De kern: een voetnoot bij de ★-kolommen.** De kop leest `★★★ ≥0.85`, een kaal getal dat als percentage gelezen wordt. Dat is het niet. Gemeten tegen de twaalf onafhankelijke scorers van PSG-IPA correleert die score met de fractie scorers die een event markeert op **r = 0,19**, en ligt het niveau ruim **30 procentpunt** te hoog — een event dat als `★★★ ≥0.85` verschijnt wordt door ongeveer **44%** van de scorers gemarkeerd.

De voetnoot zegt nu wat de score is: een rangschikking naar hoe goed het event aan de AASM-criteria voldoet, geen kans. Toegevoegd in nl/fr/en/de.

Verder komen twee rapportvelden terug die het breath-profiel stil liet vallen:
- `min_spo2` — de saturatienadir per event, voorheen leeg
- `hypopnea_central` / `hypopnea_mixed` — subtypering, nu overgeerfd van het overlappende envelope-event

psgscoring 0.13.1 staat live op PyPI.

author: stingd85
body:
## Phase 6A — triage gate. No feature code in this PR.

Adds `docs/PHASE6_CLIENTLESS_CONTROLLER_TRIAGE.md`. **Awaiting review before anything is built.**

## Your correction is confirmed

Re-derived the clientless list myself across 1,856 client files, **including** `Planscape.Server/src/Planscape.API/wwwroot` and **excluding** `wwwroot/_next/**` and `wwwroot/vendor/**`.

`PublicConfig` (`api/public-config`), `RoleBuckets` (`api/state-machine/role-buckets`), `TenantKeywords` and `TenantBimManagerRoles` are all called from `wwwroot/js/dashboard.js` — the last two also from `wwwroot/index.html` and `wwwroot/app/index.html`. Not clientless, left alone. (My first grep used the wrong needles and found nothing; corrected before reporting.)

All ten in the brief are confirmed clientless by exact route-string grep. **Two more are too:**

- **MaterialSync** (`api/MaterialSync`, 53 ln) — not on your list, and it has a security finding.
- **PhotoExport** — already scheduled as Phase 5, listed for completeness.

## Three findings that change the plan

### S1 — MaterialSync is a cross-tenant read

`[Authorize]` and **nothing else**: no `[ProjectAccess]`, no membership check, no tenant filter. And it **bypasses EF entirely** — it reads/writes `ContentRootPath/App_Data/material_snapshots/{projectId}.json` directly (`:31-35, :47-50`).

Because it never touches EF, **the global tenant query filter cannot protect it.** Any authenticated user in any tenant who has a project GUID can `GET api/MaterialSync/snapshot/{id}` and read that project's material library.

This is not a UI gap. It is an authorization fix, and it is independent of every client decision below. Not touched — flagging for your call.

### B1 — WorkOrders and GlobalIdRegistry have no table

Both are in the EF model snapshot — `b.ToTable("WorkOrders")` (`PlanscapeDbContextModelSnapshot.cs:8910`), `b.ToTable("GlobalIdRegistry")` (`:2372`) — but **no migration creates either**. Grep for `name: "WorkOrders"` / `name: "GlobalIdRegistry"` across all non-Designer migrations: nothing.

On a database built by `dotnet ef database update`, every action on these two throws "relation does not exist". **Missing migration, not missing UI** — which moves both to Tier 3 regardless of their merits.

Worth recording the opposite result for WorkOrders' *downstream*: `StingTools/BIMManager/PlatformEvents/ParamStampEventHandler.cs` is a real handler that writes the parameter onto the Revit element. So the K2 loop is live and the feature genuinely completes — once the table exists.

*Caveat:* I could not check the production database. The tables may exist there via another path. That is exactly what the runtime pass would have settled.

### C1 — ApprovalChains duplicates a mechanism that already ships

| | route | client |
|---|---|---|
| `DocumentsController` | `POST /documents/{id}/approval-request`, `PUT .../approval/{aid}`, `GET .../approval-status` | **mobile** (`endpoints.ts:1005,1012`) |
| `ApprovalChainsController` | `/documents/{docId}/approval-chain` + `/decisions` | none |

The chain version adds multi-step and parallel approval, so it is not simply redundant — but "wire a client" is the wrong first question. Shipping a UI for the second without deciding which is canonical produces **two approval records for one document**.

## Both docstring-drift examples confirmed

- **Mfa** — `:13` says *"Production implementation would use a TOTP library (e.g. Otp.NET)"*. It already does: `using OtpNet;` (`:5`), `IDataProtector` (`:23`), `totp.VerifyTotp(req.Code, out _, new VerificationWindow(2, 2))` (`:119`) — the ±2-step window you described. Implementation real, comment wrong.
- **DeviceTwins** — `:11-12` claims it *"Powers the mobile Live tab (RAG list)"*. There is **no Live tab** in `Planscape/app/`; the only case-insensitive match is `de`**live**`rables`. Telemetry ingest does exist and is registered, so the downstream is not dead — but the claimed consumer isn't real.

Neither fixed here, because 6A carries no code.

## DI is clean across the group

All six injected services resolve: `IAuditService` (`Program.cs:428`), `ITenantContext` (`:365`), `IDeviceTwinService` (`:727`), `ITwinBindingService` (`:729`), `IPlatformEventService` (`:724`), `IDataProtector` via `AddDataProtection()` (`:506`).

So the known-prior failure mode — a controller 500ing on every call from a missing registration, misreported by the browser as CORS — **does not apply to any of these ten**. My first grep reported all six as unregistered; that was a false negative from a too-strict pattern, caught before it reached the report.

## Tier recommendations

**Tier 1 — CdeContainers.** Agreed, and I verified your note: the gate at `:255` is `ProjectRole in {Manager, Admin, Owner}`, a vocabulary that **is** assignable from the web dropdown today, so unlike the PM gates it is **live**. It must **not** be folded into Phase 1's `CanCurateProject` without a deliberate decision — that helper also admits `Coordinator` and three ISO codes, which would *widen* who can restructure the CDE folder tree. Backed, scoped, DI-clean.

**Tier 1 — DataRights: STOP, as you anticipated.** `POST erase` touches `Users`, `Projects`, `ProjectMembers`, `Documents`, `ProjectModels`, `Issues`, `Invoices`, `Subscriptions`, `AuditLogs`, `Tenants`. I have **not** yet traced whether each is a soft-delete, an anonymisation or a hard delete, nor whether `cancel-erase` can genuinely undo it. No button should ship until the UI copy can describe truthfully what it destroys. That trace is read-only and needs no server — it is the first thing I would do in 6B.

**Tier 2** — `AssetDataSheets`, `OfflineManifest`, `Mfa` (fix M1), `ApprovalChains` *after C1 is decided*.

**Tier 3** — `WorkOrders` + `GlobalIdRegistry` (blocked on B1), `DeviceTwins` (fix M2; needs a real telemetry consumer decision), `CaseStudy` (sales-ops, not product parity).

**Out of band** — `MaterialSync` (S1).

## ⚠️ Runtime column is NOT measured

Item 2 requires exercising every action against a running server. I could not:

- Docker Desktop is installed but its daemon would not start (`npipe:////./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine` — no such file; launching the app left no process in `tasklist`).
- No local Postgres listening on 5432.
- SQLite is not a substitute — `Program.cs`'s schema block issues a Postgres-only `information_schema` query with no try/catch, so the host dies before serving a request.

Where a static proxy exists I used it and labelled it: **DI registration** (clean) and **migration presence** (found B1). What remains unmeasured: real status codes and error bodies per action, whether the two missing tables exist in a deployed database, and whether anything 500s for a reason not visible in source.

**To close it I need** the Docker daemon started, or a Postgres reachable on 5432 plus a connection string. Happy to run the full runtime pass and amend this table once either exists.

## Notes

Docs-only, no code. Known-broken CI: "Build & Test / CI Gate" fails on a Postgres container (`role "root" does not exist`) — pre-existing on `main`, unrelated.

body:
## Summary

Restore Windows Terminal-compatible keyboard navigation in gabCode’s retained WPF terminal surfaces.

## Why

WPF treated terminal arrows, Tab, and Shift+Tab as focus navigation when the terminal had focusable WPF siblings such as the splitter. This moved focus out of the native terminal before the pinned terminal engine could translate the input.

The repair uses the established WPF navigation-containment pattern on the terminal-content wrapper. It avoids a custom raw-key forwarder, a gabCode key-to-VT mapping, and any Microsoft Terminal source/binary patch.

## Related work

- Issue: #17
- PRD: `Documentation/design/windows-terminal-input-compatibility-prd.md`

## Changes

- Contain directional navigation within each terminal surface.
- Cycle Tab navigation within each terminal surface so both Tab and Shift+Tab remain terminal-owned.
- Remove the failed top-level `HwndSource` keyboard-forwarding experiment and its synthetic routing tests.
- Add a regression asserting the terminal surface’s WPF navigation contract.
- Document the WPF hosting requirement and the Shift+Tab `Cycle` distinction.

## Validation

```text
pwsh -NoProfile -File eng/windows-terminal/Build-WpfControl.ps1 -Verify — PASS

dotnet build GabCode.slnx --configuration Release --no-restore — PASS, 0 warnings/errors

dotnet test GabCode.slnx --configuration Release --no-build — PASS, 33/33

git diff --check — PASS

Windows manual validation — PASS:
- arrows and shell completion navigation
- Tab and Shift+Tab
- Pi Shift+Tab thinking-mode behavior
- splitter does not consume terminal arrows
- Ctrl+Tab remains available for higher-level navigation

Independent upstream-control reproduction — PASS:
- upstream WPF `TerminalControl` plus a splitter and focusable sibling reproduced the escape
- `DirectionalNavigation=Contained` and `TabNavigation=Cycle` retained arrows, Tab, and Shift+Tab
```

### Platforms tested

- [x] Windows

author: scc33
body:
## The bug

The instrument wall was clipping every figure it published.

Sixteen instruments sat in one uniform auto-row grid that had no idea how tall a fitted gauge actually is. Each was handed ~174px for ~250px of content and painted its figure, vintage line and history strip *outside* the card, underneath the tile below. At 1280×720 the wall showed needles and no numbers at all — I had to pull values out of the DOM to know what my own economy was doing.

The perverse part: it got **worse** the more surveys you funded. A blank plate is 88px; funding it turns it into a 245px dossier card. The reward for playing the capacity mechanic well was a less readable screen.

Three more defects in the same area:

- **Dial faces were redrawn under their own needles** — bounds derived from the trailing 24 prints, so approval at 55 sat mid-dial one quarter and left-of-centre the next purely because the window rolled. Needle position carried no meaning across time, which destroys the one skill the game asks for.
- **The REVISED stamp fired on ~67% of instrument-quarters** — effectively every gauge, every quarter. A warning that never turns off carries zero bits, and this one is load-bearing for the §3.4 political-capital mechanic.
- The ledger and corridor tiles demanded 474px in a 199px bay; the corridor's square viewBox letterboxed itself into a third of its space.

## The change

**Board + rack + docked.** Four player-pinned instruments at full size, then every instrument as a fixed-height strip in a stable order — the whole measurement apparatus at a glance, unfitted ones included, each still in its own era's register. Click a strip to pin it; a fifth pin evicts the oldest. Pins live in `localStorage` (a view preference, not part of the save).

The rack being fixed-height and complete is what makes this structural rather than cosmetic: the wall's minimum height becomes a number instead of a hope.

Also in scope:

- **Fixed per-indicator dial faces** (`ui/src/domains.ts`), measured with the new `pnpm ranges` tool rather than guessed from units. Off-scale readings peg at the rail with a chevron — going off the dial is information, not a reason to rescale. Only `capital_stock` ratchets (175→900 over a century has no honest fixed face), monotonically by construction.
- **Marks the rules put on the face**: the electoral threshold on the approval dial, zero on growth/inflation/credit. You know where the line is in law; you don't know exactly where you are against it. That gap is the game, and it was invisible before.
- **Quarter-on-quarter deltas** on every instrument, at both maturities and in the rack.
- **Revision stamps carry their delta** (`REVISED +2.1`) and now fire on ~10% of instrument-quarters.
- **Space advances the quarter**, Escape closes overlays. A century was 400 trips to a button.
- The four duplicated `Record<IndicatorId, …>` label tables are now one compile-enforced table.

## Engine impact: none

Bit-identical. `ELECTION_WIN_THRESHOLD` is newly exported from the engine barrel so the approval dial can print the line — that is the entire engine diff. Random-policy batch is unchanged (200×120: 26% deposed, same percentiles, no NaN, no price explosions).

## How this is pinned down

Every bug here was a **layout** fact, and layout facts are untestable without a layout engine — a jsdom render test would have passed happily throughout the entire period the wall was clipping its own output. Rather than bolt a browser onto CI, the *decisions* moved out of the components into pure modules that can be tested:

| test | holds |
|---|---|
| `wall-plan` | the wall fits 1280×720, computed not hoped; reports headroom (24 more indicators) and fails at zero |
| `gauge-domains` | re-measures a surveyed century, rejects any face an instrument spends >2% of its life pegged against |
| `revision-stamp` | firing rate stays in 3–18% — guards both wallpaper and a fog mechanic that silently stopped biting |

Two of these caught real bugs while being written:

1. The ratchet wasn't monotone — the narrow-range branch recentred on a moving midpoint, so a new low could drag the upper bound *down*. Exactly the bug fixed faces exist to prevent.
2. The stamp gate I'd already "fixed" was still firing 67% of the time. That's how I found a **final print confesses zero error band**, so any band-relative test divides by zero and stamps everything. It now needs two gates: wrong by more than twice the band confessed on the *first* print, **and** far enough to visibly move the needle (6% of the dial).

Because these tests re-measure rather than snapshot, a future engine retune that pushes an instrument off its dial fails loudly and names the instrument.

For the part that genuinely can't be unit-tested, `WallTile` owns the fit contract (`overflow-hidden`, definite `minmax(0,1fr)` rows, `min-h-0` on the body) so following it is the path of least resistance. `CLAUDE.md` gets an add-an-indicator checklist (two steps are compile-enforced via total `Record<IndicatorId, …>` tables) and the browser one-liner that is the whole regression check for this bug class.

## Reviewer notes

- Verified in the browser at 1280×720, 1440×820 and 1728×1080: no scroll, nothing below the fold, at both dossier and terminal maturity.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, 126 tests, coverage 99.5% stmts — all green.
- The label-table consolidation is a slightly wider diff than strictly required. Adding an indicator was previously four edits across four files with no compiler help; that's the decay path this milestone is meant to close.
- Known remaining gaps, deliberately out of scope: the Narrow Corridor still doesn't move (`CorridorPlot.tsx` has said "static until Layer 3" since M2), and an election is still one line of ticker text. Those are M6.

author: alejandrotatum
body:
## Qué pasaba

`reports/page.tsx:584-585` declaraba constantes locales `TH`/`TD` que **duplicaban** `ui/Table`. Al copiar la primitiva se quedó con dos valores viejos y perdió las dos correcciones de accesibilidad que la primitiva sí tiene documentadas:

| Elemento | `ui/Table` | La copia en reports |
|---|---|---|
| Relleno del encabezado | `bg-sunken` (`#F4F4F7`) | literal `bg-[#FAFAFB]` |
| Texto del encabezado | `text-ink-3-strong` | `text-ink-3` |

Las tres tablas de `/reports` servían su encabezado a **4.21:1** mientras el resto del producto estaba en AA.

## Alcance real: tres sitios, no dos

El issue nombraba reports y el encabezado falso de Horarios. Buscando el literal aparece un tercero que no estaba registrado:

- `reports/page.tsx:584` — encabezado de tabla.
- `groups/page.tsx:1030` — encabezado falso de Horarios. Ya usaba `text-ink-3-strong`; solo le faltaba el relleno.
- `payments/page.tsx:212` — barra de título del visor de comprobantes.

El criterio de aceptación pedía **cero** `bg-[#FAFAFB]` en `frontend/src/`, así que los tres quedan en `sunken`.

## Dónde va el guard, y por qué no en el candado

El impulso era agregar un eje de color al candado de valores arbitrarios. No corresponde: el candado deja los colores fuera de alcance **a propósito** y lo dice en su cabecera (`arbitrary-style-values.test.ts:44-46`), remitiendo a la guarda de paleta.

Así que el guard nuevo vive en `color-contrast.test.ts`, que es su dueño. Dos tests: uno para el valor retirado, y uno para la regla — ningún `bg-[#hex]` en `frontend/src/`. Un hex escrito a mano se saltea toda la escalera de superficies que ese archivo demuestra; ya está mal antes de que nadie lo mida.

El guard filtra comentarios antes de buscar: `Table.tsx:15-18` explica largamente por qué el relleno dejó de ser ese literal, y una regla que se dispara con la explicación de sí misma enseña a borrar la explicación.

## Verificación

- Los dos tests nuevos fallaban antes del arreglo, listando los tres archivos.
- Suite completa: 148 archivos, 2381 pasan, 3 skipped.
- `tsc --noEmit` limpio, `next lint` sin warnings.

Closes #34

author: paoloantinori
body:
## Summary

- Declare the direct `io.apicurio` inter-module dependencies that 34 modules were consuming via transitive resolution only (66 added `<dependency>` entries, zero deletions, no versions: all covered by the root `dependencyManagement`)
- Evidence-based, not blanket: entries and scopes come from serial (`-T1`) `dependency:analyze` runs over the full 67-module reactor; the per-module extraction plan was cross-checked entry-by-entry against the final diff
- **Scope rule applied:** scopes follow where references actually live, not what `analyze` prints (it reports the resolved scope). Concretely: seven of `app`'s schema-util additions (asyncapi, openapi, graphql, xml, xsd, wsdl, iceberg) are referenced only from test code and are declared `test`; iceberg looks main-referenced at first glance but those are `app`'s own same-prefix REST packages, and the full reactor compiling with it at `test` scope is the mechanical proof
- **`-Dlocal` tier preserved:** four serde test dependencies live in `app`'s existing `local-excluded-test-deps` profile (their modules are absent from the `-Dlocal` reactor); verified with `./mvnw -T1 validate -Dlocal` (37 modules, all green)

## Why

Issue #9134: a future pom refactor of any intermediate module could silently break up to 34 modules that currently compile by accident. Declaring the direct edges is additive robustness; the resolved dependency set of this build does not change.

One framing caveat for reviewers: consumer-visible poms do gain direct entries, which in mixed-version downstream graphs can change nearest-wins mediation depth and exclusion reach. Within this reactor nothing changes; external consumers pinning older Apicurio artifacts should be aware. Also worth a note: `serde-common` now declares its real (pre-existing) compile edge on `apicurio-registry-java-sdk`, previously hidden behind `schema-resolver`.

Follow-ups deliberately not in this PR: a CI gate to prevent drift recurrence belongs to the `dependency-check` profile work (#9136 / PR #9152); the unused-declared cleanup is #9135.

Closes #9134.

## Test plan

- [x] Full reactor `./mvnw -T1 install -DskipTests -Dfull -DcliSkipNative`: green (proves no cycles)
- [x] `./mvnw -T1 validate -Dlocal`: green (local tier resolution intact)
- [x] `dependency:analyze` re-run: `io.apicurio` used-undeclared warnings 66 -> 0 (verified with two independent parsers)
- [x] All 66 entry scopes cross-checked against the analyze logs; `app`'s seven test-only entries additionally re-derived from source references

body:
## Sammanfattning

- `listaProjektMedRetry()` i `scripts/check-staging-preflight-wiring.mjs` — G0-stegets `playwright --list`-anrop får 3 bounded försök (200/400 ms backoff) innan fail-closed exit 64. Sju instanser på två dygn (#505, main 08:51, #527, #524, #539, #557×2) delade samma signatur: FÖRSTA `--list`-anropet faller i sandlådekopian medan 15+ efterföljande anrop i samma sandlåda körde felfritt — buffert/last under parallell CI-körning, inte trädinnehåll (kortets § Belägg för transient).
- Två av instanserna konsumerade merge-kö-armeringen (`failed_checks`-dequeue) — ett fjärde `autoMergeRequest`-läge CLAUDE.md § Landning-tabellen inte täckte. Tillagt i tabellens befintliga form + en kort förklarande paragraf.
- Varje misslyckat försök loggar rå stdout + `os.loadavg()` — gratis rotorsaks-instrumentering utan egen mekanism (väg 2 tillgodosedd, väg 3 mät-först avstått öppet — se kortets AC #1-motivering).

## Tvåsidigt bevis (AC #2), som testfall

`scripts/test-check-staging-preflight-wiring.mjs`:
- **G3** — transient: 1:a `--list`-försöket faller, 2:a lyckas → grönt, exakt 2 anrop.
- **R16** — deterministiskt/uttömt: faller VARJE försök → kastar efter exakt `PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_FORSOK` (3) anrop, aldrig grönt.
- Negativ kontroll körd manuellt (ej i sviten): `PLAYWRIGHT_LIST_FORSOK=1` → G3 föll korrekt röd, R16 opåverkad — bevisar G3 inte är vakuöst grönt.

## Bifynd under bygget

`main()`-gränsens import-guard bytt till `import.meta.main` (Node 24+, repots engines-golv). Den äldre `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(argv[1]).href`-formen (samma mönster som `purge-staging-sentinels.mjs`) gav en TYST false-negativ (`main()` körde aldrig, exit 0 utan utdata) när testsviten körde denna vakt-kopia från `/tmp` på macOS — `/tmp` är en symlink till `/private/tmp`, `import.meta.url` realpath-upplöses, `pathToFileURL(argv[1])` gör det inte. Mätt under bygget: hela G0–R15-sviten föll tyst innan felet spårades. Ingen funktionell ändring för normal CLI-körning (verifierad oförändrad).

## Test plan

- [x] `node scripts/test-check-staging-preflight-wiring.mjs` — 23/23 gröna (exit 0)

author: karlkfi
body:
Q501's remaining work was two measurements. This closes one of them off a capture already in the repo, and instruments the run that takes the other.

## Phase 0 was already answered — the repo had the capture

[Q468's retention probe](docs/plan/archive/q468-jobcompleted-retention.md) cancelled a real workflow run and recorded the result: `POST …/runs/{id}/cancel` accepted, and the job's `JobCompleted` with `result: canceled` on the scale set's message queue **~0.2 s later** (2026-07-28). The observation is load-bearing enough that the spelling — `canceled`, one L — is what `scalesetstub` was corrected to.

That is the trigger Q501 set out to find. Downstream of it the actuator is also already built: `completeJob` → `CleanupScaleSetJob` → `markJobCompleted` stamps `actions-gateway.com/job-completed-at` on the worker, and the reaper deletes a pod still `Running` five minutes later (the Q420 arm, proven against a real apiserver by `TestV2_RunnerSet_OrphanedRunningPodReaped`).

So the ScaleSet worst case is two graces, not the job's remaining runtime — against classic's whole remaining job, bounded only by `maxWorkerLifetime` (12 h). **Q501's unbounded form is classic-only**, on a tier removed at `v2.0.0`, so candidate B (a per-run REST poll) is not worth building. No Tier C run was needed to establish any of this.

What stays unmeasured is recorded as such: Q468's cancel had no runner attached, so the composed cancel→queue→stamp→reap chain has never been observed as one number for a job with a live worker. Neither residual can move the bound above the two graces, which is all Phase 0 was asked to decide.

## Phase 2 rides along on the run the spec already makes

Candidate A — does `renewjob` stop being honoured once GitHub concludes a cancelled job — is now read by `E2E_GitHub_CancelledRunLeavesNoDeletionMark`. It baselines the renew loop's two failure lines before the cancel and reports what the window added, and samples the `deletion-reason` stamp alongside phase and `deletionTimestamp` so a renew-loop teardown shows up on the pod as well as in the log. A reclaim stamps the worker `job_abandoned` before deleting it, which makes the answer a *positive* observation on both branches rather than an absent log line. The verdict lands under `Q501 candidate A outcome`.

## The assertion had to move with it

The spec demanded a terminal phase carrying **no** `deletionTimestamp`. That was right when nothing could delete this worker — Q501's actuator now can, so a working gateway would have failed the spec on its next run. It asserts instead that no terminal phase carries a deletion mark **the gateway cannot account for**: the shape [Q502](docs/design/04-operational-flows.md) actually recovers, and the property Q459 was protecting all along.

## Docs

- `docs/operations/troubleshooting.md` claimed the defect "applies to both acquisition tiers"; the Phase 0 finding contradicts that. Corrected, with the tier difference, the metric to expect, and the caveats on the ten-minute figure.
- `docs/design/04-operational-flows.md` §4.2 step 7 gets the same scoping.
- Q501 moves to Deferred — nothing is buildable until the reading lands, so it is an Event trigger rather than a Queue position.
- **Q595 filed** for a hazard in the runbook's own workaround: a hand-deleted worker matches `externallyDeletedBeforeTerminal`, so the AGC would ask GitHub to re-run a run the operator deliberately cancelled. Source-read and flagged as unmeasured; the runbook now warns about it.

## Testing

`make check` green, including `build-tags-check` (`go vet -tags …,e2e`) over the changed spec. The jsonpath the sampler now uses was verified against a real apiserver for the absent-annotation case (returns empty, exit 0) rather than assumed. The live reading itself needs a Tier C run.

author: joepetjr
body:
## Summary

Dependabot's grouped `npm-deps` bump keeps proposing two majors that **cannot pass CI in this repo**, because both require a newer Node than the declared floor. `package.json` sets `engines.node: >=18.17.0` and CI runs an `18.17 / 20 / 22` matrix.

**`chalk` 6** requires Node `>=22`. The 18.17 and 20 legs fail `EBADENGINE` before a single test runs.

**`vitest` 4** declares `engines.node: ^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0` — Node 18 unsupported. Its bundled `rolldown` imports `styleText` from `node:util`, added in Node 20.12, so the 18.17 leg dies at **startup**:

```
SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:util' does not provide an export named 'styleText'
```

Because the bump is grouped (`patterns: ["*"]`, deliberately), a single un-installable dependency reds the whole group and hides every other update travelling with it. That is what happened to #386, and it also masked a real defect riding along with it — the plugin loader fixed in #396.

This adds `ignore:` entries holding both below the breaking major so the group stays mergeable. Grouping itself is unchanged (still weekly + wildcard for both ecosystems). Together the entries stop dependabot recreating the bump closed as #386.

Both stanzas are deliberately self-expiring: each comment states the same exit condition — raise the Node floor, trim the CI matrix, delete the entry and take the major — so this does not become a permanent silent pin.

`@vitest/coverage-v8` is held alongside `vitest`; the two are version-locked and a split would break the suite on its own.

## Test plan

- `.github/dependabot.yml` parsed with the repo's own `yaml` dependency. Valid YAML; both ecosystems still present; the `npm-deps` group still reads `{"patterns":["*"]}`; `ignore` resolves to:

```json
[{"dependency-name":"chalk","versions":[">=6.0.0"]},
 {"dependency-name":"vitest","versions":[">=4.0.0"]},
 {"dependency-name":"@vitest/coverage-v8","versions":[">=4.0.0"]}]
```

- The vitest 4 startup failure above is quoted from a real CI run on this repo (18.17 / ubuntu-latest).
- `npm test` — 168 files, 2225 passed | 59 skipped, exit 0.
- `npm run verify:docs` — `docs-gate: OK (29 checks, 29 docs)`, exit 0.
- `npm run test:fixture` — 5 passed, exit 0.

No source or runtime files touched; installed versions are unchanged.

author: rianfc
body:
# Pull Request: Features, Improvements, and Refactoring from RianFC Fork

This Pull Request brings a comprehensive set of features, performance improvements, Docker compatibility enhancements, and codebase refactoring from the `RianFC/watgbridge` fork to the main repository.

Below is a detailed breakdown of all the additions and improvements introduced in this version.

---

## 🚀 Key Features & Enhancements

### 1. 📱 Advanced WhatsApp Client Emulation (Android & Android Business)
* **Detailed Emulation:** Configures the WhatsApp client payload to emulate a physical Android device (Samsung SM-G900F, Android 14) or an Android Business client.
* **View-Once Media Support:** Emulating an Android client allows the bot to receive and decrypt view-once media which WhatsApp normally blocks on web/desktop clients.
* **Flexible Configuration:** The emulation mode is configured dynamically using `client_mode` (`android`, `android_business`, or `web` companion).

### 2. 🔄 Two-Way Message Editing Support
* **Telegram to WhatsApp:** Message edits and caption updates made on Telegram are seamlessly mirrored to WhatsApp.
* **WhatsApp to Telegram:** WhatsApp message updates and edits are captured and edited on Telegram, with option toggles like `send_edited_message_updates`.

### 3. 🎭 Media & Sticker Improvements
* **Animated Stickers:** Added full WEBM/WebP conversion for animated stickers in both directions.
* **WhatsApp Media as Files:** Support for sending WhatsApp images and stickers to Telegram as uncompressed files/documents.
* **Audio Transcoding:** Added automatic audio conversion to WhatsApp-compatible format when bridging from Telegram.

### 4. 📊 Reactions & Message Tracking
* **Read Receipts Auto-Reactions:** Automatically reacts to bridged messages when they are marked as read.
* **Receipt Tracking:** Tracks WhatsApp message delivery/read receipts with an `/info` command on Telegram to query message details.
* **Delayed Reaction Clean-up:** Automatically removes temporary message reaction confirmations after a customizable delay.

### 5. 👥 Group Management & Commands
* **Group Member Listing:** Added `/findgroupmembers` command on Telegram to list all members of a linked WhatsApp group.
* **Tag All Configuration:** Configurable control over the `@all` tagging functionality (`tag_all_allowed_groups`, `tag_all_enabled`).

### 6. 💾 Cron-Based Automatic Backups
* **Schedule via Cron:** Replaced simple hour intervals with standard cron schedule expressions for automatic database backups.
* **Manual Backups:** Added a command to trigger manual database backups on-demand.

---

## 🛠️ Docker, CI/CD & System Enhancements
* **GitHub Actions Workflow:** Added CI workflows for automatically building and publishing Docker images to registry.
* **Go Version Upgrades:** Bumped Go base version to `1.25` in Dockerfiles and workflows.
* **Docker Compose Setup:** Included standard `docker-compose.yml.sample` and improved container configuration setup.
* **OS Portability:** Replaced basic path manipulation with Go's `path/filepath` package for better cross-OS compatibility.

---

## 🧹 Codebase Maintainability & Refactoring
* **Modularized Message Bridging:** Extracted bridging logic from the giant `handlers.go` file into a new helper module [whatsapp/helpers.go](file:///home/rian/Documentos/GitHub/watgbridge/whatsapp/helpers.go).
* **Bridge Context Pattern:** Introduced a clean `bridgeContext` structure in Go to manage state across asynchronous media-type handlers, significantly improving readability and error handling.

author: wajidalii
body:
## Summary
- Fixes a real bug: `POST /batches/:id/publish` enqueued every row's real publish job immediately regardless of platform. For Instagram — which has no platform-side scheduling; a container simply expires 24h after creation (TDD.md §1.2/§5 risk 1) and `adapter.publish()` always runs the full create→poll→publish sequence synchronously — scheduling a post for next week actually published it to Instagram right away.
- `/publish` now leaves rows without native scheduling (Instagram) in `awaiting_app_managed_publish`, untouched by BullMQ, when `scheduledAt` is in the future. Rows with no `scheduledAt`, or one already due, still publish immediately (unchanged behavior).
- New `cron/appManagedPublishSweep.ts`: a due-job poller on a 20s cadence (tighter than poll-status's 5-minute one, since this sweep *is* the scheduler for Instagram, not just a confirmation check) that enqueues the real publish job once `scheduled_at` arrives, flipping the row to `queued`.
- Deliberately DB-state-driven, same pattern as the existing poll-status/health-check sweeps, rather than a BullMQ delayed job scheduled far in advance — a worker/API restart just re-derives "what's due" from Postgres on the next tick, so redelivery/durability falls out of the design instead of needing separate handling.
- Rows found more than a configurable threshold (`APP_MANAGED_PUBLISH_LATE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES`, default 5 minutes) past their `scheduled_at` are logged as a distinct `[app-managed-publish-late]` alert event before being enqueued anyway — still published, just flagged as late, matching PROJECT.md's observability NFR for this specific SLO.
- Dashboard status wording ("Scheduled — ReelBridge will publish" vs "Scheduled — platform will publish") was already correct from the earlier unified-status-dashboard work — no UI changes needed for that AC.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `post_targets` rows for Instagram targets with a future `scheduled_at` sit in `awaiting_app_managed_publish`, not `native_scheduled`
- [x] A due-job poller triggers the publish sequence at (or within a tight, documented tolerance of) the scheduled time — not run early
- [x] Alerting fires if an `awaiting_app_managed_publish` item is more than N minutes late (N configurable)
- [x] Worker restart/redelivery recovers and publishes late items rather than losing them — by design (stateless DB polling), demonstrated by the "late" test
- [x] UI language already frames this as "ReelBridge-managed" rather than "platform-guaranteed" (pre-existing)

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run test` — 171 passed, 0 skipped (ran with local Postgres/Redis/MinIO up)
- [x] New integration tests: `appManagedPublishSweep.integration.test.ts` (due rows enqueued + flipped to `queued`, future rows left alone, lateness alert logged for a stale row) and two new `batchesPublish.integration.test.ts` cases (future-scheduled Instagram row deferred without enqueuing; no-`scheduledAt` Instagram row enqueued immediately)
